data.description: 47-year-old male with tenesmus and mucoid stool, admitted from a local clinic. He had a 20-year smoking history and a past history of pulmonary tuberculosis treated for 9 months, with no alcohol use. On admission, he had no weight loss, fever, or night sweats. Physical examination was largely unremarkable except for a depressed anterior chest wall; no lymphadenopathy, and heart/lung examinations were normal. Vital signs were stable. Laboratory tests were largely normal, including hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL, WBC 4,600/μL, and platelets 305,000/μL. Chest radiograph showed a right upper lung scar consistent with old tuberculosis. Upper endoscopy showed a healed duodenal bulb ulcer with negative Helicobacter pylori rapid urease test. Additional evaluation showed normal β2-microglobulin, polyclonal gammopathy on serum protein electrophoresis, no abdominal lymphadenopathy on CT, and no abnormalities on bone marrow aspiration and biopsy.

data.diagnosis: Primary rectal extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma)
data.description: An indolent B-cell lymphoma arising in rectal mucosal lymphoid tissue. The apparent small-lymphocyte infiltrate and lymphoepithelial lesions make this the leading possibility, pending confirmation with immunophenotyping and clonality studies.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent nodular rectal mucosal lesions on endoscopy
Dense small lymphoid infiltrate with apparent gland invasion on biopsy
Absence of constitutional symptoms, lymphadenopathy, or bone marrow involvement is compatible with localized disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No major discordant presenting symptoms; the healed duodenal ulcer and old pulmonary tuberculosis scar are likely unrelated

data.description: A benign proliferation of mucosal lymphoid tissue that can produce rectal nodules and mimic lymphoma. Preserved follicular architecture and a polyclonal tissue lymphocyte population would favor this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of weight loss, fever, or night sweats
Normal blood counts and no lymphadenopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent gland-invasive lymphoid lesions on biopsy are more concerning for MALT lymphoma than uncomplicated reactive hyperplasia

data.diagnosis: Mantle cell lymphoma involving the colorectum
data.description: A mature B-cell lymphoma that can involve the gastrointestinal tract as multiple lymphomatous polyps. Diagnosis requires appropriate markers, including cyclin D1 or evidence of a CCND1 rearrangement.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent polypoid or nodular mucosal lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal or peripheral lymphadenopathy
Normal bone marrow examination
Apparent lymphoepithelial lesions are more characteristic of MALT lymphoma

data.description: An indolent germinal-center B-cell lymphoma that can occasionally produce gastrointestinal nodules. A follicular growth pattern and characteristic immunophenotype are needed for confirmation.
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent gland-invasive lymphoid lesions rather than a clearly follicular pattern
Rectal presentation is less typical than small-intestinal involvement in primary gastrointestinal follicular lymphoma

data.description: Inflammatory bowel disease confined to the rectum, typically causing urgency, tenesmus, mucus, and rectal bleeding. Biopsy usually shows chronic crypt architectural changes and active crypt inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Normal systemic laboratory findings can occur in limited disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Nodular or polypoid lesions rather than typical diffuse friability
Dense small lymphoid infiltrate with apparent lymphoepithelial lesions is not the usual biopsy pattern
No reported rectal bleeding

data.diagnosis: Extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of MALT (rectum/colon)
data.description: Low-grade B-cell lymphoma arising in mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue; in the colorectum it appears as nodular or polypoid mucosal lesions with dense small lymphoid infiltrates forming lymphoepithelial lesions, usually localized and indolent.
symptoms_in_common: Nodular/polypoid rectal mucosal lesions and a depressed erythematous lesion on colonoscopy
Dense infiltrate of small to medium lymphoid cells around crypts on biopsy
Membranous B-cell marker (CD20-type) staining with lymphoepithelial lesions
No B symptoms (no fever, weight loss, night sweats)
Normal blood counts and normal β2-microglobulin
No lymphadenopathy on examination or CT
Normal bone marrow, consistent with localized disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative Helicobacter pylori test (association is mainly with gastric MALT lymphoma)
Polyclonal rather than monoclonal gammopathy
Colorectal location is uncommon compared with the stomach
Healed duodenal ulcer is unrelated

data.description: Aggressive B-cell lymphoma (cyclin D1 positive) that frequently involves the gastrointestinal tract as multiple polypoid lesions in middle-aged to older men.
symptoms_in_common: Small to medium B-cell lymphoid infiltrate in the mucosa
symptoms_not_in_common: No lymphadenopathy on examination or CT
Normal bone marrow (marrow involvement is common)
Normal β2-microglobulin and blood counts
Lymphoepithelial lesions are unusual in mantle cell lymphoma
No B symptoms
Lesions appear localized rather than diffuse polyposis

data.diagnosis: Follicular lymphoma of the gastrointestinal tract
data.description: Indolent germinal-centre-derived B-cell lymphoma that can present in the gut as small whitish nodules or polyps, often found incidentally.
symptoms_in_common: Normal laboratory tests and normal bone marrow
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse infiltrate with lymphoepithelial lesions rather than a follicular pattern
Rectal location (GI follicular lymphoma favours the duodenum/small bowel)
No lymphadenopathy
Polyclonal gammopathy is not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Benign lymphoid hyperplasia of the rectum (rectal tonsil)
data.description: Reactive, localized proliferation of lymphoid tissue in the rectal mucosa that forms nodules or polyps and can mimic lymphoma clinically and histologically.
symptoms_in_common: Dense lymphoid infiltrate in the mucosa
Polyclonal gammopathy, suggesting a reactive process
No systemic symptoms, lymphadenopathy or marrow involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse sheets of B cells with lymphoepithelial lesions destroying crypt epithelium favour lymphoma
Lack of clearly organized reactive follicles with germinal centres in the biopsy shown
Additional depressed erythematous lesion is atypical
Persistent tenesmus and mucoid stool are more than expected for an often incidental finding

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the bowel, usually ileocaecal, causing ulcers, nodularity and strictures with caseating granulomas on histology.
symptoms_in_common: Past history of pulmonary tuberculosis with right upper lobe scar
Nodular and depressed/ulcerated colonic mucosal lesions
Polyclonal gammopathy consistent with chronic inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, weight loss or night sweats
Biopsy shows monotonous lymphoid infiltrate without granulomas or caseation
Strong diffuse B-cell marker staining with lymphoepithelial lesions
Rectal involvement is uncommon (ileocaecal region is typical)
No abdominal lymphadenopathy on CT
No evidence of active pulmonary disease

data.description: 36-year-old obese woman with a 5-year history of type 2 diabetes presented with 5 days of fever, chills, cough with yellow sputum, and sharp right lower chest pain worsened by deep breathing. Initial examination was unremarkable, but on return 5 days later she was febrile (39°C) with mild tachycardia (104 bpm) and had decreased air entry with bronchial breath sounds in the right lower chest. History includes a positive Mantoux test, smoking one pack per day, social alcohol use, and a recent stay at a lakeside cottage with two nights sleeping in a gazebo about 1 week before symptom onset.

Acute bacterial infection of the lung, commonly caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae. The clinical presentation and right-sided consolidation strongly support pneumonia, although imaging cannot identify the organism.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased air entry and bronchial breath sounds
Right-predominant consolidation with bilateral air-space opacities on the supplied images
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly discordant presenting symptoms; the lakeside exposure is not specifically explained by routine bacterial pneumonia

data.description: Fungal lung infection acquired by inhaling Blastomyces spores from soil, often near waterways. It can resemble bacterial pneumonia and produce progressive focal or multifocal consolidation.
symptoms_in_common: Recent outdoor stay at a lakeside cottage
Focal consolidation and bilateral patchy pulmonary opacities
symptoms_not_in_common: Symptom onset only about one week after the reported exposure is shorter than the usual incubation period
Abrupt illness over several days is less typical than a subacute presentation, although acute pneumonia can occur

data.description: Bacterial pneumonia acquired through inhalation of contaminated water aerosols. Diabetes and smoking increase susceptibility, and pulmonary infiltrates may become multifocal.
symptoms_in_common: Diabetes and cigarette smoking as susceptibility factors
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent yellow sputum is less characteristic than an initially dry or minimally productive cough
Sleeping outdoors near a lake does not itself establish exposure to contaminated water aerosols

data.description: Francisella tularensis infection involving the lungs, acquired through inhalation of contaminated environmental material or following vector-associated infection. Outdoor exposure makes it a consideration.
symptoms_not_in_common: Purulent yellow sputum is less typical than a dry cough
No specific tick bite, animal contact, or aerosol-generating environmental exposure is reported

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the lungs. A previous positive Mantoux test suggests prior sensitization but does not establish active disease; diabetes increases the risk of progression.
symptoms_in_common: History of a positive Mantoux test
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset with high fever and chills over several days is less typical than a prolonged illness
Acute purulent sputum production is more suggestive of bacterial pneumonia
Lower-lung-predominant consolidation without visible upper-lobe cavitation is less typical of classic reactivation tuberculosis

data.description: Infection with the dimorphic fungus Blastomyces dermatitidis, acquired by inhaling spores from moist soil and decaying wood near lakes and waterways (endemic around the Great Lakes and Northern Ontario). It often mimics bacterial pneumonia, fails to respond to antibiotics, and can progress to multilobar disease or ARDS, particularly in diabetics.
symptoms_in_common: Right lower lobe consolidation with bronchial breath sounds
Progression on serial imaging from lobar consolidation to bilateral patchy, mass-like air-space disease
Lakeside cottage stay with outdoor sleeping in a gazebo
Diabetes as a risk factor for more severe disease
Worsening over days to weeks, consistent with pneumonia not responding to initial management
symptoms_not_in_common: Incubation is usually 3-6 weeks, so onset about 1 week after exposure is short
No skin lesions
No bone or genitourinary involvement described
Acute onset is more typical of bacterial pneumonia

data.description: Acute bacterial infection of the lung parenchyma, most commonly pneumococcal, producing lobar consolidation. Smokers and diabetics are at higher risk.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased air entry and bronchial breath sounds in the right lower chest
Right lower lobe consolidation on chest X-ray
Smoking and diabetes as risk factors
symptoms_not_in_common: Progression to bilateral multifocal nodular and mass-like consolidation on later imaging is atypical
Apparent worsening over weeks rather than resolution
The lakeside outdoor exposure is not specifically relevant

data.description: Atypical pneumonia caused by Legionella pneumophila, acquired from aerosolised fresh water sources. It can be severe and rapidly progressive with multilobar involvement, and smokers and diabetics are particularly susceptible.
symptoms_in_common: Lobar consolidation progressing to bilateral multilobar infiltrates
Smoking and diabetes as risk factors
Water-related exposure at a lakeside cottage within the 2-10 day incubation window
Failure to improve, as would occur with beta-lactam therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: No gastrointestinal symptoms such as diarrhoea
No confusion or other neurological symptoms
No relative bradycardia (she is tachycardic)
Sputum is purulent, whereas Legionella often gives scant or non-purulent sputum
No hyponatraemia reported

data.description: Infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Latent infection can reactivate, especially in diabetics, causing subacute to chronic pneumonia. Diabetics more often have atypical lower-lobe involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Diabetes as a risk factor for reactivation
Progressive infiltrates not resolving over time
Lower-lobe disease, which is seen more often in diabetics
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute onset over 5 days rather than weeks to months
No night sweats, weight loss or haemoptysis
No upper-lobe predominance or cavitation
Lobar consolidation with rapid bilateral spread is unusual

data.description: Endemic fungal infection caused by Histoplasma capsulatum, acquired by inhaling spores from soil contaminated with bird or bat droppings. Acute disease presents as a flu-like illness with pneumonia 1-3 weeks after exposure.
symptoms_in_common: Outdoor exposure about 1 week before symptoms, with possible bird or bat droppings around the gazebo
Bilateral patchy and nodular infiltrates on later imaging
Lack of response as expected with antibacterial therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: Dense lobar consolidation is uncommon; diffuse nodular infiltrates are more typical
No hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy described
Purulent sputum is atypical because the cough is usually dry
Acute disease is usually self-limited in immunocompetent hosts
No definite history of heavy exposure to bird or bat droppings or to caves

data.description: A 44-year-old man was hospitalized because of jaundice. Physical examination revealed normal findings except jaundice, and his past medical history was unremarkable. Complete blood count showed hemoglobin of 15 g/dL, white blood cell count of 8,200/μL with differential of 79% segmented neutrophils, 15% lymphocytes, 5% monocytes, and 1% eosinophils, and platelet count of 248,000/μL. Liver function test showed elevation of total bilirubin (15.3 mg/dL), direct bilirubin (9.4 mg/dL), and alkaline phosphatase (298 IU/L). Immunohistochemical stains showed tumor cells positive for leukocyte common antigen (CD 45) and negative for CD 3,4,5,8,10,21,23,56 and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase. Bone marrow aspirate and biopsy showed neither significant abnormalities nor evidence of myelodysplasia or leukemic infiltration.

data.diagnosis: Isolated myeloid sarcoma of the bile duct
data.description: An extramedullary tumor of immature myeloid cells that can involve the bile duct and cause obstruction without detectable leukemia in the bone marrow. Myeloperoxidase, CD117, and other myeloid markers are needed to establish lineage.
symptoms_in_common: Jaundice with markedly elevated direct and total bilirubin
Elevated alkaline phosphatase consistent with biliary obstruction
Imaging suggests a hilar or proximal bile duct lesion with upstream biliary dilation
CD45-positive tumor cells lacking the reported lymphoid markers
Normal blood counts and uninvolved bone marrow are compatible with isolated myeloid sarcoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear contradictory clinical finding; however, myeloid lineage is not established by the reported immunostains alone

data.diagnosis: Primary biliary diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: An uncommon extranodal B-cell lymphoma involving the bile duct or adjacent hilar tissue, potentially mimicking cholangiocarcinoma. Confirmation requires B-cell markers such as CD20 and PAX5.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated direct bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
Apparent hilar or proximal biliary lesion
Negative CD3 and other reported T-cell markers
Normal bone marrow is compatible with localized extranodal disease
symptoms_not_in_common: The biopsy image does not clearly demonstrate the characteristic large-cell morphology
B-cell lineage has not been demonstrated by the supplied marker panel

data.diagnosis: Histiocytic sarcoma involving the bile duct
data.description: A rare malignant tumor showing mature histiocytic differentiation that can occur at extranodal sites. Diagnosis requires characteristic morphology and histiocytic markers such as CD163, CD68, and lysozyme.
symptoms_in_common: Negative reported T-cell, follicular dendritic-cell, and natural killer-cell markers
Normal blood counts and absence of marrow infiltration
symptoms_not_in_common: The provided histology does not clearly show the abundant cytoplasm and marked pleomorphism typically expected
No histiocytic differentiation markers are reported

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor arising in the bile ducts near the hepatic hilum, commonly causing biliary narrowing and obstructive jaundice. The reported tumor immunophenotype strongly argues against this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Jaundice as the principal presenting symptom
Imaging suggests proximal biliary obstruction with upstream ductal dilation
Normal blood counts and bone marrow
symptoms_not_in_common: CD45 positivity in the tumor cells is inconsistent with an epithelial carcinoma
The histology appears to show a predominantly nongland-forming cellular infiltrate rather than malignant epithelial glands

data.diagnosis: B-lymphoblastic lymphoma involving the bile duct
data.description: A tumor of immature B-lineage lymphoid cells that can present as an extranodal mass with little or no marrow involvement. B-lineage markers and markers of immaturity are required for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: A localized lesion producing obstructive jaundice
Normal blood counts and lack of marrow infiltration are compatible with a lymphoma presentation
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase strongly argues against typical lymphoblastic lymphoma
Negative CD10 is less typical, although it does not independently exclude the diagnosis
No B-lineage markers are provided

data.diagnosis: Granulocytic (myeloid) sarcoma of the bile duct
data.description: Extramedullary tumor of immature myeloid cells that can arise without bone marrow involvement (isolated/non-leukemic form) and may infiltrate the biliary tree, mimicking hilar cholangiocarcinoma.
symptoms_in_common: Obstructive jaundice with elevated direct bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
Hilar bile duct wall thickening/stricture with intrahepatic duct dilatation on CT/MRCP
Diffuse infiltrate of small-to-medium round cells around preserved bile duct glands
Negative for T-cell markers (CD3, CD4, CD5, CD8), B-cell/follicular markers (CD10, CD21, CD23), CD56 and TdT
Cytoplasmic granular positivity on special immunostain (consistent with myeloperoxidase/lysozyme)
Normal bone marrow and normal peripheral blood counts (isolated form)
symptoms_not_in_common: No history or evidence of acute myeloid leukemia or myelodysplasia
Normal complete blood count
Biliary tract is a very rare site

data.description: Adenocarcinoma arising from the bile duct epithelium at the hepatic duct confluence, the most common cause of malignant hilar biliary stricture.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated direct bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase
Hilar stricture with intrahepatic bile duct dilatation on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Tumor cells are CD45 positive (hematopoietic, not epithelial)
Histology shows discohesive round cell infiltrate with benign-appearing preserved glands rather than malignant glands with desmoplasia
Relatively young age without risk factors

data.diagnosis: Primary non-Hodgkin lymphoma of the bile duct (e.g., diffuse large B-cell lymphoma)
data.description: Rare extranodal lymphoma arising in the biliary tree, presenting with obstructive jaundice and mimicking cholangiocarcinoma.
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative T-cell markers (CD3, CD4, CD5, CD8)
Negative CD10, CD21, CD23 with no reported B-cell marker positivity
No lymphadenopathy, B symptoms or splenomegaly
Granular cytoplasmic staining pattern suggesting myeloid lineage

data.diagnosis: Extramedullary plasmacytoma of the bile duct
data.description: Localized plasma cell neoplasm in soft tissue outside the bone marrow; rarely involves the biliary tract causing obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Infiltrate of discohesive round cells, some with eccentric nuclei
Negative for T-cell and most B-cell lineage markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Strong CD45 positivity (plasma cell neoplasms are often CD45 weak/negative)
CD56 negative (often positive in neoplastic plasma cells)
No monoclonal protein, anemia, renal or bone abnormality reported

data.description: Immune-mediated fibroinflammatory disease of the bile ducts with dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate that causes strictures mimicking hilar cholangiocarcinoma.
symptoms_in_common: Painless obstructive jaundice in a middle-aged man
Bile duct wall thickening and hilar stricture with upstream dilatation
Dense CD45-positive inflammatory cell infiltrate around preserved bile duct glands
Normal blood counts and bone marrow
symptoms_not_in_common: Infiltrate described as tumor cells (monotonous neoplastic population)
Negative CD3, CD4, CD8 (a reactive infiltrate would contain many T cells)
No storiform fibrosis, obliterative phlebitis or pancreatic involvement described
No elevated serum IgG4 reported

data.description: 32-year-old woman, gravida 1 para 0, with prior CIN II treated by loop excision 2 years earlier, bilateral breast reduction with delayed but spontaneous wound healing 13 years earlier, and chronic hypertension diagnosed at 18 weeks’ gestation. At 31 weeks 4 days of pregnancy, she presented with 2 weeks of preceding flu-like symptoms, headache, and sore throat, then developed lower abdominal pain and fever. Examination showed temperature 38.3°C, uterine contractions, fundal height at 29 weeks, cervix 1 cm dilated and fully effaced with intact membranes. Ultrasound showed fetal growth at the 5th percentile and oligohydramnios; cardiotocography showed fetal heart rate 160 bpm with late decelerations. Labs revealed leukocytosis with neutrophilia and markedly elevated C-reactive protein. After cesarean delivery for suspected fetal distress, she developed persistent postoperative fever, rising inflammatory markers, and a non-healing surgical wound despite antibiotics and standard wound care.

A noninfectious neutrophilic skin disorder that can be triggered by surgery and cause progressive ulceration with violaceous borders. This is the leading consideration for the wound, but requires exclusion of infection and other ulcerative disorders.
symptoms_in_common: Non-healing cesarean wound despite antibiotics and standard wound care
Large ulcerated surgical wound with violaceous margins visible in the photograph
Persistent fever, neutrophilic leukocytosis, and markedly elevated inflammatory markers
Previous delayed healing after breast reduction, potentially suggesting an earlier surgery-triggered episode
symptoms_not_in_common: Antepartum sore throat and flu-like illness are not characteristic
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios are not typical direct manifestations
Preterm contractions and fetal distress are not usually explained by a localized postoperative skin disorder

data.description: A bacterial infection involving a surgical incision and potentially deeper tissues, causing inflammation, wound breakdown, and systemic illness. Failure of antibiotics can occur with resistant organisms or an undrained collection.
symptoms_in_common: Neutrophilic leukocytosis and rising inflammatory markers
Open wound with inflammatory changes and yellowish slough visible in the photograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Violaceous ulcer margins are more suggestive of an inflammatory ulcerative disorder
Previous delayed healing at an unrelated surgical site is not explained by a single current infection
Antepartum fever and fetal abnormalities preceded the surgical incision and cannot be explained by its infection

data.description: A potentially life-threatening infection that destroys subcutaneous tissue and fascia. It must be urgently excluded in a postoperative patient with systemic inflammation and progressive wound breakdown.
symptoms_in_common: Postoperative fever with substantial systemic inflammation
Discolored wound margins and ulceration visible in the photograph
symptoms_not_in_common: A persistent non-healing course is less typical than the rapid progression usually seen
Previous delayed but spontaneous healing after breast surgery does not fit an untreated necrotizing infection
Antepartum flu-like symptoms, fetal growth restriction, and oligohydramnios are not explained by a postoperative necrotizing infection

data.description: An acute febrile neutrophilic dermatosis that can follow infection or surgery. Rare postoperative necrotizing variants can resemble wound infection or pyoderma gangrenosum.
symptoms_in_common: Preceding flu-like symptoms and sore throat
Neutrophilic leukocytosis and elevated C-reactive protein
symptoms_not_in_common: A large ulcer with violaceous borders is more characteristic of pyoderma gangrenosum than classic Sweet syndrome
Previous prolonged surgical wound healing is not a typical feature
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios are not characteristic manifestations

data.description: Maternal infection with Listeria monocytogenes can begin as a nonspecific febrile illness and spread to the placenta, causing preterm labor and fetal compromise. It could explain the antepartum presentation but not the distinctive wound findings.
symptoms_in_common: Lower abdominal pain and preterm uterine contractions
Neutrophilic leukocytosis and markedly elevated C-reactive protein
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive postoperative ulceration with violaceous margins is not characteristic
Persistent non-healing surgical wound is not a usual manifestation
Previous delayed healing after breast reduction is unrelated
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios are nonspecific rather than characteristic findings

data.description: A sterile neutrophilic dermatosis in which surgical trauma triggers rapidly enlarging, painful ulceration with violaceous undermined borders at the incision site; it mimics wound infection but does not respond to antibiotics or debridement and improves with immunosuppression.
symptoms_in_common: Non-healing cesarean wound despite antibiotics and standard wound care
Ulcerated wound with violaceous border and surrounding erythema in the image
Fibrinous, cribriform-appearing ulcer bed extending symmetrically along the incision
Leukocytosis with neutrophilia and markedly elevated, rising C-reactive protein
History of delayed wound healing after breast reduction (possible earlier pathergy)
Pregnancy and the postpartum period as a recognized trigger
symptoms_not_in_common: Flu-like symptoms, headache and sore throat for 2 weeks before delivery
Fever, abdominal pain and contractions before the surgery
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios
Chronic hypertension
No known associated systemic disease such as inflammatory bowel disease, arthritis or hematologic malignancy

data.diagnosis: Surgical site infection with wound dehiscence
data.description: Bacterial infection of the cesarean incision, often by Staphylococcus aureus, streptococci or mixed flora, causing erythema, purulent discharge, wound breakdown and fever.
symptoms_in_common: Open, non-healing surgical wound with exudate and surrounding erythema
Possible intrauterine infection before delivery as a risk factor for wound infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No response to antibiotics and standard wound care
Rising inflammatory markers despite treatment
Violaceous undermined wound border
Previous delayed wound healing after an unrelated operation
Preceding flu-like illness and sore throat

data.description: A rapidly spreading, life-threatening bacterial infection of subcutaneous tissue and fascia, frequently due to group A streptococcus or polymicrobial flora, causing tissue necrosis and systemic toxicity; it requires urgent surgical debridement.
symptoms_in_common: Postoperative fever with rising inflammatory markers
Progressive wound breakdown with dusky, violaceous skin margins
Failure to improve on antibiotics alone
Preceding sore throat, a possible source of group A streptococcus
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported hemodynamic instability, sepsis or organ failure
No crepitus, bullae, or frank black necrosis described or seen
Subacute course with a relatively clean, granulating and fibrinous wound bed rather than fulminant spread
Earlier episode of delayed wound healing that resolved spontaneously
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios

data.description: Infection of the fetal membranes, amniotic fluid and uterus, which presents with maternal fever, uterine tenderness, preterm labor and fetal tachycardia, and can continue after cesarean delivery as endometritis with ongoing fever.
symptoms_in_common: Lower abdominal pain and uterine contractions with preterm cervical change
Fetal heart rate at the upper limit of normal (160 bpm) with late decelerations
Leukocytosis with neutrophilia and markedly elevated C-reactive protein
Previous loop excision of the cervix as a risk factor for ascending infection and preterm labor
symptoms_not_in_common: Intact membranes
Ulcerating skin wound with violaceous border
No response to antibiotics
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios (more suggestive of placental insufficiency from hypertension)
Previous delayed wound healing after breast surgery

data.description: Food-borne infection with Listeria monocytogenes, which in pregnancy typically causes a flu-like illness followed by intrauterine infection, preterm labor, fetal distress and risk of fetal loss.
symptoms_in_common: Two weeks of flu-like symptoms, headache and sore throat in the third trimester
Subsequent fever and lower abdominal pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Non-healing ulcerated surgical wound with violaceous border
Persistent fever and rising inflammatory markers despite antibiotics
Fetal growth restriction and oligohydramnios
Previous delayed wound healing after breast surgery
No reported dietary exposure or gastrointestinal symptoms

data.description: 10-month-old male admitted with fever. Born at 38 weeks gestation after unremarkable pregnancy, birth weight 2,960g. History of cephalhematoma over parietooccipital region at birth, bilateral inguinal hernia repair at 2 months, recurrent pneumonia and urinary tract infection. Growth parameters below 3rd percentile (weight: 7,500g, length: 73.7cm). Physical exam showed pale skin, sparse/light/curly hair with pili torti on microscopy. Neurologic exam revealed diffuse hypotonia with poor head/trunk support, no visual fixing/following, hyperreflexic deep tendon reflexes bilaterally with ankle clonus, bilateral Babinski extension. Lab results: serum copper 27 μg/dL (normal 70-130), ceruloplasmin 9.07 μg/dL (normal 20-60).
The most likely diagnosis: an X-linked ATP7A-related copper transport disorder causing copper deficiency, severe infantile neurologic impairment, abnormal hair, and connective-tissue weakness.
symptoms_in_common: Male infant with severe developmental impairment and poor growth
Sparse, light, curly hair with pili torti
Markedly low serum copper and ceruloplasmin
Diffuse hypotonia with poor head and trunk support
Hyperreflexia, ankle clonus, and extensor plantar responses
Imaging shows marked arterial tortuosity and symmetric white-matter signal and diffusion abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever is not a defining feature and may reflect a concurrent infection
Cephalhematoma at birth is nonspecific

data.description: A milder ATP7A-related copper transport disorder dominated by connective-tissue abnormalities, including hernias, vascular tortuosity, and bladder diverticula; profound infantile neurologic disease is unusual.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe neurologic impairment by 10 months
Absent visual fixing and following
Prominent hyperreflexia and ankle clonus
Pronounced pili torti
Extensive symmetric white-matter abnormalities

data.description: Copper depletion from inadequate intake, malabsorption, or excess zinc can cause anemia, impaired growth, hypopigmentation, immune dysfunction, and neurologic abnormalities, but does not readily explain this complete phenotype.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pili torti is more characteristic of inherited copper transport disease
Marked arterial tortuosity
Early bilateral inguinal hernias
Profound infantile developmental impairment with absent visual tracking

data.description: An inherited defect in biotin recycling that can cause infantile neurologic dysfunction, hypotonia, visual impairment, hair loss, and metabolic white-matter injury.
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly low copper and ceruloplasmin
Pili torti rather than typical alopecia
Marked arterial tortuosity
Bilateral inguinal hernias

data.description: A heterogeneous inherited disorder characterized by sulfur-deficient brittle hair, often accompanied by growth restriction, developmental impairment, and recurrent infections.
symptoms_not_in_common: Pili torti rather than the characteristic tiger-tail hair pattern under polarized microscopy
Markedly low serum copper and ceruloplasmin
Marked arterial tortuosity
Bilateral inguinal hernias
Symmetric diffusion abnormalities are not a defining imaging feature

data.description: X-linked recessive disorder of copper transport caused by ATP7A mutations, leading to systemic copper deficiency with progressive neurodegeneration, connective tissue abnormalities, characteristic kinky hair and tortuous vessels.
symptoms_in_common: sparse, light, curly hair with pili torti
diffuse hypotonia with poor head and trunk control
hyperreflexia, ankle clonus and Babinski signs
recurrent urinary tract infection (possibly from bladder diverticula)
tortuous intracranial and cervical arteries on MR angiography
bilateral deep white matter and corpus callosum lesions with restricted diffusion on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: seizures not reported although typical
symmetrical restricted diffusion of the white matter is a less commonly described imaging finding

data.description: Milder allelic variant of ATP7A-related copper transport disorder, with predominantly connective tissue manifestations (occipital exostoses, lax skin and joints, bladder diverticula, hernias) and mild neurological involvement.
symptoms_not_in_common: severe early neurological deterioration
marked hypotonia with pyramidal signs
lack of visual fixation
severe failure to thrive in infancy
extensive white matter lesions with restricted diffusion
copper and ceruloplasmin levels usually only mildly reduced

data.description: Copper deficiency due to inadequate intake, malabsorption or excess zinc, causing anaemia, neutropenia, bone changes and hypopigmentation.
symptoms_not_in_common: pili torti
tortuous cerebral vessels
severe neurodegeneration with pyramidal signs
cephalhematoma and inguinal hernias from early life
term infant with no history of malabsorption, prematurity or parenteral nutrition
white matter lesions with restricted diffusion

data.diagnosis: Mitochondrial leukoencephalopathy (e.g., Leigh syndrome or other mitochondrial encephalopathy)
data.description: Disorders of mitochondrial energy metabolism causing infantile neurodegeneration, with hypotonia, developmental regression and symmetrical brain lesions that may show restricted diffusion.
symptoms_in_common: symmetrical white matter lesions with restricted diffusion
symptoms_not_in_common: pili torti and sparse light hair
low serum copper and ceruloplasmin
tortuous intracranial arteries
inguinal hernias
cephalhematoma
recurrent urinary tract infection

data.description: Autosomal recessive disorder of biotin recycling presenting in infancy with hypotonia, seizures, developmental delay, alopecia or sparse hair, skin rash, optic atrophy and recurrent infections; may produce white matter lesions with restricted diffusion.
symptoms_in_common: failure to thrive and developmental delay
white matter abnormalities with restricted diffusion
symptoms_not_in_common: pili torti
low serum copper and ceruloplasmin
tortuous arteries
inguinal hernias and cephalhematoma
no skin rash or seizures reported
no metabolic acidosis reported

data.description: 63-year-old man with well-controlled hypertension and diabetes was referred from primary clinic due to hepatic mass found on ultrasonography. Physical examination was unremarkable. Laboratory findings showed normal hematological indexes, liver function tests, and renal functions. Patient was negative for viral markers with normal α-fetoprotein levels. Bone marrow biopsy showed 30% marrow cellularity but was otherwise normal. Serum calcium, β-2 microglobulin, and serum/urine protein immunoelectrophoresis were normal. Skeletal radiography revealed no abnormalities.

data.diagnosis: Solitary extramedullary plasmacytoma of the liver
data.description: A localized tumor of clonal plasma cells arising outside bone marrow. This is the leading consideration, although confirmation requires identification of the immunostains and demonstration of plasma-cell clonality.
symptoms_in_common: Biopsy appearance suggestive of a plasma-cell-rich tumor
Normal serum and urine protein immunoelectrophoresis, which can occur in localized plasmacytoma
Normal calcium, renal function, blood counts, and skeletal radiographs
Normal alpha-fetoprotein and negative viral hepatitis markers

data.diagnosis: Primary hepatic marginal zone lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation
data.description: An uncommon indolent B-cell lymphoma confined predominantly to the liver that can contain numerous differentiated plasma cells. Immunophenotyping is needed to distinguish it from plasmacytoma.
symptoms_in_common: Asymptomatic presentation with normal blood counts
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative viral hepatitis markers, although chronic hepatitis is an association rather than a requirement
Normal liver function tests are less characteristic of clinically extensive hepatic lymphoma

data.description: A benign mass-forming inflammatory lesion containing fibrosis and inflammatory cells, often including abundant plasma cells, that can mimic hepatic malignancy.
symptoms_in_common: Plasma-cell-rich tissue with apparent fibrous stroma
Normal bone marrow and systemic plasma-cell studies
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of fever, abdominal tenderness, or other inflammatory symptoms
Normal hematological indexes and liver function tests, whereas inflammatory abnormalities may occur

data.description: A primary malignancy of hepatocytes that can occasionally arise without viral hepatitis or elevated alpha-fetoprotein. The apparent plasma-cell-rich histology makes it less likely here.
symptoms_in_common: Hepatic mass in an older man
Diabetes, which is associated with increased hepatocellular carcinoma risk
An incidental, asymptomatic presentation is possible
Normal alpha-fetoprotein does not exclude the disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative viral hepatitis markers and no reported cirrhosis
Biopsy appearance suggestive of plasma cells rather than malignant hepatocytes

data.diagnosis: Multiple myeloma with hepatic extramedullary involvement
data.description: A systemic clonal plasma-cell malignancy that can involve the liver as an extramedullary mass. The negative systemic evaluation makes this substantially less likely than solitary hepatic plasmacytoma.
symptoms_in_common: Hepatic mass potentially composed of plasma cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Otherwise normal bone marrow biopsy
Normal serum and urine protein immunoelectrophoresis
Normal calcium and renal function
Normal hematological indexes
No abnormalities on skeletal radiography
Normal beta-2 microglobulin

diagnoses.name: Solitary extramedullary plasmacytoma of the liver
diagnoses.title: Extramedullary plasmacytoma

data.diagnosis: Solitary extramedullary plasmacytoma of the liver
data.description: Localized monoclonal plasma cell neoplasm arising in soft tissue outside the bone marrow, without evidence of systemic multiple myeloma.
symptoms_in_common: Hepatic mass found on ultrasonography and seen on CT/MRI
Biopsy showing sheets of plasma cells with eccentric nuclei
Diffuse immunohistochemical positivity consistent with plasma cell marker/light chain restriction
Bone marrow without plasma cell infiltration
Normal serum calcium, renal function and hematologic indexes
Normal alpha-fetoprotein and negative viral markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Liver is a very rare site (most occur in the upper aerodigestive tract)
Hypocellular marrow (30%) is nonspecific

data.diagnosis: Multiple myeloma with hepatic extramedullary involvement
data.description: Systemic malignant plasma cell disorder with marrow infiltration, monoclonal protein and end-organ damage; may involve the liver as nodular plasmacytomas.
symptoms_in_common: Hepatic mass composed of plasma cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Bone marrow without plasmacytosis
Normal serum/urine immunoelectrophoresis (no M-protein)
Normal calcium, renal function and hemoglobin
Normal beta-2 microglobulin
No lytic lesions on skeletal radiography

data.description: Primary malignant tumor of hepatocytes, usually arising in chronic liver disease or cirrhosis.
symptoms_in_common: Often asymptomatic with normal liver function early
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative viral markers
Normal alpha-fetoprotein
No evidence of chronic liver disease
Histology shows plasma cells rather than malignant hepatocytes

data.diagnosis: Primary hepatic lymphoma (e.g., MALT/marginal zone lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation or plasmablastic lymphoma)
data.description: Rare extranodal non-Hodgkin lymphoma confined to the liver; some subtypes show marked plasmacytic differentiation.
symptoms_not_in_common: No B symptoms
Normal liver function tests
Negative viral markers (often associated with hepatitis C/B)
Monotonous mature plasma cell population rather than lymphoid cells
No lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly reported

data.diagnosis: Hepatic inflammatory pseudotumor (plasma cell granuloma) / IgG4-related disease
data.description: Benign mass-forming inflammatory lesion composed of fibrous stroma with polyclonal plasma cells and other inflammatory cells, mimicking malignancy.
symptoms_in_common: Plasma cell-rich infiltrate with fibrous bands on biopsy
Normal alpha-fetoprotein and negative viral markers
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, abdominal pain or elevated inflammatory markers
Normal liver function tests
Sheets of monotonous plasma cells with diffuse uniform immunostaining suggest monoclonality rather than a mixed polyclonal infiltrate
No storiform fibrosis or obliterative phlebitis described

data.description: 34-year-old man with generalized tonic-clonic seizure and transient right-sided weakness, plus recurrent hemoptysis for 1 month. History otherwise previously well. Renal ultrasound showed normal kidney size, shape, and echogenicity. Labs: hemoglobin 10.5 g/dL, WBC 6.3 × 10³/mm³, normal complement, creatinine 1.04 mg/mL, urinalysis without protein and with a few old RBCs. Anti-GBM antibody, ANCA, dsDNA, and anti-smooth muscle antibody were negative. Bronchoscopy cultures, viral serology, and echocardiography were negative. Immunofluorescence showed linear and granular IgG deposits in lung and renal tissue.

data.diagnosis: Seronegative anti-glomerular basement membrane disease (Goodpasture disease)
data.description: An autoimmune disorder targeting basement membranes in pulmonary and renal capillaries. Circulating anti-GBM antibodies can occasionally be undetectable despite characteristic linear tissue IgG deposition. This is the leading consideration, although cerebral involvement is rare.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent hemoptysis consistent with pulmonary hemorrhage
Bilateral patchy ground-glass lung opacities compatible with alveolar hemorrhage
Linear IgG deposits in lung and renal tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative circulating anti-GBM antibody, although seronegative disease is possible
Granular IgG deposition in addition to linear deposition
Absence of proteinuria or clearly established renal dysfunction
Seizure, transient right-sided weakness, and multifocal brain abnormalities are uncommon manifestations

data.description: A small-vessel necrotizing vasculitis that can cause pulmonary capillaritis and glomerulonephritis. Some patients are ANCA-negative; central nervous system involvement is possible but uncommon.
symptoms_in_common: Seizure and focal weakness could reflect uncommon cerebral vascular involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Linear and granular IgG tissue deposits conflict with the typically pauci-immune pattern
No proteinuria or clear evidence of active glomerulonephritis
Negative ANCA reduces support, although it does not exclude the disease

data.description: A necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis affecting the respiratory tract and kidneys, sometimes involving the nervous system. ANCA-negative cases occur.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary opacities compatible with alveolar hemorrhage
Seizure, transient focal weakness, and multifocal brain lesions could reflect neurological involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Linear and granular IgG deposition is atypical for its usually pauci-immune renal pathology
No reported chronic sinusitis, nasal disease, or other upper-airway manifestations
No evident pulmonary nodules or cavitation on the supplied chest image
Negative ANCA
No proteinuria or clear renal dysfunction

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage and neuropsychiatric involvement
data.description: A systemic autoimmune disease that can cause immune-complex nephritis, pulmonary hemorrhage, seizures, and cerebral vascular or inflammatory lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Hemoptysis and bilateral ground-glass opacities compatible with alveolar hemorrhage
Multifocal cerebral and cerebellar MRI abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative anti-dsDNA antibodies
Normal complement
Linear IgG deposits are not characteristic of lupus nephritis
No reported rash, arthritis, oral ulcers, or other typical systemic manifestations
Absence of proteinuria

data.description: A diagnosis of exclusion characterized by recurrent alveolar hemorrhage and iron-deficiency anemia without an identified systemic autoimmune cause. It would not readily explain the renal tissue deposits or neurological findings.
symptoms_in_common: No proteinuria or clearly established renal dysfunction
Negative reported infectious and cardiac investigations
symptoms_not_in_common: Linear and granular IgG deposits in lung and renal tissue suggest an immune-mediated alternative
Microscopic hematuria is not a characteristic manifestation
Seizure and transient right-sided weakness are not typical
Multifocal brain MRI abnormalities are not explained by isolated pulmonary hemosiderosis

data.diagnosis: Seronegative anti-GBM disease (Goodpasture syndrome) with cerebral vasculitis
data.description: Autoimmune disease caused by antibodies against type IV collagen in alveolar and glomerular basement membranes, producing pulmonary hemorrhage and glomerulonephritis; circulating antibody can occasionally be undetectable, and CNS vasculitis is a rare association.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral ground-glass opacities on chest CT consistent with alveolar hemorrhage
Linear IgG deposits in lung and renal tissue
Seizure and transient hemiparesis with multifocal cortical and cerebellar MRI lesions consistent with reported cerebral vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative serum anti-GBM antibody
Normal creatinine and no proteinuria (renal involvement is usually rapidly progressive)
Granular component of the IgG deposits
CNS involvement is rare

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with neuropsychiatric involvement and diffuse alveolar hemorrhage
data.description: Multisystem immune-complex autoimmune disease that can cause alveolar hemorrhage, nephritis and CNS disease (seizures, stroke-like episodes).
symptoms_in_common: Granular IgG deposits in lung and kidney (immune-complex pattern)
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative dsDNA
Normal complement
Male sex
No proteinuria
No rash, arthritis, serositis or cytopenias other than anemia
Linear IgG component

data.diagnosis: ANCA-negative small-vessel vasculitis (microscopic polyangiitis / granulomatosis with polyangiitis)
data.description: Necrotizing small-vessel vasculitis causing pulmonary capillaritis with alveolar hemorrhage, glomerulonephritis and sometimes CNS vasculitis; a minority of cases are ANCA-negative.
symptoms_in_common: Seizure and transient hemiparesis with multifocal enhancing brain lesions suggesting CNS vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative ANCA
Immunofluorescence shows IgG deposits (these vasculitides are typically pauci-immune)
Normal renal function without proteinuria
No sinus/upper airway disease, nodules or cavities
No fever, rash or neuropathy reported

data.description: Autoimmune thrombophilia causing arterial and venous thromboses; can present with stroke/TIA, seizures and, rarely, diffuse alveolar hemorrhage from capillaritis.
symptoms_in_common: Multifocal cortical and cerebellar lesions that could represent small infarcts
symptoms_not_in_common: Linear and granular IgG deposition in lung and kidney
No history of venous or arterial thrombosis
No thrombocytopenia reported
Normal echocardiography (no valve vegetations)
Antiphospholipid antibodies not reported

data.diagnosis: Infective endocarditis or septic/embolic infection with pulmonary and cerebral involvement
data.description: Infection with embolization to the brain and lungs and immune-complex glomerulonephritis; can cause seizures, focal deficits, hemoptysis and hematuria.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple small enhancing brain lesions, particularly in the cerebellum
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative echocardiography
Negative bronchoscopy cultures and viral serology
Normal white cell count
No fever reported
Normal complement (usually low in infection-related glomerulonephritis)
Linear IgG deposits
Diffuse ground-glass opacities rather than peripheral nodules or cavities

data.description: A 26-year-old man presented with a firm, nontender palpable lymph node in his left cervical area. The patient had no specific past medical history. On admission, his vital signs were stable with blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, pulse rate 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min, and body temperature 36.5°C. Routine laboratory investigations showed a normal complete blood count, serum chemical tests, and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR). Serologic tests for cytomegalovirus, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis of mycobacteria yielded negative results. Serum immunoglobulin levels were within normal ranges: IgG 1,680 mg/dL (normal 700-1,700 mg/dL), IgA 117 mg/dL (normal 70-400 mg/dL), IgM 129 mg/dL (normal 40-230 mg/dL), and IgE 33.8 IU/mL (normal 0-100 IU/mL). The patient had no history of fever during the clinical course.

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, nodular sclerosis subtype
data.description: A lymphoma common in young adults that often involves cervical and mediastinal lymph nodes. The apparent fibrous bands and large lacunar-like cells in the biopsy make this the leading possibility; confirmation requires identified immunostains and formal pathology review.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent fibrous bands and scattered large atypical cells in the biopsy
Absence of fever and normal routine laboratory results are compatible with disease without systemic symptoms

data.description: A T-cell lymphoma characterized by large atypical cells, usually with strong CD30 expression. It can resemble classical Hodgkin lymphoma, particularly in young patients.
symptoms_in_common: Large atypical cells visible in the biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal ESR and absence of fever are less characteristic of a systemic inflammatory presentation
Apparent lacunar-like cells and broad fibrous bands favor nodular sclerosis Hodgkin lymphoma instead

data.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma arising in the mediastinum, usually in young adults, that can extend to cervical nodes and show tissue sclerosis.
symptoms_in_common: Large atypical cells and fibrosis in the biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: No bulky anterior mediastinal mass is clearly established by the supplied CT slice
Scattered lacunar-like cells in a mixed inflammatory background are less typical than a diffuse large B-cell proliferation

data.description: An aggressive lymphoma of mature B cells that can present as painless enlargement of cervical lymph nodes and requires tissue immunophenotyping for diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Large atypical lymphoid-appearing cells in the biopsy
Normal blood counts can occur when disease is confined to lymph nodes
symptoms_not_in_common: Young adult age is less typical than older adult presentation
The apparent scattered atypical cells and fibrous bands are less typical than diffuse sheets of malignant large B cells

data.description: A benign immune response that enlarges lymph nodes and can produce activated large lymphoid cells resembling lymphoma cells.
symptoms_in_common: Normal complete blood count and ESR
A mixed population of small lymphocytes and larger cells in the biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Firm, nontender nodal enlargement is less characteristic of acute infectious lymphadenitis
Apparent fibrous bands and lacunar-like atypical cells raise concern for lymphoma rather than uncomplicated reactive hyperplasia
Negative cytomegalovirus testing provides no support for that specific infectious trigger

data.diagnosis: Rosai-Dorfman disease (sinus histiocytosis with massive lymphadenopathy)
data.description: Rare benign non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis in which lymph node sinuses are distended by large histiocytes showing emperipolesis; the histiocytes are S-100 and CD68 positive and CD1a negative. Usually affects young people with painless cervical lymphadenopathy and may involve mediastinal nodes.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent mediastinal soft tissue/lymphadenopathy on chest CT
Biopsy showing sinuses filled with large pale histiocytes that appear to contain intact lymphocytes (emperipolesis, arrows)
Diffuse immunostain positivity in histiocytes (likely S-100) with only scattered cells positive on second stain
Negative infectious work-up (CMV, HIV, mycobacterial PCR)
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
Normal ESR
Normal complete blood count (no leukocytosis)
No polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia (IgG only borderline)
Unilateral node rather than massive bilateral lymphadenopathy

data.description: Malignant B-cell derived lymphoma characterised by Reed-Sternberg cells in a mixed inflammatory background; commonly presents in young adults with painless cervical and mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Large cells in a background of small lymphocytes
symptoms_not_in_common: No B symptoms (no fever)
Normal ESR and blood count
Large cells look like histiocytes with emperipolesis rather than Reed-Sternberg cells
Staining pattern suggests histiocytic (S-100) rather than CD15/CD30 positive cells

data.description: Clonal proliferation of Langerhans cells (S-100, CD1a and langerin positive, with grooved nuclei and eosinophils) that can involve lymph nodes, bone, skin and lung.
symptoms_not_in_common: Emperipolesis is not a feature
No grooved nuclei or prominent eosinophils evident
Second stain only marks scattered cells (consistent with CD1a negativity of the lesional cells)
No bone, skin or lung lesions
Normal serum IgE and blood count

data.description: Mycobacterial infection of lymph nodes, most often cervical, producing caseating granulomatous inflammation; nodes may be painless and chronic.
symptoms_in_common: Painless cervical lymphadenopathy in a young adult
symptoms_not_in_common: Mycobacterial PCR negative
No caseating granulomas or Langhans giant cells on biopsy
Normal ESR
Emperipolesis and S-100 positive histiocytes are not features
No pulmonary symptoms

data.diagnosis: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (e.g., anaplastic large cell lymphoma with sinusoidal pattern)
data.description: Malignant lymphoid neoplasm presenting with painless lymphadenopathy; anaplastic large cell lymphoma can infiltrate nodal sinuses with large cells and so mimic sinus histiocytosis.
symptoms_in_common: Large cells in a sinusoidal distribution
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or other B symptoms
Normal blood count, chemistry and ESR
Large cells appear cytologically bland with emperipolesis rather than atypical
Histiocytic (S-100) immunophenotype rather than lymphoid/CD30 positive
Preserved background of small lymphocytes

data.description: A 52-year-old Korean man presented with a 1-month history of general weakness that was aggravated three days before his emergency room visit. Initial neurologic examination revealed disorientation of time, place, and person, attention deficit, immediate memory disturbance, dysarthria, weakness of bilateral upper extremities with increased deep tendon reflexes, and right hemiparetic gait. Blood work showed an elevated eosinophil count of 5,500/μL, representing 41% of total white blood cells. The patient's clinical history and basic examinations did not reveal any identifiable cause of hypereosinophilia, including parasitic infection, neoplasm, vasculitis, or allergy. Additionally, the patient had no prior clinical symptoms or signs suggesting Churg-Strauss syndrome, such as sinusitis or asthma. Cardiac enzymes were elevated with creatine kinase-MB at 7.3 ng/ml and troponin-I at 4.78 ng/ml. An echocardiogram revealed mild left ventricular inferior wall hypokinesia.

data.diagnosis: Idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome with cerebral and cardiac involvement
data.description: A disorder of unexplained marked eosinophilia causing organ injury through inflammation and thrombosis. This is the leading consideration, although repeat eosinophil measurements and exclusion of clonal causes are needed.
symptoms_in_common: No identified allergic, infectious, neoplastic, or vasculitic cause
Disorientation, impaired attention, and memory disturbance
Dysarthria, limb weakness, hyperreflexia, and right hemiparetic gait
Multiple bilateral cerebral lesions on MRI suggesting multifocal ischemic injury
Elevated cardiac enzymes and left ventricular wall hypokinesia
symptoms_not_in_common: Focal cerebral susceptibility abnormality suggesting blood products is less common than ischemic injury, although hemorrhage can occur

data.diagnosis: Eosinophilic myocarditis or Loeffler endocarditis with cerebral embolization
data.description: Eosinophil-mediated cardiac inflammation or endocardial injury can produce intracardiac thrombi and embolic strokes. It may represent a cardiac manifestation of hypereosinophilic syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Multifocal bilateral cerebral MRI lesions compatible with embolic infarcts
Dysarthria, right hemiparetic gait, and cognitive impairment
symptoms_not_in_common: Pulmonary nodules are not directly explained by isolated eosinophilic cardiac disease
Bilateral upper-extremity hyperreflexia and weakness require associated cerebral injury rather than myocarditis alone

data.description: A systemic eosinophilic small-vessel vasculitis, usually associated with asthma and sinonasal disease, that can affect the lungs, heart, and nervous system.
symptoms_in_common: Neurologic deficits and multifocal cerebral lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of asthma
No history of sinusitis
No identified clinical evidence of systemic vasculitis
Central cognitive impairment and hyperreflexic weakness are less typical than peripheral neuropathy

data.diagnosis: Clonal eosinophilic disorder, including chronic eosinophilic leukemia
data.description: A hematologic disorder in which abnormal clonal cells drive eosinophil production, potentially causing cardiac damage, thrombosis, and neurologic injury. Diagnosis requires bone marrow and molecular testing.
symptoms_in_common: Multifocal cerebral lesions and focal neurologic deficits compatible with eosinophil-associated thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Pulmonary nodules are nonspecific and are not a defining manifestation
The predominantly neurologic presentation is less typical than a hematologic or systemic presentation

data.diagnosis: Tissue-invasive helminth infection causing secondary hypereosinophilia
data.description: Parasitic infections such as toxocariasis can cause substantial eosinophilia and pulmonary lesions, with occasional neurologic or cardiac involvement. Targeted exposure assessment and testing are needed to establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Initial evaluation did not identify parasitic infection
Multifocal ischemic-appearing cerebral lesions are less typical than inflammatory or granulomatous lesions
The combination of acute focal deficits and myocardial injury is uncommon in most helminth infections

data.diagnosis: Idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome (with cerebral infarction/encephalopathy and eosinophilic cardiac involvement)
data.description: Persistent marked eosinophilia (>1,500/μL) without identifiable secondary cause, producing eosinophil-mediated end-organ damage, typically of the heart (eosinophilic myocarditis/Loeffler endocarditis), brain (multiple border-zone or embolic infarcts, encephalopathy) and lungs.
symptoms_in_common: No parasitic, neoplastic, vasculitic or allergic cause identified
Multiple bilateral diffusion-restricted infarcts in border-zone distribution
Encephalopathy with disorientation, attention and memory deficits
Dysarthria, bilateral upper extremity weakness, hyperreflexia, right hemiparetic gait
Elevated troponin-I and CK-MB with left ventricular wall hypokinesia
symptoms_not_in_common: Formal definition classically requires eosinophilia documented over time (only 1-month history here)
No skin involvement reported
Small focal haemorrhagic lesion on gradient-echo MRI is less typical

data.description: ANCA-associated small-to-medium vessel necrotising vasculitis with asthma, sinusitis, eosinophilia and multi-organ involvement including heart, lungs and nervous system.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac involvement with elevated enzymes and wall hypokinesia
symptoms_not_in_common: No asthma
No sinusitis
No evidence of vasculitis on work-up
No peripheral neuropathy (mononeuritis multiplex), purpura or renal involvement
No vasculitic changes on cerebral angiography

data.diagnosis: Cardioembolic stroke from Loeffler endocarditis / eosinophilic myocarditis with mural thrombus
data.description: Eosinophil-mediated endomyocardial damage leading to mural thrombus formation and showers of emboli to the brain and other organs; often a manifestation of hypereosinophilic syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple bilateral infarcts in several vascular territories
Normal large cerebral vessels on angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: No intracardiac thrombus or endomyocardial thickening reported on echocardiogram
Infarcts predominantly in border-zone rather than cortical territorial pattern
Subacute one-month course of weakness rather than abrupt onset

data.diagnosis: Parasitic infection with eosinophilia and visceral/CNS involvement (e.g., toxocariasis, paragonimiasis)
data.description: Tissue-invasive helminth infections, relatively common in Korea, causing marked eosinophilia with migratory pulmonary nodules, eosinophilic myocarditis and cerebral lesions including infarcts or haemorrhagic foci.
symptoms_in_common: Korean patient (endemic exposure risk, raw food ingestion)
Multiple brain lesions, including a haemorrhagic focus
symptoms_not_in_common: History and basic examinations did not reveal parasitic infection
No fever, cough, haemoptysis or gastrointestinal symptoms
No hepatic lesions reported
Border-zone infarct pattern more typical of hypereosinophilia-related injury than of direct parasitic invasion

data.diagnosis: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia (chronic eosinophilic leukaemia, e.g., FIP1L1-PDGFRA-positive)
data.description: Clonal haematological disorder causing sustained eosinophilia with frequent cardiac, neurological and pulmonary end-organ damage; responsive to imatinib when PDGFRA-rearranged.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac injury with elevated enzymes and hypokinesia
symptoms_not_in_common: No neoplasm identified on initial evaluation
No splenomegaly, anaemia, thrombocytopenia or circulating blasts reported
No bone marrow or molecular confirmation of clonality

data.description: 66-year-old man with progressive neurologic symptoms beginning around 2000, including recurrent unexplained falls while riding a motorcycle. By 2003 he developed blurred vision, photophobia, frequent falls, gait imbalance, and unsteadiness. He had bilateral cataract surgery with lens implantation in 2000 without improvement. Over time he worsened with progressive imbalance, backward falls, slurred speech, inability to look down, and dysphagia. On examination he had irregular pupils with sluggish light reflexes, slow and limited vertical voluntary eye movements, slowed horizontal gaze with bilateral adduction paresis, preserved convergence initially, and later absent vertical and medial eye movements, no doll’s eye or caloric responses, and no Bell’s phenomenon. He also had slow distal rapid movements, severe nuchal rigidity and retrocollis, axial rigidity, inability to sit independently, and recurrent backward falls. Reflexes were symmetric and minimally brisk with bilateral flexor plantar responses, and there was no resting tremor.

The leading diagnostic possibility: a progressive tau-related neurodegenerative disorder characterized by early backward falls, vertical gaze palsy, and axial rigidity. The supplied MRI appears to show disproportionate midbrain atrophy, which supports this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Early, recurrent unexplained falls progressing to backward falls
Progressive gait imbalance and severe postural instability
Slow vertical eye movements and inability to look down
Severe axial and nuchal rigidity with retrocollis
Slowed distal movements without resting tremor
symptoms_not_in_common: Irregular pupils with sluggish light responses are not characteristic
Bilateral adduction paresis is less typical than vertical gaze impairment
Absent doll’s eye and caloric responses are atypical early in a supranuclear disorder, although reflex eye movements can become impaired in advanced disease

data.description: A progressive neurodegenerative disorder causing combinations of parkinsonism, cerebellar dysfunction, and autonomic failure; it can produce severe gait impairment and bulbar symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent vertical gaze palsy, particularly inability to look down
Progression to near-complete ophthalmoplegia
Retrocollis rather than the more characteristic disproportionate forward neck flexion
Early recurrent backward falls with marked axial rigidity

data.diagnosis: Corticobasal degeneration presenting as a progressive supranuclear palsy syndrome
data.description: A tau-related neurodegenerative disease that usually causes asymmetric rigidity, apraxia, and cortical dysfunction but can present with a PSP-like pattern of falls and gaze impairment.
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly symmetric motor findings
Early backward falls as the dominant manifestation
Profound bilateral ophthalmoplegia with absent vestibulo-ocular responses
Irregular, sluggishly reactive pupils

data.description: An inherited neurodegenerative disorder, also called Machado-Joseph disease, that can cause progressive ataxia, ophthalmoplegia, dysarthria, dysphagia, and parkinsonian features.
symptoms_in_common: Slow eye movements progressing to ophthalmoplegia
symptoms_not_in_common: Early, predominantly backward falls
Marked axial rigidity and retrocollis dominating the presentation
Selective early downgaze impairment
Irregular pupils with sluggish light reflexes

data.description: A rare infection caused by Tropheryma whipplei that can involve the brain and mimic PSP through supranuclear gaze palsy, gait dysfunction, and progressive neurological decline.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe axial rigidity and retrocollis as dominant features
Repeated backward falls in a classic PSP-like pattern
Complete loss of vestibulo-ocular responses
Irregular pupils with sluggish light responses

data.description: A 4-repeat tauopathy causing degeneration of the midbrain, basal ganglia and brainstem, with vertical supranuclear gaze palsy, early postural instability with backward falls, axial rigidity and pseudobulbar features. MRI typically shows midbrain atrophy (hummingbird and morning glory signs).
symptoms_in_common: Early unexplained falls and progressive imbalance
Slow and limited vertical eye movements, inability to look down
Severe nuchal rigidity with retrocollis and axial rigidity
Staring facial expression with retracted lids
symptoms_not_in_common: Absent doll's eye and caloric responses (reflex eye movements are usually preserved until very late)
Absent Bell's phenomenon
Bilateral adduction paresis resembling internuclear ophthalmoplegia with preserved convergence
Irregular pupils with sluggish light reflexes
Unusually long disease course (over 10 years)

data.description: A 4-repeat tauopathy with asymmetric akinetic-rigid syndrome, limb apraxia, dystonia, myoclonus, cortical sensory loss and alien limb; some cases present with a PSP-like phenotype.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symmetric findings without limb asymmetry
No apraxia, alien limb, myoclonus or cortical sensory loss
Prominent early vertical gaze palsy
Severe retrocollis and axial-predominant rigidity
Absent oculocephalic and caloric responses
Pupillary abnormalities

data.description: An alpha-synucleinopathy with parkinsonism, cerebellar ataxia and autonomic failure in varying combination, usually poorly responsive to levodopa.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe vertical gaze palsy and complete ophthalmoplegia
Retrocollis (antecollis is more typical)
No reported autonomic failure (orthostatic hypotension, urinary dysfunction)
Midbrain rather than pontine/cerebellar/putaminal atrophy on MRI
Long disease duration
Flexor plantar responses

data.description: An autosomal recessive lysosomal lipid storage disorder that in adults causes vertical supranuclear gaze palsy, ataxia, dystonia, dysarthria, dysphagia and cognitive or psychiatric decline.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly progressive course over many years
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset in the mid-50s (usually much younger)
No reported cognitive or psychiatric decline, splenomegaly or cataplexy
Prominent axial rigidity with parkinsonism
Absent oculocephalic and caloric responses
Pupillary abnormalities
Adduction paresis

data.diagnosis: Whipple disease of the central nervous system
data.description: A chronic Tropheryma whipplei infection that can cause supranuclear gaze palsy, oculomasticatory myorhythmia, cognitive decline, ataxia and brainstem signs; a treatable mimic of PSP.
symptoms_in_common: Vertical supranuclear gaze palsy progressing to more complete ophthalmoplegia
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss, diarrhoea, arthralgia or fever reported
No oculomasticatory myorhythmia or myoclonus
No reported cognitive decline
Slow course over more than a decade without systemic illness
Severe axial rigidity with retrocollis
Isolated midbrain atrophy on MRI without inflammatory lesions

data.description: 20-year-old male with neonatal bleeding tendency and family history of easy bruising in his father, evaluated preoperatively for chronic maxillary sinusitis surgery. He had conductive hearing loss after childhood meningitis. Preoperative labs showed normal blood counts and serum chemistry, but prolonged PT (24.5 sec) and aPTT (47.3 sec) with normal bleeding time; mixing studies suggested factor deficiency. Fibrinogen activity was markedly low (<25 mg/dL) with normal fibrinogen antigen (437 mg/dL). FGA and FGB gene testing was negative. His parents had normal coagulation studies and fibrinogen activity, with genetic testing showing wild-type alleles, indicating a de novo mutation.

data.diagnosis: Congenital dysfibrinogenemia due to a de novo FGG variant
data.description: An inherited qualitative fibrinogen disorder in which circulating fibrinogen is present but functions poorly. The sequencing image appears to show a heterozygous nucleotide change in the patient that is absent in both parents, supporting a de novo FGG variant.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly reduced fibrinogen activity despite normal fibrinogen antigen
Normal bleeding time and blood counts
Mixing studies suggesting deficiency of functional coagulation activity
Normal parental testing, consistent with a de novo variant
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic maxillary sinusitis is not a characteristic manifestation
Conductive hearing loss following meningitis is not a characteristic manifestation
Paternal easy bruising is not explained by the patient's de novo variant

data.description: A qualitative fibrinogen abnormality associated with conditions such as liver disease, paraproteinemia, or antibodies that interfere with fibrinogen function. It can produce low functional activity despite preserved antigen levels.
symptoms_in_common: Low fibrinogen activity with normal fibrinogen antigen
symptoms_not_in_common: Bleeding beginning in the neonatal period favors a congenital disorder
Normal serum chemistry provides no support for significant liver disease
An apparent de novo FGG sequence variant favors congenital dysfibrinogenemia
Chronic sinusitis and postmeningitic conductive hearing loss are not characteristic

data.description: A fibrinogen disorder combining reduced fibrinogen quantity with impaired function. Activity is disproportionately lower than antigen, but antigen is generally reduced as well.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal fibrinogen antigen of 437 mg/dL argues against a quantitative component
Chronic maxillary sinusitis is not characteristic
Conductive hearing loss following meningitis is not characteristic

data.description: A severe quantitative fibrinogen deficiency, usually caused by biallelic variants in a fibrinogen gene, that commonly presents with neonatal bleeding and markedly abnormal coagulation tests.
symptoms_in_common: Mixing studies suggesting a coagulation deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal fibrinogen antigen strongly contradicts absent fibrinogen production
The apparent heterozygous de novo sequencing finding is less consistent with the usual recessive inheritance
Chronic sinusitis and postmeningitic conductive hearing loss are not characteristic

data.description: A rare coagulation-factor deficiency that affects the common pathway, prolonging both PT and aPTT while typically preserving platelet count and bleeding time.
symptoms_in_common: Normal blood counts and bleeding time
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced fibrinogen activity with normal antigen is not explained by isolated factor V deficiency
An apparent de novo FGG variant points toward a fibrinogen disorder
Chronic maxillary sinusitis is not characteristic
Conductive hearing loss following meningitis is not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Congenital dysfibrinogenemia (FGG gene de novo heterozygous missense mutation)
data.description: Qualitative fibrinogen disorder in which a structurally abnormal fibrinogen is produced at normal quantity but with impaired function, usually due to heterozygous missense mutations in FGA, FGB or FGG. Patients may be asymptomatic, bleed, or have thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Normal bleeding time and platelet count
Mixing studies consistent with factor deficiency
Markedly low fibrinogen activity (<25 mg/dL) with normal fibrinogen antigen (437 mg/dL)
Negative FGA and FGB testing, with FGG sequencing chromatogram showing a heterozygous T/C (Y) substitution in the patient
Parents with wild-type sequence and normal coagulation studies, consistent with a de novo mutation
symptoms_not_in_common: Conductive hearing loss after childhood meningitis (unrelated)
Chronic maxillary sinusitis (unrelated)
Reported easy bruising in father despite his normal coagulation studies and wild-type genotype
Usually autosomal dominant and inherited rather than de novo

data.description: Combined quantitative and qualitative fibrinogen defect with reduced antigen levels and disproportionately lower functional activity, caused by mutations in the fibrinogen genes.
symptoms_in_common: Lifelong bleeding tendency from the neonatal period
Discrepancy between fibrinogen activity and antigen
symptoms_not_in_common: Fibrinogen antigen is normal to high (437 mg/dL) rather than reduced
Parents have normal fibrinogen activity and wild-type alleles
Conductive hearing loss and chronic sinusitis

data.description: Quantitative fibrinogen deficiency (absent or reduced fibrinogen) due to mutations in fibrinogen genes, typically autosomal recessive for afibrinogenemia. It presents with neonatal bleeding such as umbilical cord bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Mixing studies consistent with factor deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal fibrinogen antigen level (antigen would be low or absent)
Heterozygous de novo mutation rather than biallelic inheritance
Parents with wild-type alleles (carrier parents expected in afibrinogenemia)
Normal bleeding time (often prolonged in afibrinogenemia)
Conductive hearing loss and chronic sinusitis

data.diagnosis: Acquired dysfibrinogenemia (liver disease or other acquired cause)
data.description: Functionally abnormal fibrinogen acquired through liver disease (abnormal sialylation), malignancy, autoimmune disease or drugs, giving low fibrinogen activity with normal antigen.
symptoms_in_common: Low fibrinogen activity with normal fibrinogen antigen
Parents with normal coagulation studies (no inherited pattern)
symptoms_not_in_common: Bleeding tendency since the neonatal period
Normal serum chemistry with no evidence of liver disease
Young age without underlying systemic illness
Identified heterozygous FGG gene variant
Normal blood counts

data.diagnosis: Common pathway coagulation factor deficiency (factor X, V or prothrombin deficiency)
data.description: Rare inherited, usually autosomal recessive, deficiencies of common pathway factors that prolong both PT and aPTT and cause lifelong bleeding of variable severity.
symptoms_in_common: Mixing studies consistent with factor deficiency
Normal bleeding time and platelet count
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly low fibrinogen activity with normal antigen (fibrinogen is normal in these deficiencies)
FGG gene variant on sequencing
Parents with normal studies and wild-type alleles, without a recessive inheritance pattern
Conductive hearing loss and chronic sinusitis

data.description: A 25-year-old female in her third trimester of pregnancy presented with paroxysmal headache, palpitations, sweating, and hypertension up to 230/130 for three weeks. Her medical history was negative for previous hypertension, and physical examination was unremarkable. Initial work-up excluded pre-eclampsia.
