Her urine catecholamines were markedly elevated: Dopamine 607 μg/24 hours (range 65-400), Norepinephrine 978 μg/24 hours (range 15-80), Metanephrine 108 μg/24 hours (range 24-96), Normetanephrine 4067 μg/24 hours (range 75-375), and Vanillyl mandelic acid 13.6 mg/24 hours (range 2-7). Epinephrine level was normal at 0.8 μg/24 hours (range 0.0-20.0). Initial abdominal MRI showed a 28×19 mm left juxta-adrenal mass that was later found to be brown fat.

An extra-adrenal neuroendocrine tumor arising near the heart that can secrete norepinephrine. This is the leading diagnosis given the biochemical findings and the apparent cardiac-adjacent mass on the supplied images.
symptoms_in_common: Severe episodic hypertension up to 230/130 mmHg
Markedly elevated urinary norepinephrine and normetanephrine
Normal epinephrine, consistent with an extra-adrenal secretory pattern
Apparent tracer-avid mass adjacent to the heart

data.description: A catecholamine-secreting tumor of the adrenal medulla that causes episodic or sustained hypertension. The clinical and biochemical syndrome fits, but the reported adrenal-region finding was brown fat rather than an adrenal tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated urinary norepinephrine and normetanephrine
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent cardiac-adjacent rather than adrenal mass
Left juxta-adrenal finding subsequently identified as brown fat

data.description: A usually benign sympathetic nervous system tumor that can occur in the mediastinum and occasionally secrete catecholamines. It is a less likely alternative to paraganglioma.
symptoms_in_common: Headache, palpitations, sweating, and hypertension if hormonally active
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound normetanephrine elevation is more suggestive of paraganglioma
Severe paroxysmal hypertension is uncommon in ganglioneuroma
Apparent cardiac-adjacent location is less typical than a posterior mediastinal location

data.description: Excess thyroid hormone can produce adrenergic symptoms, including palpitations, sweating, and elevated systolic blood pressure, but does not adequately explain the tumor-associated findings in this case.
symptoms_not_in_common: Extreme hypertension with a diastolic pressure of 130 mmHg
Paroxysmal headache with abrupt hypertensive episodes
Markedly elevated urinary norepinephrine and normetanephrine
Apparent tracer-avid cardiac-adjacent mass

data.description: New hypertension developing after 20 weeks of pregnancy without the defining features of pre-eclampsia. Although the timing fits, it is unlikely to explain the catecholamine excess or imaging findings.
symptoms_in_common: New-onset hypertension during the third trimester
Headache accompanying severe blood pressure elevation
symptoms_not_in_common: Paroxysmal palpitations and sweating
Markedly elevated urinary catecholamines and normetanephrine
Apparent tracer-avid cardiac-adjacent mass
Distinct episodic adrenergic attacks

data.description: Rare extra-adrenal catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor arising from cardiac paraganglia, typically near the left atrium or interatrial groove; predominantly secretes norepinephrine and may be associated with SDHx mutations.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated urinary norepinephrine and normetanephrine
Intensely tracer-avid mass adjacent to left atrium/interatrial region on PET/CT
T2-hyperintense mass on cardiac MRI with perfusion and peripheral late enhancement around a non-enhancing (necrotic) core
No true adrenal tumor (juxta-adrenal lesion was brown fat)
symptoms_not_in_common: Mildly elevated metanephrine (uncommon in extra-adrenal tumors)
Onset during pregnancy is coincidental
Unremarkable physical examination

data.description: Catecholamine-secreting tumor of adrenal medullary chromaffin cells causing paroxysmal hypertension and adrenergic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated urinary catecholamines, metanephrines and VMA
Initial left juxta-adrenal mass on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Juxta-adrenal mass proved to be brown fat
Normal epinephrine (adrenal tumors often secrete epinephrine)
Avid mass located in the heart/mediastinum rather than the adrenal gland

data.diagnosis: Hereditary paraganglioma syndrome (SDHB/SDHD-related) with mediastinal paraganglioma
data.description: Germline succinate dehydrogenase mutations predisposing to extra-adrenal, often noradrenergic/dopaminergic, sometimes multifocal or malignant paragangliomas in young patients.
symptoms_in_common: Brown fat activation from catecholamine excess
symptoms_not_in_common: No family history reported
No multifocal or head-and-neck tumors described
No metastases described
Mildly elevated metanephrine

data.description: Pregnancy-specific new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks with proteinuria or end-organ dysfunction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Work-up excluded pre-eclampsia
Paroxysmal nature of symptoms
Palpitations and sweating
Markedly elevated catecholamines and metabolites
Tracer-avid cardiac mass

data.diagnosis: Other cardiac tumor (e.g., left atrial myxoma or cardiac sarcoma)
data.description: Primary cardiac neoplasms; myxoma is the most common benign tumor arising in the left atrium, while sarcomas are malignant and may be hypermetabolic on PET.
symptoms_in_common: Mass in the region of the left atrium on MRI
Hypermetabolic mass on PET (as seen in sarcoma)
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated catecholamines and metabolites
Paroxysmal severe hypertension
Headache and sweating
No embolic, constitutional or obstructive heart failure symptoms
Myxomas usually show low tracer uptake

data.description: A 31-year-old woman underwent barium enema examination as part of a medical checkup. She had been healthy without specific complaints and had no significant past medical or family history. The patient was 161 cm in height and weighed 44 kg, appeared well, and the physical examination showed no abnormalities. Complete blood cell count and biochemical analysis of the blood for hepatic and renal function, urine analysis, and fecal occult blood test were all within normal limits. The tumor markers for CEA and CA 19-9 were also normal. No lesions were observed on the upper endoscopy and the abdominal ultrasound.

advanced.reason: first diagnosis had no list: the web does not offer it

data.description: 19-year-old female with hypotonia and weak breathing/crying at birth. During the first month of life, she developed respiratory failure requiring tracheotomy and mechanical ventilation. She had patent ductus arteriosus repaired at age 2, recurrent respiratory infections, and scoliosis surgery at age 12. Electrophysiology at age 4 showed a 36% decrement in compound muscle action potential area with no repetitive CMAPs after single nerve stimulation; AChR and MuSK antibodies were negative. Recent examination showed normal cognition, bilateral ptosis, mild limitation of upward gaze, facial, bulbar, neck, and proximal limb weakness, with intact deep tendon reflexes.

An inherited neuromuscular junction disorder caused by collagen XIII deficiency, impairing endplate development. Severe neonatal respiratory weakness and abnormal postsynaptic architecture make this a leading possibility; molecular testing is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Hypotonia and weak breathing and crying at birth
Respiratory failure during the first month requiring prolonged ventilation
Bilateral ptosis and mild limitation of upward gaze
Facial, bulbar, neck, and proximal limb weakness
Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Normal cognition and intact deep tendon reflexes
Electron micrographs suggesting abnormal neuromuscular endplate architecture
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus is not a characteristic feature

data.diagnosis: CHRNE-related congenital myasthenic syndrome with acetylcholine receptor deficiency
data.description: An inherited postsynaptic disorder in which reduced acetylcholine receptor expression causes impaired neuromuscular transmission, often presenting with early ocular and generalized weakness.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral ptosis and limited upward gaze
Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Absence of repetitive CMAPs after single nerve stimulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Continuous ventilatory dependence beginning in the first month is unusually severe for many CHRNE-related cases
Patent ductus arteriosus is not characteristic

data.description: An inherited disorder of acetylcholine receptor clustering that commonly causes neonatal hypotonia, bulbar weakness, and potentially life-threatening respiratory episodes.
symptoms_in_common: Hypotonia and weak crying at birth
Facial, bulbar, neck, and proximal limb weakness
Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Limitation of ocular movements is less typical than ptosis alone
Persistent mechanical ventilation is less typical than episodic respiratory crises
Patent ductus arteriosus is not characteristic

data.description: An inherited defect in muscle-specific kinase signaling that disrupts neuromuscular junction formation and maintenance. It is distinct from autoimmune MuSK-antibody myasthenia.
symptoms_in_common: Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
Preserved cognition and deep tendon reflexes
Electron micrographs suggesting structural endplate abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Patent ductus arteriosus is not an established characteristic feature
Ocular movement limitation is variable and not a defining feature

data.description: An inherited disorder of neuromuscular junction signaling, typically producing limb-girdle weakness, sometimes with neonatal respiratory or bulbar involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Decremental response on repetitive nerve stimulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Ocular movement limitation is uncommon because extraocular movements are usually relatively spared
Severe continuous ventilatory dependence from the first month is less typical than the usual limb-girdle presentation
Patent ductus arteriosus is not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Presynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome due to impaired synaptic vesicle release (e.g., SNAP25B/synaptotagmin-2/Munc13-1 or MYO9B-related)
data.description: Rare congenital myasthenic syndromes caused by defects in the presynaptic vesicle exocytosis machinery, reducing quantal release. Present at birth with severe hypotonia, respiratory failure, ptosis and bulbar weakness; electron microscopy typically shows structurally preserved endplates with normal postsynaptic folds and small or normal nerve terminals.
symptoms_in_common: Neonatal hypotonia with weak cry and breathing
Early respiratory failure requiring tracheotomy and ventilation
Decremental CMAP response on repetitive stimulation
Facial, bulbar, neck and proximal limb weakness
Electron microscopy showing largely preserved postsynaptic folds with a nerve terminal present
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal cognition (several presynaptic release defects are associated with intellectual disability, ataxia or seizures)
Intact deep tendon reflexes (often reduced in synaptotagmin-2 type)
Patent ductus arteriosus is not a recognised feature

data.diagnosis: Congenital myasthenic syndrome with episodic apnea (CHAT deficiency or other presynaptic ACh resynthesis/packaging defects such as SLC5A7, SLC18A3)
data.description: Autosomal recessive presynaptic defect of acetylcholine resynthesis or vesicular packaging. Causes neonatal hypotonia, bulbar weakness, and life-threatening apneic or respiratory crises, with ptosis and fatigable weakness; endplate ultrastructure is usually normal.
symptoms_in_common: Hypotonia and weak cry at birth
Seronegative for AChR and MuSK antibodies
Normal-appearing endplate structure on electron microscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent fixed weakness with ventilator dependence rather than episodic apneas
Ophthalmoparesis is usually absent or minimal
Decrement is often only seen after prolonged stimulation or exercise
Patent ductus arteriosus not typical

data.diagnosis: Primary acetylcholine receptor deficiency (CHRNE or other AChR subunit mutations)
data.description: The most common congenital myasthenic syndrome, caused by recessive mutations in AChR subunit genes leading to reduced endplate receptor expression. Presents from birth or infancy with ptosis, ophthalmoparesis, bulbar and limb weakness.
symptoms_in_common: Onset at birth with hypotonia and weak cry
Bilateral ptosis and limited eye movements
Facial, bulbar and proximal limb weakness
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe neonatal respiratory failure with long-term ventilation is uncommon
Ophthalmoparesis is usually severe rather than mild
Electron microscopy usually shows simplified postsynaptic folds, whereas folds here appear well developed
Patent ductus arteriosus not typical

data.description: Postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome due to impaired AChR clustering. The early-onset form presents with neonatal hypotonia, arthrogryposis, feeding difficulty and respiratory crises, often triggered by infections.
symptoms_not_in_common: Ophthalmoparesis is usually absent
Typically improves with age rather than requiring lifelong ventilation
No arthrogryposis or contractures reported
Electron microscopy usually shows shallow, sparse postsynaptic folds
Patent ductus arteriosus not typical

data.description: Synaptopathy caused by defective MuSK signalling through DOK7, producing small, simplified neuromuscular junctions. Causes predominantly proximal limb-girdle weakness with ptosis, bulbar and respiratory involvement, and commonly scoliosis.
symptoms_in_common: Proximal limb, neck and facial weakness
Respiratory insufficiency, sometimes with neonatal stridor or hypotonia
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset is usually in early childhood after normal early milestones rather than severe neonatal respiratory failure
Eye movements are usually spared
Electron microscopy typically shows small endplates with simplified folds
Patent ductus arteriosus not typical

data.description: A 37-year-old woman presented with a 4-month history of right facial pain and a 3-month history of progressive painful swelling beneath the right ear lobe. Physical examination revealed a soft swelling in the anteroinferior auricular area that was smooth, elastic, mobile and painful on pressure, but not fluctuant. The facial nerve function was normal and the cervical lymph node was not palpable. There were no systemic symptoms. The patient was screened for metastases, and no lung or abdomen lesions were detected.

data.diagnosis: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor of the parotid region
data.description: A rare malignant spindle-cell tumor arising from a peripheral nerve or its sheath. Pain and the spindle-cell histology make this a consideration, but confirmation requires labeled immunostains and assessment of atypia, mitoses, and invasion.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive painful swelling beneath the right ear
Right facial pain preceding the swelling
Spindle-cell proliferation visible in the histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Smooth, mobile, elastic swelling is less characteristic of an infiltrative malignancy
Normal facial nerve function despite a possible nerve-associated tumor

data.description: A usually benign, encapsulated tumor of Schwann cells that may arise from the facial nerve or another nerve within the parotid region. The spindle-cell appearance and apparent proximity to a nerve support consideration.
symptoms_in_common: Smooth, mobile, elastic swelling near the right ear lobe
Pain potentially related to nerve compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent facial pain and pronounced tenderness are less typical than a painless mass
Progressive enlargement over only three months is less typical of its usual slow growth

data.diagnosis: Localized neurofibroma of the parotid region
data.description: A benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor containing Schwann cells and other nerve-supporting cells. It can present as a soft spindle-cell mass near or within the parotid gland.
symptoms_in_common: Soft, elastic swelling in the infra-auricular region
No systemic symptoms or palpable cervical lymph nodes
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent pain and pressure tenderness are less typical of an uncomplicated neurofibroma
A distinctly mobile, circumscribed mass is less typical than for an encapsulated schwannoma

data.diagnosis: Spindle-cell myoepithelial carcinoma of the parotid gland
data.description: A rare salivary gland malignancy composed predominantly of myoepithelial cells, sometimes with spindle-cell morphology. Diagnosis requires evidence of invasion and an appropriate epithelial and myoepithelial immunostaining profile; the supplied stains are unlabeled.
symptoms_in_common: No detected distant lesions, compatible with localized disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Soft, smoothly mobile swelling is less typical of an invasive carcinoma
Preserved facial nerve function is less typical of advanced local invasion

data.diagnosis: Pleomorphic adenoma with spindle-cell-predominant myoepithelial differentiation
data.description: A common benign salivary gland tumor containing epithelial and myoepithelial elements in variable stroma. A spindle-cell-rich variant can resemble a nerve sheath tumor, although diagnostic ducts and characteristic stroma are not clearly established in the supplied image.
symptoms_in_common: Smooth, mobile, elastic mass in the parotid region
symptoms_not_in_common: Facial pain preceding the swelling
Persistent tenderness on pressure
Noticeable progressive swelling over three months rather than the usual slow, painless growth

data.diagnosis: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) of the parotid gland / facial nerve
data.description: Rare aggressive spindle cell sarcoma arising from peripheral nerve sheath cells, occasionally from the intraparotid facial nerve; shows fascicular hypercellular spindle cells with focal S-100 positivity and elevated Ki-67.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive painful swelling beneath the ear lobe over months
Facial pain preceding the mass (neuropathic pain)
Heterogeneous hypodense parotid mass on CT
Tumor seen in close relation to the facial nerve at surgery
Spindle cell proliferation with alternating cellular and myxoid areas on histology
Positive immunostaining (likely S-100/vimentin) with a raised proliferation index
Negative staining for epithelial, muscle and other lineage markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal facial nerve function
Soft, mobile, smooth mass (malignancy often firm and fixed)
No history of neurofibromatosis type 1 or prior irradiation
Relatively young age for sporadic MPNST

data.diagnosis: Schwannoma (neurilemmoma) of the intraparotid facial nerve
data.description: Benign encapsulated nerve sheath tumor of Schwann cells with Antoni A and Antoni B areas and diffuse strong S-100 positivity; may undergo cystic degeneration.
symptoms_in_common: Tumor attached to the facial nerve
Spindle cell histology with cellular and loose myxoid areas
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked pain and fairly rapid progression over 3-4 months
High cellularity with apparent nuclear atypia
Apparently elevated Ki-67 index
S-100 staining appears focal rather than diffuse

data.description: The most common benign parotid tumor, made of epithelial and myoepithelial cells in a chondromyxoid stroma; spindle myoepithelial-rich variants can mimic mesenchymal tumors.
symptoms_in_common: Spindle cells in a myxoid background
S-100 may be positive in myoepithelial cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain and tenderness (usually painless)
Progression over only a few months (usually slow over years)
No ductal/epithelial component on histology
Negative epithelial and myoepithelial markers (cytokeratin, SMA)
Tumor arising from the nerve itself

data.diagnosis: Synovial sarcoma (monophasic spindle cell type) of the parotid region
data.description: Malignant soft tissue tumor of young adults with t(X;18), composed of uniform spindle cells in fascicles; can occur in the head and neck and is often painful.
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative epithelial markers (cytokeratin/EMA usually at least focally positive)
Origin from the facial nerve
No calcification on CT
Parotid is a very rare site

data.diagnosis: Spindle cell (desmoplastic) malignant melanoma, primary or metastatic to the parotid
data.description: Melanoma variant composed of S-100-positive spindle cells that can be neurotropic and involve the parotid or its intraparotid nodes, mimicking nerve sheath tumors.
symptoms_in_common: Parotid region mass with facial pain (neurotropism)
symptoms_not_in_common: No known primary skin or mucosal lesion
Negative melanocytic markers (HMB-45/Melan-A presumed negative)
Young age
No cervical lymphadenopathy
Soft mobile mass arising from the nerve trunk
S-100 usually diffuse and strong in melanoma

data.description: 32-month-old Korean boy presented with irritability and fever. Born at 40 weeks gestation with 2.9kg birth weight via normal vaginal delivery to a healthy 28-year-old G3P2 mother. Had flexion deformity of both middle fingers at birth. Showed mild general hypotonia in early infancy with weak cry and poor sucking. History of epileptic seizures 6 times since age 15 months. Developmental delay: raised head at 7 months, sat at 26 months, not yet standing. Physical exam showed prognathism, low-set ears, small crashed nose, widely spaced incisors, round back. Demonstrated repeated stereotyped behavior like hitting chin with palm. Neurologic exam showed decreased muscle tone (grade IV/IV bilaterally) but normal deep tendon reflexes, no spasticity or pathologic reflexes, normal sensory function, and no meningeal signs.

data.diagnosis: Alpha-thalassemia X-linked intellectual disability syndrome (ATR-X syndrome)
data.description: An ATRX-related genetic disorder affecting mainly boys, characterized by severe developmental delay, hypotonia, distinctive facial features, and sometimes alpha-thalassemia. The red-cell images appear to show golf-ball-like inclusions suggestive of hemoglobin H, making this the leading possibility; molecular testing is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Early hypotonia with weak cry and poor sucking
Flat nasal bridge, low-set ears, and prognathism
Apparent hemoglobin H inclusions in the red-cell images
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute fever and irritability are not defining features and may reflect an intercurrent illness

data.diagnosis: Alpha-thalassemia–intellectual disability syndrome associated with chromosome 16 deletion (ATR-16 syndrome)
data.description: A contiguous-gene deletion disorder involving chromosome 16p13.3 and the alpha-globin genes, causing alpha-thalassemia with variable developmental impairment and congenital abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: The combination of severe developmental impairment, characteristic facial appearance, and stereotyped behavior is more suggestive of ATR-X syndrome
Recurrent seizures are not a defining feature
Acute fever and irritability are not characteristic

data.description: An RPS6KA3-related X-linked developmental disorder that is usually more severe in boys and causes intellectual disability, hypotonia, characteristic facial changes, and progressive skeletal abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent hemoglobin H inclusions are not associated with this disorder
Congenital bilateral middle-finger flexion deformities are less typical than the characteristic soft, tapered fingers
Chin-hitting stereotypy is not a defining feature
Acute fever is not characteristic

data.description: A disorder caused by deletion of chromosome 17p11.2 or pathogenic variants in RAI1, featuring developmental delay, hypotonia, distinctive facial features, sleep disturbance, and stereotyped or self-injurious behavior.
symptoms_in_common: Prognathism and a flattened nasal bridge
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent hemoglobin H inclusions are not characteristic
Congenital middle-finger flexion deformities are not a typical defining feature
The profound motor delay is more severe than in many affected children
Acute fever is not characteristic

data.description: An X-linked disorder affecting predominantly boys, characterized by infantile hypotonia, severe developmental delay, feeding problems, epilepsy, and sometimes recurrent respiratory infections.
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent hemoglobin H inclusions are not characteristic
Congenital finger flexion deformities are not typical
Prognathism and widely spaced incisors are not defining features
A single febrile episode does not establish the recurrent infections often associated with this syndrome

diagnoses.name: X-linked alpha-thalassemia/mental retardation syndrome
diagnoses.title: X-linked alpha thalassaemia with mental retardation

data.description: X-linked disorder caused by ATRX gene mutations, characterized by severe developmental delay, characteristic facial dysmorphism, neonatal hypotonia, seizures, genital anomalies and mild alpha-thalassemia with HbH inclusions (golf ball-like red cells) on brilliant cresyl blue staining.
symptoms_in_common: Early infantile hypotonia with weak cry and poor sucking
Small depressed nose with low nasal bridge
Open mouth with full, everted lips on photographs
HbH inclusion bodies (golf ball-like red cells) on supravital stained blood smear
symptoms_not_in_common: Prognathism (midface hypoplasia more typical, though relative prognathism can develop)
Fever and irritability (likely intercurrent illness)
No genital anomalies described

data.description: Neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss of maternal UBE3A function on 15q11-13, with severe developmental delay, absent speech, seizures, ataxia, stereotypies and a happy demeanor.
symptoms_in_common: Epileptic seizures with onset in the second year of life
symptoms_not_in_common: HbH inclusions on blood smear
Congenital finger flexion deformity
Low-set ears and small depressed nose
No paroxysmal laughter or happy demeanor described
Round back

data.description: X-linked disorder caused by RPS6KA3 mutations, with intellectual disability, coarse facial features, hypotonia, tapering fingers and progressive skeletal changes such as kyphoscoliosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: HbH inclusions on blood smear
Small depressed nose (broad nose with hypertelorism more typical)
Camptodactyly rather than soft tapering fingers
Stereotyped self-hitting
No stimulus-induced drop attacks

data.description: Contiguous gene deletion syndrome of 16p13.3 that includes the alpha-globin genes, causing alpha-thalassemia with variable intellectual disability and mild, variable dysmorphism.
symptoms_in_common: HbH inclusions / alpha-thalassemia picture on blood smear
symptoms_not_in_common: Severity of developmental delay (usually milder in ATR-16)
Marked early hypotonia
Characteristic ATR-X-like facial appearance
Stereotyped self-hitting behavior
Round back

data.description: Autosomal recessive disorder of cholesterol synthesis (DHCR7 deficiency) with intellectual disability, hypotonia, feeding difficulty, dysmorphic face, limb anomalies and behavioral problems including self-injury.
symptoms_not_in_common: HbH inclusions on blood smear
Prognathism (micrognathia typical)
No 2-3 toe syndactyly or polydactyly described
Normal birth weight
Widely spaced incisors
Seizures are uncommon

data.description: 54-year-old woman with no significant past medical history developed progressive weakness in all four extremities and sensory changes over 1 month, followed by urinary difficulty. Examination showed hyperreflexia, positive Babinski sign, bilateral Hoffmann and Tromner signs, and asymmetric weakness (MRC grade 2 on the right, grade 4 on the left). Sensory exam showed decreased pinprick and temperature sensation from the C4 level, predominantly on the left, and decreased vibration and proprioception predominantly on the right. Serologic autoimmune studies, CSF analysis, brain MRI, chest and abdominal CT, and nerve conduction study were unrevealing; ACE was mildly elevated.

Granulomatous inflammation of the spinal cord, sometimes occurring without detectable systemic sarcoidosis. This is the leading consideration because the supplied histology appears to show non-necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells, alongside a cervical cord lesion and mildly elevated ACE. Infectious causes must be excluded.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive weakness of all four extremities
Hyperreflexia and positive Babinski, Hoffmann, and Tromner signs
Asymmetric motor and sensory deficits consistent with cervical myelopathy
Cervical spinal cord signal abnormality and enhancement
Apparent granulomatous inflammation on the supplied histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Unrevealing CSF analysis is less typical of active inflammatory neurosarcoidosis, although possible
Normal chest and abdominal CT provides no evidence of systemic sarcoidosis, although isolated spinal disease can occur

data.description: Tuberculous infection can produce a spinal cord granuloma or inflammatory myelitis. It is an important alternative when spinal cord biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation, although microbiologic confirmation is required.
symptoms_not_in_common: Unrevealing CSF analysis and systemic CT provide little supporting evidence for tuberculosis
The supplied histology does not show obvious caseous necrosis, which would more strongly support a tuberculous granuloma
Mild ACE elevation is nonspecific and does not specifically support tuberculosis

data.description: An uncommon fungal infection of the spinal cord can cause granulomatous inflammation and progressive myelopathy. Tissue fungal stains, cultures, and organism-specific testing are needed to distinguish it from sarcoidosis.
symptoms_in_common: Sensory level and asymmetric sensory deficits
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported immunosuppression or significant past medical history
Unrevealing CSF analysis and chest and abdominal CT

data.description: Inflammatory injury of the spinal cord causing motor, sensory, and autonomic dysfunction. An asymmetric presentation can occur, but the apparent granulomatous biopsy findings favor a specific granulomatous disorder rather than idiopathic myelitis.
symptoms_in_common: Weakness progressing over approximately one month
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent granulomas and multinucleated giant cells are not characteristic of idiopathic transverse myelitis
Unrevealing CSF analysis offers no laboratory support for spinal inflammation
Mild ACE elevation raises consideration of an alternative granulomatous cause

data.description: 73-year-old woman with a 10-year history of severe paraspinal muscle atrophy and cerebellar ataxia. Symptoms began at age 63 with slight stooping posture and progressed to gait instability requiring a walking stick by age 68 and difficulty climbing stairs by age 70. Exam showed moderate neck flexion weakness, mild proximal limb weakness, poor tandem gait balance without limb ataxia, and MMSE 25/30. Labs: mildly elevated CK, normal lactate, low TSH, elevated antithyroglobulin and antithyroid peroxidase antibodies, elevated rheumatoid factor, and low-titer ANA. Needle EMG showed mild myopathic features. Audiometry revealed sensorineural high-frequency hearing loss, and Holter monitoring showed frequent premature contractions.

A mitochondrial DNA disorder that can cause myopathy, cerebellar ataxia, hearing loss and cardiac abnormalities. The biopsy appears to show ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial staining, while the pedigree suggests maternal transmission. Genetic testing is needed for confirmation; a late-onset presentation need not include epilepsy.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive paraspinal muscle atrophy and stooped posture
Neck flexion and proximal limb weakness
Cerebellar ataxia and progressive gait instability
Mild CK elevation and myopathic EMG findings
Apparent mitochondrial abnormalities on muscle biopsy
Maternal-line clustering of bent spine and elevated CK
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset at age 63 is later than the classic presentation
Elevated thyroid autoantibodies, rheumatoid factor and ANA are not defining features
Low TSH is not a characteristic diagnostic finding

data.description: A nuclear gene disorder affecting mitochondrial DNA maintenance that can produce adult-onset ataxia, myopathy and multisystem involvement. It can resemble mitochondrial DNA disease, although its inheritance would not usually explain a strictly maternal pattern.

Muscle biopsy findings suggestive of mitochondrial dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent maternal transmission pattern is less typical of POLG-related disease
Severe predominantly paraspinal atrophy is not its usual defining presentation
Thyroid autoantibodies and other autoimmune serologies are not characteristic

data.description: An autosomal dominant neurodegenerative disorder causing progressive cerebellar ataxia, sometimes accompanied by muscle wasting, peripheral nerve involvement and cognitive changes. It explains familial ataxia less well than mitochondrial disease explains the complete case.

Myopathic rather than primarily neurogenic EMG findings
Apparent ragged-red fibers on muscle biopsy

Apparent maternal-line inheritance
Positive thyroid autoantibodies

symptoms_not_in_common: No myoclonus

data.description: A 29-year-old man presented to the hospital after several weeks of lumbar pain and fever up to 38°C. He had no significant past medical history. Physical examination revealed vital signs of blood pressure 130/80 mmHg, heart rate 121/min, and body temperature 38.2°C. There was no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly detected on examination. Laboratory tests showed anemia with hematocrit 31.8% and hemoglobin 11.8 g/dL, white blood cell count 3.92 × 10³/μL, elevated liver enzymes with AST 78 IU/L and ALT 71 IU/L, and markedly elevated lactate dehydrogenase 1,591 IU/L. Serum cortisol level was 17.47 μg/dL at 8 AM and ACTH level was 12.1 pg/mL (normal range: 10-90). Ten days after admission, the patient developed pancytopenia with WBC 2.88 × 10³/μL, Hb 10.7 g/dL, and platelets 129 × 10³/μL. Bone marrow biopsy was negative for specific hematologic or malignant disorder.

data.diagnosis: Primary bilateral adrenal lymphoma, most likely diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: An aggressive lymphoid malignancy predominantly involving the adrenal glands. The apparent bilateral adrenal masses and retroperitoneal extension make this a leading consideration, but tissue biopsy is required for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent bilateral bulky adrenal masses on abdominal imaging
Absence of palpable peripheral lymphadenopathy can occur in primary adrenal lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 29 is younger than the usual presentation
Preserved morning cortisol and normal blood pressure are less typical of extensive bilateral adrenal destruction, although adrenal insufficiency is not universal
Negative bone marrow biopsy does not support marrow involvement as the explanation for pancytopenia

data.diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis with bilateral adrenal involvement

Marked lactate dehydrogenase elevation is less characteristic than in aggressive lymphoma
No hypotension or demonstrated adrenal insufficiency despite bilateral involvement
No granulomatous process reported on bone marrow biopsy

data.description: A systemic fungal infection that can cause bilateral adrenal enlargement, fever, hepatic abnormalities, and cytopenias, particularly in patients with impaired immunity.
symptoms_not_in_common: No known immunocompromising condition
No hepatosplenomegaly on examination
Preserved morning cortisol without clinical signs of adrenal insufficiency
Bone marrow biopsy did not identify an infectious or infiltrative process

data.description: Catecholamine-producing adrenal medullary tumors that may be bilateral in hereditary syndromes. Plasma free or urinary fractionated metanephrines are needed to assess this possibility before adrenal biopsy.

Fever can occur with advanced malignancy

data.description: 23-year-old Korean female with 1 day of left eye visual disturbance and visual field defect, preceded by 6 months of recurrent bilateral visual field defects and headache that worsened 1 month before presentation. Two days later, she developed sudden left-sided hearing loss. Three weeks after the initial presentation, she reported right eye visual field defect, and 2 days later was admitted for tinnitus, severe headache, and arm numbness. She denied diabetes, hypertension, connective tissue disease, tuberculosis, hematologic disease, cardiovascular disease, oral contraceptive use, and pregnancy. Initial exam showed reactive pupils without relative afferent pupillary defect, visual acuity 20/20 in the right eye and 20/25 in the left eye, intraocular pressure 18 mmHg in both eyes, and no anterior segment abnormalities. Laboratory studies, including lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin antibody, ESR, and CRP, were normal; CSF showed mildly elevated protein (74.4 mg/dL) without oligoclonal bands.

An autoimmune microangiopathy affecting the brain, retina, and inner ear. This is the strongest diagnostic possibility given the apparent retinal branch arterial ischemia, low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, and corpus callosum lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent bilateral visual field defects with relatively preserved central visual acuity
Retinal whitening and arterial hyperfluorescence on the supplied retinal images, suggesting branch retinal artery involvement
Sudden left-sided hearing loss with predominantly low-frequency sensorineural impairment on audiometry
Recurrent severe headache and arm numbness
Apparent central corpus callosum lesions on MRI
Mildly elevated CSF protein without oligoclonal bands
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear encephalopathy or cognitive disturbance is reported, although these are not required and may develop later

data.description: An immune-mediated demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system that can cause recurrent visual and sensory disturbances and corpus callosum lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Young adult woman with recurrent neurologic symptoms
Visual disturbance and visual field defects
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent branch retinal arterial ischemia and arterial hyperfluorescence are not typical of optic neuritis
Sudden low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus are uncommon
Preserved central visual acuity and absence of a relative afferent pupillary defect are less supportive of substantial unilateral optic neuritis
Absence of CSF oligoclonal bands lowers support but does not exclude the disease
Central callosal lesions suggesting microinfarction are less typical than the usual demyelinating lesion distribution

data.description: A rare inflammatory disorder combining ocular inflammation and audiovestibular dysfunction, sometimes with systemic vasculitis. Atypical forms may involve retinal vessels rather than interstitial keratitis.
symptoms_in_common: Headache and neurologic symptoms can occur with associated vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: No interstitial keratitis or other anterior segment inflammation
Central corpus callosum lesions are not characteristic
Recurrent branch retinal arterial ischemia is less characteristic than the ocular inflammation of classic Cogan syndrome
Normal inflammatory markers and absence of reported systemic inflammatory manifestations provide less support

data.description: An autoimmune thrombophilic disorder that can produce retinal arterial occlusions and cerebral ischemia; inner-ear ischemia can occasionally cause hearing loss.

MRI lesions potentially representing small ischemic injuries
Sudden hearing loss could reflect inner-ear vascular injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative lupus anticoagulant and anticardiolipin antibody testing substantially reduce support
No reported systemic thrombosis or pregnancy morbidity

Retinal arterial wall hyperfluorescence suggests an inflammatory microangiopathy rather than isolated thrombosis

data.diagnosis: Systemic small-vessel vasculitis with retinal, cerebral, and cochlear involvement

Sudden sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus

data.description: Autoimmune endotheliopathy of the small vessels of the brain, retina and cochlea, producing the triad of encephalopathy/headache, branch retinal artery occlusions and low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, typically in young women.

Hearing loss is mild and unilateral rather than bilateral

data.description: Chronic immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system causing relapsing neurological deficits, common in young women and often presenting with optic neuritis and sensory symptoms.

data.diagnosis: Antiphospholipid syndrome / systemic lupus erythematosus-associated vaso-occlusive disease

Normal ESR and CRP (can be normal in primary CNS angiitis)

Retinal arterial involvement is uncommon in primary CNS angiitis

data.description: A 2-year-old Korean male was admitted for evaluation and management of left hip pain. Physical examination revealed several palpable lymph nodes in the left inguinal area and an ill-defined heterogeneous mass-like lesion in the left anteromedial muscle. Peripheral blood examination showed hemoglobin 9.6 g/dL, white blood cell count 6.83 × 10^9/L, platelet count 182 × 10^9/L, and 5 atypical lymphocytes per 100 white blood cells. Immunophenotyping of neoplastic cells showed positivity for CD45 (99.0%), CD19 (94.84%), CD10 (27.64%), CD20 (94.24%), HLA-DR (95.70%), surface IgG lambda (96.45%), CD13 (22.46%), and CD117 (22.22%), and negativity for CD34 (0.01%), Tdt (0.64%), myeloperoxidase (0.01%), and various T-cell and myeloid markers.

An aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma that can involve lymph nodes, extranodal tissues, and bone marrow. This is a leading consideration, although definitive classification requires tissue pathology and molecular testing.
symptoms_in_common: Left hip pain with an adjacent intramuscular mass
Strong CD19, CD20, CD45, and HLA-DR expression
Lambda-restricted surface IgG with absent TdT and CD34, supporting mature B-cell differentiation
Large atypical lymphoid cells in the supplied microscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation at 2 years of age is uncommon
Partial CD13 and CD117 expression is unusual
Prominent cytoplasmic vacuoles are less characteristic than in Burkitt lymphoma

data.description: A highly aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma, usually associated with a MYC rearrangement, that frequently affects children and may involve extranodal sites or blood.
symptoms_in_common: CD19, CD20, and CD10 expression with absent TdT
Basophilic, vacuolated lymphoid cells in the supplied smear
symptoms_not_in_common: Surface IgG rather than the more usual surface IgM
Only partial CD10 expression
Apparent variation in tumor-cell size rather than a uniformly medium-sized population
Partial CD13 and CD117 expression
Intramuscular hip presentation is less typical than abdominal disease

data.diagnosis: High-grade B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified

Mature clonal B-cell phenotype with strong CD19 and CD20 and lambda-restricted surface immunoglobulin

Absent TdT and CD34

data.diagnosis: Burkitt lymphoma/leukemia (mature B-cell, with t(8;14) IGH-MYC rearrangement)

Mature B-cell phenotype: CD19+, CD20+, CD10+, HLA-DR+, surface immunoglobulin light-chain (lambda) restriction
Karyotype with abnormalities of chromosomes 8 and 14 and a MYC/IGH FISH pattern suggesting t(8;14)
symptoms_not_in_common: CD10 only partially positive (27.6%)
Aberrant myeloid markers CD13 and CD117
Surface IgG rather than the usual IgM
Complex karyotype with additional abnormalities (chromosomes 11, 13, 17, 19)
Muscle/hip presentation rather than typical abdominal or jaw mass
Normal white cell and platelet counts

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with marrow/leukemic involvement
data.description: Aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma of large cells that can present with nodal or extranodal masses; a subset carries MYC rearrangement.
symptoms_in_common: Soft tissue mass and regional lymphadenopathy
Mature B-cell phenotype (CD19+, CD20+, surface Ig lambda restricted)
symptoms_not_in_common: Very young age (2 years) is unusual
Burkitt-like vacuolated basophilic blast morphology
Leukemic presentation with circulating atypical cells is uncommon
Aberrant CD13 and CD117 expression

data.diagnosis: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC rearrangement and complex karyotype (Burkitt-like lymphoma with 11q aberration / high-grade B-cell lymphoma, NOS)
data.description: Aggressive mature B-cell neoplasms with features intermediate between Burkitt lymphoma and DLBCL, often with complex karyotypes; a Burkitt-like variant has chromosome 11q gain/loss.
symptoms_in_common: Mature B-cell phenotype with light-chain restriction
symptoms_not_in_common: Rare in toddlers
Presence of an apparent MYC/IGH rearrangement (the 11q-aberration variant typically lacks MYC rearrangement)
Leukemic blood/marrow involvement is less typical
CD13 and CD117 expression

data.diagnosis: Precursor B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoblastic lymphoma
data.description: Most common childhood malignancy, arising from immature B lymphoblasts; often presents with bone/joint pain, cytopenias and lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Aberrant myeloid antigen expression (CD13) can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: TdT negative and CD34 negative
Bright CD20 and surface immunoglobulin with lambda restriction (mature phenotype)
L3 vacuolated morphology
MYC/IGH-type cytogenetics
Discrete muscle mass

data.diagnosis: Rhabdomyosarcoma (or other small round blue cell tumor such as Ewing sarcoma) with marrow metastasis
data.description: Malignant mesenchymal small round cell tumors of childhood that arise in soft tissue or bone, may spread to regional nodes and bone marrow and mimic leukemia.
symptoms_in_common: Toddler with ill-defined heterogeneous intramuscular mass
Small round blue cell appearance on biopsy
CD117 expression can occasionally be seen
symptoms_not_in_common: CD45 strongly positive
B-cell markers CD19 and CD20 positive
Surface immunoglobulin light-chain restriction
Chromosome 8/14 rearrangement pattern rather than FOXO1 or EWSR1 fusion
Circulating atypical lymphoid cells

data.description: 27-year-old male presented with headache, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting for 3 days before admission. Physical examination showed no palpable lymph-node enlargement or hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory findings showed: WBC count 49.5×109/L, hemoglobin 161 g/L, platelet count 36×109/L, with 95% blasts in peripheral blood smear. Serum lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) was markedly elevated to 13,022 IU/L. Flow cytometry showed leukemic blasts were positive for CD2, CD7, CD5, and CD3, and negative for TdT, CD34, CD13, CD33, CD10, CD19, CD20, and CD22.

data.diagnosis: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL), potentially TdT-negative
data.description: An aggressive malignancy of immature T cells. This is the leading consideration given the patient's age, overwhelming blast population, T-lineage markers, and apparent T-cell receptor locus rearrangements. Negative TdT and CD34 do not completely exclude T-ALL; confirmation requires integrated hematopathology and molecular review.
symptoms_in_common: Acute presentation in a young adult male
Blasts expressing CD2, CD3, CD5, and CD7 without B-cell or myeloid markers
Images showing extensive infiltration by blast-like cells
Cytogenetic images indicating TCRAD-associated translocations, including an Xq22.3 region near IRS4
Headache, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting, which may accompany acute leukemia or its complications
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative TdT, which is usually expressed in T-ALL
Absence of lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly, although neither is required
Preserved hemoglobin despite extensive circulating blasts

data.description: An aggressive mature T-cell leukemia usually occurring in older adults, often with marked lymphocytosis and organ enlargement. CD3, CD5, and CD7 expression with absent TdT warrants consideration, but the age and blast-dominant presentation are atypical.
symptoms_in_common: CD2, CD3, CD5, and CD7 expression
T-cell receptor locus rearrangements, although the illustrated partners are not classic for this disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 27 years, much younger than the usual presentation
95% cells reported as blasts rather than prolymphocytes
Absence of hepatosplenomegaly
Absence of lymphadenopathy
Acute headache, dizziness, nausea, and vomiting rather than a typical systemic presentation

data.description: An aggressive mature T-cell malignancy associated with HTLV-1 infection. It can produce leukocytosis, cytopenias, and high LDH, but requires evidence of HTLV-1 infection and appropriate cellular morphology and immunophenotype.
symptoms_in_common: Nausea and vomiting, which can occur with metabolic complications
symptoms_not_in_common: Strong CD7 positivity, whereas CD7 is commonly lost
Young age
Blast-dominant morphology rather than characteristic multilobulated flower cells
Absence of lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly

data.diagnosis: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified, with leukemic involvement
data.description: A heterogeneous mature T-cell lymphoma that can involve marrow and occasionally peripheral blood. This is a less likely alternative if additional testing establishes a mature rather than precursor T-cell population.
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of lymphadenopathy, a common presenting feature
95% circulating blasts, which is unusual
Young age compared with the usual patient population
Preserved expression of all reported pan-T-cell markers, whereas antigen loss is common

data.description: A rare aggressive mature T-cell lymphoma, often affecting young men, with preferential involvement of splenic, hepatic, and marrow sinusoids. The demographic and cytopenia fit, but the absent organ enlargement and CD5 positivity strongly argue against it.
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of hepatosplenomegaly, a hallmark of this lymphoma
CD5 positivity, whereas CD5 is usually absent
Marked leukocytosis with 95% circulating blasts
Diffuse blast-like infiltration rather than a clearly demonstrated sinusoidal pattern
Illustrated TCRAD-associated translocations rather than the more characteristic isochromosome 7q

data.diagnosis: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (T-ALL) with TCRA/D rearrangements [t(X;14)(q22;q11) involving IRS4 and t(12;14)]
data.description: Aggressive neoplasm of T-lineage lymphoblasts involving blood and marrow, often with translocations juxtaposing oncogenes to the TCR alpha/delta locus at 14q11; it typically affects adolescents and young adult males with high WBC counts and CNS involvement risk.
symptoms_in_common: Acute onset with headache, dizziness, nausea, vomiting (possible CNS involvement or leukostasis)
Blasts positive for T-lineage markers CD2, CD3, CD5, CD7
Negative for myeloid (CD13, CD33) and B-cell markers (CD10, CD19, CD20, CD22)
Karyotype and FISH showing TCRA/D (14q11) translocations with Xq22.3 (IRS4 region) and chromosome 12
symptoms_not_in_common: TdT negative (most T-ALL are TdT positive)
CD34 negative (can occur, but an immature marker is often expected)
No lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, or reported mediastinal mass
Preserved hemoglobin (161 g/L)

data.description: Aggressive mature post-thymic T-cell leukemia with marked lymphocytosis, usually in older adults, characteristically associated with 14q11 (TCRA/D) rearrangements such as inv(14) or t(14;14) involving TCL1, or t(X;14)(q28;q11) involving MTCP1.
symptoms_in_common: Leukocytosis with predominant circulating abnormal lymphoid cells
Mature T-cell phenotype: CD2+, CD3+, CD5+, CD7+ with TdT and CD34 negative
Rearrangement of the TCRA/D locus at 14q11, including an X;14 translocation
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 27 (T-PLL is typically a disease of patients over 60)
No splenomegaly, hepatomegaly, lymphadenopathy, or skin lesions
Blast morphology rather than prolymphocytes
X breakpoint at Xq22.3 (IRS4) rather than Xq28 (MTCP1)
WBC usually exceeds 100×10^9/L
Very acute 3-day presentation

data.description: Aggressive mature T-cell neoplasm caused by HTLV-1, presenting with leukocytosis, circulating atypical 'flower' cells, very high LDH, hypercalcemia, organomegaly, and skin lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Leukocytosis with circulating malignant T cells
Mature T-cell phenotype (CD2+, CD3+, CD5+, TdT−, CD34−)
Nausea, vomiting, and headache (could reflect hypercalcemia or CNS involvement)
symptoms_not_in_common: CD7 positive (ATLL is typically CD7 negative)
Young age (ATLL usually presents in middle-aged to older adults)
No lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, or skin lesions
No reported HTLV-1 infection or hypercalcemia
Blast morphology rather than flower cells
TCRA/D translocations are not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Peripheral T-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified, in leukemic phase
data.description: Heterogeneous group of aggressive mature T-cell lymphomas that can occasionally spread to blood and marrow, usually with nodal or extranodal disease.
symptoms_in_common: Mature T-cell immunophenotype (CD2+, CD3+, CD5+, CD7+, TdT−, CD34−)
symptoms_not_in_common: No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly
95% circulating blasts with acute leukemic presentation is unusual
Young age
Usually shows loss of pan-T antigens such as CD5 or CD7
Blastic morphology
Specific TCRA/D translocations with IRS4 are described in T-ALL rather than PTCL

data.description: Rare, fulminant EBV-associated leukemia of NK cells, mostly in young to middle-aged adults, with fever, cytopenias, organomegaly, and very high LDH.
symptoms_in_common: CD2+ and CD7+ cells negative for TdT, CD34, myeloid and B-cell markers
symptoms_not_in_common: CD5 positive (NK cells are typically CD5 negative)
CD3 positive (if surface CD3; NK cells lack surface CD3)
No hepatosplenomegaly
No fever reported
Rearrangement of the TCRA/D locus indicates T lineage
No CD56 or EBV data reported
Blast percentage of 95% is unusually high

data.description: 13-year-old girl with a multiply recurrent hypothalamic/chiasmatic pilocytic astrocytoma with ventricular metastases. Had never received steroids or bisphosphonates. After 16 courses of treatment, complained of wrist pain. Physical examination revealed tenderness to palpation of the left dorsal wrist with decreased range of motion.

Loss of blood supply to the lunate causes bone injury and potentially collapse. The apparent abnormal lunate marrow signal on the supplied MRI makes this a leading consideration, although a complete imaging review is needed.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent lunate marrow abnormality on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation at age 13 is uncommon
The recurrent intracranial tumor is not a typical feature of Kienböck disease

data.diagnosis: Occult lunate fracture or stress injury
data.description: An initially subtle fracture or repetitive-load injury of the lunate can cause focal pain and marrow abnormalities. Additional MRI sequences or CT may distinguish this from osteonecrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent focal lunate abnormality on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: The recurrent intracranial tumor and prolonged treatment history are not typical features of a traumatic fracture

data.description: Infection of the lunate can produce focal bone pain and abnormal marrow signal. It is an uncommon diagnosis that would require correlation with inflammatory markers, additional imaging, and evidence of infection.
symptoms_not_in_common: An apparently isolated lunate abnormality without described surrounding inflammatory changes is less characteristic of infection

data.diagnosis: Juvenile idiopathic arthritis involving the wrist
data.description: An inflammatory arthritis beginning before age 16 that can cause wrist pain, stiffness, restricted motion, synovitis, and secondary bone changes. Persistent arthritis and exclusion of other causes are required for diagnosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: An apparently focal lunate marrow abnormality is less typical than joint-centered synovitis
The recurrent intracranial tumor is not a characteristic feature

data.diagnosis: Intraosseous ganglion cyst of the lunate
data.description: A benign cystic lesion within the lunate that can cause focal wrist pain and occasionally weaken the bone. A sharply defined cystic lesion on complete imaging would support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: An abnormality localized to the lunate
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent heterogeneous lunate marrow change is less typical than a well-defined cyst
The recurrent intracranial tumor and treatment history are not characteristic features

data.diagnosis: Kienböck disease (avascular necrosis of the lunate), likely related to anti-angiogenic therapy (e.g., bevacizumab)
data.description: Osteonecrosis of the lunate bone due to compromised blood supply, causing dorsal wrist pain and stiffness; MRI shows decreased T1 marrow signal in the lunate. Reported in children receiving anti-VEGF therapy for low-grade gliomas even without steroid exposure.
symptoms_in_common: Tenderness to palpation over dorsal wrist
Low T1 signal in the lunate on MRI (arrow)
Onset after prolonged (16 courses) antineoplastic treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age (typically adults 20-40 years)
Female sex (more common in males)
No history of steroids, trauma or repetitive manual labor

data.diagnosis: Occult lunate fracture / stress fracture with bone contusion
data.description: Traumatic or stress-related injury of a carpal bone producing marrow oedema and pain, sometimes not visible on radiographs.
symptoms_in_common: Low T1 marrow signal in the lunate
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported trauma or overuse
No discrete fracture line described
Isolated lunate fractures are rare
Temporal association with chemotherapy unexplained

data.diagnosis: Osteomyelitis / septic arthritis of the wrist
data.description: Bacterial infection of bone or joint, with increased risk in immunosuppressed patients on chemotherapy, causing pain, swelling and marrow signal abnormality.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal marrow signal in a carpal bone
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported
No swelling, erythema or warmth reported
No joint effusion or soft tissue abscess described
Lesion confined to a single carpal bone

data.description: Chronic autoimmune inflammatory arthritis of childhood, commonly involving the wrist with synovitis, pain and stiffness.
symptoms_in_common: Wrist pain in an adolescent girl
symptoms_not_in_common: No swelling or morning stiffness reported
Single joint with focal bone lesion rather than synovitis or effusion
No other joints involved
Focal lunate marrow change is atypical

data.diagnosis: Skeletal metastasis or primary bone lesion of the carpus
data.description: Tumour deposit in bone replacing normal fatty marrow, producing low T1 signal and local pain; could theoretically arise from a disseminated tumour or a primary bone neoplasm.
symptoms_in_common: Low T1 marrow signal lesion in the lunate
symptoms_not_in_common: Pilocytic astrocytoma almost never metastasises outside the central nervous system
Carpal bones are a very rare site for metastasis
No soft tissue mass or cortical destruction described
No systemic symptoms reported

data.description: 44-year-old man with 1 month of intermittent nonexertional substernal burning chest pain, recently becoming severe and persistent for 1 hour, radiating to the left arm and associated with nausea and nonbilious, nonbloody vomiting. He denied dyspnea, edema, fever, cough, trauma, or other cardiopulmonary symptoms. Past history was unremarkable, but he recalled a prior platelet count of about 600,000/mm³ 12 years earlier and reported intermittent generalized pruritus after hot showers, without bleeding, thrombosis, neurologic symptoms, or erythromelalgia. On examination, he was afebrile, in distress clutching his chest, with normal vital signs, regular cardiac rhythm, no JVD or edema, clear lungs, and a nontender chest and abdomen. Labs showed WBC 22,000/mm³, platelets 771,000/mm³, hemoglobin 17.5 g/dL, troponin 0.08 ng/mL, and glucose 192 mg/dL.

Acute myocardial injury from coronary artery occlusion, most likely involving the left anterior descending artery. The ECG shows marked anterior precordial ST-segment elevation with prominent hyperacute T waves, making this an emergency requiring immediate evaluation and reperfusion consideration.
symptoms_in_common: Severe, persistent substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm
Marked anterior precordial ST-segment elevation and hyperacute T waves
Distress during the acute pain episode
Marked thrombocytosis, which may predispose to coronary thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized itching after hot showers is not explained by myocardial infarction
Thrombocytosis documented 12 years earlier suggests an underlying hematologic disorder rather than an acute infarction alone

data.diagnosis: Essential thrombocythemia with possible coronary thrombosis
data.description: A chronic myeloproliferative neoplasm characterized by sustained platelet overproduction and increased thrombotic risk. It could explain the longstanding thrombocytosis and contribute to an acute coronary event; diagnosis requires molecular testing, bone marrow assessment, and exclusion of other causes.
symptoms_in_common: Reported platelet count near 600,000/mm³ 12 years earlier
Possible coronary thrombosis presenting with ischemic chest pain and anterior ST-segment elevation
Pruritus, which can occur in myeloproliferative neoplasms
symptoms_not_in_common: Hemoglobin of 17.5 g/dL and hot-shower-associated pruritus raise particular concern for polycythemia vera
Nausea, vomiting, and severe chest pain are not usual manifestations of uncomplicated essential thrombocythemia

data.diagnosis: Polycythemia vera with possible coronary thrombosis
data.description: A myeloproliferative neoplasm involving increased red cell production, often accompanied by leukocytosis, thrombocytosis, aquagenic pruritus, and thrombosis. The hemoglobin raises suspicion but does not establish the diagnosis; hematocrit, JAK2 testing, erythropoietin level, and bone marrow findings are needed.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe chest pain with vomiting is not typical of uncomplicated polycythemia vera and would suggest a thrombotic complication
The historical finding of isolated thrombocytosis is less specific for polycythemia vera than confirmed sustained erythrocytosis

data.diagnosis: Vasospastic angina with acute myocardial injury
data.description: Transient coronary artery spasm can produce chest pain at rest and ST-segment elevation. Prolonged spasm can cause myocardial injury, but acute coronary occlusion must be excluded urgently in this presentation.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent nonexertional chest pain over one month
Severe chest pain occurring at rest
Nausea and vomiting during severe pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Longstanding marked thrombocytosis is not explained by coronary vasospasm
Hot-shower-associated generalized pruritus is not typical
Persistent severe pain with marked anterior ECG abnormalities makes coronary thrombosis a major competing concern

data.description: Inflammation of the myocardium can cause chest pain, troponin elevation, and focal ST-segment elevation that mimics myocardial infarction. It is a less likely alternative here and should not delay evaluation for coronary occlusion.
symptoms_not_in_common: Left-arm radiation and the marked regional anterior ECG pattern favor acute coronary ischemia
No fever, viral prodrome, or dyspnea was reported
Thrombocytosis present for at least 12 years is not explained by acute myocarditis
Hot-shower-associated pruritus and elevated hemoglobin suggest a separate myeloproliferative disorder

diagnoses.name: ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction
diagnoses.title: Acute ST segment elevation myocardial infarction

data.diagnosis: Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction due to coronary thrombosis in polycythemia vera (JAK2-positive myeloproliferative neoplasm)
data.description: Polycythemia vera is a clonal myeloproliferative neoplasm causing erythrocytosis, often with leukocytosis and thrombocytosis, and a high risk of arterial thrombosis, including coronary occlusion at a young age. Aquagenic pruritus is a characteristic symptom.
symptoms_in_common: Severe persistent substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm
ECG with ST-segment elevation and hyperacute T waves in the anterior/anterolateral leads (V2-V6, I, aVL)
Thrombocytosis (771,000/mm³) with elevated platelet count 12 years earlier
Young age with no known cardiac risk factors
symptoms_not_in_common: No prior thrombosis or bleeding
No erythromelalgia
No neurologic symptoms (headache, visual disturbance)
Hemoglobin only modestly elevated
Preceding month of nonexertional burning pain is atypical for classic angina

data.diagnosis: Acute myocardial infarction associated with essential thrombocythemia
data.description: Essential thrombocythemia is a myeloproliferative neoplasm with sustained thrombocytosis (JAK2, CALR or MPL mutations) that predisposes to arterial thrombosis, including coronary thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Acute chest pain radiating to the left arm with ST elevation on ECG
Young patient without other medical history
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated hemoglobin (17.5 g/dL) suggests polycythemia vera rather than essential thrombocythemia
Marked leukocytosis (22,000/mm³) is unusual
Aquagenic pruritus is more characteristic of polycythemia vera
No erythromelalgia or bleeding

data.diagnosis: Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction from atherosclerotic plaque rupture
data.description: Rupture of an atherosclerotic coronary plaque with superimposed thrombus causing acute occlusion, typically of the left anterior descending artery in anterior infarction. Stress leukocytosis and hyperglycemia can accompany it.
symptoms_in_common: Substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm lasting 1 hour
Patient in distress clutching his chest
Anterior ST elevation with hyperacute T waves on ECG
Hyperglycemia (192 mg/dL; possible undiagnosed diabetes or stress response)
Leukocytosis (may be partly a stress response)
symptoms_not_in_common: Relatively young age with unremarkable past history
Marked thrombocytosis, chronic over 12 years
Elevated hemoglobin
Leukocytosis of 22,000/mm³ is higher than expected for a stress response
Aquagenic pruritus
Prior pain was nonexertional and burning

data.diagnosis: Chronic myeloid leukemia with coronary thrombosis or leukostasis
data.description: A BCR-ABL1-positive myeloproliferative neoplasm with leukocytosis and often thrombocytosis; it can rarely cause vascular occlusion and myocardial ischemia.
symptoms_in_common: Acute coronary event as a possible thrombotic complication
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated hemoglobin (CML usually causes normal or low hemoglobin)
Thrombocytosis present for 12 years without progression is atypical
No fatigue, weight loss, night sweats, or abdominal fullness suggesting splenomegaly
Nontender abdomen with no organomegaly reported
Pruritus specifically triggered by hot water points to polycythemia vera

data.description: Inflammation of the pericardium causing chest pain, ST elevation and sometimes a mild troponin rise (myopericarditis), often with leukocytosis.
symptoms_in_common: Nonexertional substernal chest pain over several weeks
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain is burning and radiates to the left arm rather than being pleuritic or positional
No fever or viral prodrome
No pericardial friction rub
ST elevation is regional (anterior) with hyperacute T waves rather than diffuse with PR depression
Thrombocytosis and elevated hemoglobin
Aquagenic pruritus
Prominent nausea and vomiting

data.description: A 62-year-old man with chronic hepatitis C virus infection and alcohol-induced cirrhosis presented with 10 days of epigastric pain and vomiting. Laboratory findings revealed an elevated serum lipase level of 6715 U per liter (reference range 0 to 160). On hospital day five, the patient developed nodules measuring 1 cm by 1 cm that became increasingly tender over the following days.

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic panniculitis secondary to acute pancreatitis
data.description: The most likely diagnosis: circulating pancreatic enzymes cause subcutaneous fat necrosis and painful nodules. The abdominal CT appears to show substantial peripancreatic inflammation, and the skin biopsy is compatible with lobular panniculitis with fat necrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Epigastric pain and vomiting consistent with acute pancreatitis
Tender, erythematous nodules on the legs developing during hospitalization
Apparent peripancreatic inflammatory changes on CT
Subcutaneous fat necrosis on the biopsy image
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic hepatitis C infection is not a characteristic feature, although it may coexist
Cirrhosis itself does not explain pancreatic panniculitis

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma with lipase hypersecretion syndrome
data.description: A rare pancreatic malignancy that can release large quantities of lipase, producing systemic fat necrosis and pancreatic panniculitis. A discrete tumor would require confirmation on dedicated imaging or tissue sampling.
symptoms_in_common: Painful subcutaneous nodules compatible with enzyme-mediated fat necrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: The acute presentation and apparent inflammatory CT changes favor acute pancreatitis rather than an established tumor
Chronic hepatitis C infection and alcohol-induced cirrhosis are not characteristic manifestations

data.description: A reactive, predominantly septal panniculitis that causes tender red nodules, usually on the lower legs, in association with infections, inflammatory disorders, or medications.
symptoms_in_common: Nodules developing during an acute illness
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked lipase elevation is not explained by erythema nodosum
Epigastric pain and vomiting from pancreatic inflammation are not characteristic
The biopsy appears to show lobular fat necrosis rather than typical septal panniculitis

data.description: An immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis associated with chronic hepatitis C, usually causing palpable purpura and sometimes ulcers, arthralgia, neuropathy, or kidney disease.
symptoms_in_common: Painful inflammatory skin lesions on the lower extremities
symptoms_not_in_common: Subcutaneous nodules are less typical than palpable purpura
Markedly elevated lipase and apparent pancreatic inflammation are not characteristic
The biopsy image suggests fat necrosis rather than a primary small-vessel vasculitis
Epigastric pain with vomiting is not a typical presentation

data.description: A rare necrotizing panniculitis caused by deficient antiprotease activity, producing painful nodules that may ulcerate and discharge oily material; the underlying deficiency can also cause liver disease.
symptoms_in_common: Inflammation and necrosis of subcutaneous fat
Underlying cirrhosis, although the reported causes are hepatitis C and alcohol
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked lipase elevation is not characteristic
Epigastric pain, vomiting, and apparent peripancreatic inflammation favor pancreatic disease
The reported attribution of cirrhosis to alcohol and hepatitis C does not specifically support alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency

data.description: Subcutaneous fat necrosis caused by circulating pancreatic enzymes (lipase, amylase) released during pancreatic disease, producing tender erythematous nodules, usually on the legs; histology shows lobular panniculitis with fat necrosis, 'ghost' adipocytes and basophilic calcium saponification.
symptoms_in_common: CT showing peripancreatic inflammation/fluid consistent with acute pancreatitis
Tender erythematous 1 cm nodules on the legs appearing during hospitalization
Biopsy showing fat necrosis with basophilic deposits and inflammatory infiltrate
Alcohol use as a pancreatitis risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: No arthritis or joint symptoms reported (sometimes accompanies the condition)
Nodules appeared several days after pancreatitis onset rather than preceding it, as they sometimes do

data.description: A reactive septal panniculitis producing tender red nodules, classically on the shins, associated with infections, sarcoidosis, inflammatory bowel disease and drugs.
symptoms_in_common: Tender erythematous nodules on the lower extremities
Acute onset during a systemic illness
Chronic hepatitis C infection as a possible trigger
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology shows lobular fat necrosis with saponification rather than septal panniculitis without necrosis
Markedly elevated lipase
Pancreatic inflammation on CT
Lesions around the knees and thighs rather than classically pretibial

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma with panniculitis
data.description: A rare lipase-secreting pancreatic malignancy that can cause the triad of panniculitis, polyarthritis and eosinophilia through very high circulating lipase levels.
symptoms_in_common: Tender subcutaneous nodules with fat necrosis on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute 10-day presentation typical of pancreatitis
CT shows diffuse inflammatory change rather than a discrete mass
No arthritis or eosinophilia reported
No weight loss reported
Clear alternative cause (alcohol)

data.diagnosis: Hepatitis C-associated cryoglobulinemic vasculitis / cutaneous polyarteritis nodosa
data.description: Immune-complex mediated small- to medium-vessel vasculitis associated with chronic HCV, causing palpable purpura, tender nodules, arthralgia, neuropathy and renal disease; mesenteric involvement can cause abdominal pain.
symptoms_in_common: Tender skin lesions on the lower extremities
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy shows fat necrosis with saponification rather than vasculitis
Lesions are nodules rather than palpable purpura, livedo or ulcers
Lipase of 6715 U/L
CT evidence of pancreatitis
No renal, neurologic or joint involvement reported

data.diagnosis: Infectious panniculitis (bacterial or fungal septic emboli/dissemination)
data.description: Infection of the subcutaneous fat by bacteria, mycobacteria or fungi, arising by direct inoculation or haematogenous spread, especially in immunocompromised or cirrhotic patients; causes tender nodules that may suppurate.
symptoms_in_common: Tender subcutaneous nodules developing in hospital
Neutrophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate in fat on biopsy
Possible infected pancreatic necrosis as a source
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or sepsis reported
Ghost adipocytes and saponification point to enzymatic fat necrosis
No organisms described
Symmetric distribution of multiple nodules on both legs
Extremely high lipase gives an alternative explanation

data.description: A 50-year-old man with a history of injecting drug use presented to the emergency department with reduced level of consciousness and left arm weakness following five days of swinging fever, rigors, and headache. His past medical history included hepatitis C infection, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, and a recent hospital admission for discitis and psoas abscess. On examination, his temperature was 38.4°C but he was hemodynamically stable and alert. Physical findings included a soft early diastolic decrescendo murmur along the left sternal border, splinter hemorrhages, a small digital infarct of the left third toe, and mild upper motor neuron pattern weakness in the left arm. Laboratory investigations revealed normocytic anemia and leukocytosis, with blood cultures growing methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.

data.diagnosis: MRSA native aortic valve infective endocarditis
data.description: Bacterial infection of the aortic valve causing vegetations, valve damage, and systemic septic emboli. This is the leading diagnosis given MRSA bacteremia, peripheral embolic signs, an aortic regurgitation murmur, and apparent aortic valve abnormalities on echocardiography.
symptoms_in_common: Five days of swinging fever and rigors
Blood cultures growing methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus
Early diastolic decrescendo murmur consistent with aortic regurgitation
Digital infarct of the left third toe
Left arm weakness and reduced consciousness, potentially reflecting cerebral septic embolization
History of injecting drug use and recent deep bacterial infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent marked PR prolongation on ECG is not typical of uncomplicated valve infection and raises concern for perivalvular extension

data.diagnosis: Aortic root or perivalvular abscess complicating infective endocarditis
data.description: Extension of aortic valve infection into surrounding tissue, potentially involving the cardiac conduction system. The apparent prolonged PR interval and abnormal tissue around the aortic valve on echocardiography raise concern for this complication, although further imaging is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent PR prolongation consistent with first-degree atrioventricular block
Apparent aortic valve and adjacent tissue abnormalities on echocardiography
