data.description: 37-year-old man with 3 months of recurrent episodes of weakness, irritability, poor concentration, craving sweets, foggy sensorium, and cold, clammy fatigue, often after several hours without eating and worse at night or early morning. He had associated strange behavior and memory loss noted by his wife, and gained 30 lb after drinking large amounts of cola for symptom relief. He had a similar episode several days earlier. Past history was unremarkable except umbilical hernia repair and back surgery 10 years earlier; no regular medications, no smoking or drug use, social alcohol use, and family history of diabetes. On examination he was confused, cold, and clammy; vital signs and other system exams were unremarkable. Routine labs, HbA1c, adrenal, thyroid, and calcium studies were normal except mildly elevated prolactin. Imaging showed a 1.8 × 1.3 cm hypervascular slightly exophytic lesion in the pancreatic head/neck region. Labs showed hypoglycemia with inappropriately elevated insulin and C-peptide.
An insulin-secreting pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor causing endogenous hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia. This is the strongest fit for the fasting episodes, biochemical findings, and pancreatic lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent weakness, irritability, and poor concentration during fasting
Confusion, strange behavior, and memory loss from neuroglycopenia
Symptoms worse at night or early morning
Symptom relief after consuming sugary drinks
Weight gain from frequent carbohydrate intake
Hypoglycemia with inappropriately elevated insulin and C-peptide
symptoms_not_in_common: Mildly elevated prolactin is not explained by an isolated insulinoma

data.diagnosis: Multiple endocrine neoplasia type 1 with an insulinoma
data.description: A hereditary syndrome involving pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors, parathyroid disease, and pituitary tumors. An insulinoma could explain the hypoglycemia, while elevated prolactin raises the possibility of pituitary involvement but is not diagnostic.
symptoms_in_common: Hypervascular pancreatic lesion consistent with a pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor
Hypoglycemia with elevated insulin and C-peptide
Mildly elevated prolactin, potentially indicating pituitary involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal calcium studies provide no evidence of the commonly associated hyperparathyroidism
No reported family history of multiple endocrine neoplasia or related endocrine tumors

data.description: Exposure to insulin-secretagogue medications can produce hypoglycemia with elevated insulin and C-peptide, closely mimicking an insulinoma. A drug screen is needed to distinguish this possibility.

Weakness, confusion, irritability, and memory loss
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported use of diabetes medications or other regular medications

Mildly elevated prolactin is not a typical feature

Mildly elevated prolactin is not a typical feature

symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly fasting and early-morning episodes are less typical than postprandial episodes

Mildly elevated prolactin is not a typical feature

data.description: A 19-year-old man with no previous medical problems presented with a six-day history of breathlessness and left-sided chest pain that had started acutely. On examination, his respiratory rate was 22 breaths per minute with oxygen saturations of 95% on room air. The patient had no significant past medical history and no other baseline characteristics were reported.

Air enters the pleural space without trauma or known lung disease, causing lung collapse. This is the leading diagnosis: the radiograph appears to show a large left pneumothorax and a collapsed left lung. A pneumothorax of this apparent size requires urgent clinical assessment.

Young man without known underlying medical problems
Marked left-sided radiographic lucency with absent peripheral lung markings

data.description: Pleural air accumulates under pressure, potentially impairing circulation. This is an emergency complication to assess for with a large pneumothorax, but tension physiology cannot be established from this image alone.

symptoms_not_in_common: Oxygen saturation of 95% on room air and only mild tachypnea are less typical of advanced tension physiology
Six-day course without reported circulatory deterioration is less typical of rapidly progressive tension pneumothorax

data.diagnosis: Secondary spontaneous pneumothorax from occult cystic or bullous lung disease

symptoms_not_in_common: No known previous medical or pulmonary problems
Age 19 is less typical of common acquired causes such as COPD

data.description: 27-year-old man with a few days of cough, hemoptysis, and low-grade fever. He denied night sweats and weight loss. Past history notable for left supraclavicular lymph node enlargement that had intermittently enlarged and regressed since age 15. On examination he was thin, with low-grade fever, mild hypoxemia, left upper lung crackles, and a 2 cm left supraclavicular lymph node that was nontender, firm, nonfixed, circumscribed, and rubbery. Labs showed leukocytosis with neutrophilia, elevated ESR and CRP, and elevated soluble IL-2 receptor. Blood and sputum cultures, autoimmune serologies, HIV, and tumor markers were negative. Transbronchial lung biopsy showed granulomatous inflammation without identifiable pathogens.

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, particularly nodular sclerosis subtype, with pulmonary involvement
data.description: A lymphoid malignancy affecting young adults that can involve supraclavicular nodes and occasionally produce cavitary pulmonary lesions. Low-grade fever and elevated ESR and CRP
Cough, hemoptysis, and cavitary left upper-lung abnormalities compatible with pulmonary involvement

data.description: A 66-year-old man presented with a 4 to 5-month history of fever, chills, drenching night sweats, and unintentional 35-kg weight loss. He had previously undergone work-up for fever of unknown origin including evaluation for infectious causes such as tuberculosis, typhoid, and brucellosis, but these were not revealing. On physical examination, his spleen was palpable but no adenopathy was detected. Blood tests revealed anemia with hemoglobin of 9.0 g/dL (normal 13.0-18.0 g/dL), microcytosis with mean corpuscular volume of 75 fl (normal 80.0-94.0 fl), normal platelet count of 354,000/μL, and elevated international normalized ratio of 1.30 (normal 0.85-1.20). His serum ferritin level was significantly elevated at 1,796.0 ng/mL (normal 25-310 ng/mL).

data.diagnosis: Primary splenic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma that can present predominantly in the spleen without peripheral lymphadenopathy. Elevated ferritin consistent with systemic inflammation
Absence of peripheral adenopathy is compatible with a primary splenic presentation

Mildly elevated INR is not a characteristic diagnostic feature

data.diagnosis: Splenic marginal zone lymphoma, potentially with large-cell transformation

data.description: A rare aggressive malignancy of splenic vascular endothelial cells that can cause splenic masses, anemia, systemic symptoms, and sometimes bleeding or consumptive coagulopathy. Diagnosis requires vascular morphology and endothelial immunostains.

Microcytosis is not a specific feature

data.description: An uncommon extrapulmonary tuberculosis presentation that can produce splenomegaly and focal splenic lesions with prolonged constitutional symptoms. Prior unrevealing testing lowers its likelihood, and confirmation would require appropriate tissue microbiology or characteristic histology.
symptoms_in_common: Splenomegaly and a focal splenic lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous tuberculosis evaluation was unrevealing
The supplied histology does not clearly show characteristic caseating granulomas
Apparent large atypical cells favor a neoplastic process over uncomplicated tuberculosis
Mildly elevated INR is not a typical defining feature

diagnoses.name: Splenic involvement
diagnoses.title: Fibrosis of spleen[Schistosomiasis involving the skin]

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma with primary splenic involvement
data.description: A B-cell derived lymphoma characterized by scattered large Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells (CD30+, CD15+) in a reactive inflammatory background; it may rarely present as an isolated splenic mass with prominent B symptoms and fever of unknown origin.
symptoms_in_common: Prolonged fever and chills (fever of unknown origin)
Splenomegaly with splenic mass on endoscopic ultrasound
Anemia of chronic inflammation with microcytosis
Large atypical cells with prominent nucleoli on fine-needle aspirate
Scattered large cells with membranous and Golgi-pattern immunostaining (consistent with CD30/CD15) among small lymphocytes
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of peripheral lymphadenopathy
Isolated splenic presentation is rare
Mildly elevated INR
Extreme degree of weight loss (35 kg)

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the spleen
data.description: An aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma that is the most common primary splenic lymphoma, typically presenting as a solitary or multiple hypoechoic splenic masses with B symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: No peripheral adenopathy (compatible with primary splenic disease)
symptoms_not_in_common: Atypical large cells are scattered among many small lymphocytes rather than in diffuse sheets
Staining pattern (membranous and Golgi) is more suggestive of CD30/CD15 positive Reed-Sternberg cells
Normal platelet count despite splenic disease

data.description: A CD30-positive T-cell lymphoma composed of large pleomorphic 'hallmark' cells, often presenting with B symptoms and extranodal involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Fever, night sweats and weight loss
Large pleomorphic atypical cells on cytology
Strong membranous and Golgi-pattern immunostaining consistent with CD30
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of lymphadenopathy
Isolated splenic mass is unusual
Tumor cells are usually in cohesive sheets rather than scattered in a lymphocyte-rich background
No skin or other extranodal lesions

data.diagnosis: Metastatic carcinoma or melanoma to the spleen
data.description: Secondary splenic involvement by a solid tumor (e.g., melanoma, lung, gastrointestinal), producing a splenic mass and constitutional symptoms; microcytic anemia may reflect occult gastrointestinal blood loss.
symptoms_in_common: Clusters of large atypical cells with prominent nucleoli on aspirate
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent prolonged fever, chills and drenching night sweats are less typical
No known primary tumor
Splenic metastases are uncommon and usually occur with widespread disease
Lymphocyte-rich background with scattered positive large cells favours lymphoma
Very high ferritin rather than iron deficiency

data.diagnosis: Splenic abscess or granulomatous infection (e.g., tuberculosis, brucellosis)
data.description: Chronic infection of the spleen producing focal hypoechoic lesions, prolonged fever and wasting; an important cause of fever of unknown origin.
symptoms_in_common: Splenomegaly with focal hypoechoic splenic lesion
Elevated ferritin as an acute phase reactant
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative work-up for tuberculosis, typhoid and brucellosis
Aspirate shows large atypical neoplastic-appearing cells rather than pus or granulomas
Immunostain-positive malignant cells
Solid-appearing mass rather than a fluid collection

data.description: A 38-year-old woman presented with a three-day history of fever, generalized myalgia and arthralgia, and the sensation of difficulty when breathing in. She had poorly localized discomfort in the left diaphragmatic region on deep inspiration and loose stools over the preceding three days. Three days before presentation she had returned from a three-week trip to Western Australia, and 18 months earlier she had traveled to Vietnam. On examination she appeared well but was febrile at 38.0°C and tachypnoeic at 22 breaths/min, with all other observations normal. Examination of all other systems was unremarkable. Blood tests showed severe neutrophilia (18.9 × 10⁹/L; reference range 2.0-8.1), raised C reactive protein (354 mg/L; reference value <10), and normal renal and liver biochemistry. Chest radiography and urinalysis were normal. Blood cultures taken at presentation were negative.

A hepatic abscess caused by Entamoeba histolytica, sometimes presenting months or years after exposure in an endemic region. The apparent low-attenuation liver lesions require further characterization but are compatible with abscesses.
symptoms_in_common: Previous travel to Vietnam, where exposure is possible
Fever with marked neutrophilia and elevated C-reactive protein
Inspiratory diaphragmatic discomfort and tachypnoea, potentially from a left-lobe hepatic lesion
Apparent low-attenuation hepatic lesions on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Left-sided rather than the more usual right-upper-quadrant discomfort
Multiple apparent hepatic lesions rather than the more typical solitary abscess
Generalized arthralgia is nonspecific and not a characteristic feature

data.description: A bacterial infection forming one or more pus-filled cavities in the liver, arising through biliary infection, bloodstream spread, or an abdominal source. Blood cultures may be negative.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent focal low-attenuation liver lesions on CT
Diaphragmatic pain on inspiration and tachypnoea
symptoms_not_in_common: Loose stools are not a characteristic manifestation
Generalized arthralgia is not typical
No abdominal tenderness or identifiable biliary or intra-abdominal source was reported

data.description: Infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei, acquired through contaminated soil or water in endemic areas, including northern Western Australia and Southeast Asia. It can cause multiple visceral abscesses.
symptoms_in_common: Recent travel to Western Australia, potentially relevant if northern endemic areas were visited
Marked neutrophilia and elevated C-reactive protein
Apparent multiple hepatic lesions compatible with abscesses
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal chest radiography does not support the common pulmonary presentation
Loose stools are not a characteristic feature
Negative blood cultures provide no microbiological support, although they do not exclude localized disease

data.description: A liver cyst caused by Echinococcus infection that becomes bacterially infected, producing an abscess-like inflammatory illness. Diagnosis requires characteristic imaging findings and relevant exposure history.

Fever, neutrophilia, and markedly elevated C-reactive protein if secondary infection is present
Diaphragmatic discomfort from a lesion near the liver dome
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt three-day systemic illness is atypical for uncomplicated hydatid disease

The supplied image does not clearly demonstrate characteristic daughter cysts or detached membranes

data.description: A liver fluke infection acquired through contaminated aquatic plants or water. Migrating parasites can cause fever, abdominal discomfort, and hypodense hepatic lesions; exposure history and eosinophil testing are important.

Marked C-reactive protein elevation is more suggestive of an abscess-forming infection

No aquatic-plant exposure or typical migratory hepatic tracks were described

data.diagnosis: Pyogenic liver abscess with portal vein thrombosis (pylephlebitis)
data.description: Bacterial infection of the liver parenchyma, often from enteric or streptococcal organisms (e.g., Streptococcus anginosus group, Klebsiella, Fusobacterium), which may be complicated by septic thrombophlebitis of the portal vein. CT typically shows a hypodense lesion with a peripheral enhancing rim.
symptoms_in_common: Left diaphragmatic discomfort on deep inspiration (diaphragmatic irritation from left lobe lesion)
Sensation of difficulty breathing in and tachypnoea
Hypodense rim-enhancing lesion in left lobe of liver on CT
Apparent filling defect in the portal vein on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative blood cultures (positive in about half of cases)
Normal liver biochemistry (alkaline phosphatase is often raised)
Appeared well with no abdominal tenderness on examination
No known predisposing factor such as biliary disease or diabetes

data.description: Extra-intestinal amoebiasis causing a liver abscess, which can present months to years after travel to an endemic area such as South East Asia. Usually presents with fever and upper abdominal or pleuritic pain.
symptoms_in_common: Travel to Vietnam 18 months earlier (endemic area, long latency possible)
Neutrophilia and raised C reactive protein
Solitary hypodense liver lesion on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesion in the left lobe (amoebic abscesses are usually in the right lobe)
Female sex (strong male predominance)
Portal vein thrombosis is uncommon
Very marked neutrophilia is more suggestive of bacterial infection
Prominent myalgia and arthralgia
No hepatomegaly or abdominal tenderness on examination

data.description: Infection with a soil and water Gram-negative bacterium endemic in northern Australia and South East Asia, which can cause sepsis, pneumonia and abscesses in the liver, spleen and other organs. It may present acutely or reactivate after a long latent period.

Neutrophilia and raised C reactive protein
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal chest radiograph (pneumonia is the commonest presentation)

No risk factors such as diabetes, alcohol excess or renal disease

Appeared clinically well

data.description: Cystic liver infection from a canine tapeworm, acquired in sheep-farming regions including rural Australia. Cysts grow slowly over years and are usually asymptomatic until they become secondarily infected, rupture or cause mass effect.
symptoms_in_common: Cystic hypodense liver lesion on CT
Fever and raised inflammatory markers if secondarily infected
Diaphragmatic discomfort from mass effect or inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute three-day illness (cysts take years to develop, so recent travel would not explain it)

data.diagnosis: Necrotic or secondarily infected liver tumour (e.g., metastasis or cystic neoplasm)

data.description: A 70-year-old woman presented to the clinic for a routine examination. The patient reported that this mass had been present since birth. Her symptoms were minimal, with occasional difficulty cleaning the area and halitosis from entrapped food, but she was otherwise asymptomatic regarding the lesion.

A benign bony outgrowth along the midline of the hard palate, sometimes large and multilobulated. This is the leading possibility based on the photograph, although examination is needed to confirm a hard, bony consistency.
symptoms_in_common: Midline, multilobulated palatal mass covered by normal-appearing mucosa
Very long-standing lesion with minimal symptoms
Absence of pain or visible ulceration

data.description: A benign, slow-growing tumor of mature bone that can produce a painless, mucosa-covered mass on the palate.

Broad, midline, multilobulated appearance is more typical of torus palatinus than a solitary osteoma

data.diagnosis: Pleomorphic adenoma of a minor salivary gland

symptoms_in_common: Minimal symptoms despite a substantial lesion
Possible food trapping around a protruding mass

Persistence for approximately 70 years with minimal symptoms

symptoms_in_common: Local hygiene difficulty and food retention

The pictured appearance is not specific for a hamartoma

data.description: 27-year-old female, 162cm tall, 30kg weight. Born after normal pregnancy/delivery. No family history of neurological diseases. Normal early development. At age 6, developed general muscle weakness and gait disturbance with decreased muscle tone/strength and atrophic muscle mass. At age 8, muscle biopsy showed mitochondrial myopathy of pleoconial type. At age 24, had sudden syncope. At age 26, had stroke with general weakness, aphagia, and dysarthria. Current presentation at age 27 with left hemiplegia and aphasia. Lab findings: plasma lactate 21.8 mg/dL (elevated), normal CBC/electrolytes/BUN/creatinine, free T4 1.76 ng/dL, TSH 0.04 μIU/mL, C3 13 mg/dL (low), C4 18 mg/dL (normal). Negative for ASO antibody, rheumatoid factor, anti-dsDNA, lupus anticoagulants, and anti-cytoplasmic antibody. DNA sequencing showed m.3303C>T mutation in mitochondrial tRNA leucine 1 gene.

data.diagnosis: MT-TL1-related mitochondrial myopathy with cardiac involvement
data.description: A mitochondrial energy-production disorder associated with the m.3303C>T variant in MT-TL1. It can cause progressive skeletal muscle weakness and cardiomyopathy, potentially complicated by intracardiac thrombosis and embolic stroke. This is the strongest unifying diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Childhood-onset generalized muscle weakness and gait disturbance
Decreased muscle tone, strength, and muscle mass
Echocardiographic intracavitary masses concerning for ventricular thrombi
symptoms_not_in_common: Low C3 is not a characteristic finding
Suppressed TSH with high-normal or elevated free T4 is not a defining feature

data.diagnosis: Cardioembolic ischemic stroke from a left ventricular thrombus
data.description: A clot formed within the left ventricle can embolize to a cerebral artery. The supplied images suggest a right-sided cerebral infarct, markedly reduced visualization of the right anterior circulation, and ventricular masses concerning for thrombi; formal imaging interpretation is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent major cerebral arterial occlusion on MR angiography
Echocardiographic masses concerning for a ventricular embolic source
symptoms_not_in_common: Childhood-onset generalized muscle weakness and muscle atrophy are not explained by stroke
Mitochondrial muscle biopsy abnormalities require an underlying disorder
The MT-TL1 mutation and elevated lactate are not features of isolated cardioembolic stroke
Low C3 is not typical

data.diagnosis: Mitochondrial cardiomyopathy complicated by left ventricular thrombosis
data.description: Mitochondrial dysfunction can impair myocardial contraction, producing cardiomyopathy and blood stasis that promotes ventricular thrombus formation. The echocardiographic masses are suspicious for thrombi, although ventricular function and morphology cannot be reliably established from these still images alone.
symptoms_in_common: m.3303C>T mutation associated with mitochondrial myopathy and cardiomyopathy
Echocardiographic intracavitary masses concerning for thrombi
Recurrent strokes potentially caused by systemic embolization
symptoms_not_in_common: Low C3 is not a characteristic feature
Thyroid test abnormalities are not explained directly by mitochondrial cardiomyopathy
Aphasia and hemiplegia indicate a cerebral complication rather than a direct cardiac manifestation

data.diagnosis: Mitochondrial encephalomyopathy, lactic acidosis, and stroke-like episodes (MELAS spectrum)
data.description: A mitochondrial syndrome featuring myopathy, elevated lactate, and stroke-like neurological episodes. The clinical history supports consideration, but apparent large-vessel occlusion and a possible cardiac embolic source favor true ischemic stroke over a classic MELAS stroke-like episode.
symptoms_in_common: Normal early development followed by childhood-onset weakness
Mutation in the mitochondrial tRNA leucine 1 gene
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent major cerebral arterial occlusion is atypical for classic MELAS stroke-like episodes
Possible ventricular thrombi suggest an alternative embolic mechanism
Low C3 is not characteristic
The m.3303C>T variant is more commonly associated with myopathy and cardiomyopathy than classic MELAS

data.description: Excess thyroid hormone can cause tachyarrhythmias and cardiac dysfunction, potentially increasing embolic risk. The thyroid results warrant evaluation, but this is a less likely primary diagnosis and would not explain the established mitochondrial disease.
symptoms_in_common: Free T4 that may be elevated depending on the laboratory reference range
Stroke potentially associated with a cardiac embolic source
symptoms_not_in_common: Childhood-onset muscle atrophy and biopsy-confirmed mitochondrial myopathy are not explained
The pathogenic mitochondrial gene variant indicates a separate underlying disorder
Elevated lactate is not a defining feature
Low C3 is not typical
Ventricular thrombi are not a usual manifestation without substantial associated cardiac dysfunction

data.description: A 6-year-old girl with a 1-year history of intermittent migratory bone and joint pain presented with recent fever and abdominal distention. After a fall on her left hand 1 year earlier, she developed migratory joint pain, then intermittent rib pain, right knee pain with limping, and left flank pain radiating to the left leg. Six days before admission, she developed back pain, worsening limping, and intermittent fever up to 39.8°C. The day before admission, she developed periorbital swelling/discoloration, abdominal distention, and periumbilical discoloration. On examination, she was febrile, had bilateral periorbital discoloration, a soft nontender abdomen, slight limping, and pain with external rotation of the right hip. Past history included infant gastroesophageal reflux and pollen allergy with allergic rhinitis; family history was notable for rheumatoid arthritis and breast cancer in the paternal grandmother.

data.diagnosis: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia with extramedullary involvement
data.description: A malignancy of immature B lymphocytes that can involve marrow, bone, and soft tissues. This is the leading consideration because the supplied pathology shows blast-like cells and a CD19-positive, CD10-positive population; CD33 expression can be aberrant and does not alone establish myeloid leukemia.
symptoms_in_common: Prolonged migratory bone and joint pain
Rib, knee, hip, and back pain with limping
Periorbital and periumbilical discoloration potentially related to bleeding or tissue infiltration
Apparent multifocal soft-tissue abnormalities on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: A year-long intermittent course is less typical than a shorter progressive presentation
Bilateral periorbital discoloration is less characteristic than in metastatic neuroblastoma

data.description: A childhood malignancy of sympathetic nervous system cells, often arising in the adrenal gland or paraspinal tissues. Bone and orbital metastases can cause limping, skeletal pain, and characteristic periorbital bruising, but the supplied B-lineage flow-cytometry findings argue against this diagnosis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Migratory joint pain over a year is less typical than progressive metastatic bone pain
Periumbilical discoloration is not a characteristic presenting feature

data.description: A malignancy of immature B lymphocytes presenting predominantly as tissue masses, with limited marrow involvement. It shares the immunophenotype of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia; distinguishing them requires assessment of marrow involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal distention associated with an apparent abdominal mass
Periorbital swelling potentially caused by tissue infiltration
symptoms_not_in_common: A year of migratory skeletal pain is less typical than progressive mass-related symptoms
Periumbilical bruising is not a usual presenting feature
Bilateral periorbital bruising is not a classic hallmark

data.diagnosis: Acute myeloid leukemia with myeloid sarcoma
data.description: A malignancy of immature myeloid cells that may form masses in bone, orbital tissues, or other organs. CD33 expression raises this possibility, but the CD19-positive, CD10-positive population favors B-lineage disease unless additional testing demonstrates myeloid differentiation.

data.description: An aggressive small round-cell malignancy arising in bone or soft tissue that can cause pain, fever, and metastatic lesions. It is less likely here because the symptoms are broadly migratory and the supplied flow cytometry supports a hematolymphoid malignancy.

Abdominal distention if an abdominal or pelvic tumor is present

Bilateral periorbital swelling and discoloration
Periumbilical discoloration

data.description: Malignancy of immature B-lymphoblasts that often presents in children with bone and joint pain, fever, and extramedullary masses (bone, nodes, kidneys, pelvis). Blasts express CD19 and CD10, sometimes with aberrant myeloid markers such as CD33.

abdominal distention with large pelvic mass on CT
bilateral enlarged kidneys with infiltrative lesions

sheets of small round blue cells/lymphoblasts on biopsy

data.description: Embryonal tumor of the sympathetic nervous system in young children, commonly arising in the adrenal gland or retroperitoneum and metastasizing to bone, bone marrow and orbits.

pelvic mass and abdominal distention

data.description: 29-year-old right-hand dominant male chef with hypothyroidism on thyroxine, presented with 4 days of gradually worsening dull left neck pain radiating to the head, diplopia, right-sided numbness, dropping objects, and unsteady gait. He denied alcohol or illicit drug use, seizure, head injury, or loss of consciousness. Exam showed he was alert and oriented, BP 141/94 mmHg, with right-sided weakness (MRC 4/5, mainly upper limb) and pronator drift, decreased pinprick, light touch, and proprioception on the right, resting and intention tremor with dysdiadochokinesia (more on the right), broad-based ataxic gait, right extensor plantar response, and diplopia on both extremes of gaze without ocular palsy or papilloedema.

data.diagnosis: Brainstem cavernous malformation with recent hemorrhage
data.description: A cluster of abnormal, thin-walled vessels in the brainstem that can bleed. The focal hyperdense brainstem lesion on CT and heterogeneous MRI appearance favor a hemorrhagic cavernous malformation, although additional MRI sequences are needed for confirmation. Brainstem hemorrhage requires urgent specialist assessment.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively worsening neurological symptoms over four days
symptoms_not_in_common: Unilateral neck pain radiating to the head is less characteristic than the focal neurological deficits

data.description: An abnormal direct connection between arteries and veins that may rupture and cause brainstem hemorrhage. It is an important vascular alternative in a young adult, but the supplied images do not clearly demonstrate a vascular nidus.
symptoms_not_in_common: Gradual dull pain and progression over four days are less typical of a large acute rupture
Resting tremor is less typical than weakness or ataxia

data.diagnosis: Vertebral artery dissection with posterior circulation infarction
data.description: A tear in the vertebral artery wall can cause unilateral neck pain followed by ischemic injury to the brainstem or cerebellum. The clinical presentation fits, but the focal hyperdense lesion is more suggestive of hemorrhage than uncomplicated infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Left-sided neck pain radiating to the head
symptoms_not_in_common: Resting tremor is not a common presenting feature
Steadily progressive deficits over four days are less typical than abrupt or fluctuating ischemic deficits

data.description: A glial tumor within the brainstem can disrupt motor, sensory, and coordination pathways; bleeding into the tumor can accelerate symptoms. This is less favored than a vascular lesion without evidence of an infiltrative mass or characteristic enhancement.
symptoms_not_in_common: A four-day course is unusually short unless intratumoral hemorrhage occurred
Unilateral neck pain radiating to the head is not a typical presenting symptom

data.description: Downward displacement of the cerebellar tonsils can cause crowding at the foramen magnum, neck pain, and neurological symptoms. The sagittal MRI suggests low-lying tonsils, but measurement is needed; this could be a coexisting finding rather than the cause of the acute presentation and does not explain the focal hemorrhagic lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Neck pain radiating to the head
symptoms_not_in_common: Rapid progression over four days is atypical
Marked unilateral weakness and hemisensory loss are less characteristic
Resting tremor is uncommon

data.diagnosis: Brainstem (pontine) cavernous malformation with haemorrhage, associated with Chiari I malformation
data.description: A cavernoma is a low-flow cluster of thin-walled vascular channels that can bleed repeatedly; in the pons it causes subacute, stepwise brainstem deficits. Imaging shows a hyperdense pontine lesion on CT with mixed-signal 'popcorn' appearance and dark haemosiderin rim on MRI. Coexistent cerebellar tonsillar descent (Chiari I) can crowd the foramen magnum and cause hydrocephalus.
symptoms_in_common: Young adult with subacute onset over 4 days
Gradually worsening neck pain radiating to the head
Right-sided weakness with pronator drift and extensor plantar response
Right-sided loss of pinprick, light touch and proprioception
Intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia and broad-based ataxic gait
Hyperdense pontine lesion on CT with mixed-signal lesion on MRI
Ventricular dilatation and low-lying cerebellar tonsils on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Resting tremor
No seizure history (more relevant to supratentorial cavernomas)
Mildly elevated blood pressure is not a feature
No papilloedema despite ventricular dilatation

data.description: Bleeding into the pons from rupture of small perforating arteries, usually related to chronic hypertension. Typically presents abruptly with coma, pinpoint pupils and quadriparesis, though small haematomas may cause limited deficits.
symptoms_in_common: Right hemiparesis with extensor plantar response
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age (29 years) with no known hypertension history
Gradual progression over 4 days rather than sudden onset
Alert and oriented with no loss of consciousness
Only mild weakness (4/5)
Only mildly raised blood pressure
Tonsillar descent on MRI not explained

data.diagnosis: Vertebral artery dissection with posterior circulation stroke
data.description: A tear in the vertebral artery wall causing neck pain and thromboembolic or haemodynamic ischaemia of the brainstem and cerebellum; a leading cause of stroke in young adults.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral neck pain radiating to the head
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of neck trauma or manipulation
CT shows a hyperdense haemorrhagic lesion rather than an infarct
No Horner syndrome, dysphagia, vertigo or crossed sensory signs
Ventricular dilatation and tonsillar descent not explained

data.diagnosis: Haemorrhagic brainstem tumour (e.g., brainstem glioma or metastasis)
data.description: An intrinsic neoplasm of the brainstem that can bleed, producing progressive cranial nerve, long tract and cerebellar signs, sometimes with obstructive hydrocephalus.
symptoms_in_common: Right-sided long tract signs (weakness, extensor plantar)
symptoms_not_in_common: Very short history of only 4 days
Small well-circumscribed lesion without significant mass effect or oedema
No papilloedema
No known primary malignancy or systemic symptoms
No frank cranial nerve palsies on examination

data.description: An immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system affecting young adults, with subacute relapses commonly involving the brainstem and cerebellum.
symptoms_in_common: Intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia and ataxic gait
Pyramidal signs with extensor plantar response
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent neck pain and headache
Hyperdense (haemorrhagic) lesion on CT
Ventricular dilatation
Cerebellar tonsillar descent
No internuclear ophthalmoplegia or optic neuritis
No previous neurological episodes

data.description: 52-year-old man with a history of hypertension, benign prostatic hypertrophy with obstructive nephropathy, chronic renal insufficiency requiring dialysis before a living-related renal transplant 1 year earlier, and hyperparathyroidism with bilateral cataract surgery, presented with acute palpitations and chest pressure after 2 days of epigastric burning, fatigue, weakness, and vomiting. He denied fever or chills. On arrival, heart rate was 200 bpm with atrial fibrillation and rapid ventricular response; after cardioversion, pulse was 53 bpm and blood pressure 128/90 mmHg. Exam showed a diffuse, laterally displaced apical impulse, prominent second heart sound, and audible fourth heart sound, without murmurs or jugular venous distention. Labs showed creatinine 1.5 mg/dL, troponin T 1.04 ng/mL, normal electrolytes and thyroid function, 2+ proteinuria, and markedly reduced leukocyte α-galactosidase activity.

data.diagnosis: Fabry disease with cardiac and renal involvement
data.description: An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient alpha-galactosidase A activity. Glycosphingolipid accumulation causes renal disease, gastrointestinal symptoms, ventricular hypertrophy, and arrhythmias. This is the strongest unifying diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic renal insufficiency requiring dialysis and transplantation
Marked ventricular wall thickening apparent on echocardiography
High-voltage QRS complexes with repolarization abnormalities on ECG
Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
Epigastric burning, vomiting, fatigue, and weakness
symptoms_not_in_common: Benign prostatic hypertrophy with obstructive nephropathy is not a characteristic manifestation
Hyperparathyroidism is not a primary manifestation, although it can follow chronic kidney disease
Cataracts requiring surgery are less characteristic than the corneal changes typically associated with Fabry disease

data.description: Chronic hypertension can cause concentric left ventricular hypertrophy and impaired relaxation, predisposing to atrial fibrillation and myocardial injury during rapid tachycardia.
symptoms_in_common: Ventricular wall thickening apparent on echocardiography
High-voltage QRS complexes with repolarization abnormalities
Chest pressure and elevated troponin during marked tachycardia
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity is not explained
Epigastric burning and vomiting are not characteristic manifestations
Cataracts are not a typical direct manifestation

data.description: A usually inherited myocardial disorder characterized by ventricular hypertrophy not adequately explained by loading conditions. It can cause diastolic dysfunction, ischemic chest discomfort, and atrial arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Marked ventricular wall thickening apparent on echocardiography
High-voltage QRS complexes and repolarization abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity instead favors Fabry-associated hypertrophy
Renal failure and proteinuria are not typical primary manifestations
Epigastric burning and vomiting are not characteristic
Cataracts and hyperparathyroidism are not typical manifestations

data.description: Extracellular amyloid deposition can produce thickened ventricular walls, restrictive physiology, arrhythmias, proteinuria, and renal dysfunction. It is an alternative cardiac-renal diagnosis but is less consistent with the enzyme result and ECG.
symptoms_in_common: Ventricular wall thickening apparent on echocardiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity is not explained
High ECG voltages are less typical than the voltage-to-wall-thickness mismatch often seen in cardiac amyloidosis
Cataracts and hyperparathyroidism are not characteristic primary manifestations

data.diagnosis: Acute myocardial infarction, including possible type 2 myocardial infarction
data.description: Acute ischemic myocardial injury may result from coronary plaque disruption or oxygen supply-demand imbalance during extreme tachycardia. The symptoms and troponin warrant evaluation, but serial troponins and additional ischemic evidence are needed to establish infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Atrial fibrillation with a ventricular rate of 200 bpm
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced leukocyte alpha-galactosidase activity is not explained
Marked ventricular hypertrophy is a chronic structural finding rather than a consequence of an acute infarction
Longstanding renal failure and proteinuria are not explained by an isolated acute infarction
Cataracts and hyperparathyroidism are not characteristic manifestations

data.description: X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by α-galactosidase A deficiency, with globotriaosylceramide accumulation in heart, kidney, and vessels. It causes left ventricular hypertrophy, arrhythmias, short PR interval or pre-excitation-like ECG changes, proteinuric renal failure, and early cataracts or corneal opacities.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic renal failure requiring dialysis and transplant
Atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response
ECG with very high precordial voltages and short PR/slurred QRS upstroke (arrows)
Concentric left ventricular wall thickening on echocardiogram with reduced tissue Doppler velocities
Diffuse, laterally displaced apical impulse and fourth heart sound
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported acroparesthesias, angiokeratomas, or hypohidrosis
Renal failure previously attributed to obstructive nephropathy from benign prostatic hypertrophy
Cataracts attributed to hyperparathyroidism
Diagnosis at a relatively late age

data.description: Left ventricular hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction from long-standing pressure overload, common in patients with chronic kidney disease and dialysis history; predisposes to atrial fibrillation.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic renal insufficiency with prior dialysis
Left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG and echocardiogram
Fourth heart sound and prominent second heart sound
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly reduced α-galactosidase activity
Short PR interval with slurred QRS upstroke
Markedly elevated troponin T
Epigastric burning and vomiting
Degree of hypertrophy may be out of proportion to current blood pressure (128/90 mmHg)

data.description: Autosomal dominant disorder of sarcomere proteins causing unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy, diastolic dysfunction, atrial and ventricular arrhythmias, and risk of sudden death.
symptoms_in_common: Marked left ventricular hypertrophy on echocardiogram
High ECG voltages with repolarization abnormalities
Troponin elevation (can occur from supply-demand mismatch)
symptoms_not_in_common: Reduced α-galactosidase activity
Renal failure and proteinuria
No systolic outflow murmur
Concentric rather than asymmetric septal hypertrophy
Gastrointestinal symptoms
Cataracts

data.diagnosis: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome with pre-excited atrial fibrillation
data.description: Accessory atrioventricular pathway causing a short PR interval and delta waves, predisposing to very rapid ventricular rates during atrial fibrillation. A similar pattern with hypertrophy occurs in storage cardiomyopathies such as PRKAG2 or Danon disease.
symptoms_in_common: Atrial fibrillation with ventricular rate of 200 bpm
Short PR interval with slurred QRS upstroke (delta-like waves at arrows)
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked left ventricular hypertrophy on echocardiogram
Renal failure and proteinuria
Reduced α-galactosidase activity
Displaced apical impulse and fourth heart sound
Epigastric burning, vomiting, fatigue, and weakness over 2 days
Cataracts

data.description: Myocardial ischemia or infarction from coronary plaque rupture or supply-demand mismatch, a common complication in patients with hypertension, chronic kidney disease, and transplant immunosuppression.
symptoms_in_common: Epigastric burning, vomiting, fatigue, and weakness (possible anginal equivalents)
Risk factors: hypertension, chronic kidney disease, renal transplant
symptoms_not_in_common: Reduced α-galactosidase activity
Marked concentric left ventricular hypertrophy
Short PR interval with slurred QRS upstroke
Troponin elevation may be explained by tachyarrhythmia, hypertrophy, and renal dysfunction
Proteinuria
Cataracts

data.description: 76-year-old man from the Indian subcontinent presented with fever and priapism. Physical exam showed painful, engorged penis with intact skin, no lymphadenopathy, hepatomegaly, or splenomegaly. No skin rash or nodules were found.

A rare aggressive lymphoma in which malignant B cells accumulate within small blood vessels, potentially obstructing penile circulation. The apparent intravascular large atypical cells in the biopsy make this the leading consideration, although confirmation requires identification of the immunohistochemical stains.
symptoms_in_common: Painful priapism potentially caused by obstruction of penile microvasculature
Absence of lymphadenopathy, which is characteristic of this lymphoma
Absence of skin lesions does not exclude internal-organ involvement
Apparent clusters of large atypical cells within vascular spaces on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Isolated penile involvement is an exceptionally rare presentation
Absence of hepatomegaly or splenomegaly is less typical of some systemic presentations

data.diagnosis: Primary penile diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: An uncommon extranodal lymphoma involving penile tissues. Infiltration of the corpora cavernosa can interfere with venous drainage and cause malignant priapism.
symptoms_in_common: Intact penile skin despite possible deeper tissue involvement
Marked penile radiotracer uptake on the supplied PET/CT images
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent predominantly intravascular distribution of atypical cells favors intravascular lymphoma over conventional diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
No discrete penile mass or nodules were described

data.diagnosis: Metastatic urothelial carcinoma involving the penis
data.description: Urothelial cancer can rarely spread to penile erectile tissues and obstruct venous outflow, producing malignant priapism. Histology and epithelial immunostains are needed to establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Intact skin can occur with deep penile metastases
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever is not a typical presenting feature unless there is infection or advanced malignancy
No hematuria or urinary symptoms were reported
No penile nodules were found
The supplied biopsy appears more suggestive of intravascular hematolymphoid cells than epithelial carcinoma

data.diagnosis: Metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma involving the penis
data.description: Advanced prostate cancer can rarely metastasize to the penis, causing corporal infiltration or vascular obstruction and painful persistent erection.
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever is not typical of uncomplicated prostate cancer
No urinary obstruction, bone pain, or known prostate malignancy was reported
No penile nodules were identified
The biopsy does not show an obvious gland-forming carcinoma

data.diagnosis: Chronic myeloid leukemia with leukostasis-associated priapism
data.description: A myeloproliferative cancer that can cause extreme leukocytosis and impaired penile blood flow, resulting in ischemic priapism. A blood count and BCR::ABL1 testing would be necessary to assess this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Fever can accompany the underlying hematologic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of splenomegaly is less typical of symptomatic chronic myeloid leukemia
Localized penile radiotracer uptake and intravascular aggregates of large atypical cells are more suggestive of lymphoma
No leukocytosis or other supporting blood abnormalities were provided

data.description: Rare aggressive extranodal lymphoma in which large neoplastic B cells (CD20+) proliferate within the lumina of small vessels, causing organ-specific vascular occlusion, often with fever of unknown origin and without lymphadenopathy or mass lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Priapism from vascular occlusion of the corpora cavernosa
Intense FDG uptake in the penis and prostate/pelvic region on PET/CT
Biopsy showing large atypical cells confined within vessel lumina with strong membranous immunostaining (consistent with a B-cell marker such as CD20)
symptoms_not_in_common: Priapism is a very unusual presenting feature
No skin lesions (seen in the cutaneous variant)
No neurological symptoms reported
No hepatosplenomegaly or cytopenias reported (common in the Asian/hemophagocytic variant)

data.diagnosis: Leukemia (e.g., chronic myeloid leukemia or acute leukemia) with leukostasis
data.description: Hematologic malignancy with marked leukocytosis causing hyperviscosity and sludging in the corpora cavernosa; the most common malignant cause of priapism.
symptoms_not_in_common: No splenomegaly
No hepatomegaly
No lymphadenopathy
Advanced age less typical for leukemic priapism
Intravascular cells appear to be large lymphoid cells rather than myeloid blasts
Focal FDG avidity of the penis and prostate rather than diffuse marrow/spleen uptake

data.diagnosis: Metastatic or locally invasive carcinoma of the penis (malignant priapism from prostate or urothelial carcinoma)
data.description: Infiltration of the corpora cavernosa by a pelvic malignancy, most often prostate or bladder cancer, causing venous outflow obstruction and persistent painful erection.
symptoms_in_common: Tumor cells within vascular spaces could mimic lymphovascular invasion
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever is not typical
No palpable penile nodules
No lymphadenopathy
Tumor cells are discohesive and confined to vessel lumina with a lymphoid immunophenotype rather than forming cohesive epithelial nests
No known primary carcinoma or urinary symptoms reported

data.diagnosis: Systemic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with genitourinary (prostate/penile) involvement
data.description: Aggressive B-cell lymphoma that may arise in or spread to extranodal sites, including the prostate and penis, forming FDG-avid infiltrative masses.
symptoms_in_common: Large atypical lymphoid cells with strong B-cell marker staining
symptoms_not_in_common: No lymphadenopathy
No hepatosplenomegaly
No discrete mass lesion
Malignant cells restricted to vessel lumina rather than forming a parenchymal mass
Priapism is rare

data.diagnosis: Infective cavernositis / prostatic abscess with secondary priapism
data.description: Bacterial infection of the corpora cavernosa or prostate causing fever, penile pain and swelling, and sometimes thrombosis with ischemic priapism.
symptoms_in_common: Increased FDG uptake in penis and prostate (inflammation is FDG-avid)
symptoms_not_in_common: Intact skin without erythema, discharge or fluctuance
No abscess or collection on CT
Histology shows atypical large intravascular cells rather than neutrophilic inflammation
No urinary symptoms or predisposing factors (diabetes, instrumentation, trauma) reported

data.description: 62-year-old man with a history of hypertension and diabetes mellitus presented with 3 months of progressive fatigue, anorexia, weight loss, and vague upper abdominal pain. He had a 40-pack-year smoking history, quit 2 years earlier. On presentation, he had renal insufficiency (creatinine 3.2 mg/dL), severe anemia (hemoglobin 7 g/dL), thrombocytopenia (77,000/μL), hypercalcemia (12.7 g/dL), elevated total protein (>10 g/dL), elevated LDH (1,157 U/L), marked hyperuricemia (20.8 mg/dL), and coagulopathy with prolonged PT and aPTT, low fibrinogen, and elevated D-dimer/fibrin split products.

A malignant plasma-cell disorder producing monoclonal immunoglobulins. This is the leading consideration given hypercalcemia, renal insufficiency, anemia, elevated total protein, apparent plasma-cell-rich tissue, and renal tubular casts. An aggressive variant could account for the abdominal mass and high LDH.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss
Renal histology showing apparent intratubular protein casts, compatible with myeloma cast nephropathy
Apparent plasma-cell-rich marrow or tissue infiltrates
Upper abdominal pain and a bulky abdominal mass, potentially representing extramedullary disease
Elevated LDH and hyperuricemia in aggressive disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Disseminated intravascular coagulation–type coagulopathy is an uncommon presenting complication
A bulky abdominal mass is less typical than skeletal involvement in conventional myeloma

data.description: An aggressive plasma-cell malignancy characterized by circulating clonal plasma cells, often with extensive marrow and extramedullary involvement. Peripheral blood examination is required to distinguish it from multiple myeloma.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss
Markedly elevated LDH and uric acid
Bulky abdominal disease consistent with possible extramedullary involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Disseminated intravascular coagulation–type coagulopathy is possible but not a defining or usual feature

data.description: A highly aggressive lymphoma with plasma-cell differentiation that can resemble plasmablastic myeloma histologically. Immunophenotyping, EBV studies, monoclonal protein testing, and clinical correlation are needed for distinction.
symptoms_in_common: Bulky abdominal mass and upper abdominal pain
Severe hyperuricemia suggesting rapid tumor turnover
Anemia and thrombocytopenia with possible marrow involvement
Tissue infiltrates with apparent plasmacytic or plasmablastic morphology
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked hyperproteinemia is less typical than in multiple myeloma
The combination of hypercalcemia and apparent renal cast nephropathy favors a plasma-cell disorder
Disseminated intravascular coagulation–type coagulopathy is not a usual defining presentation

data.description: An aggressive mature B-cell lymphoma that can produce bulky abdominal disease, constitutional symptoms, marrow infiltration, and metabolic complications from rapid tumor turnover.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive fatigue, anorexia, and weight loss
Upper abdominal pain and bulky abdominal mass
Anemia and thrombocytopenia with marrow involvement
Disseminated intravascular coagulation can complicate advanced disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated total protein is not typical
Apparent plasma-cell-rich histology is less characteristic of conventional diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
Renal tubular casts suggestive of light-chain cast nephropathy favor a plasma-cell malignancy

data.description: A mature B-cell neoplasm with lymphoplasmacytic marrow infiltration and usually an IgM monoclonal protein. It can cause hyperproteinemia, cytopenias, constitutional symptoms, and abdominal lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal pain and possible bulky lymphadenopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypercalcemia is unusual
Apparent myeloma-type renal cast nephropathy is uncommon
Very high LDH and severe hyperuricemia are atypical for an untreated indolent presentation
Disseminated intravascular coagulation–type coagulopathy is not typical

data.diagnosis: Multiple myeloma with extramedullary plasmacytoma (plasmablastic/aggressive myeloma) and cast nephropathy
data.description: Malignant clonal plasma cell neoplasm producing monoclonal immunoglobulin, causing hypercalcemia, renal failure, anemia and bone disease; aggressive forms develop extramedullary soft-tissue masses with high LDH. Light chain casts obstruct renal tubules.
symptoms_in_common: Renal insufficiency with tubular casts on kidney biopsy
Markedly elevated total protein (>10 g/dL) suggesting paraprotein
Bone marrow sheets of plasma cells
Elevated LDH and hyperuricemia from high tumor burden
Strong membranous staining consistent with CD138
symptoms_not_in_common: Disseminated intravascular coagulation-like coagulopathy is uncommon
Very high LDH and uric acid are unusual for typical myeloma
Bulky retroperitoneal mass is atypical at presentation
No bone pain or lytic lesions described

data.description: The most aggressive plasma cell dyscrasia, defined by circulating clonal plasma cells, with frequent extramedullary involvement, high LDH, cytopenias, renal failure and hypercalcemia.
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented leukocytosis or circulating plasma cells
Coagulopathy with low fibrinogen not typical
3-month subacute course is somewhat long

data.diagnosis: Plasmablastic lymphoma / diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation
data.description: Aggressive B-cell lymphoma with plasmablastic morphology and plasma cell immunophenotype (CD138+, CD20-), presenting with bulky nodal or extranodal masses, high LDH and spontaneous tumor lysis.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse sheets of monotonous cells in the mass
Coagulopathy/DIC can occur with aggressive lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Total protein >10 g/dL (large paraprotein) is unusual
Hypercalcemia with cast nephropathy favors myeloma
No known HIV or immunosuppression
Marrow shows mature-appearing plasma cells

data.description: Indolent B-cell lymphoma of lymphoplasmacytic cells secreting IgM paraprotein, causing anemia, lymphadenopathy, hyperviscosity and bleeding tendency.
symptoms_in_common: Coagulation abnormalities can occur from paraprotein interference
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypercalcemia is rare
Renal failure with cast nephropathy is uncommon
Very high LDH and uric acid are atypical
Histology shows pure plasma cell sheets rather than lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate
Low fibrinogen with elevated D-dimer

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma with metastases and DIC
data.description: Aggressive exocrine pancreatic malignancy, linked to smoking and diabetes, presenting with weight loss, abdominal pain and hypercoagulability, sometimes with chronic DIC.
symptoms_in_common: Older man with heavy smoking history and diabetes
Mass in the pancreatic/retroperitoneal region on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Total protein >10 g/dL
Hypercalcemia is uncommon
Marked hyperuricemia
Tubular casts in the kidney
Biopsies show plasma cells, not gland-forming carcinoma
No jaundice

data.description: A 30-month-old boy presented with sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction with sevoflurane and nitric oxide before plastic surgery on June 7, 2004. The patient had never undergone ECG before the operation. Physical examination revealed distinctive facial features including a round face, small upper jaw and teeth, and nearly bald head. He had normal toes, with no history of seizure or syncope, and normal neurodevelopment. The patient was born via vaginal delivery without complications. Echocardiogram showed no intracardiac anomaly with normal ventricular function. Preoperative biochemical analysis and electrolyte levels were normal. Family history was notable for his older sister showing paradoxical QT interval prolongation on epinephrine stress test (QTc baseline 0.4 → peak 0.53 sec), though she was asymptomatic. The QT intervals of parents and sister were not significantly prolonged on ECG, and there was no family history of syncope, seizure, or sudden death.

data.diagnosis: Timothy syndrome (CACNA1C-related long QT syndrome type 8)
data.description: A calcium-channel disorder causing severe QT prolongation, life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias, and variable syndactyly and craniofacial abnormalities. The pictured heterozygous c.1216G>A (p.G406R) variant strongly supports this diagnosis when confirmed in CACNA1C.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction
Apparent QT prolongation and abnormal repolarization on the supplied ECG
Bilateral cutaneous finger syndactyly visible in the hand images
Round face, small upper jaw and teeth, and sparse scalp hair
Normal electrolytes and structurally normal heart, consistent with a primary electrical disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal toes, although toe syndactyly is not required
Normal neurodevelopment, although developmental abnormalities are variable
The sister's abnormal epinephrine response is not readily explained by a typically de novo CACNA1C variant without additional family testing

data.description: An inherited potassium-channel disorder that delays ventricular repolarization and predisposes to torsades de pointes, particularly during adrenergic stimulation. Baseline QT intervals can be normal in affected relatives.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent QT prolongation on the supplied ECG
Sister with paradoxical QT prolongation during epinephrine testing
Normal cardiac structure and ventricular function
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral finger syndactyly
Distinctive facial and dental abnormalities
Nearly bald scalp
The pictured p.G406R variant favors CACNA1C-related disease rather than KCNQ1-related disease

data.description: An inherited channelopathy characterized by ventricular arrhythmias, prominent U waves or prolonged QU intervals, periodic paralysis, and characteristic facial and skeletal abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac arrest potentially caused by a ventricular arrhythmia
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported episodes of periodic paralysis
Normal toes
Sparse scalp hair and small teeth are not characteristic features
The pictured p.G406R variant favors Timothy syndrome

data.description: Medication-associated prolongation of ventricular repolarization that can cause torsades de pointes and cardiac arrest. Sevoflurane can prolong QT and may also unmask an underlying congenital channelopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac arrest occurring during sevoflurane anesthesia induction
Apparent QT prolongation on the supplied ECG
symptoms_not_in_common: Finger syndactyly and craniofacial abnormalities
Sister with abnormal QT response to epinephrine, suggesting inherited susceptibility
The pictured pathogenic-appearing channel variant supports a congenital rather than purely acquired disorder
Normal electrolytes provide no electrolyte-related explanation for acquired QT prolongation

data.description: An inherited calcium-handling disorder causing adrenergically triggered bidirectional or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia in a structurally normal heart, usually with a normal resting QT interval.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden cardiac arrest at a young age
No preceding syncope does not exclude an initial presentation with cardiac arrest
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent resting QT prolongation
Sister's epinephrine-induced QT prolongation rather than documented ventricular tachycardia
Finger syndactyly and craniofacial abnormalities
The pictured p.G406R variant favors CACNA1C-related long QT syndrome

data.diagnosis: Timothy syndrome (Long QT syndrome type 8, CACNA1C G406R)
data.description: Rare multisystem channelopathy caused by a gain-of-function mutation in CACNA1C (G406R) affecting the L-type calcium channel Cav1.2, characterized by marked QT prolongation, 2:1 functional AV block, T-wave alternans, life-threatening ventricular arrhythmias, syndactyly, facial dysmorphism, baldness at birth, small teeth, and often neurodevelopmental problems or autism.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction with sevoflurane
Markedly prolonged QT interval on ECG
2:1 AV block and T-wave alternans on ECG monitoring
Cutaneous syndactyly of the fingers on hand photograph and X-ray (probable reason for plastic surgery)
Small upper jaw and small teeth
Heterozygous CACNA1C c.1216G>A p.(G406R) mutation on sequencing
Structurally normal heart with normal ventricular function
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal neurodevelopment (developmental delay or autism is common)
Normal toes (toe syndactyly is frequent)
No history of seizure or syncope
No intracardiac anomaly (PDA, PFO or VSD are often present)
Sister with paradoxical QT response to epinephrine (the mutation is usually de novo)

data.diagnosis: Congenital long QT syndrome type 1 (Romano-Ward syndrome, KCNQ1)
data.description: Autosomal dominant potassium channelopathy causing QT prolongation and torsades de pointes, typically triggered by adrenergic stimulation; shows paradoxical QT prolongation on epinephrine challenge.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden cardiac arrest under anesthetic and adrenergic stress
Sister with paradoxical QT prolongation on epinephrine stress test
Family members can have normal resting QT (incomplete penetrance)
symptoms_not_in_common: Finger syndactyly
Round face, small upper jaw and small teeth
Nearly bald head
2:1 AV block (uncommon in LQT1)
CACNA1C G406R mutation rather than a KCNQ1 mutation
No family history of syncope or sudden death

data.diagnosis: Andersen-Tawil syndrome (Long QT syndrome type 7, KCNJ2)
data.description: Autosomal dominant potassium channel disorder with the triad of ventricular arrhythmias with prolonged QT/QU interval, periodic paralysis, and dysmorphic features including micrognathia, dental anomalies, clinodactyly and syndactyly.
symptoms_not_in_common: No periodic paralysis or muscle weakness
Nearly bald head
Finger syndactyly with normal toes (toe 2-3 syndactyly and clinodactyly are more typical)
2:1 AV block with markedly prolonged QT
Normal potassium level
CACNA1C mutation rather than a KCNJ2 mutation

data.description: Connexin-43 disorder featuring syndactyly of the 4th and 5th fingers, small teeth with enamel hypoplasia, sparse hair, characteristic facial features with a narrow nose, microphthalmia, and occasional cardiac conduction defects or arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Finger syndactyly involving the ulnar digits
Possible conduction abnormality (AV block) and arrhythmia
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly prolonged QT interval with T-wave alternans
Sudden cardiac arrest in early childhood
No eye abnormalities (microphthalmia, microcornea) described
Round face rather than a thin nose with hypoplastic alae
CACNA1C mutation rather than a GJA1 mutation
Sister's abnormal epinephrine QT response

data.description: Pharmacogenetic disorder of skeletal muscle calcium regulation triggered by volatile anesthetics such as sevoflurane, causing a hypermetabolic crisis with hyperthermia, rigidity, hypercapnia, hyperkalemia, arrhythmia and cardiac arrest.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac arrest during induction with sevoflurane
Previously asymptomatic child with no syncope or seizures
Normal preoperative laboratory tests and echocardiogram
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, hypercapnia or hyperkalemia
Persistent QT prolongation with 2:1 AV block and T-wave alternans
Finger syndactyly
Round face, small upper jaw, small teeth and baldness
Sister's paradoxical QT prolongation on epinephrine test
CACNA1C G406R mutation rather than an RYR1 mutation

anonymization.anonymizedText: A 30-month-old boy presented with sudden cardiac arrest during anesthesia induction with sevoflurane and nitric oxide before ************* on June 7, 2004. The patient had never undergone ECG before the operation. Physical examination revealed distinctive facial features including a round face, small upper jaw and teeth, and nearly bald head. He had normal toes, with no history of seizure or syncope, and normal neurodevelopment. The patient was born via vaginal delivery without complications. Echocardiogram showed no intracardiac anomaly with normal ventricular function. Preoperative biochemical analysis and electrolyte levels were normal. Family history was notable for his older sister showing paradoxical QT interval prolongation on epinephrine stress test (QTc baseline 0.4 → peak 0.53 sec), though she was asymptomatic. The QT intervals of parents and sister were not significantly prolonged on ECG, and there was no family history of syncope, seizure, or sudden death.
