The patient had never undergone ECG before the operation. Physical examination revealed distinctive facial features including a round face, small upper jaw and teeth, and nearly bald head. He had normal toes, with no history of seizure or syncope, and normal neurodevelopment. The patient was born via vaginal delivery without complications. Echocardiogram showed no intracardiac anomaly with normal ventricular function. Preoperative biochemical analysis and electrolyte levels were normal. Family history was notable for his older sister showing paradoxical QT interval prolongation on epinephrine stress test (QTc baseline 0.4 → peak 0.53 sec), though she was asymptomatic. The QT intervals of parents and sister were not significantly prolonged on ECG, and there was no family history of syncope, seizure, or sudden death.

data.description: 72-year-old white woman with 10-year history of recurrent cystitis. No systemic symptoms. Physical exam showed slight anemia. Urine cultures were positive for Escherichia coli. No hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy detected by CT and ultrasound. Esophagogastroduodenoscopy and subsequent biopsies were negative for both pathologic lymphoid infiltrate and Helicobacter pylori. Otolaryngologic examination and bone marrow biopsy were negative. Serology for hepatitis C virus and hepatitis B virus was negative. No monoclonal component found in serum protein electrophoresis.

data.diagnosis: Primary urinary bladder extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT lymphoma)
data.description: An indolent B-cell lymphoma that can develop in bladder mucosa affected by chronic inflammation. This is the leading consideration, although confirmation requires immunophenotyping and interpretation of the molecular study.
symptoms_in_common: Long history of recurrent cystitis with Escherichia coli infection
Absence of systemic symptoms, lymphadenopathy, or hepatosplenomegaly
Negative bone marrow and extravesical evaluations, supporting a localized process
Biopsy images suggest a small lymphoid infiltrate involving the urothelium, compatible with lymphoepithelial lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild anemia is nonspecific and is not characteristic of localized bladder MALT lymphoma

data.diagnosis: Reactive lymphoid hyperplasia of the urinary bladder (follicular cystitis)
data.description: A benign lymphoid proliferation caused by chronic bladder irritation or infection that can resemble lymphoma.
symptoms_in_common: No lymphadenopathy, organ enlargement, or bone marrow involvement
Lymphoid cells in the bladder biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent dense lymphoid infiltrate with urothelial involvement raises concern for lymphoma rather than uncomplicated reactive inflammation
Mild anemia is not a characteristic finding
A confirmed lymphoma-associated clonal rearrangement would argue against a purely reactive process; the displayed fluorescence image cannot establish its identity without probe information

data.diagnosis: Primary urinary bladder diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
data.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma that can rarely arise in the bladder and cause symptoms resembling cystitis.
symptoms_in_common: Negative staging outside the bladder can occur in primary localized disease
symptoms_not_in_common: A 10-year indolent history is less typical of an aggressive lymphoma
The biopsy images appear predominantly composed of smaller lymphoid cells rather than sheets of large atypical cells
Absence of systemic symptoms is less suggestive of aggressive disease, although it does not exclude it

data.diagnosis: Follicular lymphoma involving the urinary bladder
data.description: An indolent germinal-center B-cell lymphoma that rarely involves the bladder, either primarily or as part of systemic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Small lymphoid cells in the biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: No lymphadenopathy or bone marrow involvement makes the usual systemic presentation less likely
The supplied biopsy fields do not demonstrate a clear neoplastic follicular architecture
Apparent lymphoepithelial lesions favor MALT lymphoma
Recurrent Escherichia coli infection is not a characteristic association

data.diagnosis: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma involving the urinary bladder
data.description: An indolent B-cell lymphoma with lymphocytic and plasmacytic differentiation, usually involving bone marrow and often producing a monoclonal IgM protein.
symptoms_in_common: Some cells in the biopsy have a plasmacytoid appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative bone marrow biopsy
No monoclonal component on serum protein electrophoresis
No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly
Apparently isolated bladder involvement is exceptionally uncommon
Chronic Escherichia coli cystitis and apparent lymphoepithelial lesions favor bladder MALT lymphoma

data.diagnosis: Primary extranodal marginal zone B-cell lymphoma of MALT type of the urinary bladder
data.description: Rare low-grade B-cell lymphoma arising in the bladder mucosa, typically in elderly women with a long history of chronic or recurrent cystitis; composed of small centrocyte-like/monocytoid cells with plasmacytic differentiation and lymphoepithelial lesions, sometimes with MALT1 translocations such as t(11;18) detectable by FISH.
symptoms_in_common: 10-year history of recurrent cystitis with E. coli (chronic antigenic stimulation)
Cystoscopic mucosal lesion of the bladder
Histology showing dense infiltrate of small monocytoid lymphoid cells with clear cytoplasm infiltrating the urothelium
FISH showing fusion signals consistent with a translocation
Disease localized to the bladder: no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly, negative bone marrow, negative gastric and otolaryngologic work-up
No monoclonal serum component, negative HCV/HBV serology
symptoms_not_in_common: No gross hematuria reported
No discrete bladder mass described

data.description: Benign reactive lymphoid infiltrate of the bladder mucosa with lymphoid follicle formation, caused by chronic or recurrent bacterial infection.
symptoms_in_common: Positive urine cultures for E. coli
Lymphoid infiltrate in the bladder mucosa
symptoms_not_in_common: Monotonous sheet-like infiltrate rather than polymorphous follicles with germinal centres
Infiltration of the urothelium by lymphoid cells (lymphoepithelial-type lesions)
FISH evidence of a chromosomal translocation indicating clonality
Anemia

data.diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma of the bladder
data.description: Aggressive B-cell lymphoma that may arise primarily in the bladder or by transformation of a low-grade lymphoma; composed of sheets of large atypical lymphoid cells.
symptoms_not_in_common: Cells are small to medium rather than large with prominent nucleoli
Indolent course with no systemic symptoms
No bulky mass, lymphadenopathy or disseminated disease
Negative bone marrow

data.diagnosis: Secondary bladder involvement by systemic low-grade B-cell lymphoma (e.g., lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma, CLL/SLL, mantle cell lymphoma, or disseminated gastric MALT lymphoma)
data.description: Bladder infiltration by a lymphoma arising elsewhere; this is more common than primary bladder lymphoma and usually accompanies nodal, marrow or other extranodal disease.
symptoms_in_common: Small-cell lymphoid infiltrate in the bladder
symptoms_not_in_common: No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly on CT and ultrasound
Negative bone marrow biopsy
Negative gastric biopsies and negative H. pylori
Negative otolaryngologic examination
No monoclonal component on serum protein electrophoresis
No systemic symptoms

data.diagnosis: Urothelial carcinoma (including carcinoma in situ or plasmacytoid/lymphoma-like variant)
data.description: The most common bladder malignancy in the elderly; it can present with irritative urinary symptoms mimicking cystitis, and some variants have discohesive cells that resemble lymphoma or plasmacytoma.
symptoms_in_common: Discohesive cells with clear cytoplasm on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Infiltrate is lymphoid; the urothelium itself appears non-dysplastic
FISH translocation typical of lymphoma
No papillary or solid tumour described
Work-up was directed at lymphoma staging
No hematuria reported

data.description: 30-year-old Hispanic male with history of heavy NSAID use. Presented with melena and severe abdominal pain for 3 weeks, with similar but milder symptoms over prior 4-5 months. Initial hemoglobin 7.8 g/dL and mean corpuscular volume 78 fL. Later endorsed having a right swollen testicle (initially missed on previous exams). Physical exam revealed nontender enlarged right testicle. Laboratory markers showed: human chorionic gonadotropin 50 mIU/mL (normal <10), α-fetoprotein 1,990 ng/mL (normal <8), lactate dehydrogenase 534 IU/L (range 25-175).

data.diagnosis: Metastatic mixed nonseminomatous testicular germ cell tumor with gastrointestinal involvement
data.description: The leading possibility is a testicular malignancy containing multiple germ cell components, potentially including teratoma and yolk sac tumor. Gastrointestinal invasion or metastasis can cause ulceration and bleeding. The supplied endoscopic, histologic, and CT images raise concern for an ulcerated tumor and abdominal involvement, but tissue review is needed to confirm the components.
symptoms_in_common: Painless enlargement of the right testicle
Elevated human chorionic gonadotropin and lactate dehydrogenase
Melena and severe microcytic anemia compatible with gastrointestinal blood loss
Ulcerated gastrointestinal lesions visible on endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Gastrointestinal bleeding is an uncommon initial presentation of testicular germ cell cancer

data.diagnosis: Testicular yolk sac tumor with gastrointestinal metastasis
data.description: An AFP-producing nonseminomatous germ cell malignancy that, in adults, commonly occurs as part of a mixed tumor. Metastatic abdominal disease can invade the gastrointestinal tract and cause bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Melena and microcytic anemia if gastrointestinal involvement is present
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated human chorionic gonadotropin is not typical of a pure yolk sac tumor
Gastrointestinal bleeding is an unusual presenting manifestation

data.diagnosis: Testicular embryonal carcinoma with gastrointestinal metastasis
data.description: An aggressive nonseminomatous germ cell cancer affecting young adults that may produce AFP and hCG. It can spread to abdominal lymph nodes and other organs, occasionally causing gastrointestinal invasion and bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated alpha-fetoprotein, human chorionic gonadotropin, and lactate dehydrogenase
Melena and severe anemia in the setting of gastrointestinal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Gastrointestinal bleeding is an uncommon initial presentation
The apparent diversity of tissue patterns in the supplied histology would be less typical of a pure embryonal carcinoma

data.description: NSAIDs can damage gastric and duodenal mucosal defenses, producing ulcers, abdominal pain, and potentially severe upper gastrointestinal bleeding. This could coexist with a separate testicular malignancy but would not explain the entire case.
symptoms_in_common: Microcytosis consistent with chronic blood loss
symptoms_not_in_common: Painless right testicular enlargement
Markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein
Elevated human chorionic gonadotropin
Possible tumor-like gastrointestinal and abdominal findings

data.diagnosis: Lymphoma involving the testis and gastrointestinal tract
data.description: Lymphoma can involve the testis and gastrointestinal tract, producing painless testicular enlargement, abdominal masses, ulceration, and bleeding. The patient's age and germ cell tumor marker profile make this substantially less likely.
symptoms_in_common: Possible abdominal mass and ulcerated gastrointestinal lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated alpha-fetoprotein is not characteristic of lymphoma
Elevated human chorionic gonadotropin is not characteristic of lymphoma
Age 30 is younger than the usual presentation of primary testicular lymphoma

data.diagnosis: Metastatic mixed nonseminomatous germ cell tumor of the testis (teratoma with embryonal/yolk sac components) with duodenal invasion
data.description: Malignant testicular germ cell tumor containing multiple histologic elements; spreads to retroperitoneal lymph nodes, which can erode into the duodenum and cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Melena and microcytic anemia from ulcerated duodenal lesion on endoscopy
Right retroperitoneal/perirenal hypodense mass on CT
Histology showing cystic glandular (teratomatous) structures and nests of malignant cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Gastrointestinal bleeding is an uncommon presenting feature of testicular cancer
Heavy NSAID use is unrelated and suggests an alternative cause of the ulcer

data.description: Mucosal ulceration of the stomach or duodenum caused by NSAID inhibition of prostaglandin synthesis, frequently presenting with upper gastrointestinal bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia with low MCV from chronic blood loss
symptoms_not_in_common: Enlarged nontender testicle
Elevated α-fetoprotein
Elevated hCG
Elevated LDH
Retroperitoneal mass on CT
Malignant cells and teratomatous glands on histology

data.diagnosis: Pure testicular seminoma with retroperitoneal metastasis
data.description: Most common single-histology germ cell tumor of the testis, presenting as a painless testicular mass with possible retroperitoneal nodal spread; may mildly raise hCG and LDH.
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated α-fetoprotein (not produced by pure seminoma)
Glandular/cystic teratomatous structures on histology
Duodenal invasion with melena is rare
Heavy NSAID use is unrelated

data.description: Malignant epithelial tumor of the upper gastrointestinal tract that presents with an ulcerated mass, bleeding, pain and iron deficiency anemia; rare hepatoid variants can secrete α-fetoprotein.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated α-fetoprotein possible in the hepatoid variant
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age (30 years)
Enlarged testicle
Elevated hCG
Benign-appearing teratomatous cystic glands on histology
Retroperitoneal perirenal mass is more typical of a testicular primary

data.diagnosis: Lymphoma (non-Hodgkin) involving the testis, retroperitoneum and gastrointestinal tract
data.description: Lymphoid malignancy that can involve the testis, retroperitoneal nodes and bowel at the same time, causing masses, ulceration and raised LDH.
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated α-fetoprotein
Elevated hCG
Young age (testicular lymphoma usually occurs after 60)
Histology showing glandular/epithelial structures rather than sheets of lymphoid cells
Heavy NSAID use is unrelated

data.description: 55-year-old woman with a 13-year history of right breast invasive ductal carcinoma, stage IV with metastases to bone, lungs, and liver, status post mastectomy, multiple systemic therapies, and stem-cell transplantation 8 years prior. She had been on anastrozole for 3 months and paracetamol for pain. She developed progressive generalized weakness and episodic confusion over several days, rapidly worsening to unresponsiveness. On admission she was found disoriented on the floor with lower leg weakness and inability to follow basic instructions. Exam showed she was awake but unresponsive and uncooperative, without focal neurologic deficits initially; vital signs were notable for mild tachycardia and no fever. Baseline brain MRI 2 weeks earlier was normal.

data.diagnosis: Cancer-associated multifocal ischemic strokes, potentially from nonbacterial thrombotic endocarditis
data.description: Advanced malignancy can promote thrombosis and sterile cardiac valve vegetations that embolize to multiple brain regions. The apparent bilateral diffusion abnormalities raise concern for multifocal infarction, although ADC maps are needed to confirm restricted diffusion.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly progressive confusion and impaired responsiveness
Small susceptibility foci that could represent associated hemorrhage
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized rather than clearly focal neurologic dysfunction
Progressive deterioration over several days rather than one abrupt stroke episode
Bilateral posterior-predominant abnormalities could also reflect a nonembolic process

data.description: A syndrome of cerebral edema associated with endothelial dysfunction, hypertension, renal disease, or certain cancer treatments. Severe cases can include restricted diffusion and small hemorrhages; blood pressure data and ADC imaging are needed to assess this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Acute or subacute confusion progressing to unresponsiveness
Bilateral posterior cortical and subcortical signal abnormalities
History of malignancy and systemic treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent lower leg weakness is less characteristic than seizures or visual disturbance
Marked focal diffusion abnormalities would be less typical of uncomplicated vasogenic edema

data.description: A rare complication in which tumor cells spread within small cerebral vessels, obstructing blood flow and producing multifocal ischemic or hemorrhagic injury rather than conventional metastatic masses.
symptoms_in_common: Multifocal bilateral brain abnormalities without an obvious dominant mass in the supplied images
Possible combined ischemic and microhemorrhagic lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly discordant feature, but the clinical and imaging findings are nonspecific and do not establish this rare diagnosis

data.diagnosis: Cerebral venous thrombosis with hemorrhagic venous infarction
data.description: Thrombosis of cerebral veins or dural sinuses can cause edema, infarction, hemorrhage, and impaired consciousness. Malignancy increases the risk; MR or CT venography would be needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Possible hemorrhagic components on susceptibility-sensitive imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse generalized weakness without an initially clear focal deficit is less characteristic of localized venous infarction
Scattered bilateral abnormalities are not specific for a single venous drainage territory

data.diagnosis: Hepatic encephalopathy, potentially associated with hyperammonemia
data.description: Severe hepatic dysfunction can produce toxic-metabolic brain dysfunction ranging from confusion to coma. Extensive liver metastases provide a possible substrate, but liver function and ammonia measurements are required, and the supplied imaging is not classic.
symptoms_in_common: Episodic confusion progressing to profound unresponsiveness
symptoms_not_in_common: Patchy posterior diffusion abnormalities are less typical than the usual patterns of hyperammonemic injury
Small cerebral susceptibility foci suggesting hemorrhage are not a characteristic feature
Lower leg weakness is not a defining manifestation

data.diagnosis: Cerebral tumor embolism / intravascular tumor emboli from metastatic breast carcinoma
data.description: Occlusion of small cerebral arteries and arterioles by circulating tumor cell emboli from widely metastatic carcinoma (often with lung involvement), causing multifocal bilateral watershed and cortical infarcts with petechial hemorrhages and a rapidly progressive encephalopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Stage IV breast carcinoma with lung, liver and bone metastases
Subacute progressive generalized weakness and episodic confusion progressing to unresponsiveness
Normal brain MRI 2 weeks earlier with new multifocal lesions
Bilateral parieto-occipital cortical and deep white matter (centrum semiovale) FLAIR hyperintensities with restricted diffusion in a watershed pattern
Multiple punctate microhemorrhages on gradient-echo imaging
Absence of focal deficits initially (diffuse encephalopathy)
symptoms_not_in_common: No discrete mass lesions on imaging
Rare entity; more often described with cardiac or pulmonary vein tumor invasion
Gradual course over days rather than abrupt stroke-like onset

data.diagnosis: Nonbacterial thrombotic (marantic) endocarditis with multifocal embolic infarcts / cancer-associated hypercoagulability
data.description: Sterile valvular vegetations associated with advanced malignancy (especially adenocarcinoma) that embolize to the brain, producing multiple infarcts of varying sizes in multiple vascular territories, often with accompanying disseminated intravascular coagulation.
symptoms_in_common: New lesions compared with normal recent MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Symmetric watershed/deep white matter distribution rather than scattered territorial infarcts
Numerous microhemorrhages are less typical
No reported murmur or systemic emboli
Progressive rather than stepwise abrupt course

data.description: Neurotoxic state with vasogenic edema, predominantly in parieto-occipital regions, associated with hypertension, chemotherapy or immunosuppressive agents, and renal failure; may be complicated by hemorrhage or restricted diffusion in atypical cases.
symptoms_in_common: Confusion and altered consciousness evolving over days
Bilateral posterior parieto-occipital cortical/subcortical FLAIR hyperintensities
History of cancer and multiple systemic therapies
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented severe hypertension
No seizures, headache or visual disturbance reported
Prominent restricted diffusion suggests cytotoxic rather than vasogenic edema
No recent cytotoxic or immunosuppressive drug exposure (only anastrozole)
Deep watershed white matter involvement

data.diagnosis: Thrombotic microangiopathy (TTP / cancer-associated microangiopathy) or disseminated intravascular coagulation with cerebral microinfarcts
data.description: Widespread microvascular thrombosis from platelet or fibrin thrombi, seen with disseminated carcinoma or after stem-cell transplant, leading to fluctuating neurologic deficits, multifocal small infarcts and petechial hemorrhages.
symptoms_in_common: Disseminated malignancy and prior stem-cell transplantation
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
No reported thrombocytopenia, hemolytic anemia, renal failure or bleeding
Transplant was 8 years ago, making transplant-associated TMA unlikely
Large confluent parieto-occipital lesions are less typical

data.diagnosis: Intravascular / leptomeningeal carcinomatosis with secondary vasculopathy (differential includes CNS vasculitis)
data.description: Tumor infiltration of leptomeninges and perivascular spaces (or inflammatory vessel wall disease) causing vessel narrowing, multifocal ischemic lesions and encephalopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Metastatic breast cancer (common source of leptomeningeal spread)
symptoms_not_in_common: No headache, cranial neuropathies or radicular symptoms reported
No leptomeningeal enhancement or hydrocephalus described
Very rapid development within 2 weeks of a normal MRI
Watershed-pattern distribution less typical

data.description: 59-year-old man with history of prostate cancer metastatic to lumbar spine and periaortic lymph nodes diagnosed in 2001, with initial PSA of 11.3 ng/mL. In August 2011, presented to emergency room with abdominal pain. Lab tests showed elevated lipase (874 U/L), alkaline phosphatase (289 IU/L), and ALT (222 IU/L), with normal bilirubin. Later returned with right upper quadrant abdominal pain, tachycardia but afebrile. Physical exam showed positive Murphy's sign and palpable gallbladder. Labs showed elevated alkaline phosphatase of 357 IU/L and normal serum lipase.

Rare spread of prostate cancer to the pancreas, potentially causing pancreatitis and biliary obstruction. The known metastatic prostate cancer and apparent pancreatic-region lesion make this an important possibility. Confirmation requires biopsy interpretation and prostate-lineage immunostains; the stains shown are not labeled.
symptoms_in_common: History of prostate cancer metastatic to bone and lymph nodes
Initial lipase elevation consistent with pancreatitis
Palpable gallbladder, potentially reflecting downstream biliary obstruction
Apparent lesion on endoscopic ultrasound and malignant-appearing cells in the tissue images
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive Murphy's sign is more typical of gallbladder inflammation
Normal bilirubin is less typical of advanced malignant biliary obstruction

data.description: A primary pancreatic malignancy that can obstruct the pancreatic or bile ducts, producing pancreatitis, cholestatic liver-test abnormalities, and gallbladder distension.
symptoms_in_common: Malignant-appearing epithelial cells in the tissue images
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive Murphy's sign is not a characteristic feature
Normal bilirubin is less typical when substantial bile-duct obstruction is present
Known metastatic prostate cancer raises the competing possibility of a secondary tumor

data.description: Inflammation of the gallbladder, commonly caused by cystic-duct obstruction from a gallstone. It fits the later episode of localized right upper quadrant pain but would not independently explain a malignant pancreatic-region lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Normal lipase during the later presentation
Normal bilirubin, which can occur with isolated cystic-duct obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked lipase elevation during the initial episode suggests associated pancreatitis rather than isolated cholecystitis
Afebrile presentation is less typical, although it does not exclude cholecystitis
Apparent pancreatic-region lesion and malignant-appearing tissue are not explained by uncomplicated cholecystitis

data.description: Pancreatic inflammation caused by a gallstone temporarily obstructing the ampulla or common bile duct. Stone passage can explain subsequent normalization of lipase and bilirubin.
symptoms_in_common: Positive Murphy's sign suggesting concurrent gallbladder disease
Normal bilirubin and later normal lipase, compatible with resolved transient obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent alkaline phosphatase elevation may suggest ongoing obstruction or another cause
Palpable gallbladder is less typical of an uncomplicated transient stone episode
Apparent pancreatic-region lesion and malignant-appearing tissue are not explained by gallstones alone

data.description: Cancer arising in the distal common bile duct, potentially causing partial biliary obstruction, gallbladder distension, and occasionally pancreatitis. Distinguishing it from pancreatic or metastatic cancer requires precise lesion localization and pathology.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal and right upper quadrant pain
Malignant-appearing epithelial cells in the tissue images
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal bilirubin is less typical of established obstructing cholangiocarcinoma
Positive Murphy's sign is more typical of acute cholecystitis
A pancreatic-centered lesion would favor pancreatic malignancy or metastasis rather than a bile-duct primary

data.diagnosis: Metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma to the pancreatic head/periampullary region with biliary obstruction
data.description: Rare spread of prostate cancer to the pancreas or peripancreatic tissue, producing a mass that obstructs the pancreatic and common bile ducts. Diagnosis is confirmed by EUS-guided fine-needle aspiration with immunostaining positive for prostate markers (PSA, PSAP, androgen receptor/NKX3.1).
symptoms_in_common: Known metastatic prostate cancer with periaortic nodal disease
Abdominal pain with initial lipase elevation (obstructive pancreatitis)
Cholestatic pattern with rising alkaline phosphatase and elevated ALT
Right upper quadrant pain with palpable gallbladder (distal biliary obstruction)
Approximately 2.8 x 2.0 cm hypoechoic mass on endoscopic ultrasound
Cytology/histology showing nests of epithelial cells with prominent nucleoli and clear/vacuolated cytoplasm
Immunostains with cytoplasmic and strong nuclear positivity consistent with prostate markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Pancreas is a very uncommon site for prostate cancer metastasis
Normal bilirubin despite biliary obstruction
Positive Murphy's sign more typical of acute cholecystitis
Alkaline phosphatase elevation could partly reflect bone metastases

data.description: Malignant tumour of the pancreatic ductal epithelium, commonly arising in the head and causing obstruction of the bile and pancreatic ducts.
symptoms_in_common: Pancreatitis episode with elevated lipase from duct obstruction
Hypoechoic pancreatic head mass on endoscopic ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal bilirubin and no jaundice
Histology shows solid nests of cells with clear cytoplasm rather than infiltrating glands with desmoplastic stroma
Strong nuclear and cytoplasmic staining pattern suggesting prostate-lineage markers
Positive Murphy's sign with painful rather than painless gallbladder

data.description: Inflammation of the gallbladder, usually from cystic duct obstruction by a gallstone, causing right upper quadrant pain and tenderness.
symptoms_not_in_common: Afebrile
Markedly elevated and rising alkaline phosphatase
Preceding pancreatitis with lipase of 874 U/L
Discrete mass on endoscopic ultrasound
Malignant cells on biopsy

data.description: Gallstones in the common bile duct causing transient ampullary obstruction, biliary colic, cholestasis and acute pancreatitis.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated lipase that later normalised (transient obstruction)
Right upper quadrant pain on return
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal bilirubin
Palpable gallbladder (stone disease usually gives a shrunken, fibrotic gallbladder)
Solid mass rather than stones on imaging
Malignant cells on fine-needle aspiration
Progressive rise in alkaline phosphatase

data.description: Malignancy of the distal bile duct or ampulla of Vater causing biliary and sometimes pancreatic duct obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Episode of pancreatitis from ampullary obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal bilirubin and absence of jaundice
Histology with solid nests and clear cytoplasm rather than gland-forming biliary-type adenocarcinoma
Immunostaining pattern favouring prostate origin
Positive Murphy's sign

data.description: 13-year-old boy with Addison’s disease, dysphagia since age 11, muscle weakness, excessive fatigue, and recent gait ataxia. He had bilateral cryptorchidism, inguinal hernia, and hypospadias at birth; early global developmental delay with mild intellectual disability noted by age 9; and deficient tear production since infancy. At age 2 he developed recurrent vomiting, failure to thrive, and progressive skin pigmentation; at age 4 he had recurrent hypotonia, hypoglycemia, and hypothermia leading to diagnosis of Addison’s disease. Examination showed severe hyperpigmentation and hyperkeratosis of elbows and knuckles, facial dysmorphism, dysarthria, nasal speech, saccadic eye movements with horizontal gaze nystagmus, dilated pupils with poor light response, mild bilateral optic atrophy, distal arm muscle wasting and weakness, milder leg pyramidal weakness, unsteady gait, hyperreflexia, and bilateral extensor plantar responses. Laboratory studies showed markedly elevated ACTH with normal electrolytes, aldosterone, and renin, consistent with isolated glucocorticoid deficiency.

The most likely unifying diagnosis: an autosomal recessive AAAS-related disorder characterized by alacrima, achalasia, and ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency, often accompanied by autonomic dysfunction and progressive neurological disease. Dysphagia suggests achalasia but requires confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Isolated glucocorticoid deficiency with markedly elevated ACTH and preserved mineralocorticoid function
Severe hyperpigmentation, hypoglycemia, vomiting, and failure to thrive
Progressive weakness, distal muscle wasting, hyperreflexia, and extensor plantar responses
Ataxia, dysarthria, nasal speech, and optic atrophy
Dilated pupils with poor light response suggesting autonomic dysfunction
Developmental delay and mild intellectual disability
symptoms_not_in_common: Congenital bilateral cryptorchidism, hypospadias, and inguinal hernia are not defining features
The apparent central spinal cord cavity on MRI is not a characteristic diagnostic feature

data.description: An ABCD1-related disorder of very-long-chain fatty acid metabolism causing adrenal insufficiency and progressive neurological dysfunction in boys. It is an important alternative, although the alacrima-dysphagia combination strongly favors Allgrove syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Childhood adrenal insufficiency with elevated ACTH
Progressive gait disturbance and pyramidal weakness
Hyperreflexia and bilateral extensor plantar responses
symptoms_not_in_common: Deficient tear production since infancy
Dysphagia suggestive of achalasia
Congenital cryptorchidism and hypospadias
Facial dysmorphism and hyperkeratosis
Prominent distal arm muscle wasting
An apparent spinal cord cavity rather than characteristic cerebral white-matter disease

data.description: A genetically heterogeneous disorder of adrenal cortisol production or ACTH responsiveness, commonly associated with MC2R or MRAP variants, producing cortisol deficiency while usually preserving mineralocorticoid function.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated ACTH with isolated glucocorticoid deficiency
Recurrent hypoglycemia, vomiting, hypotonia, and failure to thrive
symptoms_not_in_common: Congenital deficient tear production
Dysphagia suggestive of achalasia
Progressive ataxia, distal muscle wasting, and pyramidal signs
Optic atrophy and abnormal pupillary responses
Congenital genital abnormalities
Apparent spinal cord cavitation on MRI

data.description: An autosomal recessive glycosylation disorder causing alacrima, achalasia, developmental impairment, and sometimes neurological or autonomic abnormalities. Unlike Allgrove syndrome, adrenal insufficiency is not characteristic.
symptoms_in_common: Possible autonomic abnormalities reflected by poor pupillary responses
symptoms_not_in_common: Confirmed ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency
Marked ACTH elevation and severe hyperpigmentation
Recurrent adrenal-associated hypoglycemia
Congenital cryptorchidism and hypospadias
Apparent spinal cord cavitation on MRI

data.description: A fluid-filled cavity within the spinal cord that can cause segmental arm muscle wasting and weakness with pyramidal signs in the legs. The supplied MRI appears to show a central intramedullary fluid-signal cavity, potentially representing syringomyelia or hydromyelia; formal radiological review is needed. This could be a coexisting condition rather than the unifying diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Distal arm muscle wasting and weakness
Hyperreflexia and bilateral extensor plantar responses
Apparent central spinal cord cavity on axial and sagittal MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Isolated glucocorticoid deficiency with elevated ACTH
Severe hyperpigmentation and recurrent hypoglycemia
Deficient tear production since infancy
Early global developmental delay and intellectual disability
Congenital cryptorchidism, hypospadias, and inguinal hernia
Optic atrophy
Dysphagia and bulbar speech abnormalities without demonstrated brainstem extension

data.description: Autosomal recessive disorder due to AAAS gene mutations, characterized by ACTH-resistant adrenal insufficiency (usually isolated glucocorticoid deficiency), alacrima, achalasia, and progressive neurological and autonomic dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Isolated glucocorticoid deficiency with markedly elevated ACTH and normal renin/aldosterone/electrolytes
Recurrent vomiting and failure to thrive
Dilated pupils with poor light response (autonomic dysfunction)
Distal arm muscle wasting and weakness
Pyramidal signs with hyperreflexia and extensor plantar responses
Mild intellectual disability and developmental delay
Sporadic case in pedigree compatible with autosomal recessive inheritance
Cervical spinal cord signal abnormality/syrinx-like central lesion on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral cryptorchidism
Hypospadias
Inguinal hernia
Saccadic eye movements with horizontal gaze nystagmus

data.description: X-linked peroxisomal disorder due to ABCD1 mutations causing accumulation of very long chain fatty acids, with primary adrenal insufficiency and progressive demyelination of brain, spinal cord and peripheral nerves.
symptoms_in_common: Male with primary adrenal insufficiency in childhood
Pyramidal weakness, hyperreflexia, extensor plantar responses
symptoms_not_in_common: Alacrima since infancy
Congenital cryptorchidism, hypospadias and inguinal hernia
Early global developmental delay preceding regression
Facial dysmorphism
Hyperkeratosis of elbows and knuckles
Dilated poorly reactive pupils
Distal arm muscle wasting
No affected maternal male relatives in pedigree

data.description: Autosomal recessive group of disorders with adrenal unresponsiveness to ACTH, causing isolated cortisol deficiency with preserved mineralocorticoid function, presenting in early childhood with hypoglycemia and hyperpigmentation.
symptoms_in_common: Isolated glucocorticoid deficiency with very high ACTH
Possible learning difficulties from recurrent hypoglycemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Alacrima
Dysphagia
Ataxia, pyramidal signs, distal muscle wasting
Optic atrophy
Pupillary abnormalities
Nystagmus
Dysarthria and nasal speech
Genital anomalies and inguinal hernia
Facial dysmorphism
Spinal cord MRI abnormality

data.diagnosis: Mitochondrial disease (e.g., Kearns-Sayre syndrome or other mtDNA deletion/depletion syndrome)
data.description: Multisystem disorders of oxidative phosphorylation that can combine endocrine failure, including adrenal insufficiency, with myopathy, ataxia, optic neuropathy, eye movement abnormalities and developmental delay.
symptoms_not_in_common: Alacrima since infancy
Isolated glucocorticoid deficiency with preserved mineralocorticoids is unusual
Congenital genital anomalies and inguinal hernia
Hyperkeratosis of elbows and knuckles
Dilated poorly reactive pupils
Facial dysmorphism
No ptosis, ophthalmoplegia, pigmentary retinopathy, hearing loss or cardiac conduction defect reported

data.diagnosis: GMPPA-related congenital disorder of glycosylation (AAMR syndrome: alacrima, achalasia, mental retardation)
data.description: Autosomal recessive triple A-like disorder caused by GMPPA mutations, featuring alacrima, achalasia, intellectual disability and neurological and autonomic abnormalities, typically without adrenal insufficiency.
symptoms_in_common: Early global developmental delay and intellectual disability
Recurrent vomiting and failure to thrive
symptoms_not_in_common: Adrenal insufficiency with markedly elevated ACTH
Severe hyperpigmentation
Hypoglycemia and hypothermia episodes
Optic atrophy
Distal muscle wasting with pyramidal signs
Cryptorchidism, hypospadias and inguinal hernia
Hyperkeratosis of elbows and knuckles

data.description: A 45-year-old white man was found dead at home and underwent autopsy as the cause of death was not apparent. He had recently been under review by the respiratory team for poor respiratory function and patchy fibronodular lung changes. His medical history included osteomyelitis of the elbow, congenital kyphoscoliosis, and testicular seminoma, which had been treated with orchidectomy and chemotherapy. At postmortem examination, the abdominal cavity contained copious pus covering the serosal aspect of the small bowel. There was an obvious perforation at the level of the mid-ileum, as well as three ulcers on the mucosal aspect of the ileum, one of which had perforated. Widespread pale nodules measuring up to 5 mm each were noted throughout the parenchyma of both lungs and a small pale lesion was present in the left kidney. No abnormalities were seen in the cardiovascular, endocrine, or central nervous systems.

Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection involving multiple organs. This is the leading possibility given the apparent necrotizing granulomas and acid-fast bacilli in the supplied histology; species confirmation would require molecular testing or culture.
symptoms_in_common: Poor respiratory function and patchy fibronodular lung changes
Widespread small nodules in both lungs
Ileal ulcers with perforation and purulent peritonitis
Small renal lesion compatible with disseminated infection
Apparent necrotizing granulomas with multinucleated giant cells
Numerous apparent acid-fast bacilli on the special stain
Previous osteomyelitis, potentially representing another site of infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Congenital kyphoscoliosis is not explained by tuberculosis
Previous testicular seminoma is a separate condition

data.description: An opportunistic nontuberculous mycobacterial infection that can affect the lungs, gastrointestinal tract, and other organs, particularly in patients with substantial immunosuppression.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary dysfunction and nodular lung abnormalities
Multiorgan lesions involving the bowel, lungs, and kidney
Previous chemotherapy, if associated with persistent immunosuppression
symptoms_not_in_common: Well-formed necrotizing granulomas are less characteristic in severely immunocompromised patients with disseminated infection
Discrete ileal ulcers causing perforation are an uncommon presentation
Congenital kyphoscoliosis is unrelated

data.description: A nontuberculous mycobacterial infection that commonly resembles pulmonary tuberculosis and can occasionally disseminate, especially in immunocompromised patients.
symptoms_in_common: Poor respiratory function with fibronodular lung changes
Previous osteomyelitis, which can occur in extrapulmonary infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Ileal ulceration and perforation are very unusual manifestations
Renal involvement is uncommon
Congenital kyphoscoliosis is not explained

data.description: A systemic fungal infection that can produce pulmonary nodules, granulomatous inflammation, and gastrointestinal ulceration, especially in immunocompromised patients.
symptoms_in_common: Respiratory impairment and widespread pulmonary nodules
Previous chemotherapy as a possible predisposing factor
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent acid-fast bacilli favor mycobacterial infection rather than histoplasmosis
No characteristic intracellular yeast forms are evident in the supplied images
Congenital kyphoscoliosis is unrelated

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease causing transmural intestinal inflammation, sometimes with granulomas, deep ulcers, and perforation. It is a substantially weaker explanation for the complete case.
symptoms_in_common: Granulomatous inflammation in the bowel wall
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent acid-fast bacilli are not a feature of Crohn disease
Necrotizing granulomas favor infection rather than Crohn disease
Widespread pulmonary nodules and a focal renal lesion are not a typical accompanying pattern
Previous osteomyelitis is not directly explained

data.diagnosis: Disseminated (miliary) tuberculosis with intestinal tuberculosis and ileal perforation
data.description: Hematogenous and/or swallowed-sputum spread of Mycobacterium tuberculosis producing necrotizing granulomas in multiple organs; ileal involvement causes ulcers that may perforate and cause fatal peritonitis.
symptoms_in_common: Ileal ulcers with perforation and purulent peritonitis
Widespread pale lung nodules up to 5 mm (miliary pattern)
Prior patchy fibronodular lung changes and poor respiratory function
Granulomas with Langhans-type giant cells in the bowel wall
Numerous acid-fast bacilli on Ziehl-Neelsen stain
Prior chemotherapy as a possible cause of immunosuppression
History of osteomyelitis and kyphoscoliosis (possibly earlier skeletal tuberculosis)
symptoms_not_in_common: Free perforation is uncommon in intestinal tuberculosis, which more often causes strictures
Mid-ileal rather than the classic ileocecal location
No documented constitutional symptoms such as fever, night sweats or weight loss
Kyphoscoliosis described as congenital

data.diagnosis: Disseminated nontuberculous mycobacterial infection (e.g., Mycobacterium avium complex)
data.description: Systemic infection by environmental mycobacteria, usually in immunocompromised hosts, involving lungs, gut, lymph nodes and other organs, with abundant acid-fast bacilli in tissue.
symptoms_in_common: Structural chest abnormality (kyphoscoliosis) predisposing to NTM lung disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Well-formed necrotizing granulomas with Langhans giant cells are more typical of M. tuberculosis
Intestinal ulceration with perforation is rare in NTM infection
Miliary pattern of lung nodules is unusual
No known HIV infection or profound immunodeficiency
No sheets of foamy histiocytes described

data.description: Chronic idiopathic transmural granulomatous inflammatory bowel disease, most often affecting the ileum, with ulcers, fistulae and occasionally perforation.
symptoms_in_common: Transmural inflammation with granulomas and giant cells in the bowel wall
symptoms_not_in_common: Acid-fast bacilli present in tissue
Necrotizing (caseating) granulomas
Widespread miliary lung nodules
Kidney lesion
No history of chronic diarrhea or abdominal pain

data.description: Germ cell tumor of the testis that can relapse with metastases to retroperitoneal nodes, lungs and other organs; it may be accompanied by a sarcoid-like granulomatous reaction.
symptoms_in_common: History of testicular seminoma treated with orchidectomy and chemotherapy
symptoms_not_in_common: No tumor cells seen on histology
Acid-fast bacilli demonstrated
Necrotizing granulomas in the lung
Ileal ulcers with perforation are not typical of seminoma spread
Uniform nodules of 5 mm or less are atypical for metastases

data.description: Systemic granulomatous fungal infection that can mimic tuberculosis, with lung nodules, gastrointestinal ulceration (often ileal) and involvement of other organs, particularly in immunocompromised patients.
symptoms_in_common: Miliary-type lung nodules and fibronodular lung changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Organisms are acid-fast bacilli rather than yeast forms
No fungal elements described
No travel or exposure history to an endemic area
No adrenal, liver, spleen or marrow involvement described

data.description: 28-year-old woman with no significant medical history presented with fatigue and migratory joint pain. Symptoms began with several days of pain and swelling in the right foot and ankle causing difficulty walking, then resolved and were followed by pain in the knees and hips with right elbow pain. She reported intermittent low-grade fevers. On initial exam she was febrile (38.3°C) with diffuse joint tenderness, tachycardia, no joint swelling or erythema, normal range of motion, and no chest infiltrate on radiograph. Five days later she returned with progressive shortness of breath worse when supine and persistent right knee pain and stiffness. Repeat exam showed mild fever, tachycardia, elevated jugular venous pressure, bilateral lung crackles, a holosystolic murmur at the apex radiating to the axilla, and a warm left knee with limited range of motion and severe pain on flexion. She was born in Brazil, moved to the northeastern United States 10 years earlier, and recalled childhood exertional shortness of breath.

data.diagnosis: Acute rheumatic fever with carditis, possibly recurrent on underlying rheumatic heart disease
data.description: An immune-mediated complication of group A streptococcal infection causing migratory arthritis and cardiac inflammation. The echocardiographic mitral valve abnormalities and regurgitant jet suggest rheumatic mitral disease, although confirmation requires additional testing.
symptoms_in_common: Migratory pain involving the ankles, knees, hips, and elbow
Transient joint swelling followed by improvement and involvement of other joints
Apical holosystolic murmur radiating to the axilla, consistent with mitral regurgitation
Orthopnea, elevated jugular venous pressure, and bilateral crackles suggesting heart failure
Childhood exertional shortness of breath suggesting possible preexisting rheumatic valve disease
symptoms_not_in_common: First recognized presentation at age 28 is less typical than presentation during childhood or adolescence

data.diagnosis: Infective endocarditis involving the mitral valve
data.description: Infection of a cardiac valve that can cause fever, immune-mediated joint symptoms, valve destruction, and acute heart failure. Preexisting mitral valve disease would increase susceptibility; the supplied images alone do not establish vegetation.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive shortness of breath and orthopnea
Elevated jugular venous pressure and lung crackles
symptoms_not_in_common: Rapidly resolving, sequential migratory large-joint inflammation is more characteristic of acute rheumatic fever
Childhood exertional shortness of breath is not explained by a newly acquired infection

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with cardiac involvement
data.description: A systemic autoimmune disease that can cause inflammatory arthritis, fever, and cardiac disease, including myocarditis or noninfectious valvular lesions such as Libman-Sacks endocarditis.
symptoms_in_common: Young woman with fatigue and fever
Initially preserved joint range of motion without obvious swelling
Heart failure findings if significant cardiac involvement is present
symptoms_not_in_common: Sequential, transient inflammation predominantly affecting large joints is less typical than symmetric peripheral arthritis
A severely painful, warm knee with restricted motion is less typical of uncomplicated lupus arthritis
Childhood exertional dyspnea is not readily explained by a new lupus presentation

data.description: Inflammatory arthritis following streptococcal infection that does not meet criteria for acute rheumatic fever. Joint symptoms are usually more persistent and less migratory; clinically significant carditis is uncommon.
symptoms_in_common: Warm, painful knee with limited range of motion
symptoms_not_in_common: Clearly migratory arthritis with spontaneous resolution in previously affected joints
Prominent mitral regurgitation murmur
Orthopnea, elevated jugular venous pressure, and bilateral crackles indicating substantial cardiac involvement
Childhood exertional shortness of breath

data.diagnosis: Disseminated gonococcal infection with gonococcal arthritis
data.description: Disseminated Neisseria gonorrhoeae infection can cause fever, migratory polyarthralgia, and subsequent septic arthritis. Endocarditis is a rare complication that could produce valvular dysfunction and heart failure.
symptoms_in_common: Subsequent warm, severely painful knee with restricted motion
Valvular murmur and heart failure findings if rare gonococcal endocarditis is present
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked cardiac congestion is unusual in uncomplicated disseminated gonococcal infection
Childhood exertional shortness of breath cannot be explained by a recent disseminated infection

data.diagnosis: Acute rheumatic fever with carditis (recurrence on chronic rheumatic heart disease)
data.description: Autoimmune inflammatory sequela of group A streptococcal pharyngitis causing migratory polyarthritis, pancarditis/valvulitis (classically mitral), fever, and other Jones criteria manifestations; common in endemic regions such as Brazil, with recurrences in adults who have prior rheumatic valve damage.
symptoms_in_common: Migratory polyarthritis of large joints (ankle, knees, hips, elbow)
New holosystolic apical murmur radiating to axilla (mitral regurgitation)
Heart failure signs (orthopnea, elevated JVP, crackles)
Echocardiogram showing thickened mitral valve with severe mitral regurgitation and elevated transmitral diastolic velocities suggesting a mixed rheumatic lesion
Childhood exertional dyspnea suggesting earlier rheumatic heart disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported preceding sore throat
No erythema marginatum, subcutaneous nodules or chorea
Adult age at presentation (first episodes typically occur in childhood)
Persistent knee arthritis rather than purely fleeting

data.description: Microbial infection of the cardiac valves, often on previously damaged valves, causing fever, new regurgitant murmurs, heart failure, and embolic or immune-mediated phenomena including arthralgia or septic arthritis.
symptoms_in_common: Acute heart failure (orthopnea, elevated JVP, crackles)
Arthralgias and a warm painful knee (possible septic or immune-mediated arthritis)
Probable underlying rheumatic valve disease as a predisposing substrate
symptoms_not_in_common: Truly migratory polyarthritis with complete resolution in earlier joints
No discrete vegetation evident on echocardiography
No peripheral stigmata (petechiae, Osler nodes, Janeway lesions, splinter hemorrhages)
No known risk factors such as injection drug use, recent dental procedure or prosthetic valve

data.diagnosis: Systemic lupus erythematosus with Libman-Sacks endocarditis
data.description: Multisystem autoimmune disease predominantly affecting young women, causing arthritis, fever, fatigue, serositis and sterile valvular vegetations or valvulitis that can lead to mitral regurgitation.
symptoms_not_in_common: Arthritis mainly of large joints rather than symmetric small joints of the hands
No rash, photosensitivity, oral ulcers, serositis, renal or hematologic involvement described
Acute severe mitral regurgitation with heart failure is uncommon in lupus
Childhood exertional dyspnea and Brazilian origin point more toward rheumatic disease

data.description: Hematogenous spread of Neisseria gonorrhoeae causing migratory polyarthralgia, tenosynovitis, dermatitis, or purulent monoarthritis, and rarely endocarditis, in young sexually active adults.
symptoms_in_common: Later warm, painful knee with limited motion (possible purulent arthritis)
Rare gonococcal endocarditis could cause valvular regurgitation
symptoms_not_in_common: No pustular or vesicular skin lesions
No tenosynovitis
No genitourinary symptoms or exposure history reported
Severe mitral regurgitation with heart failure is very rare (and gonococcal endocarditis favors the aortic valve)
Childhood exertional dyspnea not explained

data.diagnosis: Lyme disease with arthritis and carditis
data.description: Tick-borne Borrelia burgdorferi infection endemic to the northeastern United States, causing erythema migrans, migratory arthralgias, large-joint (especially knee) arthritis and carditis, typically presenting as atrioventricular block.
symptoms_not_in_common: No recalled tick bite or erythema migrans
Lyme carditis causes conduction block or myocarditis, not severe mitral regurgitation or valvulitis
Lyme knee arthritis usually has large effusions with relatively little pain, unlike the severe pain here
Arthritis and carditis occur at different stages and rarely together
Childhood exertional dyspnea not explained

data.description: 70-year-old man with history of Gleason 9 (4+5) adenocarcinoma treated with radical prostatectomy 10 years ago. Presented to primary care with rectal pain persisting for several weeks. Patient had lost 20 lbs over 3-4 weeks and complained of progressive fatigue, poor appetite, severe tenesmus, and rectal pain. Patient had been living independently on West Coast but relocated to East Coast to be closer to adult children.

data.diagnosis: Recurrent prostate adenocarcinoma with rectal invasion and distant metastases
data.description: Recurrence of previously treated prostate cancer can form a prostate-bed mass, invade the rectum, and spread to distant organs. The images suggest a pelvic mass, pulmonary nodules, and a liver lesion concerning for metastatic disease; tissue confirmation is needed.
symptoms_in_common: Severe tenesmus from possible rectal invasion or compression
History of high-grade Gleason 9 prostate adenocarcinoma
Apparent pelvic mass near the prostatectomy bed
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly rectal symptoms are less typical than urinary or skeletal symptoms
Apparent prominent lung and liver involvement is less typical than bone or lymph-node metastases

data.description: An aggressive prostate cancer variant that can arise de novo or through transformation of adenocarcinoma. It may produce bulky pelvic disease and visceral metastases, sometimes without a proportionate PSA elevation; biopsy is required to distinguish it from conventional adenocarcinoma.
symptoms_in_common: Rectal pain and severe tenesmus associated with a pelvic mass
Pulmonary nodules and a liver lesion concerning for visceral metastases
symptoms_not_in_common: Rectal pain and tenesmus as the dominant presentation are less typical
A ten-year interval after prostatectomy is less characteristic of rapidly progressive neuroendocrine disease, although it does not exclude it

data.diagnosis: Rectal adenocarcinoma with liver and lung metastases
data.description: A malignant tumor of the rectal lining that can cause local pain and tenesmus and commonly spreads to the liver and lungs. The pelvic abnormality could represent a rectal primary rather than recurrent prostate cancer.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent pelvic mass involving or adjacent to the rectum
Liver lesion and pulmonary nodules concerning for metastases
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported symptom is clearly incompatible with this diagnosis
The prior high-grade prostate cancer provides a competing explanation for the pelvic mass

data.diagnosis: Anal squamous cell carcinoma with distant metastases
data.description: Cancer arising from the squamous lining of the anal canal can produce persistent anorectal pain and tenesmus. Advanced disease can invade adjacent pelvic tissues and spread to the liver or lungs.
symptoms_in_common: Possible pelvic malignancy with distant lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: An apparent mass centered higher in the pelvis near the prostatectomy bed is less typical of an anal primary
The apparent distant disease burden is less typical of an initial localized anal cancer presentation

data.diagnosis: Extranodal lymphoma involving the rectum or pelvic tissues
data.description: Lymphoma can occasionally involve the rectum or adjacent pelvic tissues, producing a bulky mass and constitutional symptoms. Disseminated disease may also involve the liver and lungs.
symptoms_in_common: Rectal pain and tenesmus from pelvic or rectal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe focal rectal pain and tenesmus are uncommon presenting symptoms of lymphoma
Discrete rounded pulmonary nodules are less characteristic than the metastatic pattern of a solid tumor

data.diagnosis: Recurrent metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma (including possible neuroendocrine/small cell transformation)
data.description: Late local recurrence of high-grade prostate cancer in the prostatectomy bed with visceral metastases; aggressive variants (small cell/neuroendocrine dedifferentiation) often spread to liver and lung, sometimes with low PSA.

Rectal pain and severe tenesmus from local invasion/compression
Rapid weight loss, fatigue, poor appetite
symptoms_not_in_common: 10-year disease-free interval
Visceral (lung/liver) metastases without evident bone metastases is atypical for conventional prostate adenocarcinoma
Large hypodense necrotic-appearing liver lesion is uncommon

data.diagnosis: Primary rectal (colorectal) adenocarcinoma with liver and lung metastases
data.description: Malignancy of the rectal mucosa that commonly metastasizes hematogenously to the liver and lungs.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported rectal bleeding or change in stool caliber
Mass appears centered in the prostatectomy bed/perirectal tissue rather than clearly arising from the rectal wall
Very rapid weight loss over only 3-4 weeks

data.diagnosis: Pelvic sarcoma (e.g., post-treatment or de novo soft tissue sarcoma) with metastases
data.description: Malignant mesenchymal tumor of the pelvis, which may arise de novo or after pelvic radiation, with hematogenous spread mainly to the lungs and sometimes the liver.
symptoms_in_common: Rectal pain and tenesmus from mass effect
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented history of pelvic radiation
Rare tumor
Recurrence of the known prostate cancer is more likely in the surgical bed

data.diagnosis: Lymphoma (e.g., diffuse large B-cell lymphoma) involving pelvis, liver and lung
data.description: Aggressive lymphoid malignancy that can present with extranodal masses in multiple organs and constitutional symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic soft tissue mass causing rectal symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fevers or night sweats
No prominent lymphadenopathy or splenomegaly described
Mass located in the prostatectomy bed
Prior high-grade prostate cancer offers a more direct explanation

data.diagnosis: Pelvic/perirectal abscess with pyogenic liver abscess and septic pulmonary emboli
data.description: Deep pelvic infection with hematogenous seeding via the portal and systemic venous circulation, producing a hypodense liver collection and lung nodules.
symptoms_in_common: Hypodense liver lesion that could represent an abscess
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, chills or sepsis reported
Lung nodules are solid and well-circumscribed without cavitation
Subacute course of several weeks with marked weight loss favors malignancy
No recent surgery or instrumentation

data.description: 46-year-old woman who experienced chest pain before having an out-of-hospital cardiac arrest. Pre-arrest rhythm strip showed sinus tachycardia. Initial troponin I was 5.9 μg/L (normal: 0-0.04 μg/L). Medical history included similar chest pain episode one year prior after taking sumatriptan for migraine, with transient inferior and lateral ST elevation on ECG but negative troponin at that time. Previous coronary angiography showed normal left coronary system and dominant right coronary artery with minor ostial spasm and slow flow. Negative bubble study for right to left shunting. Current medications: oral diltiazem, nicorandil, lansoprazole, and beclometasone inhaler. Patient was a former smoker.

data.diagnosis: Coronary vasospasm causing acute myocardial infarction and cardiac arrest
data.description: Transient severe coronary artery constriction can cause myocardial ischemia, infarction, and fatal arrhythmias despite previously normal coronary arteries. This is the leading possibility given the prior sumatriptan-associated episode and documented spasm.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated troponin I indicating myocardial injury
ECG showing prominent anterior precordial ST elevation
Previous chest pain with transient ST elevation after sumatriptan
Previously normal coronary arteries with minor right coronary ostial spasm and slow flow
symptoms_not_in_common: No major discordant findings; cardiac arrest and substantial troponin elevation indicate a severe episode rather than uncomplicated transient vasospastic angina

data.diagnosis: Acute anterior ST-elevation myocardial infarction from coronary thrombosis
data.description: Acute coronary artery occlusion, typically from plaque rupture or erosion with thrombosis, causes myocardial necrosis and can precipitate cardiac arrest. The ECG pattern requires urgent consideration of an anterior infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Marked anterior precordial ST elevation on the supplied ECG
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous angiography showed no significant obstructive coronary disease
Prior transient ST elevation after sumatriptan with negative troponin is more suggestive of reversible vasospasm
Previously documented ostial spasm and slow flow suggest an alternative ischemic mechanism

data.description: A spontaneous tear or intramural hematoma in a coronary artery can obstruct blood flow and cause acute myocardial infarction, particularly in middle-aged women without established coronary atherosclerosis.
symptoms_in_common: Acute chest pain followed by cardiac arrest
Anterior ST elevation on the supplied ECG
symptoms_not_in_common: Prior sumatriptan-associated transient ischemia is more characteristic of coronary vasospasm
Previous angiography described spasm and slow flow rather than dissection

data.description: An acute, usually reversible stress-related ventricular dysfunction that can mimic myocardial infarction with chest pain, ST elevation, and troponin release despite unobstructed coronary arteries.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac arrest can occur in severe cases
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent sumatriptan-associated chest pain and documented coronary spasm favor a vasospastic mechanism
No preceding emotional or physical trigger is described, although one is not required
The characteristic ventricular wall-motion pattern is not provided

data.description: Inflammation of the heart muscle can produce myocardial injury, ST-segment abnormalities, ventricular arrhythmias, and cardiac arrest without obstructive coronary disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prior drug-associated transient ST elevation with negative troponin is more suggestive of vasospasm
Documented coronary ostial spasm is not a typical feature of myocarditis
No infectious prodrome, fever, or systemic inflammatory symptoms are reported

data.diagnosis: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) of the left anterior descending artery
data.description: Non-atherosclerotic separation of the coronary arterial wall with intramural haematoma causing luminal obstruction and acute myocardial infarction, typically in young to middle-aged women with few conventional risk factors; can present with ventricular arrhythmia and cardiac arrest.
symptoms_in_common: Acute chest pain preceding cardiac arrest
Marked anterior ST elevation (V1-V5) on ECG
Previously normal coronary arteries without atherosclerosis
History of migraine (associated with SCAD and fibromuscular dysplasia)
Recurrent chest pain event despite vasodilator therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: Previous episode triggered by sumatriptan with transient ST elevation and negative troponin (more suggestive of spasm)
Previously documented coronary ostial spasm and slow flow
Previous ST elevation was in the inferior and lateral territory rather than anterior
Pre-arrest rhythm was sinus tachycardia rather than a documented ventricular arrhythmia

data.diagnosis: Coronary artery vasospasm (Prinzmetal/variant angina) with myocardial infarction
data.description: Transient intense constriction of an epicardial coronary artery causing transmural ischaemia with ST elevation; prolonged spasm can cause infarction, ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. Associated with smoking, migraine and vasoconstrictor drugs such as triptans.
symptoms_in_common: Prior episode after sumatriptan with transient ST elevation
Documented coronary ostial spasm and slow flow on previous angiography
Already on diltiazem and nicorandil for presumed vasospasm
symptoms_not_in_common: Event occurred despite calcium channel blocker and nicorandil therapy
Markedly elevated troponin (previous episode was troponin negative)
ST elevation now in the anterior territory, whereas earlier spasm involved the right coronary artery/inferolateral leads
No recent triptan trigger reported

data.diagnosis: Atherosclerotic plaque rupture with acute anterior STEMI (LAD thrombotic occlusion)
data.description: Rupture or erosion of an atherosclerotic plaque with superimposed thrombus occluding the left anterior descending artery, causing transmural anterior infarction that may be complicated by ventricular fibrillation and cardiac arrest.
symptoms_not_in_common: Relatively young premenopausal-age woman
Normal left coronary system on angiography one year earlier
History points to vasospastic rather than atherosclerotic disease
Few conventional cardiovascular risk factors reported
Previous transient ST elevation with negative troponin

data.description: Acute, reversible left ventricular dysfunction, usually with apical ballooning, typically in women after emotional or physical stress; mimics anterior STEMI with ST elevation and troponin rise in the absence of culprit coronary obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Can be complicated by arrhythmia and cardiac arrest
symptoms_not_in_common: Younger than typical postmenopausal patient
No clear emotional or physical stressor reported
Very marked ST elevation in V1-V4, more typical of acute LAD occlusion
Prior documented coronary spasm and triptan-triggered episode
Cardiac arrest as presenting feature is uncommon

data.diagnosis: Coronary embolism or in-situ thrombosis (MINOCA mechanism)
data.description: Occlusion of a coronary artery by an embolus (from atrial fibrillation, left heart thrombus, valve disease or paradoxical embolism) or by thrombosis in a hypercoagulable state, producing acute infarction in otherwise normal coronary arteries.
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative bubble study makes paradoxical embolism unlikely
No atrial fibrillation documented (sinus tachycardia pre-arrest)
No known valve disease, intracardiac thrombus or thrombophilia
Prior episode with transient ST elevation and documented spasm suggests a vasomotor cause

data.description: A 68-year-old woman with a longstanding history of non-specific inflammatory arthritis presented with a three-month history of flashing lights and blurred vision. She had been taking 400 mg hydroxychloroquine daily for 15 years, along with meloxicam, omeprazole, and amitriptyline. She was of normal body weight. Ophthalmological assessment revealed reduced visual acuity at 6/18 in the right eye and 6/12 in the left eye, with mild depression in color vision on Ishihara plate testing. Early cataracts were present.

Toxic damage to photoreceptors and retinal pigment epithelium from hydroxychloroquine, typically affecting the parafoveal retina. This is the leading diagnosis given prolonged exposure and bilateral ring-shaped visual field defects with central sparing.
symptoms_in_common: Hydroxychloroquine use at 400 mg daily for 15 years
Bilateral blurred vision and reduced visual acuity
Bilateral annular paracentral scotomas on visual field testing
Parafoveal pigment epithelial abnormalities with relative foveal sparing on the supplied images
symptoms_not_in_common: Early cataracts are a separate finding rather than a characteristic manifestation of retinal toxicity
Inflammatory arthritis is the treatment indication rather than a manifestation of toxic retinopathy

data.description: An inherited retinal degeneration affecting cones, sometimes followed by rods, causing central visual impairment, color discrimination loss, and occasionally a bull's-eye pattern of macular damage.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral macular abnormalities with relative central sparing
symptoms_not_in_common: New symptomatic onset at age 68 is less typical
The substantial hydroxychloroquine exposure favors an acquired toxic cause
Flashing lights are less characteristic than progressive central visual loss

data.description: An immune-mediated retinal disorder, sometimes associated with malignancy, that can cause photopsias, visual field loss, and impaired retinal function despite initially subtle fundus changes.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute bilateral blurred vision over three months
symptoms_not_in_common: The relatively symmetric parafoveal ring defects and central sparing are more suggestive of hydroxychloroquine toxicity
Long-term hydroxychloroquine exposure provides a stronger alternative explanation
Early cataracts do not explain immune-mediated retinal dysfunction

data.description: An age-associated degeneration of the macula that causes central visual impairment through drusen, pigment epithelial atrophy, or abnormal blood vessel growth.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symmetric annular paracentral scotomas with central sparing are not typical
Flashing lights are not a usual presenting symptom
The supplied images do not show convincing characteristic drusen, hemorrhage, or exudation
Prolonged hydroxychloroquine exposure favors toxic maculopathy

data.description: Opacification of the crystalline lens that can contribute to blurred vision, reduced acuity, and altered color perception, but does not explain the retinal imaging and localized visual field abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: Flashing lights are not typical of uncomplicated cataracts
Bilateral annular paracentral scotomas are not explained by cataracts
Parafoveal pigment epithelial changes on retinal imaging are not caused by cataracts

data.description: Toxic maculopathy from long-term hydroxychloroquine use, causing parafoveal retinal pigment epithelium and photoreceptor damage with a bull's eye pattern and paracentral ring scotomas.
symptoms_in_common: 15 years of hydroxychloroquine 400 mg daily (high cumulative dose)
Bilateral symmetric parafoveal pigmentary change on fundus photographs
Annular perifoveal hyperfluorescence (window defect) on fluorescein angiography
Bilateral paracentral ring scotomas on central 10-degree visual fields
symptoms_not_in_common: Early cataracts (age-related, not caused by the drug)
Normal body weight makes overdosing per kg less obvious, though the dose may still exceed 5 mg/kg real body weight

data.description: Degenerative disease of the macula in older adults with drusen, retinal pigment epithelium changes and atrophy leading to central vision loss.
symptoms_not_in_common: Highly symmetric bull's eye pattern with foveal sparing
Ring scotomas in both eyes
No prominent drusen described
Long-term hydroxychloroquine exposure offers a better explanation
Flashing lights less typical

data.description: Inherited photoreceptor dystrophy primarily affecting cones, causing progressive central vision loss, colour vision defects and often a bull's eye maculopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral symmetric bull's eye macular appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: Late onset at 68 years
Only three months of symptoms
No family history reported
No photophobia or nystagmus
Colour vision only mildly affected
Hydroxychloroquine exposure is a more likely cause

data.description: ABCA4-related inherited macular dystrophy with lipofuscin accumulation, which can produce bull's eye maculopathy and central vision loss, occasionally presenting late in life.
symptoms_in_common: Foveal sparing can occur in late-onset forms
symptoms_not_in_common: Usual onset in childhood or young adulthood
No pisciform yellow flecks described
No dark choroid on angiography (choroidal fluorescence visible)
Flashing lights not typical
No family history reported

data.description: Lens opacification causing gradual painless blurring of vision, glare and reduced contrast and colour perception.
symptoms_not_in_common: Flashing lights
Ring scotomas on visual fields
Bull's eye macular changes on fundus and angiography
Early cataract unlikely to account for this degree of visual loss

data.description: 51-year-old man undergoing venesection for haemochromatosis. During procedure, experienced sudden gurgling sensation up his arm, followed by severe central crushing chest pain with radiation to jaw and left arm, severe dyspnoea, and left sided hemiparesis and dysphasia. On arrival to hospital: hypoxic (oxygen saturation 88% on room air), left hemiplegia (resolved within 15 minutes). Initial ECG showed T-wave inversion inferiorly. Troponin I was raised at 0.14 μg/L (ref 0-0.08 μg/L). Transthoracic echocardiography with bubble study showed right-to-left shunting during normal respiration and Valsalva. Baseline right heart pressures were normal. Transoesophageal echocardiogram confirmed patent foramen ovale with passage of bubbles.

data.diagnosis: Paradoxical systemic air embolism through a patent foramen ovale
data.description: Air introduced into a peripheral vein crosses a patent foramen ovale into the arterial circulation, potentially causing simultaneous cerebral and coronary ischemia. This is the leading explanation for the abrupt procedural onset and confirmed right-to-left shunt.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden gurgling sensation in the arm during venesection
Immediate severe chest pain radiating to the jaw and left arm
Severe dyspnoea and oxygen saturation of 88%
Inferior T-wave inversion and elevated troponin
Confirmed patent foramen ovale with right-to-left bubble passage despite normal baseline right heart pressures

data.diagnosis: Venous air embolism involving the pulmonary circulation
data.description: Air entering the venous circulation can obstruct pulmonary blood flow and cause acute hypoxaemia and cardiovascular compromise. An isolated venous air embolism would not fully explain this patient's focal neurological deficits without additional systemic passage.
symptoms_in_common: Gurgling sensation in the instrumented arm
symptoms_not_in_common: Transient focal hemiplegia and dysphasia are not explained by an isolated pulmonary air embolism
Jaw and left-arm radiation is more suggestive of coronary ischemia
Patent foramen ovale with right-to-left shunting suggests an additional paradoxical embolic mechanism

data.diagnosis: Acute pulmonary thromboembolism with paradoxical systemic thromboembolism
data.description: A venous blood clot obstructs pulmonary arteries, while clot crossing a patent foramen ovale may cause cerebral or coronary embolism. This can produce respiratory symptoms together with focal neurological deficits.
symptoms_in_common: Patent foramen ovale with right-to-left shunting
symptoms_not_in_common: Gurgling sensation during venesection favors air rather than thrombus
Immediate association with venesection is not typical of spontaneous thromboembolism
Crushing chest pain radiating to the jaw and arm is less typical than pleuritic pulmonary embolism pain

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome with concurrent transient cerebral ischemia
data.description: Acute myocardial ischemia, including a possible non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction, can cause crushing chest pain, ischemic ECG changes, and elevated troponin. A separate cerebral ischemic event would be needed to explain the focal neurological findings.
symptoms_in_common: Pain radiating to the jaw and left arm
symptoms_not_in_common: Gurgling sensation in the arm immediately before symptoms
Transient hemiplegia and dysphasia are not typical of uncomplicated acute coronary syndrome
Marked hypoxaemia without reported pulmonary oedema
Confirmed right-to-left shunt is not explained by coronary atherosclerosis

data.diagnosis: Acute aortic dissection with coronary and cerebral malperfusion
data.description: A tear in the aortic wall can compromise coronary and cerebral arteries, causing abrupt chest pain, myocardial injury, and focal neurological deficits. It is an important alternative emergency diagnosis, although the procedural air-entry history favors embolism.
symptoms_not_in_common: Gurgling sensation in the arm during venesection
Crushing pain with jaw and left-arm radiation rather than characteristic tearing chest or back pain
Rapid complete resolution of hemiplegia is less typical of sustained cerebral malperfusion
Patent foramen ovale with right-to-left bubble passage is not explained by aortic dissection

data.diagnosis: Paradoxical air embolism through patent foramen ovale (iatrogenic venous air embolism during venesection)
data.description: Air entering the venous system during a venous procedure travels to the right heart and pulmonary arteries, and crosses a patent foramen ovale into the systemic circulation, causing coronary and cerebral arterial air emboli.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden gurgling sensation up the arm
Severe central crushing chest pain radiating to jaw and left arm
Left hemiparesis and dysphasia that resolved within 15 minutes
Inferior T-wave inversion (right coronary territory, typical for air)
Patent foramen ovale with right-to-left shunting on bubble study and transoesophageal echo
CT pulmonary angiogram appears to show a small low-density (air-like) filling defect in a left pulmonary artery branch
