symptoms_not_in_common: Normal baseline right heart pressures (shunt occurred without pulmonary hypertension)
Dysphasia with left-sided weakness is an unusual lateralisation unless the right hemisphere is dominant or emboli were bilateral

data.diagnosis: Acute pulmonary thromboembolism with paradoxical thrombotic embolism
data.description: Venous thrombus embolises to the pulmonary arteries causing dyspnoea and hypoxia, with part crossing a patent foramen ovale to cause stroke or coronary embolism.
symptoms_in_common: Filling defect in a pulmonary artery branch on CT
Patent foramen ovale with right-to-left shunt
symptoms_not_in_common: Gurgling sensation up the arm during venesection
Normal right heart pressures
Neurological deficit resolved within 15 minutes
No reported deep vein thrombosis or thrombotic risk factors
Crushing pain radiating to jaw and arm is more ischaemic than pleuritic

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome (non-ST elevation myocardial infarction from atherosclerotic plaque rupture)
data.description: Myocardial ischaemia and necrosis caused by atherosclerotic plaque rupture with coronary thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: Central crushing chest pain radiating to jaw and left arm
symptoms_not_in_common: Gurgling sensation up the arm
Abrupt onset during venesection
Left hemiparesis and dysphasia
Marked hypoxia without evidence of heart failure
Pulmonary artery filling defect on CT
Right-to-left shunt through patent foramen ovale as a more direct explanation

data.diagnosis: Acute ischaemic stroke or transient ischaemic attack (cardioembolic or cryptogenic, associated with patent foramen ovale)
data.description: Transient or permanent focal cerebral ischaemia from arterial occlusion, which may be due to thrombus crossing a patent foramen ovale or arising from the heart.
symptoms_in_common: Resolution within 15 minutes (consistent with a transient ischaemic attack)
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe crushing chest pain radiating to jaw and arm
Severe dyspnoea and hypoxia
Raised troponin and inferior T-wave inversion
Gurgling sensation up the arm
Pulmonary artery filling defect on CT

data.description: A tear in the aortic intima creates a false lumen that can compromise coronary and carotid branch vessels, causing chest pain with myocardial ischaemia and neurological deficits.
symptoms_in_common: Inferior ECG changes and raised troponin (right coronary involvement possible)
symptoms_not_in_common: Gurgling sensation up the arm during venesection
No dissection flap seen on contrast CT of the chest
Pain crushing rather than tearing or radiating to the back
Marked hypoxia
Rapid full resolution of neurological deficit
Right-to-left shunt through patent foramen ovale provides a better explanation

data.description: A 62-year-old fit and well Romanian man presented with a two-week history of worsening acute localized pain in the upper abdomen and vomiting. His surgical history included an open appendectomy as a child and laparoscopic cholecystectomy 20 years ago. On presentation, he had fever (39°C) and tachycardia (104 beats/min), with blood pressure of 125/73 mm Hg. Physical examination revealed generalized abdominal tenderness, worse in the right upper quadrant, with localized guarding in the right upper quadrant. Blood tests showed a raised white cell count of 16 × 10⁹/L (reference range 4-10 × 10⁹/L) and a C reactive protein concentration of 277 mg/L (reference value <9 mg/L). A frontal projection erect chest radiograph was initially reported as showing pneumoperitoneum, but showed a normal bowel gas pattern under the left hemidiaphragm.

A bacterial collection within the liver that can contain gas. The CT images show a large gas-and-fluid collection along the right hepatic margin, making a hepatic or subcapsular abscess a leading possibility; precise localization requires full CT review.
symptoms_in_common: Right upper quadrant tenderness and guarding
Leukocytosis and markedly elevated C-reactive protein
Large gas-and-fluid collection adjacent to or within the right liver on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Generalized abdominal tenderness is less typical of an uncomplicated localized liver abscess and may indicate surrounding inflammation or leakage

data.description: An infected collection between the diaphragm and liver. Gas within this collection can resemble free intraperitoneal air on an erect chest radiograph.
symptoms_in_common: Fever, tachycardia, and elevated inflammatory markers
Right upper quadrant pain and localized guarding
Gas-and-fluid collection beneath the right hemidiaphragm
Apparent pneumoperitoneum on the initial chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: The CT collection appears closely associated with the hepatic capsule, potentially favoring a hepatic or subcapsular origin rather than a purely subphrenic location

data.description: A liver cyst caused by Echinococcus infection that becomes infected by bacteria, potentially producing an abscess with gas. Romanian origin provides an epidemiologic consideration but does not establish the diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Right upper quadrant pain and vomiting
Fever and tachycardia compatible with secondary infection
Leukocytosis and markedly elevated C-reactive protein
Large cystic gas-and-fluid collection associated with the liver
symptoms_not_in_common: Gas within the lesion is not typical of an uncomplicated hydatid cyst
The supplied images do not clearly demonstrate characteristic daughter cysts or detached membranes

data.diagnosis: Contained perforated peptic ulcer with secondary upper abdominal abscess
data.description: A gastric or duodenal ulcer can perforate and become locally contained, producing a gas-containing abscess rather than widespread free air.
symptoms_in_common: Localized guarding and generalized abdominal tenderness
Fever, tachycardia, leukocytosis, and elevated C-reactive protein
Two-week progression compatible with a developing contained abscess
symptoms_not_in_common: The supplied CT images show a localized collection along the liver rather than an obvious gastric or duodenal perforation
The apparent subdiaphragmatic air is contained within a collection rather than clearly representing free pneumoperitoneum

data.description: A collection of leaked bile beneath the liver capsule or around the liver that becomes infected. A biliary leak or obstruction would need confirmation; cholecystectomy 20 years earlier alone would not establish the cause.
symptoms_in_common: Right upper quadrant pain, tenderness, and guarding
Fever, tachycardia, and markedly elevated inflammatory markers
Large fluid collection along the hepatic margin
Gas within the collection compatible with secondary infection
symptoms_not_in_common: The onset 20 years after cholecystectomy is atypical for a postoperative biloma
A prominent gas component is not typical of a sterile biloma

data.description: A walled-off collection of infected fluid and gas between the right hemidiaphragm and the liver, often a late complication of abdominal surgery (e.g. dropped gallstones after laparoscopic cholecystectomy), a perforated viscus or hepatobiliary infection. Gas-forming organisms produce an air-fluid level that can mimic pneumoperitoneum on chest radiograph.
symptoms_in_common: Two-week subacute history of worsening upper abdominal pain
Right upper quadrant tenderness with localized guarding
Raised white cell count and markedly raised CRP
Gas under the right hemidiaphragm only, with normal bowel gas pattern under the left hemidiaphragm
CT showing a large encapsulated perihepatic collection with air-fluid level compressing the liver
symptoms_not_in_common: Surgery was 20 years ago (very long latency)
Generalized abdominal tenderness
No recent surgery, trauma or known intra-abdominal source

data.diagnosis: Infected hepatic hydatid cyst (Echinococcus granulosus) with superinfection or rupture
data.description: Parasitic cystic disease of the liver, endemic in Eastern Europe including Romania. Cysts may become secondarily infected with gas-forming bacteria or rupture into the subphrenic space, producing a large gas- and fluid-containing collection.
symptoms_in_common: Right upper quadrant pain and guarding
Fever, tachycardia, leukocytosis and raised CRP (superinfection)
Large well-defined fluid collection with air-fluid level in the hepatic/perihepatic region
symptoms_not_in_common: No daughter cysts, septations or wall calcification described
Collection appears perihepatic/subcapsular rather than intraparenchymal
No reported eosinophilia, jaundice or anaphylactic features
Generalized abdominal tenderness

data.diagnosis: Pyogenic liver abscess with gas-forming organisms
data.description: Bacterial infection of the liver (commonly Klebsiella, E. coli or anaerobes) forming a pus-filled cavity that may contain gas and may extend to or rupture into the subcapsular/perihepatic space.
symptoms_in_common: Right upper quadrant pain, tenderness and guarding
Gas- and fluid-containing collection in the liver region on CT
Previous biliary surgery as a possible predisposing factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Collection lies around the liver and displaces it rather than within parenchyma
Previously fit and well with no diabetes or known biliary disease
Very large gas component is unusual
No jaundice reported

data.diagnosis: Perforated hollow viscus (e.g. perforated peptic ulcer) with pneumoperitoneum or contained perforation
data.description: Full-thickness perforation of the stomach, duodenum or bowel releasing gas and contents into the peritoneal cavity, causing peritonitis; a sealed perforation can lead to a localized collection.
symptoms_in_common: Fever, tachycardia and raised inflammatory markers
Chest radiograph initially reported as showing free gas under the diaphragm
symptoms_not_in_common: Two-week subacute history rather than sudden onset
No board-like rigidity; guarding localized to the right upper quadrant
Hemodynamically stable blood pressure
Gas confined to an encapsulated right-sided collection with an air-fluid level rather than free gas
Normal appearance under the left hemidiaphragm
No history of ulcer disease or NSAID use

data.description: Interposition of a loop of colon between the liver and right hemidiaphragm, producing pseudopneumoperitoneum on chest radiograph; it can cause abdominal pain, vomiting and occasionally obstruction or volvulus.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent gas under the right hemidiaphragm mimicking pneumoperitoneum
symptoms_not_in_common: High fever of 39°C and tachycardia
Markedly raised white cell count and CRP
Localized guarding in the right upper quadrant
No haustral folds within the gas; CT shows an encapsulated collection with an air-fluid level rather than bowel

data.description: 29-year-old man with 6 weeks of unintentional 10 kg weight loss, severe upper abdominal pain radiating to the throat and worsened by eating, followed 3 weeks later by nausea, intermittent vomiting, decreased intake, one episode of hematemesis, sore throat, and fever. History included a respiratory illness about 2 years earlier and chronic macular hyperpigmentation of the feet and legs for 10 years. On exam he was cachectic, febrile to 38.3°C, tachycardic, and had a BMI of 18.6; abdomen was initially soft and nontender, later firm without distention. He also had coarse breath sounds with scattered fine rales at both lung bases, white exudate on the underside of the tongue, and multiple 1–2 cm nontender, mobile submandibular, submental, and cervical lymph nodes. Laboratory data showed anemia, lymphopenia, hypoalbuminemia, and positive HIV testing with HIV-1 RNA 172,000 copies/mL and CD4 count 10/mm³.

data.diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis with miliary pulmonary and gastrointestinal involvement
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection spreading through the bloodstream, potentially involving the lungs, lymph nodes, and gastrointestinal tract. The diffuse pulmonary micronodules appear compatible with a miliary pattern, making this a leading possibility; microbiologic or tissue confirmation is required.
symptoms_in_common: Advanced HIV infection with CD4 count of 10/mm³
Fever and rapid, substantial weight loss
Bilateral pulmonary micronodules and basal rales
Abdominal pain, vomiting, and apparent abdominal lymphadenopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: White sublingual exudate is more suggestive of concurrent oral candidiasis
Pain radiating to the throat and hematemesis are not usual manifestations
Stable lower-extremity hyperpigmentation for 10 years is not characteristic

data.description: An opportunistic fungal infection caused by Histoplasma that can disseminate in advanced HIV, affecting the lungs, lymph nodes, bone marrow, and gastrointestinal tract. It can produce a pulmonary micronodular pattern resembling miliary tuberculosis.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse pulmonary micronodules and abnormal breath sounds
Abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and gastrointestinal bleeding
symptoms_not_in_common: Throat-radiating pain worsened by eating is not a characteristic presentation
White sublingual exudate more commonly reflects candidiasis
Longstanding stable macular hyperpigmentation is not typical of disseminated histoplasmosis

data.description: A disseminated nontuberculous mycobacterial infection occurring especially in patients with HIV and CD4 counts below 50/mm³. It commonly causes systemic illness, lymphadenopathy, anemia, and gastrointestinal involvement.
symptoms_not_in_common: A diffuse miliary pulmonary micronodular pattern is less characteristic than in disseminated tuberculosis
Hematemesis and throat-radiating pain are not typical
White sublingual exudate is more consistent with another opportunistic infection
Chronic lower-extremity hyperpigmentation is not characteristic

data.diagnosis: HIV-associated non-Hodgkin lymphoma with gastrointestinal involvement
data.description: An aggressive lymphoid malignancy associated with HIV that may involve lymph nodes and extranodal sites, including the stomach or bowel. Gastrointestinal disease can cause pain, bleeding, vomiting, and nutritional decline.
symptoms_in_common: Fever and substantial unintentional weight loss
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse, relatively uniform pulmonary micronodules favor disseminated infection over typical pulmonary lymphoma
White sublingual exudate is not explained by lymphoma alone
Lower-extremity hyperpigmentation present for 10 years is not characteristic

data.description: An opportunistic viral infection causing ulceration of the esophagus or stomach, usually in patients with advanced HIV and CD4 counts below 50/mm³. It could explain the upper gastrointestinal symptoms but would not readily explain the entire pulmonary and lymph-node presentation.
symptoms_in_common: Upper abdominal pain radiating toward the throat and worsened by eating
Sore throat and decreased oral intake
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse pulmonary micronodules are not typical of isolated CMV esophagitis or gastritis
Cervical and apparent abdominal lymphadenopathy are not characteristic
White sublingual exudate favors concurrent candidiasis rather than CMV
Longstanding lower-extremity hyperpigmentation is not explained

data.diagnosis: Disseminated (miliary) tuberculosis with abdominal involvement in advanced HIV/AIDS
data.description: Hematogenous spread of Mycobacterium tuberculosis producing innumerable tiny randomly distributed pulmonary nodules and extrapulmonary disease (lymph nodes, mesentery, peritoneum, gastrointestinal tract), common in patients with profound immunosuppression.
symptoms_in_common: 6 weeks of fever and 10 kg weight loss with cachexia
Diffuse miliary micronodules in a random distribution on chest radiograph and CT, including subpleural nodules
Bibasilar rales and coarse breath sounds
Mesenteric soft-tissue infiltration/lymphadenopathy on abdominal CT
Abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, later firm abdomen (possible peritoneal/mesenteric involvement)
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain radiating to the throat and worsened by eating (odynophagia-like, suggests concurrent esophagitis)
Hematemesis
White exudate under the tongue (suggests candidiasis)
Chronic macular hyperpigmentation of feet and legs
No prominent cough or night sweats reported

data.description: Systemic infection with Histoplasma capsulatum in severely immunocompromised patients, causing fever, wasting, miliary or reticulonodular lung infiltrates, lymphadenopathy, cytopenias, and gastrointestinal and oropharyngeal ulcerations.
symptoms_in_common: Gastrointestinal symptoms including abdominal pain, vomiting and bleeding (GI mucosal ulceration possible)
Sore throat and oral lesions (oropharyngeal involvement possible)
symptoms_not_in_common: No hepatosplenomegaly described
No known exposure in an endemic area mentioned
White tongue exudate more typical of candidiasis than histoplasma ulcers
Chronic leg hyperpigmentation for 10 years
Pain radiating to throat with eating more typical of esophagitis

data.description: Opportunistic nontuberculous mycobacterial infection occurring at CD4 counts below 50/mm³, characterized by fever, weight loss, abdominal pain, anemia and bulky mesenteric/retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Miliary pulmonary nodules are uncommon in MAC
No diarrhea reported
Hematemesis
Sore throat and pain radiating to throat
White tongue exudate
Chronic hyperpigmentation of legs

data.diagnosis: Opportunistic esophagitis (Candida, CMV or HSV) with oropharyngeal candidiasis
data.description: Infectious esophagitis in advanced AIDS causing odynophagia, retrosternal/epigastric pain, reduced oral intake and occasionally bleeding from ulcers; often accompanies oral thrush and may coexist with another disseminated infection.
symptoms_in_common: Upper abdominal pain radiating to the throat and worsened by eating
White exudate on underside of tongue
symptoms_not_in_common: Miliary pulmonary nodules on chest imaging
Bibasilar rales
Generalized cervical lymphadenopathy
Mesenteric infiltration on abdominal CT
Firm abdomen
Chronic leg hyperpigmentation

data.diagnosis: AIDS-related lymphoma (non-Hodgkin lymphoma, e.g., diffuse large B-cell or Burkitt) with gastrointestinal involvement
data.description: Aggressive B-cell lymphoma associated with advanced HIV that frequently involves extranodal sites such as the gastrointestinal tract and mesentery, presenting with B symptoms, lymphadenopathy, abdominal pain and GI bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: Fever and marked weight loss (B symptoms)
Multiple cervical, submandibular and submental lymph nodes (nontender, mobile)
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse miliary micronodular lung pattern is atypical for lymphoma
Small (1–2 cm) nodes rather than bulky adenopathy
White tongue exudate and sore throat
Pain radiating to throat with eating
Chronic leg hyperpigmentation

data.description: 34-year-old white male presented with an indurated plaque on the forehead that extended onto the scalp over approximately 1 year. Initial laboratory findings showed positive antinuclear antibodies (1:200) and slightly increased C3d complement; other laboratory tests were normal.

An uncommon form of cutaneous lupus involving deep skin and subcutaneous fat that can produce indurated plaques and scalp alopecia. A linear variant can resemble localized scleroderma. This is a leading consideration, but confirmation requires dermatopathology review.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic indurated plaque involving the forehead and scalp
Linear distribution with apparent localized hair loss
Biopsy image appears to show deep lymphocytic inflammation and increased dermal mucin
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly documented deep nodules or depressed scars, which often accompany lupus panniculitis
Slightly increased C3d is nonspecific rather than diagnostic

data.diagnosis: Linear morphea en coup de sabre
data.description: A localized form of scleroderma that produces a linear, firm plaque on the forehead and scalp, sometimes causing underlying atrophy and permanent hair loss.
symptoms_in_common: Linear forehead plaque extending onto the scalp
Induration developing over approximately one year
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent dermal mucin and deep inflammatory aggregates suggested by the biopsy are less typical than collagen sclerosis
The photographed plaque appears erythematous without an obvious deeply depressed, ivory-colored scar

data.description: A chronic cutaneous lupus disorder causing inflammatory plaques, follicular damage, dyspigmentation, and scarring alopecia, particularly on the face and scalp.
symptoms_in_common: Possible periadnexal inflammation and dermal mucin on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: The long linear configuration is unusual
Prominent surface scale and follicular plugging are not evident in the photograph
Deep induration is less characteristic than in lupus profundus

data.description: A form of cutaneous lupus characterized by smooth, edematous or indurated erythematous plaques, with abundant dermal mucin and perivascular or periadnexal lymphocytic inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent dermal mucin and lymphocytic inflammation on biopsy
Otherwise normal laboratory testing can occur with skin-limited disease
symptoms_not_in_common: A persistent linear scalp lesion with apparent hair loss is unusual
Prominent deep inflammation involving subcutaneous tissue would favor lupus profundus
Antinuclear antibody positivity is less common than in some other lupus subtypes

data.description: A disorder in which mucin accumulates within hair follicles, producing infiltrated plaques and localized alopecia, often on the head or neck. It may be idiopathic or associated with a cutaneous lymphoproliferative disorder.
symptoms_in_common: Indurated plaque on the forehead and scalp
Chronic progression over approximately one year
Mucin is suggested by the biopsy staining
symptoms_not_in_common: The linear forehead-to-scalp distribution is uncommon
Positive antinuclear antibodies are not a characteristic finding
The visible mucin appears predominantly dermal rather than clearly confined to follicular epithelium

data.diagnosis: Linear lupus erythematosus profundus (lupus panniculitis) of the scalp
data.description: A form of chronic cutaneous lupus affecting the deep dermis and subcutaneous fat with lobular lymphocytic panniculitis and dermal mucin deposition; on the scalp it can present as linear, Blaschko-distributed alopecia mimicking linear scleroderma.
symptoms_in_common: Indurated plaque on forehead extending to scalp
Complement abnormality (raised C3d suggesting complement activation)
Preserved sebaceous glands and no marked dermal sclerosis
Slow progression over 1 year in a young adult
symptoms_not_in_common: Male sex (more common in women)
Strictly linear paramedian distribution is unusual for lupus profundus
No systemic lupus features or other laboratory abnormalities
No obvious epidermal discoid changes (follicular plugging, scale, dyspigmentation)

data.diagnosis: Linear scleroderma en coup de sabre (linear morphea)
data.description: A localized form of scleroderma producing a linear, indurated, atrophic band on the frontoparietal scalp and forehead with scarring alopecia, caused by dermal and subcutaneous sclerosis.
symptoms_in_common: Linear paramedian band on forehead extending into scalp
Positive ANA (found in a substantial proportion of linear morphea)
symptoms_not_in_common: Usually begins in childhood or adolescence
Histology shows lymphocytic panniculitis with mucin rather than thickened sclerotic collagen bundles
Preserved adnexal structures rather than loss or entrapment
No obvious depression or atrophic groove, or hyperpigmentation
Complement activation is not typical

data.description: Chronic cutaneous lupus producing erythematous, scaly plaques with follicular plugging, atrophy, dyspigmentation and scarring alopecia, commonly on the scalp and face.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous plaque on scalp and forehead with alopecia
symptoms_not_in_common: Linear band-like configuration is rare
No prominent scale, follicular plugging, or dyspigmentation
Inflammation is predominantly in the subcutaneous fat rather than interface or periadnexal
Epidermis appears relatively unremarkable
Sebaceous glands preserved

data.description: A rare cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma infiltrating subcutaneous fat, presenting as indurated plaques or nodules and histologically mimicking lupus panniculitis; atypical lymphocytes rim the adipocytes.
symptoms_in_common: Lobular lymphocytic infiltrate in the subcutaneous fat
Autoimmune serology can be positive in some patients
symptoms_not_in_common: Usually multiple nodules on the limbs and trunk rather than a single linear scalp lesion
No fever, weight loss, cytopenias or haemophagocytic syndrome
Dermal mucin deposition favours lupus
No described atypical lymphocytes rimming adipocytes
Other laboratory tests normal

data.description: Autoimmune non-scarring hair loss producing smooth, well-demarcated hairless patches, due to peribulbar lymphocytic inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Well-demarcated hairless area of the scalp
Association with autoimmunity (ANA may be positive)
symptoms_not_in_common: Induration of the plaque
Erythema and extension onto non-hair-bearing forehead skin
Linear band distribution
Histology showing panniculitis and mucin rather than peribulbar 'swarm of bees' infiltrate
Complement abnormality
Steady progression over 1 year without regrowth

data.description: A 45-year-old man presented with dry cough and breathlessness. During the investigation, he was found to be infected with HIV. Physical examination and other baseline clinical details were not specifically described in this brief case report.
An opportunistic fungal pneumonia associated with advanced HIV infection. It is the leading consideration here, although imaging alone cannot confirm it.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection as a risk factor
Apparent bilateral perihilar interstitial and hazy pulmonary opacities on the chest radiograph

data.description: A mycobacterial lung infection that can have atypical or diffuse radiographic appearances in patients with HIV.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection as a risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: The predominantly perihilar hazy pattern is less typical of classic upper-lobe cavitary tuberculosis, although HIV-associated tuberculosis can appear atypical

data.description: An opportunistic viral lung infection occurring mainly in severe immunosuppression; confirmation requires evidence of pulmonary disease rather than viral detection alone.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection as a potential risk factor if immunosuppression is advanced
Bilateral interstitial or hazy pulmonary opacities

data.description: A respiratory infection caused by organisms such as Mycoplasma pneumoniae or respiratory viruses, sometimes producing diffuse interstitial rather than lobar opacities.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral interstitial or patchy pulmonary opacities

data.description: An HIV-associated malignancy that can involve the lungs and produce perihilar or peribronchovascular infiltrates.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection as a risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: The radiograph does not show obvious nodular opacities or pleural effusions, which can accompany pulmonary Kaposi sarcoma

data.description: Opportunistic fungal pneumonia in advanced HIV infection, typically causing subacute dry cough, progressive dyspnea and bilateral perihilar/diffuse interstitial or ground-glass opacities, sometimes with cysts/pneumatoceles and upper-lobe predominance.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral perihilar and upper-zone reticular/interstitial opacities on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever and hypoxia not documented
CD4 count not reported
Somewhat coarse, upper-zone predominant opacities are less classic than diffuse fine perihilar haze

data.description: Infection with Mycobacterium tuberculosis, common in HIV-infected patients; causes upper-lobe infiltrates, cavitation or atypical/diffuse patterns in advanced immunosuppression.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral upper and mid-zone opacities on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Dry rather than productive cough
No haemoptysis, fever, night sweats or weight loss described
No clear cavitation, hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy or pleural effusion
Symmetric bilateral interstitial pattern is less typical

data.description: Acute lung infection with organisms such as Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus, Mycoplasma or Chlamydophila; more frequent in HIV-infected people. Atypical organisms can cause dry cough with interstitial infiltrates.
symptoms_in_common: HIV infection as a risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Dry cough without purulent sputum
No lobar consolidation or air bronchograms
No fever or pleuritic chest pain described
Bilateral symmetric interstitial pattern is uncommon for typical bacterial pneumonia

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary cryptococcosis (or other fungal pneumonia such as histoplasmosis)
data.description: Opportunistic fungal lung infection in advanced HIV that can present with cough, dyspnea and diffuse interstitial or nodular infiltrates, often with disseminated disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: No headache or meningitic features
No skin lesions or other evidence of dissemination
No discrete nodules, masses or lymphadenopathy on radiograph
No fever described

data.description: HHV-8 associated vascular tumour in HIV patients that may involve the lungs, producing bilateral perihilar bronchovascular (flame-shaped) opacities, nodules and pleural effusions.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral perihilar opacities along the bronchovascular bundles
symptoms_not_in_common: No mucocutaneous Kaposi lesions described
No haemoptysis
No pleural effusion
No nodular opacities or lymphadenopathy
Mid-to-lower zone predominance would be expected rather than upper-zone involvement

data.description: A 57-year-old female without any medical history was admitted for evaluation of a left ventricular tumor that was discovered incidentally. The patient was asymptomatic and had no relevant past medical history. Physical examination findings were not specifically described in the case report.

A benign tumor composed predominantly of fibroblasts and collagen, usually arising in ventricular myocardium. The collagen-rich histology shown makes this a leading consideration, although adult presentation is uncommon.
symptoms_in_common: Well-defined mass near the ventricular apex
Abundant fibrous tissue in the supplied histologic images
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation at age 57 is less typical because cardiac fibromas are more commonly identified in children

data.description: A rare benign vascular tumor that can arise within the myocardium or cardiac chambers. Some lesions contain substantial accompanying fibrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Vascular channels visible within the supplied histologic images
symptoms_not_in_common: The prominently collagen-rich tissue is less typical of a predominantly vascular hemangioma

data.description: A benign cardiac tumor composed of myxoma cells in a myxoid matrix. Most arise in the left atrium, but rare ventricular tumors occur.
symptoms_in_common: Discrete mass projecting into the left ventricular cavity
Incidental discovery in an adult woman
symptoms_not_in_common: Left ventricular apical location is unusual compared with the typical atrial location
Dense collagen-rich histology is less characteristic than a myxoid matrix

data.description: A blood clot within the left ventricle that can become fibrotic and resemble a tumor. It usually develops with ventricular dysfunction, myocardial infarction, or impaired apical contraction.
symptoms_in_common: Mass near the left ventricular apex
Fibrous tissue and vascular channels can occur in an organized, recanalized thrombus
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported history of myocardial infarction or cardiomyopathy
The supplied tissue appears more suggestive of a structured fibrous lesion than a typical thrombus

data.description: A rare benign mass formed from disorganized mature cardiac muscle cells, sometimes accompanied by fibrosis and abnormal vessels. It may occur in ventricular myocardium.
symptoms_in_common: Myocardial tissue, fibrosis, and vascular structures are visible in the supplied sections
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears predominantly collagenous rather than predominantly composed of disorganized hypertrophied cardiac myocytes

data.description: Rare benign vascular tumor of the heart made of endothelial-lined vascular channels in a fibrous or collagenous stroma; often found incidentally and may arise in any chamber, including the left ventricle.
symptoms_in_common: Asymptomatic, incidentally discovered left ventricular mass
Well-circumscribed intracavitary mass at the left ventricular apex
Progressive contrast enhancement on perfusion and delayed imaging
Histology showing irregular vascular channels lined by CD31/CD34-type positive endothelium
symptoms_not_in_common: Pale, whitish-tan firm cut surface rather than the usual red, hemorrhagic, spongy appearance
Abundant dense collagenous stroma, more than in a typical hemangioma
Gradual rather than intense early enhancement

data.description: Benign connective tissue tumor of fibroblasts and collagen, usually intramural in the ventricular septum or free wall; mostly seen in children but occasionally in adults.
symptoms_not_in_common: Typically a pediatric tumor, not one presenting at 57 years
Usually intramural rather than an intracavitary apical mass
Usually low signal on T2-weighted imaging, whereas this mass is bright
Numerous endothelial-lined vascular channels are not a feature
Absence of calcification, which is common in fibroma

data.description: Most common primary benign cardiac tumor in adults, composed of stellate myxoma cells in a myxoid matrix; usually arises in the left atrium from the interatrial septum, rarely in a ventricle.
symptoms_not_in_common: Left ventricular apical location is rare (most are left atrial)
No embolic, obstructive or constitutional symptoms
Gross specimen is firm and fibrous rather than gelatinous and friable
Histology shows vascular channels in collagenous stroma rather than myxoma cells in myxoid matrix

data.description: Benign endocardial tumor with avascular papillary fronds of collagen and elastic fibers covered by endothelium; usually on valves but can arise from ventricular endocardium, with embolic potential.
symptoms_in_common: Incidental finding in an asymptomatic older adult
Endothelial marker positivity on the surface lining
symptoms_not_in_common: Usually valvular rather than apical
Typically small (about 1 cm) and mobile on a stalk
Sea-anemone papillary fronds not seen grossly
Fronds are avascular, whereas this lesion contains many vascular channels and muscular vessels
Marked contrast enhancement is unusual

data.description: Intracavitary clot, usually forming over akinetic or aneurysmal myocardium after infarction or in cardiomyopathy; when organized it can contain fibrous tissue and recanalized vessels and mimic a tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Organized thrombus may show collagen and recanalized vascular channels
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of myocardial infarction, cardiomyopathy or hypercoagulable state
No reported wall motion abnormality at the apex
Thrombus does not enhance on perfusion or delayed MRI, whereas this mass enhances
Thrombus is usually low signal on T2-weighted imaging
Histology shows a true vascular lesion with muscular vessels rather than layered fibrin

data.description: 67-year-old man with 10 days of nausea, nonbloody vomiting, bloating, and epigastric pain unrelieved by omeprazole, followed on presentation day by exertional substernal nonradiating chest heaviness progressing to rest pain with diaphoresis and dyspnea (8/10). History of mild asthma, prior hemicolectomy for dysplastic polyps with ventral abdominal hernia, and remote 20 pack-year smoking. Exam: tachycardia 125 bpm, hypotension 84/62 mmHg, tachypnea 22/min, oxygen saturation 94% on 6 L, pallor, diaphoresis, accessory muscle use, JVP 18 cm H2O, regular tachycardia with grade 2/6 holosystolic apical murmur, left basilar rales, palpable liver edge 4 cm below costal margin, and cool clammy extremities with thready pulses.

A rare, aggressive inflammatory disease causing myocardial necrosis, rapidly progressive heart failure, and potentially fatal arrhythmias. The supplied biopsy appears to show multinucleated giant cells, extensive inflammation, and myocyte injury, making this the leading possibility. The presentation indicates life-threatening cardiogenic shock.
symptoms_in_common: Rapid progression to severe chest discomfort and dyspnea
Hypotension, tachycardia, cool clammy extremities, and thready pulses consistent with cardiogenic shock
Elevated jugular venous pressure, palpable liver edge, and basilar rales indicating cardiac congestion
Apical holosystolic murmur compatible with secondary mitral regurgitation
Biopsy appearance suggestive of giant cells with myocardial inflammation and necrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Ten days of prominent bloating and vomiting are nonspecific rather than characteristic
Exertional chest heaviness progressing to rest pain more classically suggests coronary ischemia

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome with myocardial infarction and cardiogenic shock
data.description: Acute coronary obstruction can cause myocardial ischemia or infarction, severe ventricular dysfunction, and shock. This is an urgent competing diagnosis, although the inflammatory biopsy appearance favors myocarditis.
symptoms_in_common: Substernal heaviness initially triggered by exertion and subsequently occurring at rest
Severe chest pain with diaphoresis and dyspnea
Nausea, vomiting, and epigastric discomfort as possible atypical ischemic symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy appearance suggestive of multinucleated giant cells and diffuse inflammatory myocardial injury is not typical of uncomplicated infarction
Prolonged bloating is not a characteristic ischemic symptom

data.description: An eosinophil-rich inflammatory injury of the myocardium, sometimes associated with hypersensitivity, medications, or systemic eosinophilic disease. Fulminant cases can cause cardiogenic shock; confirmation requires characterization of the biopsy infiltrate.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly progressive heart failure with hypotension
Tachycardia, elevated jugular venous pressure, and basilar rales
Myocardial inflammation and injury on the supplied biopsy
History of asthma, which can accompany some eosinophilic disorders
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent multinucleated giant cells are less typical of isolated eosinophilic myocarditis
Exertional chest heaviness progressing to rest pain is more characteristic of coronary ischemia
Bloating and prolonged vomiting are not defining features

data.description: Severe myocardial inflammation, often associated with a viral or immune-mediated process, that can mimic myocardial infarction and rapidly produce ventricular failure and cardiogenic shock.
symptoms_in_common: Gastrointestinal symptoms preceding acute cardiac deterioration
Elevated jugular venous pressure, hepatic congestion, and pulmonary rales
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent multinucleated giant cells are not typical of lymphocytic myocarditis
Exertional-to-rest chest heaviness is more suggestive of coronary ischemia
Persistent bloating is nonspecific

data.description: Granulomatous inflammation involving the heart that can cause conduction abnormalities, ventricular arrhythmias, and heart failure. Giant cells can occur, but organized noncaseating granulomas would support this diagnosis more strongly than diffuse necrotizing inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Dyspnea and signs of congestive heart failure
Elevated jugular venous pressure and hepatic congestion
Apparent giant cells in myocardial tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt fulminant shock is less typical than a more chronic or arrhythmic presentation
The biopsy appears to show diffuse inflammation and myocyte injury rather than clearly organized granulomas
Ten days of nausea, vomiting, and bloating are not characteristic
Exertional chest heaviness progressing to rest pain more strongly suggests ischemia

data.description: Rare, rapidly progressive, likely autoimmune myocarditis characterized by diffuse myocyte necrosis with a mixed inflammatory infiltrate including multinucleated giant cells and eosinophils, without well-formed granulomas; presents with fulminant heart failure, cardiogenic shock, ventricular arrhythmias or heart block.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute prodrome of nausea, vomiting, bloating and epigastric pain consistent with hepatic and gut congestion from low output
Rapid progression to cardiogenic shock (hypotension, tachycardia, cool clammy extremities, thready pulses)
Chest heaviness with dyspnea and diaphoresis
Holosystolic apical murmur consistent with functional mitral regurgitation
ECG with low limb-lead voltage and anterior Q waves/poor R-wave progression (pseudo-infarct pattern)
Chest radiograph showing cardiomegaly with pulmonary congestion
Endomyocardial biopsy showing myocyte damage with dense mixed inflammatory infiltrate, multinucleated giant cells and eosinophils
symptoms_not_in_common: Older age than typical (usually middle-aged)
No ventricular arrhythmia or heart block described
No known associated autoimmune disease
Exertional angina-like onset is more suggestive of ischemia

data.diagnosis: Acute myocardial infarction with cardiogenic shock (anterior MI, possible mechanical complication)
data.description: Coronary occlusion causing myocardial necrosis; a late-presenting anterior infarction may cause pump failure, papillary muscle dysfunction or rupture with acute mitral regurgitation, and shock.
symptoms_in_common: Exertional substernal chest heaviness progressing to rest pain
Epigastric pain, nausea and vomiting as possible anginal equivalents
Age, male sex and smoking history
symptoms_not_in_common: 10-day gastrointestinal prodrome is long for an infarct
Biopsy showing giant cells and eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate rather than coagulative necrosis with neutrophils
Low limb-lead voltage
Marked right-sided failure with hepatomegaly out of proportion for isolated anterior MI

data.description: Granulomatous infiltration of the myocardium causing cardiomyopathy, conduction disease and ventricular arrhythmias; histology shows well-formed non-necrotizing granulomas with giant cells and fibrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Heart failure with elevated JVP, rales and hepatomegaly
symptoms_not_in_common: Fulminant course over days with cardiogenic shock is unusual
Biopsy shows prominent myocyte necrosis and eosinophils without well-formed granulomas or significant fibrosis
No heart block or ventricular arrhythmia
No hilar adenopathy or other extracardiac sarcoid features
Prominent gastrointestinal prodrome

data.description: Acute myocardial inflammation, usually post-viral, with lymphocytic infiltrate and myocyte necrosis, which can present with a prodrome followed by abrupt severe heart failure and shock.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiogenic shock with tachycardia and hypotension
ECG abnormalities mimicking infarction with low voltage
Inflammatory infiltrate with myocyte injury on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Multinucleated giant cells on biopsy
Prominent eosinophils in the infiltrate
No documented fever or clear viral illness
Older age than typical

data.description: Myocardial inflammation dominated by eosinophils, due to drug hypersensitivity, hypereosinophilic syndromes or eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis; the necrotizing form can be fulminant with shock.
symptoms_in_common: History of asthma (possible link to eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis)
Recent new drug exposure (omeprazole) as a potential hypersensitivity trigger
Acute heart failure and cardiogenic shock
Chest pain with ECG changes mimicking infarction
Eosinophils in the myocardial infiltrate on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Multinucleated giant cells on biopsy point away from this
No rash, fever or peripheral eosinophilia reported
Asthma is mild, with no sinusitis, neuropathy or other vasculitic features
Extensive myocyte necrosis is atypical for simple hypersensitivity myocarditis

data.description: 33-year-old man admitted with chest pain that began as epigastric pain 2 hours before admission and evolved into central chest pain, with one episode of vomiting, dizziness, dyspnea, sweating, and distal paresthesias. The pain had resolved on arrival. Later that day, he developed nausea, diaphoresis, pallor, blurred vision, muffled hearing, and tingling in both hands, with systolic blood pressure dropping to 89 mm Hg and cardiac monitoring showing a 3–4 second pause with no P wave activity. History included syncope with phlebotomy; no other vasovagal episodes. He had flu-like symptoms, and his daughter had gastroenteritis. Family history notable for a sister with drug-resistant epilepsy and multiple seizures. Physical examinations were normal before and after the hypotensive episode.

An inherited cardiac electrical disorder associated with right-precordial ECG abnormalities and potentially dangerous ventricular arrhythmias. The supplied ECGs show right-precordial changes that warrant assessment for a Brugada pattern, but are not sufficient alone to establish the diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Possible Brugada-like ST-segment morphology in leads V1–V2
Flu-like illness, which could unmask ECG abnormalities if accompanied by fever
Family history of refractory seizures, which occasionally represent arrhythmic syncope rather than epilepsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent nausea, sweating, pallor, blurred vision, and muffled hearing before the hypotensive episode favor a reflex mechanism
A pause without P-wave activity suggests sinus arrest rather than the ventricular arrhythmias typically responsible for Brugada-related syncope
Epigastric pain and vomiting are not characteristic
Prior syncope specifically triggered by phlebotomy

data.description: A reflex episode involving increased vagal activity and reduced vascular tone, producing hypotension and sometimes marked sinus slowing or sinus arrest.
symptoms_in_common: Systolic blood pressure falling to 89 mm Hg
A 3–4 second pause without P-wave activity
Normal examinations before and after the episode
Pain or gastrointestinal illness as potential triggers
symptoms_not_in_common: Right-precordial ECG abnormalities are not explained by vasovagal presyncope alone
Central chest pain and dyspnea require evaluation for additional causes
Family history of drug-resistant seizures is not a typical feature

data.diagnosis: Sinus node dysfunction with intermittent sinus arrest
data.description: Impaired initiation of electrical impulses by the sinus node, causing pauses that can reduce cerebral perfusion. In this patient, an intrinsic disorder would need to be distinguished from transient vagally mediated sinus arrest.
symptoms_in_common: Documented 3–4 second pause without P-wave activity
Blurred vision and muffled hearing during reduced perfusion
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 33 is less typical for degenerative sinus node disease
Strong autonomic prodrome with nausea, diaphoresis, and pallor favors a vasovagal mechanism
Prior phlebotomy-triggered syncope
Epigastric pain, vomiting, and flu-like symptoms are not characteristic of intrinsic sinus node dysfunction

data.description: Inflammation of heart muscle, often following a viral infection, that can cause chest pain, ECG abnormalities, and disturbances of cardiac rhythm or conduction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prior syncope with phlebotomy suggests a separate reflex predisposition
The stereotyped autonomic prodrome is more typical of vasovagal presyncope
Rapid resolution with normal examinations before and after the episode is less suggestive of clinically significant myocarditis
Bilateral hand tingling and muffled hearing are not characteristic manifestations

data.description: Acute myocardial ischemia from reduced coronary blood flow. Chest or epigastric pain with sweating, vomiting, and dyspnea warrants exclusion with serial ECGs and cardiac troponin testing, even in a younger patient.
symptoms_in_common: Epigastric pain evolving into central chest pain
Bradyarrhythmia or sinus pauses can occur with inferior myocardial ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 33 without reported coronary risk factors makes atherosclerotic acute coronary syndrome less typical
The supplied ECGs do not show a clear territorial acute ischemic pattern
Previous phlebotomy-triggered syncope
Blurred vision, muffled hearing, and bilateral hand tingling with a pronounced autonomic prodrome favor reflex presyncope
Flu-like symptoms and household gastroenteritis are not typical features

data.description: Inherited cardiac sodium channelopathy (often SCN5A) characterized by coved ST elevation with T-wave inversion in V1-V2 (type 1 pattern), often dynamic and unmasked by fever or vagal tone, with risk of ventricular arrhythmias, sinus node dysfunction, syncope and sudden death. Arrhythmic syncope with convulsions in relatives may be misdiagnosed as epilepsy.
symptoms_in_common: First ECG showing coved ST elevation with inverted T waves in V1-V2, apparently normalizing on the second ECG (dynamic pattern)
Flu-like illness (possible fever unmasking the pattern)
Sinus pause of 3-4 seconds with no P wave activity (sinus node dysfunction can coexist)
Sister with drug-resistant 'epilepsy' (possible misdiagnosed arrhythmic syncope)
Symptoms occurring at rest/with vagal features
symptoms_not_in_common: Chest pain beginning as epigastric pain
Prior syncope clearly triggered by phlebotomy (suggests vasovagal mechanism)
Prodrome of blurred vision, muffled hearing and tingling typical of reflex presyncope
No documented ventricular arrhythmia

data.description: Reflex-mediated bradycardia and vasodilation triggered by pain, illness, nausea or blood/needle stimuli, causing transient hypotension, sinus pauses and presyncope or syncope with a characteristic autonomic prodrome.
symptoms_in_common: Vomiting and gastrointestinal illness as trigger
Normal examination before and after the episode
symptoms_not_in_common: Central chest pain
Coved ST elevation in V1-V2 on ECG
Family history of drug-resistant seizures
Bilateral hand paresthesias (less typical)

data.description: Inflammation of the myocardium and/or pericardium, usually viral, presenting with chest pain after a viral prodrome, ECG ST-T changes, and occasionally conduction disturbances or arrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Recent flu-like symptoms and sick contact with gastroenteritis
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain resolved spontaneously within hours
ST elevation confined to V1-V2 with coved morphology rather than diffuse ST elevation with PR depression
No pericardial rub
Prominent vagal prodrome
Family history of seizures not explained

data.diagnosis: Acute coronary syndrome (anterior/septal STEMI or coronary vasospasm)
data.description: Myocardial ischemia from coronary plaque rupture or spasm, causing chest pain with autonomic symptoms and ST-segment changes; vasospasm can produce transient ST elevation and bradyarrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Epigastric pain evolving to central chest pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age (33 years) with no stated risk factors
Pain resolved spontaneously on arrival
Coved ST pattern limited to right precordial leads without reciprocal changes
Prodrome typical of reflex syncope
Family history of seizures rather than premature coronary disease

data.diagnosis: Acute viral gastroenteritis with volume depletion
data.description: Self-limited infectious inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract causing nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain and sometimes dehydration with hypotension and heightened vagal tone.
symptoms_not_in_common: Central chest pain
Only one episode of vomiting and no diarrhea reported
Sinus pause of 3-4 seconds
Coved ST elevation in V1-V2
Family history of drug-resistant seizures

data.description: A 1-year and 4-month-old girl was admitted for evaluation of psychomotor retardation and an operation for exotropia. She was born at term (gestational age: 40 weeks) by cesarean delivery after an uneventful pregnancy, and was the first child of healthy, unrelated parents. The family history was unremarkable. On admission, she presented with a characteristic high-pitched cry and microcephaly. She showed delayed motor functions and crawling, was able to sit unassisted but unable to stand, with developmental characteristics lagging behind for normal chronologic age. On neurologic examination, she had left leg hypotonia, with normal tendon reflexes and normal cranial nerve signs. When she was 6 months old, ventricular septal defect was detected by echocardiography. Chromosome analysis revealed 46,XX,del (5) (p15.2) one month after delivery.

A chromosomal disorder caused by deletion of the short arm of chromosome 5, producing a characteristic high-pitched cry, microcephaly, and developmental impairment. The documented 46,XX,del(5)(p15.2) establishes this as the primary diagnosis. The MRI appears to show a small pons, a recognized associated finding.
symptoms_in_common: Psychomotor and gross motor developmental delay
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypotonia confined to the left leg is less typical than generalized hypotonia

data.description: A chromosome 4p deletion disorder associated with microcephaly, developmental delay, hypotonia, and congenital malformations. It is a phenotypic alternative, but the confirmed chromosome 5p deletion supports cri-du-chat syndrome instead.
symptoms_not_in_common: Characteristic high-pitched cry is not a defining feature
Unilateral leg hypotonia is less typical than generalized hypotonia

data.description: A chromosomal deletion disorder causing developmental impairment, hypotonia, microcephaly, and sometimes congenital heart disease. This is a lower-likelihood phenotypic alternative because the documented deletion involves chromosome 5 rather than chromosome 1.
symptoms_not_in_common: Characteristic high-pitched cry is not a defining feature
Isolated left leg hypotonia is not a characteristic pattern

data.description: A neurodevelopmental disorder caused by loss of maternal UBE3A function, characterized by severe developmental impairment, speech impairment, and movement abnormalities. It can overlap clinically but does not explain the confirmed chromosome 5p deletion.
symptoms_not_in_common: Characteristic high-pitched cry
Ventricular septal defect
Hypotonia restricted to one leg

data.description: A heterogeneous group of disorders involving underdevelopment of the pons and cerebellum, often with severe motor and developmental impairment. The apparently small pons on the supplied MRI raises an imaging differential, but cerebellar hypoplasia is not clearly established, and pontine hypoplasia can occur within cri-du-chat syndrome itself.
symptoms_not_in_common: Characteristic high-pitched cry
Ventricular septal defect
Isolated left leg hypotonia rather than a more widespread motor abnormality

data.description: Chromosomal disorder caused by partial deletion of the short arm of chromosome 5, characterized by a high-pitched cat-like cry, microcephaly, psychomotor retardation, hypotonia, and sometimes congenital heart defects; MRI classically shows brainstem (pontine) hypoplasia, sometimes with cerebellar or white matter abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Psychomotor retardation and delayed motor milestones
MRI appearance suggesting a small pons/brainstem with prominent ventricles
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypotonia limited to the left leg (usually generalized)
No facial dysmorphism described

data.description: Group of autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorders with prenatal-onset hypoplasia/atrophy of the pons and cerebellum, causing progressive microcephaly, severe developmental delay, and movement or tone abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: 5p15.2 deletion on karyotype
High-pitched cat-like cry
Ventricular septal defect
Able to sit unassisted (course usually more severe)
Non-consanguineous parents with no family history

data.description: Chromosomal deletion syndrome of distal 4p with 'Greek warrior helmet' facies, growth deficiency, microcephaly, intellectual disability, seizures, hypotonia, and congenital heart defects.
symptoms_not_in_common: Deletion is on 5p, not 4p
High-pitched cat-like cry
No seizures
No characteristic facial features described
No reported prenatal growth restriction

data.description: Microdeletion syndrome causing congenital heart defects, palatal anomalies, immune deficiency, hypocalcemia, developmental delay, and hypotonia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Karyotype shows 5p deletion rather than 22q11.2 deletion
High-pitched cat-like cry
No hypocalcemia, immune deficiency, or cleft palate reported
Brainstem hypoplasia on MRI is not typical

data.description: Intrauterine infection that can lead to microcephaly, developmental delay, hearing loss, ocular abnormalities, ventriculomegaly, periventricular calcifications, and white matter or cortical malformations.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent ventricles/white matter changes on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Uneventful pregnancy
5p15.2 deletion explains the phenotype
High-pitched cat-like cry
Ventricular septal defect
No periventricular calcifications, hearing loss, or hepatosplenomegaly reported

data.description: 32-year-old woman with a history of dissociative and depressive disorders, treated as an outpatient with multiple psychiatric medications, admitted to the emergency department for somnolence after a presumed suicide attempt. On arrival, GCS 11/15; hemodynamically stable, afebrile, normal oxygen saturation, respiratory rate 16/min. Physical examination showed only somnolence. Initial labs showed metabolic acidosis with elevated lactate and markedly increased plasma osmolality and osmolal gap.

Toxic alcohol ingestion that initially causes central nervous system depression and an elevated osmolal gap, followed by metabolic acidosis as toxic metabolites accumulate. Kidney injury and hypocalcemia may develop later.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly increased plasma osmolality and osmolal gap
Elevated measured lactate, which can sometimes reflect interference from ethylene glycol metabolites
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal respiratory rate despite metabolic acidosis, although this does not exclude early poisoning

data.description: Toxic alcohol ingestion whose metabolite, formic acid, causes metabolic acidosis and potentially severe visual and neurologic injury. An elevated osmolal gap is especially prominent before methanol is fully metabolized.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly increased plasma osmolality and osmolal gap
Elevated lactate, which may accompany severe toxicity
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal respiratory rate despite metabolic acidosis
Somnolence as the only examination finding is less characteristic of established severe poisoning, though compatible with early exposure

data.description: Toxic accumulation of propylene glycol, a solvent in some medication formulations, can produce hyperosmolality, an elevated osmolal gap, lactic acidosis, and central nervous system depression.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly increased plasma osmolality and osmolal gap
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported findings directly contradict this diagnosis, although a substantial exposure to a propylene glycol-containing preparation would need confirmation

data.description: Toxic alcohol ingestion causing central nervous system depression, hyperosmolality, and ketosis through conversion to acetone. Unlike methanol and ethylene glycol, isolated isopropanol poisoning usually does not cause metabolic acidosis.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly increased plasma osmolality and osmolal gap
symptoms_not_in_common: Metabolic acidosis is atypical for isolated isopropanol poisoning
Elevated lactate without hypotension or hypoxia is not a characteristic finding

data.description: Metformin toxicity impairs cellular energy metabolism and lactate clearance, potentially causing severe lactic acidosis and altered consciousness. It requires a history of metformin exposure and does not usually explain a markedly elevated osmolal gap.
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly increased plasma osmolality and osmolal gap are not typical and suggest an additional or alternative toxic exposure
Normal respiratory rate is less typical of severe lactic acidosis

data.diagnosis: Propylene glycol toxicity from benzodiazepine (e.g., lorazepam/diazepam solution) overdose
data.description: Propylene glycol is a solvent in some benzodiazepine and other drug formulations; in large amounts it raises serum osmolality and is metabolized to lactate, causing lactic acidosis with a high osmolal gap, alongside sedation from the carried drug.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly increased plasma osmolality and osmolal gap
Psychiatric patient on multiple medications with presumed suicide attempt
Normal respiratory rate and oxygen saturation
symptoms_not_in_common: Usually described with prolonged high-dose IV infusions rather than acute oral ingestion
No documented acute kidney injury
No hypotension or arrhythmia

data.description: Ingestion of antifreeze; the parent compound raises the osmolal gap and its metabolites (glycolate, oxalate) cause severe anion gap metabolic acidosis, CNS depression and later renal failure. Glycolate may falsely elevate lactate on some analyzers.
symptoms_not_in_common: Respiratory rate 16/min without Kussmaul compensatory hyperventilation
No reported renal impairment, flank pain or oxalate crystalluria
No hypocalcemia or seizures reported
Hemodynamically stable
No known access to antifreeze; history points to medications

data.description: Ingestion of methanol (windshield fluid, adulterated alcohol, solvents) causing an osmolal gap, followed by formic acid-induced anion gap metabolic acidosis, visual disturbances and CNS depression.
symptoms_not_in_common: No visual complaints or pupillary abnormalities
No abdominal pain or vomiting
No compensatory hyperventilation
Physical exam otherwise normal

data.diagnosis: Acute ethanol intoxication (with co-ingested sedative medications)
data.description: Ethanol is the most common cause of an elevated osmolal gap; it causes CNS depression and can produce mild lactic acidosis through an increased NADH/NAD+ ratio. Often co-ingested in suicide attempts.
symptoms_in_common: Increased plasma osmolality and osmolal gap
Mildly elevated lactate with metabolic acidosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Significant metabolic acidosis is unusual with ethanol alone
No mention of alcohol odor or alcohol use history
No hypoglycemia or ketoacidosis reported

data.description: Ingestion of rubbing alcohol causes marked CNS depression and a high osmolal gap, with ketosis from acetone, typically without acidosis; gastritis and hypotension may occur in severe cases.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly increased osmolal gap and osmolality
symptoms_not_in_common: Metabolic acidosis (classically absent)
Elevated lactate
No fruity/acetone breath odor reported
No gastrointestinal symptoms such as vomiting or hematemesis

data.description: 41-year-old man with sudden, severe right lower quadrant abdominal pain radiating to the right groin and flank, partially relieved by lying down, associated with nausea and one episode of nonbloody, nonbilious vomiting. Two weeks earlier, he had a similar but milder episode in the left lower quadrant radiating to the left flank that resolved spontaneously. He also reported several months of fatigue but no fever, weight loss, chest pain, diarrhea, or urinary symptoms. Examination showed diffuse abdominal tenderness without guarding or rebound and bilateral costovertebral angle tenderness, worse on the right. Vitals were notable for severe hypertension; temperature was 37.4°C. Labs showed leukocytosis with neutrophilia, mild anemia, elevated creatinine, elevated LDH, elevated ESR and CRP, and bland urinalysis with proteinuria. Past history was unremarkable aside from tobacco and alcohol use; family history included coronary artery disease and arrhythmias.

data.diagnosis: Polyarteritis nodosa with bilateral renal infarction
data.description: A systemic necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that can cause renal and mesenteric arterial aneurysms, stenoses, and infarction. The apparent bilateral renal perfusion defects and multiple branch-vessel aneurysms on the supplied images strongly favor this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden severe abdominal and flank pain
Previous similar episode on the opposite side
Elevated creatinine and proteinuria with otherwise bland urinalysis
Elevated LDH, consistent with tissue infarction
Fatigue, mild anemia, leukocytosis, and elevated ESR and CRP
Apparent renal perfusion defects and multiple visceral arterial aneurysms
symptoms_not_in_common: Partial relief of pain by lying down is nonspecific
No skin lesions, peripheral neuropathy, or other extrarenal manifestations are reported, although these are not required

data.description: A noninflammatory disorder involving injury to the walls of visceral arteries, producing aneurysms, dissections, and arterial occlusions that can cause abdominal pain and renal infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt severe abdominal and flank pain
Elevated LDH and impaired kidney function
symptoms_not_in_common: Several months of fatigue and mild anemia suggest a systemic inflammatory process
Elevated ESR and CRP are less characteristic of a primarily noninflammatory arteriopathy, although infarction can elevate them
Severe hypertension is possible with renal involvement but is not a defining feature

data.diagnosis: Fibromuscular dysplasia involving renal and visceral arteries
data.description: A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory arterial disorder causing stenoses, aneurysms, or dissections. Renal involvement can produce severe hypertension and occasionally renal infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal and flank pain potentially caused by renal ischemia
Arterial irregularities and aneurysms on angiographic imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated ESR and CRP and prolonged fatigue are not typical primary manifestations
Mild anemia and neutrophilic leukocytosis are not characteristic unless secondary complications occur
Multiple small branch-vessel aneurysms are more suggestive of medium-vessel vasculitis than classic fibromuscular dysplasia

data.description: Occlusion of renal arteries or their branches by emboli, potentially from an occult cardiac source, causes ischemic renal injury. This explains the renal perfusion defects but would not readily explain widespread arterial aneurysms.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden severe abdominal and flank pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple visceral arterial aneurysms are not typical of uncomplicated thromboembolism
Several months of fatigue and anemia are not well explained by isolated acute embolic events
No personal arrhythmia or established embolic source is reported

data.diagnosis: Spontaneous renal artery dissection with renal infarction
data.description: A tear within a renal artery wall can obstruct blood flow and cause renal infarction, acute flank pain, and renovascular hypertension. It may occur independently or in association with an underlying arteriopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden severe pain radiating to the flank and groin
symptoms_not_in_common: Sequential bilateral episodes would be unusual for an isolated renal artery dissection
Multiple aneurysms in renal and other visceral arterial branches suggest a broader vascular disorder
Months of fatigue, mild anemia, and elevated inflammatory markers are not typical primary features
A definite dissection flap is not established by the supplied images

data.description: Systemic necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries causing microaneurysms, stenoses and organ infarction, typically involving renal and mesenteric vessels, without glomerulonephritis.
symptoms_in_common: Sequential bilateral flank/abdominal pain consistent with renal infarcts
Bilateral wedge-shaped renal hypoperfusion defects on CT
Multiple microaneurysms on renal and mesenteric angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss
No fever
No reported neuropathy, skin lesions, myalgias or testicular pain

data.diagnosis: Cardioembolic renal infarction (e.g., atrial fibrillation or endocarditis)
data.description: Emboli from a cardiac source occlude renal artery branches, causing acute flank pain, nausea, elevated LDH and wedge-shaped renal infarcts.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral wedge-shaped renal defects on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Microaneurysms on renal and mesenteric angiography
Months of fatigue with elevated inflammatory markers and anemia
No known arrhythmia, chest pain or fever
No murmur or embolic stigmata described

data.description: Rare noninflammatory, nonatherosclerotic arteriopathy with lysis of the arterial media, causing dissections, aneurysms and occlusions of visceral arteries in middle-aged adults.
symptoms_in_common: Aneurysms of renal and mesenteric arteries on angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated ESR and CRP
Months of fatigue
Anemia
Numerous small microaneurysms rather than dissections or larger aneurysms
Leukocytosis less typical

data.diagnosis: Fibromuscular dysplasia with renal artery dissection/infarction
data.description: Noninflammatory, nonatherosclerotic disease of medium-sized arteries causing stenoses (string-of-beads), aneurysms and dissections, commonly of renal arteries, leading to renovascular hypertension and renal infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal renal arteriography with aneurysmal changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Male sex (predominantly affects women)
Elevated ESR and CRP
Fatigue and anemia
Distal intraparenchymal microaneurysms rather than main-artery beading
Mesenteric microaneurysms
Leukocytosis

data.diagnosis: ANCA-associated vasculitis (e.g., granulomatosis with polyangiitis or microscopic polyangiitis)
data.description: Small-vessel necrotizing vasculitis commonly causing glomerulonephritis, pulmonary and upper-airway disease with constitutional symptoms; occasionally involves medium vessels.
symptoms_not_in_common: Bland urine sediment without hematuria or casts
Renal infarcts and microaneurysms (medium-vessel pattern)
Severe hypertension as a dominant feature
No respiratory or sinus symptoms
No fever or rash

data.description: A 35-year-old woman presented to the emergency room with a clinically incarcerated umbilical hernia. Fourteen days after the initial hernia repair surgery, she developed strong pain in the right lower abdomen and complained of umbilical secretion. Physical examination revealed the patient was afebrile. Blood analysis showed a slight elevation in leukocyte count at 11.05 × 10^9/L, while other parameters were unexceptional. Ultrasound of the abdominal wall detected a semisolid infraumbilical mass with a diameter of 5.5 cm. Initial histologic examination of the resected omental fat from the hernia repair revealed malignant cells with neuroendocrine differentiation. Immunohistochemical analysis was positive for synaptophysin and protein gene product 9.5. Fluorescent in situ hybridization revealed a rearrangement of the EWSR1 gene.

data.diagnosis: Extraosseous Ewing sarcoma with neuroectodermal differentiation
data.description: A malignant soft-tissue tumor in the Ewing sarcoma family, historically termed peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor when neuroectodermal differentiation is present. This is a leading possibility; confirmation requires compatible pathology and identification of an Ewing-associated fusion, commonly EWSR1::FLI1.
symptoms_in_common: Malignant cells in resected omental tissue
Neuroendocrine differentiation with synaptophysin and protein gene product 9.5 positivity
Abdominal pain without marked systemic inflammatory abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Umbilical secretion shortly after surgery is not a characteristic tumor manifestation
An incarcerated umbilical hernia is an unusual initial presentation

data.description: An aggressive sarcoma that typically involves abdominal and pelvic peritoneal surfaces and is characterized by an EWSR1::WT1 fusion. EWSR1 rearrangement alone cannot distinguish it from other EWSR1-associated tumors.
symptoms_in_common: Possible expression of neural or neuroendocrine markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Postoperative umbilical secretion is not a typical manifestation
Presentation as an incarcerated umbilical hernia is unusual

data.diagnosis: Poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma with omental involvement
data.description: An aggressive epithelial malignancy showing neuroendocrine differentiation that can arise in gastrointestinal or other organs and spread to the peritoneum. Epithelial markers and investigation for a primary tumor would help evaluate this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Synaptophysin and protein gene product 9.5 positivity
symptoms_not_in_common: EWSR1 rearrangement is not characteristic and favors an alternative tumor classification
Postoperative umbilical secretion is not typical
An incarcerated umbilical hernia is an unusual presentation

data.description: A rare gastrointestinal soft-tissue malignancy associated with EWSR1::ATF1 or EWSR1::CREB1 fusions. It may express neural markers and spread within the abdomen; confirmation requires compatible morphology, immunophenotyping, and fusion testing.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal pain and a malignant abdominal mass
symptoms_not_in_common: The reported mass is infraumbilical rather than an identified gastrointestinal-wall primary
Postoperative umbilical secretion is not characteristic
An incarcerated umbilical hernia is not a typical initial manifestation

data.diagnosis: Postoperative abdominal-wall abscess or infected seroma
data.description: A postoperative infected fluid collection that could explain the new pain, wound drainage, and infraumbilical mass. It could coexist with a tumor but cannot explain the malignant histology or molecular findings.
symptoms_in_common: Onset fourteen days after hernia repair
Semisolid infraumbilical collection or mass on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: Malignant cells in the omental specimen are not explained by infection
Neuroendocrine differentiation and associated immunostaining are not explained by infection
EWSR1 gene rearrangement is a tumor-related finding, not an infectious finding
Absence of fever is less typical of a substantial abscess, although it does not exclude one

data.diagnosis: Extraskeletal Ewing sarcoma / peripheral primitive neuroectodermal tumor (PNET) of the omentum/abdominal wall
data.description: A rare, aggressive small round blue cell tumor of soft tissue characterized by EWSR1 gene rearrangement (most commonly EWSR1-FLI1), strong membranous CD99 expression, variable neural/neuroendocrine marker expression and a high proliferation index.
symptoms_in_common: Rapidly growing 5.5 cm semisolid infraumbilical mass on ultrasound and CT
Tumor cells in omental fat from hernia sac
Diffuse strong membranous staining pattern on immunohistochemistry (consistent with CD99) and high proliferation index (Ki-67-like nuclear staining)
symptoms_not_in_common: Presentation as an incarcerated umbilical hernia is highly unusual
Omental/abdominal wall primary site is rare
Umbilical secretion
Age 35 is slightly older than the typical peak (adolescents and young adults)

data.description: A highly aggressive intra-abdominal small round cell sarcoma arising on peritoneal/omental surfaces, defined by the EWSR1-WT1 fusion and polyphenotypic expression (cytokeratin, desmin dot-like, neural markers).
symptoms_not_in_common: Strong male predominance, patient is female
Usually multiple peritoneal nodules rather than a single mass
No desmoplastic stroma described
No reported desmin or cytokeratin co-expression or WT1 positivity
Umbilical secretion

data.diagnosis: Poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma (small cell type) metastatic to omentum/umbilicus (Sister Mary Joseph nodule)
data.description: High-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma, usually from the gastrointestinal tract, pancreas or lung, that can seed the peritoneum and umbilicus, presenting as an umbilical nodule or within a hernia sac.
symptoms_in_common: Omental tumor deposits found in hernia sac
symptoms_not_in_common: EWSR1 gene rearrangement is not characteristic
Young age of 35
No known primary tumor identified
Diffuse membranous staining (CD99-like) is more typical of Ewing sarcoma
No cytokeratin positivity reported

data.diagnosis: Postoperative abdominal wall abscess / infected seroma or hematoma after hernia repair
data.description: A common complication following hernia surgery in which a fluid collection or infection develops at the surgical site, causing pain, swelling and wound discharge.
symptoms_in_common: Infraumbilical mass at the surgical site
symptoms_not_in_common: Afebrile
Mass is semisolid and enhancing rather than a fluid collection
Malignant cells in resected omentum
Synaptophysin and PGP 9.5 positivity
EWSR1 rearrangement

data.diagnosis: Clear cell sarcoma-like tumor of the gastrointestinal tract (malignant gastrointestinal neuroectodermal tumor)
data.description: A rare aggressive sarcoma of the bowel wall or mesentery with neuroectodermal differentiation, harboring EWSR1-ATF1 or EWSR1-CREB1 fusions, positive for S100 and SOX10 and often synaptophysin, negative for melanocytic markers.
symptoms_in_common: Intra-abdominal malignant tumor with neural/neuroendocrine differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: Usually arises in the small bowel wall rather than omentum/abdominal wall
No S100 or SOX10 positivity reported
Diffuse membranous CD99-like staining is not typical
Presentation as incarcerated umbilical hernia with umbilical secretion

data.description: 50-year-old woman with right nasal congestion and right parotid swelling for an unspecified duration, unresponsive to antibiotics and steroids. Exam and nasal endoscopy showed right-predominant adenoid pad swelling; CT demonstrated a 4.1 cm nasopharyngeal soft tissue mass. She had no significant past medical history and was a current smoker with a 35 pack-year history. Initial biopsy showed atypical lymphoid hyperplasia with scattered large atypical cells; flow cytometry showed no clonal B cells. After adenoidectomy, MRI at 3 months showed recurrent mass. Repeat endoscopic excision showed a nodular infiltrate of small lymphocytes. PET-CT showed FDG uptake confined to the nasopharynx without lymphadenopathy, and bone marrow biopsy was negative.

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma of the nasopharynx, possibly lymphocyte-rich subtype
data.description: A lymphoma characterized by scattered Hodgkin/Reed–Sternberg cells in a reactive inflammatory background. The large atypical cells and apparent CD30 and CD15 positivity favor this diagnosis; additional immunophenotyping is needed for confirmation and subtyping.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent unilateral nasal congestion with a large nasopharyngeal mass
Scattered large atypical cells within a predominantly small-lymphocyte infiltrate
Apparent CD30 and CD15 staining of large atypical cells
Negative B-cell flow cytometry, which does not exclude Hodgkin lymphoma
Localized FDG uptake and negative bone marrow, compatible with localized disease
symptoms_not_in_common: An isolated nasopharyngeal presentation without lymphadenopathy is rare
Right parotid swelling is not a characteristic feature of isolated nasopharyngeal Hodgkin lymphoma
