data.description: A large pituitary adenoma can compress the optic chiasm and impair normal pituitary function. A prolactin-secreting adenoma can additionally suppress gonadal function, causing reduced testosterone and occasionally gynecomastia.
symptoms_in_common: Small testes and decreased facial hair
Visual-field abnormalities potentially caused by optic chiasm compression
Low blood pressure and constipation potentially caused by hypopituitarism
Absence of nipple discharge does not exclude a prolactinoma in a male
symptoms_not_in_common: Central diabetes insipidus is unusual in an untreated pituitary adenoma
Separate pineal-region and ventricular enhancing lesions are not explained by a typical pituitary adenoma
Remote childhood seizures are not characteristic
Posterior anal fissure and coccygeal lump are unrelated to a typical pituitary adenoma

data.diagnosis: Intracranial germ cell tumor (germinoma, bifocal suprasellar and pineal)
data.description: Malignant germ cell tumor of midline brain structures in adolescents and young adults, often involving the suprasellar and pineal regions simultaneously, causing diabetes insipidus, hypopituitarism and visual field defects; hCG secretion may cause gynecomastia.
symptoms_in_common: Polydipsia and polyuria (central diabetes insipidus) preceding other symptoms by years
Later improvement of polyuria, possibly from developing adrenal insufficiency
Hypogonadism with decreased facial hair and small testes
Low blood pressure and constipation suggesting cortisol and thyroid deficiency
Blurred vision with visual field defects
Enhancing sellar/suprasellar mass with pineal region and ventricular wall lesions on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Childhood seizures (probably unrelated epilepsy)
Anal fissure
Coccygeal lump with central punctum (likely pilonidal sinus)
Very long indolent course

data.description: Clonal proliferation of Langerhans-type dendritic cells that commonly infiltrates the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, causing diabetes insipidus and anterior pituitary deficiencies; may also involve bone, skin and lung.
symptoms_in_common: Diabetes insipidus as the early feature
Hypogonadism with small testes and reduced facial hair
Low blood pressure and constipation from hypopituitarism
symptoms_not_in_common: Pineal involvement is uncommon
No bone lesions, skin rash or lung disease described
Gynecomastia not specifically explained beyond hypogonadism
Childhood seizures
Bulky sellar mass with visual field defect is less typical

data.description: Granulomatous inflammatory disease that can involve the hypothalamus, pituitary stalk, leptomeninges and ependyma, producing diabetes insipidus, hypopituitarism, visual disturbance and seizures.
symptoms_in_common: Multifocal enhancing midline and periventricular lesions
Low blood pressure from possible adrenal insufficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: No pulmonary, skin, ocular uveitis or lymph node involvement
Discrete pineal mass is unusual
Gynecomastia not typical
Seizures remitted in childhood long before other symptoms
Coccygeal lump and anal fissure

data.description: Benign but locally aggressive epithelial tumor of the sellar/suprasellar region arising from Rathke pouch remnants, presenting with hypopituitarism, diabetes insipidus, visual field defects and headache in children and young adults.
symptoms_in_common: Hypogonadism with small testes and decreased facial hair
Visual field defects and blurred vision
Low blood pressure and constipation from pituitary deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Concurrent pineal and ventricular wall lesions
Lesion appears solid and homogeneously enhancing rather than cystic or calcified
Gynecomastia is not typical
Childhood seizures
Diabetes insipidus is less often the presenting feature before surgery

data.description: Benign tumor of the anterior pituitary that can cause hypogonadism, gynecomastia, headaches and visual field defects through hormone secretion or mass effect.
symptoms_in_common: Hypogonadism with small testes and reduced facial hair
Low blood pressure and constipation from hypopituitarism
symptoms_not_in_common: Diabetes insipidus is rare at presentation
Pineal and periventricular lesions are not explained
No galactorrhea
Childhood seizures
Visual field defect is not a classic bitemporal hemianopia

data.description: 17-year-old male with high myopia and craniofacial/skeletal abnormalities. History includes pectus excavatum present at birth, dental crowding with class III dentofacial growth pattern and retroclined lower teeth at age 12, and a grade 3/6 systolic heart murmur noted at age 13. Height was at the 80th percentile until age 15, then plateaued at the 55th percentile. Current exam shows loss of normal upper spinal curvature and scoliosis; measurements: weight 66.3 kg, height 177.5 cm, head circumference 58.5 cm. Laboratory testing shows markedly elevated homocysteine and methionine with normal methylmalonic acid, vitamin B12, folate, hemoglobin, hematocrit, and MCV.

data.diagnosis: Classic homocystinuria due to cystathionine beta-synthase deficiency
data.description: An inherited defect in homocysteine metabolism causing elevated homocysteine and methionine, ocular abnormalities, skeletal deformities, osteoporosis, and increased thromboembolic risk. This is the strongest fit for the combined biochemical and clinical findings.
symptoms_in_common: Normal methylmalonic acid, vitamin B12, and folate
High myopia with apparent lens subluxation in the ocular images
Dental crowding and abnormal craniofacial growth
Apparent vertebral compression or biconcave deformity and low bone mineral density in the supplied imaging
Adolescent height plateau, potentially related to vertebral deformity
symptoms_not_in_common: A systolic heart murmur is not a defining feature and requires separate cardiac assessment
The specific class III dentofacial pattern is not diagnostic of this disorder

data.description: An inherited connective tissue disorder, usually caused by FBN1 variants, affecting the skeleton, ocular lenses, aorta, and cardiac valves.
symptoms_in_common: High myopia with apparent lens subluxation
Systolic murmur, potentially reflecting valvular disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated homocysteine and methionine are not explained by Marfan syndrome
Adolescent height plateau rather than persistent disproportionate linear growth
Pronounced vertebral deformity and low bone mineral density are less characteristic than in homocystinuria

data.description: An inherited collagen disorder characterized by high myopia, vitreoretinal abnormalities, craniofacial differences, and skeletal or joint disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated homocysteine and methionine
Apparent lens subluxation is less typical than vitreous abnormalities or retinal detachment
Congenital pectus excavatum is not a defining feature
Systolic heart murmur is not a core manifestation

data.description: A rare inherited connective tissue disorder associated with small spherical lenses, lenticular myopia, lens displacement, short stature, brachydactyly, and joint stiffness.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent lens displacement in the ocular images
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated homocysteine and methionine
Height of 177.5 cm rather than characteristic short stature
Pectus excavatum and scoliosis are not the characteristic skeletal pattern
Apparent low bone mineral density and vertebral compression are not defining features

data.description: A rare inherited homocysteine remethylation disorder that causes severe hyperhomocysteinemia, usually with low methionine and neurological or thromboembolic manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: Normal serum vitamin B12 and folate can occur despite impaired intracellular homocysteine remethylation
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated methionine strongly argues against this diagnosis because methionine is typically low
High myopia with apparent lens subluxation is not characteristic
Pectus excavatum, dental abnormalities, and scoliosis are not the typical presentation
Apparent vertebral compression and low bone mineral density are less characteristic than in classic homocystinuria
Systolic heart murmur is not a defining manifestation

data.description: Autosomal recessive disorder of methionine metabolism causing accumulation of homocysteine and methionine, leading to ectopia lentis, high myopia, marfanoid skeletal changes, osteoporosis, thromboembolism and variable intellectual disability.
symptoms_in_common: Normal methylmalonic acid, B12 and folate
Scoliosis and loss of normal spinal curvature
Low bone mineral density with biconcave vertebrae on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Grade 3/6 systolic murmur (valvular disease is not typical)
Pectus excavatum noted at birth (skeletal changes usually develop later)
Height plateau to 55th percentile rather than tall stature
No reported thromboembolic events or intellectual disability
Class III dentofacial growth pattern is not characteristic

data.description: Autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder due to FBN1 mutations, characterized by tall stature, long limbs, ectopia lentis, myopia, chest wall deformity, scoliosis, mitral valve prolapse and aortic root dilation.
symptoms_in_common: Scoliosis and loss of thoracic kyphosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated homocysteine
Elevated methionine
Low bone mineral density with vertebral compression changes
Height not markedly tall and plateaued at 55th percentile
Class III dentofacial pattern (retrognathia is more typical)

data.diagnosis: Remethylation defect (severe MTHFR deficiency or cobalamin metabolism disorder such as cblC/cblE/cblG)
data.description: Inherited defects in remethylation of homocysteine to methionine causing hyperhomocysteinemia with low or normal methionine; cobalamin C type also has methylmalonic acidemia; features include neurologic disease, thrombosis and sometimes megaloblastic anemia.
symptoms_in_common: Normal B12 and folate levels (can be seen in intracellular defects)
Possible marfanoid features and scoliosis in some cases
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated methionine (expected low or normal)
Normal methylmalonic acid (argues against cblC)
Normal hemoglobin and MCV
Lens subluxation and high myopia
Pectus excavatum
Osteoporosis
No neurologic deficits reported

data.description: Autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder from TGF-beta pathway mutations, with arterial aneurysms and tortuosity, craniofacial features (hypertelorism, bifid uvula, cleft palate), pectus deformity and scoliosis.
symptoms_in_common: Systolic murmur (possible valvular or aortic disease)
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated homocysteine and methionine
Lens subluxation (not a feature)
High myopia is uncommon
Class III dentofacial pattern

data.description: Hereditary collagenopathy (COL2A1/COL11A1) causing congenital high myopia, vitreoretinal degeneration with retinal detachment, midface hypoplasia, cleft palate/Pierre Robin sequence, hearing loss and early arthropathy with spinal abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Craniofacial abnormalities (midface hypoplasia can give a relative class III appearance)
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly elevated homocysteine and methionine
Lens subluxation
Pectus excavatum
Low bone mineral density
No hearing loss, cleft palate or joint disease reported

data.description: Male infant born at term to healthy, nonconsanguineous parents, with no family history of immune deficiency, presenting at 20 days of age with profound T-cell lymphopenia on newborn screening (absent TRECs). Physical findings included neonatal teeth, hypotonia, umbilical hernia, and erythematous psoriasiform dermatitis. Imaging showed wormian skull bones, mild pulmonary artery stenosis, and absence of the corpus callosum. No evidence of maternal engraftment.

A rare genetic disorder affecting T-cell development and development of the brain and other organs. It can occur through a de novo variant despite a negative family history and is a strong consideration for this combination of findings.
symptoms_in_common: Profound neonatal T-cell lymphopenia with absent TRECs
Cranial skeletal abnormalities, including wormian bones
Abundant hair and apparent hypertrichosis in the photographs
symptoms_not_in_common: Psoriasiform dermatitis is not a defining feature
Umbilical hernia is nonspecific

data.diagnosis: Complete DiGeorge syndrome with congenital athymia
data.description: Severe impairment of thymic development, sometimes associated with chromosome 22q11.2 deletion or other developmental defects, resulting in profound T-cell deficiency and congenital anomalies.
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Agenesis of the corpus callosum is not a characteristic finding
Apparent hypertrichosis
Psoriasiform dermatitis is not typical of classic complete athymia

data.description: A genetic defect in thymic epithelial development that can cause profound T-cell immunodeficiency. Classic biallelic FOXN1 deficiency also causes alopecia and nail dystrophy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Abundant hair and apparent hypertrichosis, rather than the alopecia typical of classic FOXN1 deficiency
Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Agenesis of the corpus callosum
Pulmonary artery stenosis
Umbilical hernia

data.diagnosis: CHD7-related CHARGE syndrome with severe thymic hypoplasia
data.description: A developmental syndrome that can affect the eyes, heart, upper airway, ears, genitalia, and nervous system. Severe thymic hypoplasia or athymia can occasionally produce profound T-cell deficiency.
symptoms_in_common: Profound T-cell lymphopenia with absent TRECs when athymia is present
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Psoriasiform dermatitis
Apparent hypertrichosis
Umbilical hernia

data.diagnosis: Omenn syndrome due to hypomorphic severe combined immunodeficiency
data.description: A form of severe combined immunodeficiency in which a small population of abnormal, activated T cells causes inflammatory skin disease. The absence of maternal engraftment makes maternal-cell-mediated dermatitis less likely but does not establish Omenn syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Severe impairment of normal T-cell development
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Agenesis of the corpus callosum
Pulmonary artery stenosis
Umbilical hernia
Apparent hypertrichosis

data.description: Disorder caused by a de novo heterozygous dominant-negative BCL11B variant, a transcription factor required for T-cell and neuronal development; it produces T-cell-deficient SCID with multisystem anomalies including neonatal teeth, craniofacial dysmorphism, dermatitis and absent corpus callosum.
symptoms_in_common: Profound T-cell lymphopenia with absent TRECs
Healthy nonconsanguineous parents with no family history (de novo)
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild pulmonary artery stenosis (not a consistently reported feature)
Generalized hypertrichosis on the back (not a core feature)

data.description: Developmental defect of the third and fourth pharyngeal pouches causing thymic aplasia or hypoplasia, conotruncal heart defects, hypocalcemia and facial dysmorphism; the complete form presents with absent T cells on newborn screening and may become atypical with an eczematous rash.
symptoms_in_common: Profound T-cell lymphopenia with absent TRECs
Dermatitis (as seen in atypical complete DiGeorge)
Usually de novo with no family history
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Absence of the corpus callosum
Hypertrichosis
No hypocalcemia or cleft palate reported

data.description: Multiple-anomaly syndrome with coloboma, heart defects, choanal atresia, growth and developmental retardation, genital and ear anomalies; a subset has thymic aplasia giving a SCID-like T-cell-negative phenotype.
symptoms_in_common: Profound T-cell lymphopenia with absent TRECs (thymic aplasia in a subset)
Brain malformation including corpus callosum anomalies (occasionally)
De novo occurrence with healthy parents
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Psoriasiform dermatitis
Umbilical hernia
Hypertrichosis
No coloboma, choanal atresia or ear anomalies described

data.diagnosis: Omenn syndrome (leaky SCID, e.g., hypomorphic RAG1/RAG2 variants)
data.description: Form of leaky SCID in which oligoclonal autoreactive T cells infiltrate skin and other organs, causing erythroderma, alopecia, lymphadenopathy, hepatosplenomegaly, eosinophilia and elevated IgE.
symptoms_in_common: No maternal engraftment (rash arises from autologous T cells)
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound T-cell lymphopenia (T-cell counts are usually normal or raised from oligoclonal expansion)
Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Absence of the corpus callosum
Pulmonary artery stenosis
Hypotonia
Umbilical hernia
Abundant hair and hypertrichosis (Omenn typically causes alopecia)
Nonconsanguineous parents (autosomal recessive, though still possible)

data.description: Defect of the thymic epithelial transcription factor FOXN1 causing athymia with T-cell-negative SCID, congenital alopecia and nail dystrophy; it can develop an Omenn-like erythroderma.
symptoms_in_common: Profound T-cell lymphopenia with absent TRECs
Occasional central nervous system malformations reported
symptoms_not_in_common: Abundant scalp hair and hypertrichosis (alopecia universalis expected)
Neonatal teeth
Wormian skull bones
Pulmonary artery stenosis
Absence of the corpus callosum
Umbilical hernia
Hypotonia
Nonconsanguineous parents (typically autosomal recessive)

data.description: 28-year-old man with abdominal pain and diarrhea (10–12 watery stools/day) after completing azithromycin for pneumonia. Six weeks later, after bowel habits returned to baseline, he developed 3 weeks of abdominal discomfort relieved by bowel movements with increased stool frequency (4–5 formed stools/day). At the second presentation, vital signs and physical examination were unremarkable. Stool PCR for *Clostridium difficile* was positive; CBC and albumin were normal.

A provisional diagnosis of altered bowel function following an acute intestinal infection. Abdominal discomfort associated with defecation and changed stool frequency supports this possibility, although the reported duration is too short to meet formal IBS criteria. Positive C. difficile PCR may reflect colonization rather than active infection.
symptoms_in_common: Prior episode of acute watery diarrhea
Subsequent abdominal discomfort relieved by bowel movements
Normal vital signs, physical examination, CBC, and albumin
symptoms_not_in_common: Initial episode of 10–12 watery stools daily is more suggestive of acute infection or antibiotic-associated diarrhea than IBS itself

data.description: An antibiotic-associated, toxin-mediated colonic infection that typically causes new watery diarrhea and abdominal pain. The initial episode is compatible, but PCR alone does not establish active infection, particularly when current stools are formed.
symptoms_in_common: Initial abdominal pain and 10–12 watery stools daily
Positive stool PCR for C. difficile
symptoms_not_in_common: Current stools are formed rather than watery
Bowel habits returned to baseline before the second episode
Current discomfort is relieved by bowel movements
Normal CBC and unremarkable examination provide no evidence of significant inflammatory illness, although they do not exclude mild infection

data.description: Diarrhea caused by antibiotic-related disruption of intestinal microbiota rather than C. difficile toxin production. This could explain the initial illness, with residual bowel disturbance afterward.
symptoms_in_common: Initial watery stools and abdominal pain
Normal CBC, albumin, vital signs, and examination at the later presentation
symptoms_not_in_common: A symptom-free interval followed by delayed recurrence is less typical of uncomplicated antibiotic-associated diarrhea
Current formed stools do not represent ongoing diarrhea
Defecation-related discomfort suggests a post-infectious functional bowel disorder

data.description: A functional bowel disorder characterized by recurrent loose or watery stools without predominant abdominal pain. It is less likely here because current stools are formed, discomfort is prominent, and the duration is insufficient for formal diagnostic criteria.
symptoms_in_common: Normal physical examination, CBC, and albumin
No reported systemic illness at the second presentation
symptoms_not_in_common: Current stools are formed rather than loose or watery
Abdominal discomfort relieved by defecation favors an IBS-like pattern
The initial severe episode occurred after antibiotic exposure
Only three weeks of current symptoms

data.description: Chronic intestinal inflammation, including Crohn disease and ulcerative colitis, that can cause abdominal pain and frequent diarrhea. This is a lower-probability alternative; normal laboratory results do not completely exclude mild disease.
symptoms_in_common: Episodes of increased stool frequency and diarrhea
symptoms_not_in_common: Current stools are formed
Discomfort is relieved by bowel movements
Symptoms began in close association with antibiotic exposure
Normal CBC and albumin and an unremarkable examination are less supportive of active inflammatory disease
Return to baseline bowel habits between episodes

diagnoses.name: Clostridioides difficile colonization
diagnoses.title: Intestinal infections due to Clostridioides difficile

data.diagnosis: Post-infectious irritable bowel syndrome (with C. difficile colonization)
data.description: Functional bowel disorder that arises after an episode of infectious gastroenteritis, including C. difficile infection. It causes abdominal pain related to defecation and altered stool frequency or form without active infection. C. difficile PCR can stay positive after the infection resolves because it detects the toxin gene in colonized patients.
symptoms_in_common: abdominal discomfort relieved by bowel movements
onset after an acute diarrheal illness
bowel habits returned to baseline before the new symptoms
normal vital signs and physical examination
symptoms_not_in_common: 3-week symptom duration is shorter than the formal Rome IV chronicity criteria
positive C. difficile stool PCR is not a feature of IBS itself

data.description: Return of toxin-mediated colitis, usually within 2-8 weeks of the initial episode. It typically presents with watery diarrhea, abdominal cramping, and often leukocytosis.
symptoms_in_common: positive stool PCR for C. difficile
prior episode of profuse watery diarrhea
timing within the usual recurrence window
symptoms_not_in_common: stools are formed rather than watery
pain relieved by defecation
normal CBC without leukocytosis
normal albumin
no fever or abdominal tenderness

data.diagnosis: Asymptomatic C. difficile carriage with an unrelated functional bowel disorder
data.description: Persistent colonization with toxigenic C. difficile without active toxin-mediated disease. PCR remains positive, and the current symptoms would come from a separate functional cause rather than from the organism.
symptoms_in_common: recent antibiotic exposure and prior diarrheal illness
symptoms_not_in_common: abdominal discomfort and increased stool frequency are not explained by carriage alone
close timing after the diarrheal illness makes an unrelated cause less likely

data.diagnosis: Inflammatory bowel disease (Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis)
data.description: Chronic immune-mediated inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract. It can first appear or flare after an enteric infection, and patients with it are prone to C. difficile infection.
symptoms_not_in_common: formed, non-bloody stools
normal CBC without anemia or leukocytosis
normal albumin
no weight loss, fever or nocturnal symptoms reported
unremarkable examination
pain relieved by defecation suggests a functional cause
complete return to baseline between episodes

data.diagnosis: Post-infectious bile acid malabsorption or secondary lactose intolerance
data.description: Transient malabsorption of bile acids or disaccharides after infectious enteritis or antibiotic-related disruption of the gut flora. It causes increased stool frequency and abdominal discomfort.
symptoms_in_common: onset after an infectious or antibiotic-associated diarrheal illness
symptoms_not_in_common: stools are formed rather than loose or watery
no reported bloating, flatulence or link to dairy or fatty meals
6-week symptom-free interval before onset
positive C. difficile PCR is not explained by this diagnosis

data.description: 14-month-old girl with a 3-month history of recurrent episodic vomiting beginning at 11 months, with four 3–5-day episodes associated with lethargy, decreased oral intake, and intermittent diarrhea. Over the same period, she had developmental regression, no longer attempting to walk and instead crawling unsteadily with occasional falls. Parents reported brief morning episodes of symmetric “shakes” lasting seconds to 10 minutes without loss of consciousness. Born full-term without complications. On exam, she was alert and interactive but had frontal bossing, a full fontanelle with visible pulsations when supine, and head circumference 51.5 cm. Neurologic exam showed decreased leg tone with brisk 3+ patellar reflexes and flexor plantar responses; eye movements and pupils were normal, with no nystagmus or gaze limitation.

data.diagnosis: Obstructive hydrocephalus due to cerebral aqueduct stenosis or an aqueductal web
data.description: Narrowing or a thin membrane in the cerebral aqueduct blocks cerebrospinal fluid flow. This is the leading possibility: the MRI appears to show marked lateral and third ventricular enlargement with a relatively small fourth ventricle and possible aqueductal obstruction. Symptomatic hydrocephalus requires urgent pediatric neurosurgical assessment.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive macrocephaly with head circumference crossing growth percentiles
Frontal bossing and a full fontanelle
Recurrent vomiting, lethargy, and reduced oral intake
Decreased leg tone with brisk patellar reflexes
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea is not explained by aqueductal obstruction
Brief symmetric shaking episodes without loss of consciousness are nonspecific

data.diagnosis: Tectal plate glioma causing obstructive hydrocephalus
data.description: A typically slow-growing midbrain tumor can compress the cerebral aqueduct, causing hydrocephalus before prominent focal neurological signs appear. The supplied images do not establish a tectal mass, making this less likely than intrinsic aqueductal obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Vomiting and lethargy from elevated intracranial pressure
Progressive macrocephaly and a full fontanelle
Loss of motor milestones and gait instability
Lateral and third ventricular enlargement compatible with aqueductal obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea is not typical
Symmetric shaking episodes are not characteristic
Normal eye movements and absence of gaze limitation provide no support for a dorsal midbrain syndrome

data.diagnosis: Intracranial arachnoid cyst causing obstructive hydrocephalus
data.description: A cerebrospinal-fluid-filled cyst near the third ventricle or aqueduct can obstruct fluid circulation and produce progressive or intermittently symptomatic hydrocephalus. A discrete obstructing cyst is not clearly demonstrated in the supplied images.
symptoms_in_common: Frontal bossing and a full fontanelle
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea is not typical
Brief symmetric shakes without impaired awareness are not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: Impaired absorption of cerebrospinal fluid causes ventricular enlargement without a focal intraventricular obstruction, sometimes following infection or hemorrhage. It can explain the clinical syndrome, but the apparent aqueductal abnormality and relatively small fourth ventricle favor obstructive hydrocephalus.
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea is not directly explained
Symmetric shaking spells are nonspecific
The apparent focal aqueductal obstruction on MRI is not typical of communicating hydrocephalus

data.diagnosis: Posterior fossa tumor causing obstructive hydrocephalus
data.description: A cerebellar or fourth ventricular tumor, such as an ependymoma, can block cerebrospinal fluid flow and cause vomiting, balance impairment, and hydrocephalus. No clear posterior fossa mass is visible in the supplied images, so this is a lower-priority alternative.
symptoms_in_common: Loss of previously attempted motor milestones
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea is not typical
Brief symmetric shaking episodes are not characteristic
The apparent aqueduct-level obstruction without a visible posterior fossa mass is less supportive

diagnoses.name: Aqueductal stenosis
diagnoses.title: Stenosis of the aqueduct of Sylvius

data.diagnosis: Obstructive hydrocephalus due to aqueductal stenosis (aqueductal web/late-presenting congenital)
data.description: Narrowing or a membranous web of the cerebral aqueduct blocks CSF flow, causing triventricular enlargement (lateral and third ventricles) with a normal-sized fourth ventricle, progressive macrocephaly and raised intracranial pressure.
symptoms_in_common: Head circumference rapidly crossing percentiles to 51.5 cm
Frontal bossing and full pulsatile fontanelle
Motor regression with unsteady crawling and falls
Decreased leg tone with brisk patellar reflexes
MRI showing marked lateral and third ventricular dilation with obstruction/web at the aqueduct (arrow), a normal fourth ventricle and transependymal CSF seepage
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent diarrhea
Brief morning symmetric shaking episodes
No sunsetting eyes or upgaze limitation, which are often present
Onset of symptoms as late as 11 months rather than in the neonatal period

data.diagnosis: Posterior fossa tumor (e.g., medulloblastoma, ependymoma, pilocytic astrocytoma)
data.description: Most common group of solid brain tumors in young children; they obstruct the fourth ventricle or aqueduct, causing hydrocephalus, morning vomiting and ataxia.
symptoms_in_common: Unsteadiness with falls and loss of motor milestones
symptoms_not_in_common: No posterior fossa mass visible on MRI
Fourth ventricle not dilated or distorted
No nystagmus or cranial nerve deficits
Intermittent diarrhea

data.diagnosis: Tectal plate glioma or pineal region tumor
data.description: Small, often low-grade midbrain tectal or pineal region lesions that compress the aqueduct and cause triventricular obstructive hydrocephalus.
symptoms_in_common: Triventricular hydrocephalus with obstruction at the aqueduct level
Vomiting and lethargy from raised intracranial pressure
symptoms_not_in_common: No tectal thickening or enhancing pineal mass apparent on imaging
No Parinaud syndrome (normal upgaze and pupils)
Typically presents in older children
Diarrhea

data.diagnosis: Post-hemorrhagic or post-infectious hydrocephalus (acquired aqueductal obstruction/gliosis)
data.description: Scarring of the aqueduct or arachnoid granulations after intraventricular hemorrhage or meningitis/ventriculitis, causing obstructive or communicating hydrocephalus.
symptoms_not_in_common: Full-term birth without complications
No history of meningitis, hemorrhage or trauma
No hemosiderin evident on susceptibility-type sequence
Normal head growth in early infancy before acceleration

data.diagnosis: Chiari I malformation or other posterior fossa malformation with hydrocephalus (e.g., Dandy-Walker spectrum)
data.description: Structural hindbrain anomalies that impair CSF outflow at the fourth ventricular outlets or foramen magnum, leading to hydrocephalus and cerebellar or long-tract signs.
symptoms_not_in_common: Posterior fossa, cerebellum and fourth ventricle appear normal on MRI
No tonsillar herniation or posterior fossa cyst
No nystagmus or lower cranial nerve dysfunction
Diarrhea and shaking episodes

data.description: 47-year-old female presented to emergency department after being hit while skiing by another skier at high speed from behind. Immediate pain and marked general swelling of the knee joint occurred after impact. Unable to bear weight. Physical exam showed neurovascularly intact limb with no broken skin. No relevant medical, family, or social history.

data.diagnosis: Bicondylar tibial plateau fracture with metaphyseal extension
data.description: An intra-articular fracture involving both sides of the upper tibia. The supplied radiographs suggest a complex proximal tibial fracture with extension toward the metaphysis; CT would clarify the fracture pattern and displacement.
symptoms_in_common: Radiographic fracture lines involving the proximal tibia
Intact skin and preserved neurovascular function are compatible with a closed fracture

data.description: A fracture of the tibial spine where the anterior cruciate ligament attaches. It can occur with traumatic knee loading and may accompany a tibial plateau fracture.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent disruption of the intercondylar region on the radiographs
symptoms_not_in_common: The extensive proximal tibial fracture pattern is not explained by an isolated tibial spine avulsion

data.description: A traumatic tear of the ligament that limits forward movement of the tibia. Skiing injuries commonly cause this injury, which may coexist with a tibial plateau fracture; radiographs cannot establish a ligament tear.
symptoms_in_common: Rapid marked swelling compatible with hemarthrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: The visible proximal tibial fracture is not explained by an isolated ligament rupture

data.description: A traumatic tear of the ligament that limits backward movement of the tibia, typically caused by force on the anterior tibia or severe knee bending. It is a possible associated injury, but the direction of the collision alone does not establish this mechanism.
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive proximal tibial fracture lines are not explained by an isolated posterior cruciate ligament rupture
Immediate marked generalized swelling is less characteristic of an isolated posterior cruciate ligament injury

data.description: A tear of the knee's fibrocartilage caused by twisting or compression. Meniscal injury can accompany tibial plateau fractures, although it cannot be confirmed on these radiographs.
symptoms_in_common: High-energy injury capable of compressing the meniscus
symptoms_not_in_common: Immediate marked generalized swelling is less typical of an isolated meniscal tear
The radiographic proximal tibial fracture is not explained by an isolated meniscal tear

diagnoses.name: Tibial plateau fracture
diagnoses.title: Fracture of lower end of tibia[Tibial Plateau]

data.description: Intra-articular fracture of the proximal tibia caused by high-energy axial load combined with varus/valgus or shear forces, common in skiing collisions; often produces lipohemarthrosis and may involve the posterior plateau when the impact comes from behind on a flexed knee.
symptoms_in_common: Marked knee swelling consistent with hemarthrosis
Radiographic fracture lines in the proximal tibia extending to the articular surface/intercondylar region
Closed injury with intact neurovascular status
symptoms_not_in_common: No obvious major articular depression or condylar widening on the AP view
No neurovascular compromise or compartment syndrome signs, which can accompany high-energy patterns

data.diagnosis: Tibial eminence (intercondylar spine) avulsion fracture / ACL avulsion
data.description: Avulsion of the ACL insertion at the tibial intercondylar eminence, more common in children but seen in adults after high-energy trauma such as skiing, often associated with other plateau or ligament injuries.
symptoms_in_common: Pain and inability to bear weight
Irregularity/lucency around the tibial spines on the AP radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Adult age (more typical in children and adolescents)
Fracture line appears to extend into the proximal tibial metaphysis, beyond an isolated eminence avulsion
Impact from behind is more of a direct/shear mechanism than the typical hyperextension or twisting mechanism

data.diagnosis: Posterior cruciate ligament injury with tibial avulsion fracture
data.description: Avulsion of the PCL insertion from the posterior tibial plateau, caused by forces displacing the tibia relative to the femur or by hyperflexion/hyperextension; seen on the lateral view as a posterior tibial fragment.
symptoms_in_common: Possible posterior tibial plateau fragment on the lateral view
symptoms_not_in_common: Typical mechanism is a blow to the anterior proximal tibia (dashboard-type), not a hit from behind
Isolated PCL injuries often cause less dramatic swelling and may still allow weight bearing
Fracture line on the AP view extends into the metaphysis, more than a simple avulsion

data.diagnosis: Multiligament knee injury (ACL/MCL tear, possible spontaneously reduced knee dislocation)
data.description: Rupture of one or more major knee ligaments from high-energy trauma, very common in skiing; may coexist with fractures and can represent a transient knee dislocation.
symptoms_not_in_common: Radiographs show bony fracture lines rather than a purely ligamentous injury
No vascular or peroneal nerve deficit, which frequently accompanies knee dislocation
No gross malalignment or joint incongruity on radiographs

data.diagnosis: Distal femoral condyle (osteochondral or Hoffa-type) fracture
data.description: Intra-articular fracture of the femoral condyle, including coronal-plane (Hoffa) fractures, caused by high-energy shear on a flexed knee; often subtle on AP radiographs and best seen on lateral views or CT.
symptoms_in_common: High-energy trauma to a likely flexed knee
Subtle oblique lucency over the femoral condyle on the AP view
symptoms_not_in_common: Most conspicuous radiographic abnormality is in the proximal tibia rather than the femur
No clear displaced femoral condylar fragment on the lateral view
Less common than tibial plateau fracture with this mechanism

data.description: A 60-year-old woman presented after sustaining direct trauma to the anterior neck from a fall. She developed progressively worsening hoarse voice, difficulty swallowing, and pain with neck movement. Physical examination revealed visible neck swelling with bruising tracking onto the anterior chest wall. There was no tenderness on palpation of the cervical spine. On flexible nasal endoscopy, swelling of the posterior pharyngeal wall was observed, indicating potential airway compromise.

Bleeding into the space behind the pharynx following neck trauma. This is the leading consideration given the marked prevertebral soft-tissue swelling on the supplied CT image and posterior pharyngeal bulging. An expanding hematoma can cause life-threatening airway obstruction and requires urgent airway assessment.
symptoms_in_common: Direct blunt trauma to the anterior neck
Bruising tracking onto the anterior chest wall
Posterior pharyngeal wall swelling with potential airway compromise

data.diagnosis: Traumatic cervical ligament injury with prevertebral hematoma
data.description: Injury to cervical supporting ligaments, particularly the anterior longitudinal ligament, can produce bleeding and substantial prevertebral swelling. It may occur without an obvious fracture or cervical spine tenderness; dedicated imaging review and sometimes MRI are needed.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent external bruising extending onto the anterior chest wall is less typical of an isolated ligament injury

data.diagnosis: Blunt laryngeal injury with possible laryngeal cartilage fracture
data.description: Direct anterior neck trauma can injure the laryngeal cartilage and surrounding tissues, causing hematoma, edema, vocal dysfunction, and airway narrowing. The supplied image alone does not establish a cartilage fracture.
symptoms_in_common: Direct trauma to the anterior neck
symptoms_not_in_common: Posterior pharyngeal wall swelling is less typical of an isolated laryngeal injury and suggests associated retropharyngeal or prevertebral injury

data.description: Blunt neck trauma can cause bleeding within or around the thyroid gland, producing an expanding anterior neck hematoma that compresses the airway or esophagus. This possibility requires confirmation with dedicated neck imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Bruising extending onto the anterior chest wall
symptoms_not_in_common: Posterior pharyngeal wall swelling is less typical of a localized thyroid hemorrhage
Pain specifically provoked by neck movement is less characteristic

data.description: A tear in the hypopharyngeal wall after blunt neck trauma can cause deep neck swelling and subsequent infection or mediastinitis. Confirmation generally requires evaluation for extraluminal air or a contrast leak; neither is established by the supplied image.
symptoms_not_in_common: Bruising tracking onto the anterior chest wall is more suggestive of spreading hemorrhage than an isolated pharyngeal perforation

data.description: Collection of blood in the retropharyngeal/prevertebral space after blunt neck trauma or hyperextension injury, sometimes associated with anterior osteophyte fracture or anterior longitudinal ligament tear; can cause progressive airway obstruction requiring a surgical airway.
symptoms_in_common: Direct anterior neck trauma from a fall
Bruising tracking onto the anterior chest wall (Capps triad feature)
Posterior pharyngeal wall swelling on endoscopy
Prevertebral soft tissue thickening on CT with anterior cervical osteophytes
symptoms_not_in_common: No cervical spine tenderness (an associated spinal injury often causes tenderness)

data.diagnosis: Cervical spine fracture / hyperextension injury with prevertebral hematoma
data.description: Fracture of a vertebral body or anterior osteophyte, or anterior longitudinal ligament rupture, typically in a degenerative or ankylosed spine after a fall, producing prevertebral bleeding and swelling.
symptoms_in_common: Degenerative cervical spine with anterior osteophytes and prevertebral swelling on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No tenderness on palpation of the cervical spine
No neurological deficits described
Bruising tracking to the anterior chest wall is more typical of a soft tissue hematoma
Mechanism was direct anterior neck trauma

data.description: Blunt injury to the laryngeal framework (thyroid or cricoid cartilage) causing endolaryngeal oedema or hematoma, voice change and potential airway obstruction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Swelling located on the posterior pharyngeal wall rather than the endolarynx
No subcutaneous emphysema or crepitus reported
No hemoptysis or stridor described
No obvious laryngeal framework disruption on the image

data.description: Traumatic tear of the hypopharynx or cervical oesophagus leading to air and fluid leakage into the deep neck spaces, with risk of retropharyngeal abscess and mediastinitis.
symptoms_not_in_common: No subcutaneous emphysema or significant retropharyngeal air
No fever or signs of sepsis
Extensive bruising tracking to the chest suggests bleeding rather than a leak
Rare after blunt low-energy trauma

data.diagnosis: Cervical vascular injury with expanding neck hematoma (e.g., carotid/vertebral or thyroid vessel injury)
data.description: Blunt injury to a cervical artery or thyroid vessels, causing an expanding deep neck hematoma that compresses the airway and pharynx; may be associated with dissection or pseudoaneurysm.
symptoms_in_common: Bruising extending to the chest wall
symptoms_not_in_common: No neurological deficits or stroke symptoms
No pulsatile mass, bruit or thrill described
Swelling centred in the retropharyngeal space rather than the lateral neck
No haemodynamic instability reported

data.description: 41-year-old man with morbid obesity, hyperlipidemia, and prior cholecystectomy, status post Roux-en-Y gastric bypass 8 years earlier, presented with epigastric and left upper quadrant abdominal pain worsened by eating, without melena or hematochezia; exam showed abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding, and initial labs were unremarkable. He later developed foul-smelling watery diarrhea 6–7 times daily with visible food particles, pale floating stools, increased flatus, and daily feculent eructation. Four months later, he presented with progressive weakness, myalgias, muscle cramps, and significant weight loss from 95.3 kg to 72.6 kg, appearing cachectic with dry mucous membranes, feculent breath, and diminished skin turgor.

data.diagnosis: Gastrocolic fistula following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
data.description: An abnormal connection between the gastric pouch and colon, allowing food to bypass the small intestine and colonic contents to reflux into the stomach. This is the leading diagnosis because the contrast images demonstrate communication between the gastric pouch and transverse colon.
symptoms_in_common: Daily feculent eructation and feculent breath
Foul-smelling watery diarrhea with visible food particles
Epigastric and left upper quadrant pain worsened by eating
Pale floating stools and increased flatus
Weakness, muscle cramps, and dehydration from gastrointestinal losses

data.diagnosis: Gastrojejunal marginal ulcer with fistulizing penetration
data.description: Ulceration at the gastrojejunal anastomosis after gastric bypass can cause postprandial pain and, rarely, penetrate adjacent colon to form a gastrocolic or gastrojejunocolic fistula. The endoscopic image appears to show an ulcerated area, although its exact anatomy cannot be established from this image alone.
symptoms_in_common: Feculent eructation if complicated by a fistula into the colon
Diarrhea and malnutrition if complicated by a fistula into the colon
symptoms_not_in_common: Profuse watery diarrhea is not typical of an uncomplicated marginal ulcer
Pale floating stools are not typical of an uncomplicated marginal ulcer
Feculent breath is not typical without fistulization

data.description: Excess bacteria in the small intestine, potentially promoted by altered anatomy after gastric bypass, can impair nutrient absorption and cause diarrhea and steatorrhea. It does not independently explain the fistula demonstrated on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Pale floating stools suggesting fat malabsorption
symptoms_not_in_common: Daily feculent eructation and feculent breath are unusual
Visible food particles with profound wasting suggest a more direct intestinal bypass mechanism

data.description: Inadequate pancreatic enzyme activity causes fat maldigestion, steatorrhea, and nutritional deficiencies; impaired mixing of food and pancreatic secretions after gastric bypass can contribute. This would not explain the demonstrated gastric-to-colonic communication.
symptoms_in_common: Weakness and muscle cramps associated with nutritional depletion
symptoms_not_in_common: Daily feculent eructation
Feculent breath
Prominent postprandial epigastric pain is not characteristic of enzyme insufficiency alone

data.description: Transmural inflammatory bowel disease can cause diarrhea, malnutrition, and abnormal connections between gastrointestinal segments, including rare gastrocolic fistulas. It is a less likely underlying cause here than a postoperative marginal-ulcer complication.
symptoms_in_common: Feculent eructation if an upper gastrointestinal-to-colonic fistula develops
symptoms_not_in_common: Pale floating stools are not a defining feature unless significant small-bowel malabsorption develops
Daily feculent breath is unusual without a rare upper gastrointestinal fistula
Visible food particles in stool are nonspecific rather than characteristic

data.diagnosis: Gastrocolic fistula secondary to marginal (anastomotic) ulcer after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass
data.description: An abnormal communication between the gastric pouch/gastrojejunal anastomosis and the transverse colon, usually caused by a penetrating marginal ulcer. Colonic contents reflux into the stomach and food bypasses the small bowel, producing feculent eructation, diarrhea, malabsorption and weight loss.
symptoms_in_common: Epigastric and left upper quadrant pain worsened by eating (marginal ulcer)
Endoscopic image showing an ulcer with whitish exudate
Foul-smelling watery diarrhea with undigested food particles
Weakness, myalgias and muscle cramps consistent with electrolyte depletion
Dehydration (dry mucous membranes, diminished skin turgor)
Contrast study showing a fistula from gastric pouch to transverse colon with filling of the descending colon
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of melena or hematochezia (bleeding may occur with marginal ulcer)
Unremarkable initial labs
Feculent vomiting not reported

data.diagnosis: Marginal ulcer (uncomplicated) at the gastrojejunal anastomosis
data.description: Peptic ulceration at or near the gastrojejunal anastomosis after gastric bypass, related to acid exposure, ischemia, NSAIDs, smoking or H. pylori.
symptoms_in_common: Some weight loss from food avoidance
symptoms_not_in_common: Feculent eructation and feculent breath
Profuse diarrhea with undigested food particles
Steatorrhea
Severe cachexia
Fistulous tract to the colon on contrast imaging
No melena or hematochezia

data.diagnosis: Small intestinal bacterial overgrowth (blind loop syndrome) after gastric bypass
data.description: Excess bacterial colonization of the small bowel, favored by altered anatomy and reduced gastric acid after bypass, causing bile salt deconjugation, malabsorption, bloating and diarrhea.
symptoms_in_common: Post-Roux-en-Y anatomy as a risk factor
Weakness and muscle cramps from nutrient and electrolyte deficiencies
symptoms_not_in_common: Feculent eructation and feculent breath
Visible undigested food in stool shortly after eating
Ulcer on endoscopy
Fistula on contrast study
Severity and rapidity of weight loss
Localized epigastric/left upper quadrant pain worsened by eating

data.diagnosis: Malignant gastrocolic fistula (gastric or transverse colon carcinoma)
data.description: A tumor of the stomach or transverse colon that invades the adjacent organ and creates a fistula, classically presenting with diarrhea, weight loss and feculent vomiting or eructation.
symptoms_in_common: Fistula between stomach and colon on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Relatively young age (41 years)
No melena or hematochezia
Endoscopy shows a benign-appearing ulcer rather than a mass
Prior gastric bypass provides a benign explanation (marginal ulcer)
No mass or obstruction described on imaging

data.diagnosis: Crohn's disease with fistulizing gastrocolic or enterocolic involvement
data.description: Chronic transmural inflammatory bowel disease that can cause ulcers, strictures and fistulas between bowel segments, with diarrhea, abdominal pain, malabsorption and weight loss.
symptoms_in_common: Feculent eructation possible with a gastrocolic fistula
symptoms_not_in_common: No prior history of inflammatory bowel disease
No hematochezia, perianal disease or extraintestinal manifestations
Solitary ulcer at a surgical anastomosis rather than skip lesions
Unremarkable initial labs (no inflammatory markers or anemia noted)
Gastric bypass offers a more direct cause

data.description: 18-year-old pregnant woman. Healthy with no history of smoking, drug abuse, or family history of chromosomal disease or encephalodysplasia. Experienced mild flu-like symptoms during first month of pregnancy that resolved after three days without medication.

advanced.reason: first diagnosis had no list: the web does not offer it

data.description: 73-year-old man with 2 days of worsening weakness, lethargy, chills, diarrhea, decreased oral intake, confusion, irritability, and decreased responsiveness, progressing to near-catatonia and inability to get out of bed. He also had recurrent epistaxis, chest and left arm pain, and a history of diabetes mellitus, atrial fibrillation, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, exudative pericardial effusion, hyperlipidemia, pancytopenia, obstructive sleep apnea, GERD, headaches, and lifelong recurrent epistaxis; family history was notable for recurrent epistaxis in his mother and daughter. On examination he was somnolent but arousable, oriented with waxing and waning attention, with dry mucous membranes, dried blood around the nares, multiple telangiectasias on the face/lips/torso, nonblanching cherry angiomas on the chest, irregularly irregular heart sounds, a liver edge palpable 2 cm below the right costal margin, and chronic venous insufficiency changes in the legs.

data.diagnosis: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia with hepatic vascular malformations
data.description: An inherited vascular disorder causing mucocutaneous telangiectasias, recurrent bleeding, and visceral vascular malformations. Hepatic shunting can contribute to heart failure and encephalopathy. The abdominal images suggest abnormal dilated vessels and shunting, although formal radiologic interpretation is needed.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent epistaxis in his mother and daughter
Multiple telangiectasias on the face, lips, and torso
Confusion and decreased responsiveness potentially related to hepatic shunting
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute diarrhea and chills are not characteristic manifestations
Pancytopenia is not a defining feature
Exudative pericardial effusion is not typical

data.diagnosis: Portosystemic encephalopathy from an intrahepatic or extrahepatic portosystemic shunt
data.description: Diversion of portal blood around the liver can allow ammonia and other neurotoxins to reach the brain, even without cirrhosis. The vascular abnormalities on the supplied images raise this possibility; dehydration or gastrointestinal illness could precipitate an acute episode.
symptoms_in_common: Severe weakness and inability to get out of bed
Decreased oral intake and dehydration as possible precipitants
symptoms_not_in_common: Familial recurrent epistaxis is not explained by encephalopathy itself
Mucocutaneous telangiectasias require an underlying vascular diagnosis
Chills and diarrhea suggest a separate precipitating illness
Chest and left arm pain are not typical

data.description: Advanced chronic liver disease can produce portal hypertension, cytopenias, bleeding, and impaired detoxification, resulting in altered mental status. This is an alternative to noncirrhotic shunt-related encephalopathy, but cirrhosis is not established by the supplied information.
symptoms_in_common: Dehydration as a possible encephalopathy trigger
symptoms_not_in_common: Lifelong epistaxis across multiple generations favors an inherited vascular disorder
Lip and facial telangiectasias are more suggestive of hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
Acute chills and diarrhea are not intrinsic features of cirrhosis
Chest and left arm pain are not typical

data.diagnosis: Acute infectious gastroenteritis with infection-associated delirium
data.description: An intestinal infection can cause diarrhea, chills, poor intake, and dehydration. In an older adult, systemic infection or its physiologic effects can produce marked delirium; sepsis would require additional clinical and laboratory evidence.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lifelong familial epistaxis
Multiple mucocutaneous telangiectasias
Abnormal abdominal vascular structures
Chronic pulmonary hypertension and heart failure
Chest and left arm pain are not typical of uncomplicated gastroenteritis

data.description: Fluid loss and inadequate intake can cause renal dysfunction or electrolyte disturbances that impair brain function. Diabetes also increases concern for a concurrent glucose disturbance; laboratory testing is necessary to identify the mechanism.
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent familial epistaxis
Mucocutaneous telangiectasias
Abdominal vascular malformations
Pancytopenia is not ordinarily explained by dehydration alone
Chills suggest an additional infectious trigger
Chest and left arm pain require a separate assessment

data.diagnosis: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (Osler-Weber-Rendu) with hepatic arteriovenous malformations and portosystemic shunting causing hepatic encephalopathy
data.description: Autosomal dominant vascular dysplasia causing mucocutaneous telangiectasias, recurrent epistaxis and visceral AVMs. Hepatic AVMs (arterioportal, arteriovenous, portovenous shunts) can cause high-output heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, portal hypertension and portosystemic encephalopathy, often precipitated by dehydration, infection or bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: family history of epistaxis in mother and daughter
telangiectasias on face, lips and torso
confusion, waxing and waning attention, somnolence, near-catatonia
dilated hepatic vessels with abnormal/pulsatile Doppler flow on ultrasound suggesting intrahepatic shunting
heart failure and pulmonary hypertension (high-output state)
pancytopenia (possible portal hypertension/hypersplenism, chronic blood loss)
precipitants present: diarrhea, dehydration, decreased oral intake
symptoms_not_in_common: chills
diarrhea
chest and left arm pain
exudative pericardial effusion
pneumatosis intestinalis of the right colon on CT

data.diagnosis: Acute mesenteric ischemia / ischemic colitis with pneumatosis intestinalis
data.description: Reduced intestinal blood flow from embolism (e.g., atrial fibrillation), thrombosis or low-flow states (heart failure, hypovolemia, vascular steal from shunts), leading to bowel wall injury, intramural gas, sepsis and altered mental status.
symptoms_in_common: intramural gas in the ascending colon on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: no prominent abdominal pain reported
recurrent epistaxis
telangiectasias
family history of epistaxis
hepatomegaly
chest and left arm pain

data.diagnosis: Sepsis from infectious colitis (e.g., Clostridioides difficile or bacterial enteritis) with septic/metabolic encephalopathy
data.description: Intestinal infection causing diarrhea, volume depletion and systemic inflammatory response, with delirium common in elderly patients; severe colitis may produce pneumatosis.
symptoms_in_common: confusion with waxing and waning attention
colonic abnormality with intramural gas on CT
diabetes and pancytopenia as predisposing factors
symptoms_not_in_common: recurrent epistaxis
telangiectasias
family history of epistaxis
hepatomegaly with abnormal hepatic vascular flow
chest and left arm pain
pulmonary hypertension

data.diagnosis: Cirrhosis with portal hypertension and hepatic encephalopathy (e.g., cardiac/congestive or NASH-related)
data.description: Chronic liver disease causing portal hypertension, hypersplenism, and neuropsychiatric dysfunction from ammonia and other toxins bypassing hepatic clearance; commonly precipitated by infection, dehydration or bleeding.
symptoms_in_common: right heart failure and pulmonary hypertension (congestive hepatopathy)
symptoms_not_in_common: lifelong and familial epistaxis
lip and mucosal telangiectasias in a familial pattern
chills
chest and left arm pain
pneumatosis intestinalis
no jaundice or ascites described

data.diagnosis: Brain abscess or stroke from paradoxical embolism via pulmonary arteriovenous malformation (or cardioembolic stroke from atrial fibrillation)
data.description: Pulmonary AVMs in HHT allow bacteria and thrombi to bypass the pulmonary filter, causing cerebral abscess or embolic stroke; atrial fibrillation is also a source of cardioembolic stroke. Presents with headache, altered mental status, and sometimes fever.
symptoms_in_common: features of HHT (epistaxis, telangiectasias, family history) that predispose to pulmonary AVMs
symptoms_not_in_common: no focal neurologic deficits described
diarrhea
hepatomegaly and abnormal hepatic vascular flow
pneumatosis intestinalis
pancytopenia
chest and left arm pain

data.description: 24-year-old man presents with severely itchy rash that spread over two months. Had previously used an over-the-counter cream containing clobetasol, ofloxacin, terbinafine, and ornidazole which helped initially.

data.diagnosis: Steroid-modified dermatophytosis (tinea incognito involving the groin and body)
data.description: A superficial fungal infection whose appearance and extent are altered by topical corticosteroids. This is the leading possibility given the annular plaques and prior clobetasol use; skin scrapings for fungal microscopy and culture can help confirm it.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple large, red, annular plaques on the groin, thighs, and lower abdomen
Peripheral scaling and partial central clearing visible in several plaques
Initial improvement with a steroid-containing cream followed by continued spread
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly incompatible feature is reported; some plaques have less distinct borders than untreated tinea, which steroid exposure can explain

data.description: An inflammatory dermatitis producing intensely itchy, coin-shaped, scaly plaques, sometimes resembling a fungal infection.
symptoms_in_common: Initial improvement with a corticosteroid-containing cream
symptoms_not_in_common: Large expanding rings with peripheral activity and partial central clearing are less typical
Marked concentration around the groin and adjacent thighs is less characteristic
Continued centrifugal spread despite a potent topical corticosteroid is less typical

data.description: A less common pattern of psoriasis in which inflammatory scaly plaques form rings; psoriasis can also involve the groin.
symptoms_in_common: Initial improvement with topical corticosteroid exposure
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent central clearing with narrow, active peripheral borders is more suggestive of fungal infection
Severe itching is less characteristic than in dermatophytosis or eczema
Progressive spreading after initial improvement with clobetasol is less typical of adequately treated psoriasis

data.description: A reactive inflammatory eruption causing slowly expanding ring-shaped patches, sometimes with a fine trailing scale inside the advancing edge.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe itching is less typical
Prominent groin involvement is less characteristic
The raised, visibly active outer borders favor dermatophytosis rather than the characteristic inner trailing scale

data.diagnosis: Allergic contact dermatitis from topical medication
data.description: A delayed allergic skin reaction to an ingredient in a topical product, causing itchy eczema that can persist or spread with repeated exposure.
symptoms_in_common: Exposure to a cream containing several medications
Initial suppression of inflammation by the cream's corticosteroid component
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple well-formed annular plaques with central clearing are not typical
Distinct expanding peripheral borders are more characteristic of dermatophytosis
The rash preceded the reported cream use, so contact allergy alone would not explain its initial onset

data.diagnosis: Tinea incognito (steroid-modified tinea cruris/corporis, possibly Trichophyton indotineae/mentagrophytes)
data.description: Dermatophyte infection of the skin whose appearance and extent are altered by topical corticosteroid use, often from fixed-dose combination creams; it becomes widespread, atypical and recalcitrant, sometimes with concentric rings (tinea pseudoimbricata).
symptoms_in_common: Involvement of groin, inner thighs and lower abdomen
Large annular and concentric (ring-within-ring) plaques with erythematous active borders
Initial improvement then spread after clobetasol-containing combination cream
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse, ill-defined erythema in some areas rather than classic sharply marginated rings
Hyperpigmentation and striae-like changes (attributable to steroid effect rather than the infection itself)

data.diagnosis: Classic tinea cruris (dermatophytosis without steroid modification)
data.description: Superficial fungal infection of the groin and upper inner thighs caused by Trichophyton or Epidermophyton species, presenting with pruritic annular plaques with a raised scaly border.
symptoms_in_common: Itchy rash in groin and inner thighs
Annular plaques with active scaly borders
Partial response to a terbinafine-containing cream
symptoms_not_in_common: Unusually extensive spread to abdomen and far down the thighs
Multiple concentric rings and lesions within lesions
Worsening despite antifungal-containing cream
History of potent steroid use modifying the picture

data.description: Chronic immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease with well-demarcated erythematous scaly plaques; the inverse form affects flexures such as the groin.
symptoms_in_common: Temporary improvement with a potent topical steroid (clobetasol)
symptoms_not_in_common: Annular lesions with central clearing and concentric rings
Peripheral active border rather than uniform plaque
Severe itch is less typical
No mention of extensor, scalp or nail involvement
Rapid centrifugal spread over two months

data.description: Eczematous inflammation presenting as itchy coin-shaped or ill-defined erythematous scaly plaques; contact dermatitis can result from topical medication ingredients.
symptoms_in_common: Use of a multi-ingredient topical cream (possible sensitiser)
symptoms_not_in_common: Annular lesions with raised advancing borders and central clearing
Concentric rings
Predominant groin-centred distribution spreading outward
Lack of oozing, crusting or vesiculation

data.description: Reactive figurate erythema with slowly expanding annular or polycyclic erythematous lesions, typically with a trailing scale inside the border, often on thighs and trunk.
symptoms_in_common: Annular and polycyclic expanding erythematous lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe pruritus (usually mild or absent)
Groin-centred onset
Concentric multiple rings with leading-edge scale
Clear relation to topical steroid use and partial antifungal response

data.description: A 52-year-old woman presented with a two-day history of lower back pain radiating into her left leg with associated leg weakness. She had a history of chronic back pain. Neurological examination revealed reduced power in her left leg (3/5), but was otherwise normal.

data.diagnosis: L4–L5 lumbar disc herniation with radiculopathy
data.description: Displacement of disc material can compress a lumbar nerve root, producing sciatica and weakness. The provided sagittal MRI appears to show a prominent posterior L4–L5 disc herniation, making this the leading possibility; axial images are needed to confirm left-sided nerve involvement. New 3/5 leg weakness warrants urgent clinical assessment.
symptoms_in_common: Lower back pain radiating into the left leg
Left leg weakness with power reduced to 3/5
Acute symptoms superimposed on chronic back pain

data.description: Degenerative disc and joint changes narrow the spinal canal or lateral recesses, potentially compressing nerve roots. The apparent L4–L5 disc protrusion may contribute to focal canal narrowing.
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt two-day onset is less typical than gradual or activity-related symptoms
Marked unilateral weakness with an otherwise normal neurological examination is less typical of diffuse central stenosis

data.diagnosis: Lumbar degenerative disc disease with foraminal stenosis
data.description: Disc degeneration and loss of disc height can narrow nerve-root exit openings and cause radiculopathy. Lower lumbar disc degeneration is suggested by the image, although foraminal narrowing cannot be established from this single view.
symptoms_in_common: Lower back pain radiating into the left leg
Unilateral leg weakness if a nerve root is compressed
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden onset of substantial 3/5 weakness is less typical of uncomplicated, slowly progressive degeneration

data.description: A cyst arising from a degenerative facet joint can compress an adjacent nerve root and cause sciatica. It is an alternative compressive diagnosis, but no definite cyst is identifiable on the supplied image.
symptoms_in_common: Possible acute worsening of longstanding symptoms

data.description: Bleeding into the spinal epidural space can cause acute back pain and neurological weakness and requires emergency assessment when suspected. This is a less likely alternative because the supplied image appears more consistent with disc herniation than an epidural collection.
symptoms_in_common: Pain radiating into the left leg
symptoms_not_in_common: Longstanding chronic back pain is not explained by an acute hematoma
An otherwise normal neurological examination is less typical of an extensive compressive hematoma

diagnoses.name: Intervertebral disc prolapse
diagnoses.title: Intervertebral disc degeneration without prolapsed disc with determinant

data.diagnosis: Lumbar disc herniation with radiculopathy (L4-L5 extrusion/sequestration)
data.description: Displacement of nucleus pulposus through the annulus fibrosus, compressing lumbar nerve roots and causing acute sciatica with possible motor deficit.
symptoms_in_common: MRI showing a posterior lesion at the lower lumbar disc level compressing the thecal sac
symptoms_not_in_common: Weakness of the whole leg is more marked than expected for single-root compression
No sensory or reflex changes reported

data.description: Collection of blood in the epidural space, spontaneous or related to anticoagulation or trauma, causing acute compression of nerve roots or cauda equina.
symptoms_in_common: Back pain with radicular leg pain
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of anticoagulation, coagulopathy or trauma
Chronic back pain history points to degenerative disease
Unilateral deficit only, no sphincter disturbance
Lesion centred on a disc level

data.description: Degenerative cyst arising from the facet joint that projects into the spinal canal or lateral recess and compresses nerve roots; can enlarge acutely with haemorrhage.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic back pain suggesting degenerative spine disease
Posteriorly located intraspinal lesion at the lower lumbar level
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute onset is unusual unless there is haemorrhage into the cyst
Symptoms are usually more gradual and often claudicant

data.description: Pyogenic infection of the epidural space, often with discitis/osteomyelitis, causing back pain and progressive neurological deficit.
symptoms_in_common: Epidural lesion compressing the thecal sac
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or systemic illness reported
No risk factors such as diabetes, intravenous drug use, immunosuppression or recent spinal procedure
No disc or endplate destruction or marrow oedema evident on the image

data.diagnosis: Intraspinal nerve sheath tumor (schwannoma/neurofibroma) or epidural metastasis
data.description: Neoplastic mass within the spinal canal, either a benign nerve sheath tumor or a metastatic deposit, compressing nerve roots and causing pain and weakness.
symptoms_not_in_common: Two-day acute onset is atypical for a slow-growing tumor
No known primary cancer, weight loss or night pain
No vertebral body marrow infiltration or destruction evident
Lesion appears related to the disc level

data.description: 6-month-old boy with 2 days of intermittent abdominal pain that woke him from sleep, during which he cried, drew his legs to his chest, and had a rigid abdomen. He developed three bowel movements with progressively increasing reddish blood, the last nearly entirely blood with a large clot. History includes infantile colic and gastroesophageal reflux treated with ranitidine; recently started pureed foods and was on low-lactose cow milk-based formula. On exam he had diffuse abdominal tenderness, worse on the right, later pallor, tachycardia, and borderline low blood pressure. Labs showed severe anemia (hemoglobin 5.7 g/dL, hematocrit 17.5%) with elevated reticulocyte count and leukocytosis.

data.diagnosis: Bleeding Meckel diverticulum with ectopic gastric mucosa
data.description: A congenital small-intestinal pouch that may contain acid-secreting gastric tissue, causing adjacent ulceration and substantial intestinal bleeding. The scintigraphic focus separate from the stomach is suggestive of ectopic gastric mucosa, supporting this diagnosis but not uniquely establishing it.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively bloody bowel movements with a large clot
Severe anemia with an elevated reticulocyte count
Pallor, tachycardia, and borderline low blood pressure consistent with significant blood loss
Abdominal pain and tenderness, particularly if inflammation or associated intussusception is present
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe episodic pain with drawing the legs to the chest is less typical of uncomplicated bleeding Meckel diverticulum, which often causes painless bleeding
A rigid abdomen is not typical unless an additional complication is present

data.diagnosis: Enteric duplication cyst containing ectopic gastric mucosa
data.description: A congenital duplication of part of the gastrointestinal tract that can contain gastric mucosa and cause ulceration, bleeding, or obstruction. Such tissue can also produce focal uptake on a gastric-mucosa scintigraphic study and mimic Meckel diverticulum.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent abdominal pain with crying and drawing the legs upward
Abdominal tenderness and rigidity during painful episodes
Substantial rectal bleeding with severe anemia
Pallor, tachycardia, and borderline low blood pressure from blood loss
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported symptoms clearly exclude this diagnosis; massive bleeding requires ulceration associated with ectopic gastric tissue

data.description: Telescoping of one segment of intestine into another, causing intermittent obstruction and potentially ischemic bowel injury. It is common in this age group and can be associated with a Meckel diverticulum or duplication cyst acting as a lead point.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent severe abdominal pain that wakes the infant from sleep
Crying and drawing the legs to the chest
Pallor, tachycardia, leukocytosis, and borderline low blood pressure
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound anemia from large-volume bleeding is less typical than smaller amounts of blood mixed with mucus
An elevated reticulocyte count may indicate blood loss predating the reported acute episodes

data.description: Abnormal intestinal positioning permits twisting around the mesenteric vessels, producing obstruction and potentially life-threatening bowel ischemia. This is an urgent alternative in an infant with abdominal pain, bloody stools, and circulatory instability.
symptoms_in_common: Bloody stools, potentially reflecting intestinal ischemia
Tachycardia and borderline low blood pressure
symptoms_not_in_common: Brief intermittent painful episodes are less typical than progressive pain with advanced volvulus
Profound anemia with reticulocytosis is less characteristic than an acute ischemic presentation

data.description: A non-IgE-mediated reaction, commonly to cow's milk protein, that causes blood-streaked stools in infants. Cow's milk-based formula provides a relevant exposure, although the severity of this presentation makes this diagnosis substantially less likely.
symptoms_in_common: Cow's milk protein exposure through formula
symptoms_not_in_common: Large-volume bleeding with a large clot
Severe anemia with hemoglobin of 5.7 g/dL
Severe episodic pain with drawing the legs to the chest
Abdominal rigidity and marked tenderness
Pallor, tachycardia, and borderline low blood pressure

data.diagnosis: Meckel's diverticulum with ectopic gastric mucosa
data.description: Congenital remnant of the omphalomesenteric duct containing heterotopic gastric mucosa that secretes acid, causing ulceration of adjacent ileal mucosa and often brisk lower GI bleeding in young children. Technetium-99m pertechnetate scan shows a focal area of uptake appearing simultaneously with the stomach.
symptoms_in_common: massive reddish rectal bleeding with large clot
severe anemia (hemoglobin 5.7 g/dL) with elevated reticulocyte count
pallor, tachycardia and borderline low blood pressure
focal tracer uptake in the mid/right abdomen appearing with gastric uptake on pertechnetate scan
symptoms_not_in_common: bleeding is classically painless, whereas he had 2 days of intermittent severe abdominal pain with leg drawing
rigid abdomen
leukocytosis (may be a stress response)

data.diagnosis: Intussusception (possibly with Meckel's diverticulum as lead point)
data.description: Telescoping of a proximal bowel segment into a distal one, most commonly ileocolic, in infants 3 months to 3 years of age, causing episodic colicky pain, bowel obstruction, ischemia and bloody stools.
symptoms_in_common: intermittent abdominal pain waking him from sleep
crying with legs drawn to the chest
symptoms_not_in_common: massive hemorrhage with large clot and hemoglobin 5.7 g/dL is unusual (typically currant-jelly stool with modest blood loss)
no vomiting, lethargy or palpable sausage-shaped mass reported
focal pertechnetate uptake is not explained by intussusception alone

data.diagnosis: Intestinal duplication cyst with ectopic gastric mucosa
data.description: Congenital cystic or tubular duplication of the gastrointestinal tract, most often ileal, which may contain heterotopic gastric mucosa that causes peptic ulceration, bleeding, pain, or acts as a lead point for intussusception or volvulus.
symptoms_in_common: significant lower GI bleeding with severe anemia
focal uptake on pertechnetate scan (ectopic gastric mucosa)
symptoms_not_in_common: much rarer than Meckel's diverticulum
no palpable abdominal mass
no obstructive symptoms such as vomiting or distension described

data.description: Abnormal intestinal rotation and fixation that allows the midgut to twist around the superior mesenteric artery, causing obstruction and bowel ischemia; a surgical emergency in infants.
symptoms_in_common: acute severe abdominal pain with crying and leg drawing
symptoms_not_in_common: no bilious vomiting
no abdominal distension reported
massive bleeding with a large clot and profound anemia with reticulocytosis suggests a discrete bleeding source rather than ischemia
focal pertechnetate uptake not explained
pain was intermittent over 2 days rather than rapidly progressive

data.diagnosis: Cow's milk protein allergy (allergic proctocolitis / enterocolitis)
data.description: Immune-mediated (usually non-IgE) reaction to cow's milk protein causing inflammation of the colon or small bowel in infants, typically presenting with blood- and mucus-streaked stools, irritability and sometimes feeding difficulty or reflux-like symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: history of infantile colic and gastroesophageal reflux
recent dietary change with new foods
symptoms_not_in_common: massive hemorrhage with large clot
severe acute anemia with hemodynamic compromise
rigid abdomen and focal right-sided tenderness
focal uptake on pertechnetate scan
typically blood-streaked mucousy stools in a well-appearing infant

data.description: A 39-year-old Korean male presented with intermittent and atypical chest discomfort symptoms. His medical history included burning pain originating in the extremities and radiating inwards to the limbs since childhood, which was previously dismissed as 'growing pains'. He also experienced ringing in the ears, had angiokeratomas on his trunk, and cornea verticillata. Physical examination revealed proteinuria (P/C ratio 0.501) without hematuria and normal renal function. His plasma αGal-A activity was markedly lower than controls at 4.1 nmoL/hr/mg protein (normal cutoff >35 nmoL/hr/mg protein). Genetic testing identified a hemizygous mutation in exon 4 of GLA, c.617T>C (p.Leu206 Pro).

data.diagnosis: Classic Fabry disease with cardiac and renal involvement
