data.description: An X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by deficient alpha-galactosidase A activity and glycosphingolipid accumulation. The markedly reduced enzyme activity, hemizygous GLA variant, and characteristic clinical findings strongly support this diagnosis. The images suggest ventricular hypertrophy with repolarization abnormalities and intracellular lamellar storage inclusions.
symptoms_in_common: Burning extremity pain beginning in childhood
Proteinuria without hematuria despite preserved renal function
Markedly reduced plasma alpha-galactosidase A activity
Apparent ventricular wall thickening and lamellar intracellular inclusions on the supplied images

data.description: An inherited myocardial disorder characterized by ventricular hypertrophy, sometimes causing chest discomfort and repolarization abnormalities. It is a cardiac phenocopy rather than a convincing explanation for this patient's multisystem findings.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent ventricular wall thickening on echocardiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Childhood-onset burning extremity pain
Angiokeratomas
Cornea verticillata
Tinnitus
Proteinuria
Marked alpha-galactosidase A deficiency and hemizygous GLA variant
Intracellular lamellar storage inclusions

data.diagnosis: Systemic amyloidosis with cardiac and renal involvement
data.description: A protein-deposition disorder that can cause myocardial thickening, proteinuria, and peripheral neuropathy. It is substantially less likely than Fabry disease given the specific enzyme and genetic findings.
symptoms_in_common: Burning extremity pain compatible with peripheral neuropathy
symptoms_not_in_common: Neuropathic pain beginning in childhood
Angiokeratomas
Cornea verticillata
Marked alpha-galactosidase A deficiency
Hemizygous GLA variant
Lamellar intracellular inclusions rather than typical extracellular amyloid fibrils

data.description: A drug-induced lysosomal lipid accumulation disorder, associated with medications such as hydroxychloroquine or amiodarone, that can produce corneal deposits, cardiomyopathy, and lamellar inclusions. No relevant medication exposure is provided.
symptoms_in_common: Possible cardiac involvement with chest discomfort and ventricular thickening
Proteinuria in some cases of renal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Burning extremity pain present since childhood
Angiokeratomas
Tinnitus
Marked alpha-galactosidase A deficiency
Hemizygous GLA variant

data.description: A rare autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-L-fucosidase deficiency. Angiokeratomas and intracellular storage material can resemble Fabry disease, but progressive neurologic impairment and other systemic features are usually prominent.
symptoms_not_in_common: Childhood-onset burning extremity pain as the principal neurologic symptom
Cornea verticillata
Tinnitus
Proteinuria with preserved renal function
Atypical chest discomfort with apparent ventricular hypertrophy
Marked alpha-galactosidase A deficiency rather than alpha-L-fucosidase deficiency
Hemizygous GLA variant

data.description: X-linked lysosomal storage disorder caused by GLA mutations leading to deficient alpha-galactosidase A activity and accumulation of globotriaosylceramide in vascular endothelium, kidney, heart, nerves, skin and cornea.
symptoms_in_common: Childhood-onset burning pain in the extremities (acroparesthesia)
Proteinuria without hematuria and with preserved renal function
Markedly reduced plasma alpha-Gal A activity
ECG with high voltage and deep T-wave inversions in the precordial leads suggesting left ventricular hypertrophy
M-mode echocardiogram suggesting thickened left ventricular walls
Electron microscopy showing lamellated myelin-like (zebra body) lysosomal inclusions

data.description: Autosomal dominant disorder of sarcomere proteins causing unexplained left ventricular hypertrophy, chest pain, arrhythmias and risk of sudden death.
symptoms_in_common: ECG with high voltage and deep T-wave inversions
Left ventricular wall thickening on echocardiogram
symptoms_not_in_common: Childhood acroparesthesia
Angiokeratomas
Cornea verticillata
Tinnitus
Proteinuria
Low alpha-Gal A activity
GLA mutation
Lamellated lysosomal inclusions on electron microscopy

data.description: Infiltrative disease with extracellular amyloid fibril deposition causing ventricular wall thickening, neuropathy and, in AL type, renal involvement with proteinuria.
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset of neuropathic pain in childhood
Angiokeratomas
Cornea verticillata
High ECG voltage (amyloid typically shows low voltage)
Low alpha-Gal A activity
GLA mutation
Lamellated inclusions rather than amyloid fibrils on electron microscopy
Tinnitus

data.diagnosis: Fucosidosis (or other lysosomal storage disease with angiokeratoma corporis diffusum)
data.description: Autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by alpha-L-fucosidase deficiency, featuring angiokeratomas, coarse facial features, neurodegeneration and dysostosis multiplex.
symptoms_in_common: Lysosomal storage inclusions on electron microscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal cognition and survival to adulthood without neurodegeneration
Acroparesthesia
Cornea verticillata
Proteinuria

GLA mutation

data.description: Acquired lysosomal accumulation of phospholipids due to cationic amphiphilic drugs, which mimics Fabry disease with cornea verticillata and zebra bodies in renal and cardiac cells.
symptoms_in_common: Lamellated myelin-like inclusions on electron microscopy
Possible cardiomyopathy with ventricular wall thickening
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported exposure to causative drugs
Childhood acroparesthesia
Angiokeratomas
Tinnitus
Markedly low alpha-Gal A activity
Pathogenic GLA mutation

data.description: 82-year-old man with a 6-month history of worsening back and left hip pain, worse with activity, occasionally waking him from sleep, and not relieved by bending forward. Pain did not radiate to the legs and was not associated with morning stiffness, fever, chills, night sweats, or bowel/bladder incontinence. He reported a 9 kg weight loss over several months; symptoms began after recovery from pneumonia. Past medical history included sick sinus syndrome with pacemaker, diastolic heart failure, pulmonary fibrosis, hyperlipidemia, hypertension, gout, postherpetic neuralgia, and basal-cell carcinoma. On examination, he was afebrile and in no acute distress, with no spinal or sacroiliac tenderness, normal hip exam, no neurologic deficits, slightly diminished patellar reflexes bilaterally, intact sensation, normal rectal tone, and negative straight-leg raise.

A rare fungal infection of the spine caused by Histoplasma capsulatum, potentially following pulmonary infection. The destructive lumbar endplate changes, adjacent soft-tissue abnormality, calcified thoracic lymph nodes, and small yeast-like organisms in the tissue images make this an important possibility; fungal culture or molecular testing is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Six months of progressive back and left hip pain
Pain occasionally waking him from sleep
Symptoms beginning after a pulmonary illness
Imaging suggesting destructive lumbar spondylodiscitis with adjacent soft-tissue involvement
Small rounded fungal-appearing organisms on tissue stains
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of fever or night sweats is less typical of systemic infection, although possible in localized disease
No spinal tenderness despite apparent vertebral involvement

data.description: An uncommon bone infection caused by Cryptococcus species, sometimes occurring after pulmonary infection and producing indolent vertebral destruction. Rounded yeast-like organisms with surrounding clear spaces can suggest this diagnosis, but capsule stains, antigen testing, and culture are needed to distinguish it from other fungi.
symptoms_in_common: Left hip pain potentially referred from lumbar disease
Destructive vertebral changes with adjacent soft-tissue involvement
Rounded yeast-like organisms in the tissue images
symptoms_not_in_common: Disc-centered involvement is less characteristic than isolated vertebral lesions
Calcified thoracic lymph nodes are not a characteristic finding of cryptococcosis

data.description: A disseminated fungal infection that can spread from the lungs to bone, causing destructive vertebral lesions and nearby abscesses. Diagnosis requires demonstration of characteristic broad-based budding yeast or confirmation by culture; that morphology is not clearly established in the supplied images.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive back and hip pain over several months
Destructive spinal lesion with adjacent soft-tissue abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or night sweats
The pictured organisms do not clearly show the large, broad-based budding forms typical of Blastomyces
Calcified thoracic lymph nodes are less characteristic of blastomycosis

data.description: A chronic spinal infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that can destroy adjacent vertebral bodies and discs and produce paravertebral or psoas abscesses. The clinical and spinal imaging pattern is compatible, but apparent yeast forms in the tissue favor a fungal alternative.
symptoms_in_common: Left hip pain potentially related to paravertebral or psoas involvement
Adjacent vertebral endplate destruction and disc involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or night sweats, although these may be absent in spinal tuberculosis
Rounded fungal-appearing organisms are not typical of tuberculosis
No spinal tenderness

data.description: A bacterial infection of vertebral endplates and the intervening disc, commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus or other bloodstream pathogens. It can occur after a distant infection and may be afebrile in older adults, but the tissue images raise concern for a fungal rather than bacterial cause.
symptoms_in_common: Pain worsened by activity and occasionally present at night
Weight loss during a prolonged illness
Imaging showing adjacent endplate destruction and disc involvement
Adjacent soft-tissue abnormality suggesting inflammatory extension
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, chills, or spinal tenderness
Slow six-month course is less typical of an acute pyogenic infection
Fungal-appearing organisms in tissue are not explained by a purely bacterial infection

data.description: Dimorphic fungal infection that begins in the lungs and can disseminate to bone, especially vertebrae, causing destructive osteomyelitis with paravertebral or psoas abscesses. Tissue shows large thick-walled yeast with broad-based budding on GMS/PAS stains.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic progressive back and hip pain over 6 months
Onset after an episode of pneumonia
Destructive vertebral and disc-space lesion with paravertebral soft-tissue mass on CT
Calcified mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes suggesting prior granulomatous infection
Single round thick-walled yeast form on GMS and PAS stains
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, chills, or night sweats
No skin lesions described
No spinal tenderness
Calcified nodes are more typical of histoplasmosis or tuberculosis than blastomycosis

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the spine causing indolent vertebral destruction, disc involvement and paravertebral or psoas cold abscesses, often with calcification.
symptoms_in_common: Calcified mediastinal and hilar lymph nodes
symptoms_not_in_common: Yeast form seen on GMS/PAS stains rather than acid-fast bacilli
No night sweats
No known tuberculosis exposure
No neurologic deficit or gibbus deformity

data.description: Histoplasma capsulatum infection acquired by inhalation; heals with calcified mediastinal nodes and may disseminate in elderly patients, rarely to bone. Yeasts are small (2-4 micrometres) and usually intracellular.
symptoms_in_common: Calcified hilar and mediastinal lymph nodes
symptoms_not_in_common: Bone involvement is rare in histoplasmosis
Yeast appears large and thick-walled rather than small and intracellular
No fever
No hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias or mucosal ulcers described

data.diagnosis: Metastatic cancer or multiple myeloma of the spine
data.description: Malignant infiltration of vertebrae (e.g., prostate, lung, kidney primary or plasma cell neoplasm) causing destructive lesions and pain in older adults.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive back pain with night pain
Destructive vertebral lesion with soft-tissue mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Involvement centred on the disc space and adjacent endplates favours infection
Biopsy shows a fungal organism rather than malignant cells
No known primary cancer other than basal-cell carcinoma, which rarely metastasises
Calcified nodes are not explained

data.description: Haematogenous bacterial infection (commonly Staphylococcus aureus, streptococci or gram-negatives) of the disc and adjacent vertebrae, sometimes following a distant infection or in patients with intravascular devices.
symptoms_in_common: Onset after pneumonia as a possible bacteraemic source
Pacemaker as a potential source of bloodstream infection
Disc-space and endplate destruction with paravertebral soft tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Six-month indolent course is long for pyogenic infection
No spinal tenderness
Yeast seen on histology rather than bacteria
Marked weight loss and calcified nodes are not typical

data.description: Two-year-four-month-old female with intrauterine growth restriction at birth (39 weeks, C-section for placenta failure; birth weight 1850 g, length 44.5 cm, head circumference 31 cm, all <3rd percentile). In infancy, she had severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss identified at 3 months, with hearing aids placed at 4 months. She showed persistent short stature and low weight (<3rd percentile), delayed teething, small teeth, delayed bone age, triangular face, prominent forehead, small chin, hypoplastic nasal alae, large mouth with thin downturned lips, low-set ears, deep-set eyes, thin wrinkled skin with visible vessels, and lipoatrophy. Psychomotor development was otherwise normal: sitting at 8 months, walking at 14 months, and talking at 13 months. Brain MRI was normal. Genetic testing found a de novo heterozygous PIK3R1 variant c.1956dupT (p.Lys653*), exon 15.

An autosomal dominant disorder characterized by prenatal and postnatal growth restriction, partial lipodystrophy, characteristic facial features, and delayed dentition. The phenotype and de novo PIK3R1 p.Lys653* variant strongly support this as the leading diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent short stature and low weight
Thin, wrinkled skin with visible vessels
Triangular face, prominent forehead, small chin, and hypoplastic nasal alae
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss in early infancy is uncommon, although hearing impairment has been reported

data.description: A growth disorder usually associated with abnormalities of genomic imprinting, causing prenatal growth restriction, persistent short stature, low weight, and a triangular face. It is a phenotypic alternative but does not explain the PIK3R1 finding.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent short stature and low weight
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
Lipoatrophy with thin, wrinkled skin and visible vessels
Hypoplastic nasal alae
Small head circumference at birth rather than characteristic relative head sparing

data.description: A rare neonatal progeroid disorder, usually caused by biallelic POLR3A variants, featuring prenatal growth restriction, diminished subcutaneous fat, thin skin, and an aged facial appearance.
symptoms_in_common: Thin, wrinkled skin with visible vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss is not a characteristic feature
Delayed teething contrasts with the natal teeth reported in many affected patients
Preserved psychomotor development is less typical of more severe presentations
Small head circumference at birth rather than relative macrocephaly

data.description: A premature-aging disorder usually caused by a de novo LMNA variant, producing early-childhood growth failure, loss of subcutaneous fat, skin changes, and characteristic craniofacial abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent short stature and low weight
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked intrauterine growth restriction, since birth size is usually relatively normal

Hypoplastic nasal alae rather than the more typical narrow, beaked nose

data.diagnosis: Mandibular hypoplasia, deafness, progeroid features, and lipodystrophy syndrome

Delayed teething and small teeth are not defining features

data.description: Rare autosomal dominant disorder caused by heterozygous PIK3R1 variants, characterized by Short stature, Hyperextensibility of joints/inguinal hernia, Ocular depression, Rieger anomaly and Teething delay, along with IUGR, partial lipodystrophy, characteristic triangular facies, sensorineural hearing loss and later insulin resistance.

data.description: Autosomal recessive DNA repair disorder (ERCC6/ERCC8) with growth failure, microcephaly, progressive neurodegeneration, sensorineural hearing loss, deep-set eyes, loss of subcutaneous fat, photosensitivity and premature aging appearance.

No retinopathy or cataracts reported
Triangular face with prominent forehead and hypoplastic nasal alae
PIK3R1 variant rather than ERCC6/ERCC8 variants

data.diagnosis: Mandibular hypoplasia, deafness, progeroid features and lipodystrophy (MDPL) syndrome
data.description: Autosomal dominant disorder caused by POLD1 variants, with progressive lipodystrophy, mandibular hypoplasia, sensorineural deafness, progeroid facial features, tight thin skin with telangiectasia and insulin resistance.
symptoms_not_in_common: Intrauterine growth restriction (birth size is usually normal)
Onset from birth rather than later childhood
Hearing loss in early infancy (usually develops later)
Delayed bone age and delayed teething
Short stature this early
PIK3R1 variant rather than a POLD1 variant

data.description: 20-year-old man with Crohn’s disease diagnosed at age 10, previously treated with prolonged glucocorticoids and currently improved on weekly adalimumab for 3 years, presented with 2 days of worsening cramping left calf pain and swelling extending to the foot, with a purpuric/erythematous rash on the dorsum of both feet. Three weeks earlier he developed sore throat, nonproductive cough, rhinorrhea, and chills, with a history of similar self-limited upper respiratory episodes. Exam showed left ankle synovitis, normal peripheral pulses, intact nasal septum, and discomfort from left leg pain.

An IgA-mediated small-vessel vasculitis affecting skin, joints, gastrointestinal tract, and sometimes kidneys. This is the leading diagnosis: the supplied biopsy images appear to show leukocytoclastic vasculitis with vascular IgA deposition.
symptoms_in_common: Purpuric rash on both feet and lower legs
Upper respiratory illness preceding the rash
Apparent vascular IgA, C3, and fibrin deposition on immunofluorescence
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly unilateral calf pain and swelling are less typical than predominantly symmetric lower-extremity involvement
Nasal crusting or hemorrhagic changes visible in the photograph are not characteristic

data.description: A drug-associated inflammatory injury to dermal small vessels that can occur during anti-TNF treatment, sometimes with an IgA-mediated pattern. Attribution to adalimumab requires assessment of alternative triggers.
symptoms_in_common: Biopsy appearance compatible with leukocytoclastic vasculitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Sore throat, rhinorrhea, and cough are not direct manifestations and may indicate an alternative infectious trigger
Nasal crusting or hemorrhagic changes are not typical
Marked unilateral calf swelling is not a characteristic isolated cutaneous presentation

data.description: An ANCA-associated vasculitis that commonly involves the upper airways, lungs, and kidneys and can cause cutaneous purpura and arthritis. The apparent IgA-positive biopsy favors an immune-complex vasculitis instead.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent nasal crusting or hemorrhagic changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Self-limited respiratory episodes resemble ordinary infections more than persistent inflammatory airway disease
Marked unilateral calf swelling is not characteristic
Vascular IgA deposition is atypical for the usually pauci-immune disease

data.description: A venous blood clot causing acute unilateral leg pain and swelling. Crohn’s disease increases thrombotic risk; this important possibility requires prompt exclusion with venous ultrasonography even if vasculitis explains the rash.
symptoms_in_common: Two days of worsening unilateral calf pain
Left leg swelling extending into the foot
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral purpuric foot rash
True ankle synovitis
Biopsy findings suggesting IgA-mediated small-vessel vasculitis
Nasal crusting and preceding upper respiratory symptoms are not explained by a leg clot

data.diagnosis: Crohn’s-associated erythema nodosum with peripheral arthritis
data.description: An inflammatory extraintestinal manifestation of Crohn’s disease causing tender subcutaneous leg nodules, often accompanied by ankle arthritis. The purpuric appearance and apparent small-vessel biopsy findings make this less likely.
symptoms_not_in_common: Purpuric foot lesions rather than tender subcutaneous shin nodules
Apparent leukocytoclastic vasculitis with vascular IgA deposition rather than septal panniculitis
Nasal crusting or hemorrhagic changes
Marked unilateral cramping calf pain

data.diagnosis: IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schönlein purpura), likely associated with anti-TNF therapy
data.description: Immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis with IgA deposition in vessel walls, often triggered by upper respiratory infection and reported in Crohn's disease patients receiving TNF inhibitors such as adalimumab; presents with palpable purpura, arthritis, abdominal pain and nephritis.
symptoms_in_common: Purpuric rash on the dorsum of both feet and around the ankle
Skin biopsy showing leukocytoclastic vasculitis with fibrinoid change
Perivascular IgA, C3 and fibrin on direct immunofluorescence
symptoms_not_in_common: Bloody nasal crusting seen in the photograph
Recurrent upper respiratory episodes
Markedly asymmetric unilateral calf swelling
No abdominal pain or renal involvement described
Adult age (more common in children)

data.description: Necrotizing granulomatous small-vessel vasculitis affecting the upper and lower respiratory tract and kidneys, usually PR3-ANCA positive and pauci-immune on biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent upper respiratory symptoms (rhinorrhea, sore throat, cough)
symptoms_not_in_common: IgA deposition on immunofluorescence (GPA is pauci-immune)
Intact nasal septum
No granulomas on skin biopsy
No described lung or renal involvement
Self-limited nature of the respiratory episodes

data.diagnosis: Drug-induced (anti-TNF) hypersensitivity/leukocytoclastic vasculitis or lupus-like syndrome
data.description: Small-vessel cutaneous vasculitis or lupus-like autoimmune syndrome triggered by TNF inhibitors, typically with purpura, arthralgia or arthritis and sometimes autoantibodies; improves on drug withdrawal.
symptoms_in_common: Purpuric rash on the lower extremities
symptoms_not_in_common: IgA-predominant deposits point to a specific IgA vasculitis
Preceding upper respiratory infection suggests an infectious trigger
Bloody nasal crusting
Long latency after starting the drug

data.diagnosis: Deep vein thrombosis of the left leg
data.description: Venous thrombosis of the deep leg veins causing unilateral pain and swelling; risk is increased in inflammatory bowel disease.
symptoms_in_common: Crohn's disease as a prothrombotic condition
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral purpuric rash
Ankle synovitis
Vasculitis with IgA deposits on biopsy
Upper respiratory prodrome
Nasal crusting

data.diagnosis: Infection-related vasculitis or septic process in an immunosuppressed host (e.g., post-streptococcal vasculitis/reactive arthritis, endocarditis, disseminated gonococcal or meningococcal infection)
data.description: Infections can cause immune-complex or septic small-vessel vasculitis with purpura and arthritis, particularly in patients on TNF inhibitors; post-streptococcal disease follows pharyngitis by 1 to 3 weeks.
symptoms_in_common: Sore throat and chills 3 weeks earlier
symptoms_not_in_common: IgA-dominant vascular deposits
No current fever or systemic toxicity described
No pustular lesions or tenosynovitis
No heart murmur described
Recurrent self-limited respiratory episodes

data.description: A 66-year-old woman presented to the emergency department with episodes of palpitations, dizziness, and near fainting that had lasted for a few hours. Her medical history included removal of a left atrial myxoma 15 years ago, after which she experienced recurrent atrial tachycardia managed with modified release verapamil 240 mg once daily. She had recently started sotalol 120 mg twice daily in addition to verapamil and underwent direct current cardioversion for persistent atrial tachycardia one week prior to presentation. Initial workup showed normal urea and electrolytes including magnesium. An echocardiogram revealed normal left ventricular systolic function with no recurrence of left atrial myxoma.

data.diagnosis: Sotalol-induced acquired long-QT syndrome with torsades de pointes
data.description: Drug-induced delayed ventricular repolarization causing a potentially life-threatening polymorphic ventricular tachycardia. The ECG appears to show prolonged repolarization followed by a short run of polymorphic wide-complex tachycardia. Recent sotalol initiation and additional rate slowing from verapamil strongly support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Recent initiation of sotalol 120 mg twice daily
Concurrent verapamil use, which can promote bradycardia and pause-dependent arrhythmia
ECG appearance suggestive of prolonged QT and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
symptoms_not_in_common: No major discordant symptoms; normal electrolytes and normal ventricular function do not exclude drug-induced torsades

data.diagnosis: Medication-induced sinus node dysfunction with tachycardia-bradycardia syndrome
data.description: Excessive slowing or pauses of the sinus rhythm, potentially amplified by combined sotalol and verapamil. Underlying sinus node dysfunction can become apparent after cardioversion and coexist with atrial tachyarrhythmias.
symptoms_in_common: Concurrent use of two rate-slowing medications
Relatively slow baseline rhythm and an apparent pause on the ECG
symptoms_not_in_common: The polymorphic wide-complex tachycardia is not explained by sinus node dysfunction alone
Markedly prolonged ventricular repolarization suggests an additional drug-induced electrophysiologic abnormality

data.diagnosis: Recurrent atrial tachycardia with aberrant ventricular conduction
data.description: Recurrence of an atrial tachyarrhythmia after cardioversion, with abnormal intraventricular conduction producing wide QRS complexes. Prior atrial surgery may provide a substrate for recurrent atrial tachycardia.
symptoms_in_common: Recent cardioversion for persistent atrial tachycardia
symptoms_not_in_common: The changing morphology of the wide-complex run favors polymorphic ventricular tachycardia rather than fixed aberrancy
Apparent prolonged QT and pause-associated onset are not typical of atrial tachycardia

data.diagnosis: Acute myocardial ischemia-associated polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
data.description: Ventricular electrical instability caused by acute myocardial ischemia can produce polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and presyncope. This remains a differential consideration, although the medication history and apparent QT prolongation favor torsades.
symptoms_in_common: ECG appearance of polymorphic wide-complex tachycardia
symptoms_not_in_common: No chest pain or other ischemic symptoms are reported
Apparent prolonged QT and pause-associated onset favor torsades rather than ischemic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
Recent sotalol initiation provides a more direct explanation

data.diagnosis: Previously unrecognized congenital long-QT syndrome unmasked by sotalol
data.description: An inherited repolarization disorder may remain clinically silent until a QT-prolonging medication triggers torsades de pointes. This is less likely than a purely acquired drug effect but may warrant consideration if QT prolongation persists after medication withdrawal.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent prolonged QT with polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
Arrhythmia following exposure to a QT-prolonging medication
symptoms_not_in_common: First reported presentation at age 66 is less typical of symptomatic congenital long-QT syndrome
No lifelong syncope history or family history of sudden death is provided
The close temporal relationship to sotalol initiation favors acquired long-QT syndrome

data.diagnosis: Sotalol-induced acquired long QT syndrome with torsades de pointes
data.description: Drug-induced QT prolongation (class III antiarrhythmic effect of sotalol, potentiated by bradycardia from combined verapamil) leading to pause-dependent polymorphic ventricular tachycardia with twisting QRS axis.
symptoms_in_common: Recent initiation of sotalol 120 mg twice daily
Female sex and older age (risk factors)
Recent cardioversion with slower rhythm afterward
ECG showing bradycardia with markedly prolonged QT, ventricular ectopic with short-long-short sequence initiating polymorphic VT
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal potassium and magnesium (electrolyte disturbance often coexists but is not required)

data.diagnosis: Bradycardia-dependent torsades de pointes due to sinus node dysfunction or AV block (drug-induced, verapamil plus sotalol)
data.description: Marked bradycardia or pauses from sinus node disease or AV block, often worsened by combined rate-slowing drugs, prolongs repolarisation and triggers pause-dependent polymorphic VT.
symptoms_in_common: Slow baseline rhythm with pauses on ECG
Combination of verapamil and a beta-blocking drug (sotalol)
Prior atrial surgery and atrial arrhythmias predisposing to sinus node disease
symptoms_not_in_common: QT prolongation is more directly explained by sotalol's class III effect
No clear documentation of complete heart block
Symptoms began only after sotalol was started

data.diagnosis: Ischaemic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (acute coronary syndrome)
data.description: Acute myocardial ischaemia can cause polymorphic VT or ventricular fibrillation, typically with a normal QT interval and ST-segment changes.
symptoms_not_in_common: No chest pain
Normal LV systolic function with no regional abnormality reported
Prolonged QT and pause-dependent onset favour torsades
No ischaemic ST changes described
Clear temporal link to a QT-prolonging drug

data.diagnosis: Recurrent atrial tachycardia or atrial fibrillation with aberrant conduction
data.description: Recurrence of her known atrial arrhythmia after cardioversion, conducted with rate-related bundle branch aberrancy, producing a wide-complex tachycardia.
symptoms_in_common: Long history of recurrent atrial tachycardia after myxoma surgery
Cardioversion only one week earlier (early recurrence is common)
symptoms_not_in_common: QRS morphology and axis change continuously rather than showing a fixed bundle branch pattern
Initiation by a ventricular ectopic after a pause
Marked QT prolongation in baseline beats
She is on two AV-nodal-slowing drugs, making very rapid conduction unlikely

data.diagnosis: Congenital long QT syndrome unmasked by sotalol
data.description: Inherited cardiac ion channel disorder with reduced repolarisation reserve; may be silent until a QT-prolonging drug provokes marked QT prolongation and torsades de pointes.
symptoms_in_common: Prolonged QT with torsades de pointes on ECG
Normal electrolytes and structurally normal ventricle
symptoms_not_in_common: First presentation at age 66
No reported prior syncope or family history of sudden death
No reported QT prolongation before sotalol
Onset clearly linked to starting the drug

data.description: 14-year-old boy with 2 days of acute fear of choking when swallowing after choking on chicken, followed by fear of eating, vomiting after attempting ice cream, and markedly reduced oral intake. Nine days earlier, his mother noted inspiratory stridor during sleep for several weeks. On presentation he was anxious, had persistent involuntary burping, drooling, dry oral mucosa, and poor intake with sleepiness. Exam was otherwise normal, with normal cranial nerves, speech, gait, strength, sensation, and reflexes; later he had hypertonic leg muscles and a mildly positive left Chvostek’s sign. Past history included infantile gastroesophageal reflux, milk-protein allergy, eczema/keratosis pilaris, sensory-integration training in childhood, and incomplete immunizations after age 2.5 years.

An imprinting disorder causing resistance to parathyroid hormone, typically resulting in hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia. The patient's GNAS methylation pattern—hypermethylation at NESP and hypomethylation at AS, XL, and A/B—strongly supports this diagnosis. Serum calcium, phosphate, magnesium, and parathyroid hormone measurements are needed to establish the associated biochemical abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Inspiratory stridor, potentially reflecting hypocalcemic laryngospasm
Choking and swallowing difficulty, potentially related to neuromuscular irritability
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent involuntary burping is not a characteristic feature
Acute fear of eating after a choking event suggests a secondary psychological response
Eczema and milk-protein allergy are not characteristic features

data.description: Insufficient parathyroid hormone secretion causes hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia, potentially producing tetany and laryngospasm. Unlike pseudohypoparathyroidism, parathyroid hormone levels are low or inappropriately normal. This diagnosis would not explain the abnormal GNAS methylation shown.
symptoms_in_common: Hypertonic leg muscles compatible with tetany
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent involuntary burping is not typical
Fear of eating specifically following choking is not characteristic
Eczema and milk-protein allergy are not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Vitamin D deficiency with symptomatic hypocalcemia
data.description: Severe vitamin D deficiency can reduce calcium absorption and cause secondary hyperparathyroidism, neuromuscular irritability, and occasionally laryngospasm. Calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, and 25-hydroxyvitamin D testing would help distinguish it from parathyroid hormone resistance. It does not explain the GNAS methylation abnormality.
symptoms_in_common: Inspiratory stridor potentially caused by hypocalcemic laryngospasm
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt fear of swallowing after a choking episode is not characteristic
Persistent involuntary burping is not typical
Drooling and vomiting after attempting ice cream are not characteristic presenting features

data.description: An immune-mediated inflammatory disease of the esophagus that can cause dysphagia, food impaction, vomiting, and food avoidance, especially in patients with atopic disease. Diagnosis requires endoscopy with esophageal biopsies. It would not account for the GNAS methylation findings or signs of neuromuscular irritability.
symptoms_in_common: Choking on chicken, potentially representing food impaction
Difficulty swallowing and fear of eating
Drooling, which can accompany esophageal obstruction
History of eczema and milk-protein allergy
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypertonic leg muscles
Mildly positive Chvostek's sign
Inspiratory stridor during sleep is not a typical manifestation

data.diagnosis: Post-choking phagophobia with avoidant/restrictive food intake
data.description: Fear of swallowing after a choking experience can lead to severe food avoidance, anxiety, and dehydration. This may explain the acute behavioral symptoms or coexist with an organic swallowing disorder, but it should not be treated as the sole explanation given the stridor, neuromuscular signs, and abnormal GNAS methylation.
symptoms_in_common: Acute fear of choking when swallowing after choking on chicken
Dry oral mucosa and sleepiness potentially resulting from inadequate intake
symptoms_not_in_common: Inspiratory stridor during sleep predating the choking event
Hypertonic leg muscles
Mildly positive Chvostek's sign
Drooling requires exclusion of an organic swallowing problem

data.description: Imprinting disorder of the GNAS locus causing renal resistance to parathyroid hormone, with hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia and elevated PTH, usually without the Albright hereditary osteodystrophy phenotype. The methylation panel shows gain of methylation at NESP and loss at AS, XL and A/B, while the mother's pattern is normal, consistent with a sporadic epigenetic defect.
symptoms_in_common: Inspiratory stridor during sleep (laryngospasm from hypocalcemia)
Abnormal GNAS methylation (NESP gain; AS, XL, A/B loss)
Adolescent onset with otherwise normal neurologic exam
symptoms_not_in_common: Infantile gastroesophageal reflux
Milk-protein allergy
Eczema/keratosis pilaris
Incomplete immunizations
Vomiting after eating

data.diagnosis: Primary hypoparathyroidism (autoimmune or genetic, e.g., 22q11.2 deletion)
data.description: Deficient parathyroid hormone secretion causing hypocalcemia with neuromuscular irritability, tetany, laryngospasm and sometimes seizures.
symptoms_not_in_common: Abnormal GNAS methylation pattern (points to PTH resistance rather than deficiency)
No cardiac defects, facial dysmorphism or recurrent infections reported
No mucocutaneous candidiasis or adrenal insufficiency
Milk-protein allergy and eczema

data.description: Clostridium tetani toxin-mediated disorder causing muscle rigidity, painful spasms, trismus, dysphagia and laryngospasm, mainly in under-immunized individuals.
symptoms_not_in_common: No wound or injury reported
No trismus or risus sardonicus
No painful generalized spasms or opisthotonus
Stridor for several weeks before presentation
Positive Chvostek's sign
Abnormal GNAS methylation
Persistent burping

data.description: Chronic immune-mediated esophageal inflammation in atopic individuals, causing dysphagia, food impaction, vomiting and food avoidance.
symptoms_in_common: Fear of eating and reduced oral intake
symptoms_not_in_common: Inspiratory stridor during sleep
Hypertonic leg muscles
Positive Chvostek's sign
Persistent involuntary burping
Sleepiness
Abnormal GNAS methylation

data.diagnosis: Choking phobia (phagophobia) / avoidant-restrictive food intake disorder
data.description: Psychogenic fear of swallowing that typically follows a choking event, leading to food avoidance, reduced intake and dehydration without structural disease.
symptoms_in_common: Acute fear of choking after a choking episode
symptoms_not_in_common: Inspiratory stridor during sleep for weeks before the choking event
Hypertonic leg muscles
Positive Chvostek's sign
Abnormal GNAS methylation
Sleepiness

data.description: 95-year-old woman admitted after a fall. Medical history includes Alzheimer's disease, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus (on metformin). Laboratory findings showed elevated white cell count and C reactive protein levels. Urine culture revealed Klebsiella pneumoniae infection. Blood cultures were negative.

A complicated urinary infection in which gas-producing bacteria cause gas accumulation in the bladder wall and sometimes its lumen. This is the leading consideration given the apparent gas outlining the bladder on the radiograph; CT can confirm the finding.
symptoms_in_common: Klebsiella pneumoniae isolated from urine, a recognized gas-producing pathogen
Elevated white cell count and C-reactive protein
Apparent curvilinear gas outlining the bladder on the pelvic radiograph
Type 2 diabetes mellitus, an important risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: The fall is nonspecific and is not a defining manifestation of this infection

data.description: An abnormal connection between the colon and bladder, commonly caused by diverticular disease or malignancy, that can introduce bowel gas and bacteria into the urinary tract.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent gas in the bladder region
symptoms_not_in_common: An apparent rim of gas within the bladder wall favors emphysematous cystitis rather than a fistula
The fall is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: A potentially life-threatening gas-producing infection of the kidney and surrounding tissues, especially in patients with diabetes. Renal imaging would be needed to establish or exclude this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated white cell count and C-reactive protein
symptoms_not_in_common: The visible gas appears centered on the bladder rather than the kidneys
The fall is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: A bacterial urinary infection in a patient with factors increasing the risk of complications. It explains the culture and inflammatory findings but would not explain confirmed gas within the bladder wall.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated white cell count and C-reactive protein
A fall can accompany nonspecific illness in an older adult
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent gas outlining the bladder wall is not typical of a non-emphysematous infection

data.description: Accumulation of hardened stool in the rectum, particularly in frail older adults. A stool-filled rectum can produce a pelvic gas pattern that mimics bladder abnormalities, although it would not itself explain the positive urine culture.
symptoms_in_common: Advanced age and Alzheimer's disease, which increase susceptibility
Pelvic mottled gas and soft-tissue density that could overlap with rectal stool on a plain radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Klebsiella pneumoniae urinary infection is not directly explained by fecal impaction
Apparent circumferential bladder-wall gas favors emphysematous cystitis
Elevated inflammatory markers are not typical of uncomplicated fecal impaction

data.description: Gas-forming infection of the bladder wall and/or lumen, typically caused by E. coli or Klebsiella pneumoniae, occurring mostly in elderly diabetic women. Often found incidentally on imaging as a curvilinear rim of gas outlining the bladder.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic radiograph showing curvilinear radiolucent gas outlining the bladder wall with mottled intraluminal gas
Incidental discovery during work-up after a fall
Negative blood cultures (may be localized infection)
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported dysuria, hematuria, pneumaturia or abdominal pain (history limited by Alzheimer's disease)
Fall is not a direct feature of the disease (may reflect infection-related frailty or delirium)

data.diagnosis: Uncomplicated (non-emphysematous) Klebsiella urinary tract infection / cystitis
data.description: Bacterial infection of the lower urinary tract without gas formation, common in elderly diabetic women and a frequent cause of falls and delirium in older adults.
symptoms_in_common: Fall as an atypical presentation of infection in the elderly
symptoms_not_in_common: Gas outlining the bladder wall on radiograph is not explained by simple cystitis

data.description: Abnormal communication between the bowel and the bladder, most often due to diverticulitis, malignancy or Crohn's disease, leading to gas in the bladder and recurrent urinary infections.
symptoms_in_common: Gas within the bladder on imaging
Urinary tract infection with an enteric organism
symptoms_not_in_common: Gas appears to track within the bladder wall rather than only in the lumen
Single organism rather than polymicrobial urine culture
No reported pneumaturia or fecaluria
No known diverticular disease, malignancy or inflammatory bowel disease

data.diagnosis: Iatrogenic intravesical gas (recent catheterization or instrumentation)
data.description: Air introduced into the bladder lumen by urinary catheterization or cystoscopy, producing benign intraluminal gas on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Gas in the bladder region on radiograph
Elderly hospitalized patient in whom catheterization is common
Catheter-associated bacteriuria could explain the positive urine culture
symptoms_not_in_common: No documented catheterization or instrumentation
Intramural, rim-like gas pattern is not expected with introduced air
Elevated white cell count and C reactive protein suggest active infection

data.diagnosis: Hip (proximal femoral) fracture after fall with concurrent urinary infection
data.description: Fragility fracture of the femoral neck or intertrochanteric region, common in elderly osteoporotic women after a fall; it is the usual reason for pelvic radiography in this setting and can cause a reactive rise in inflammatory markers.
symptoms_in_common: Irregular appearance of the left proximal femur on the radiograph, possibly a fracture
Dementia and diabetes as fall and fracture risk factors
Elevated white cell count and C reactive protein can occur after trauma
symptoms_not_in_common: Does not explain gas outlining the bladder
Does not explain Klebsiella pneumoniae in the urine
No hip pain, limb shortening or external rotation described

data.description: 15-year-old boy presented after injuring his left knee while carrying a tray of food at a fast food restaurant. He felt his knee 'wobble' and fell to the floor, unable to bear weight due to pain. Medical history included chronic fatigue syndrome. Had a Beighton score of 6 (indicating joint laxity) but no history of joint dislocations. On examination: laterally dislocated patella, moderate effusion, pain on palpation around medial patellofemoral ligament, range of movement reduced to extension-flexion of 0/10/60 degrees, ligamentous tests unremarkable. Two weeks later: complained of intermittent locking in left knee, had joint effusion and palpable loose body under patella.

data.diagnosis: Acute lateral patellar dislocation with an associated patellar osteochondral fracture
data.description: Displacement of the patella laterally can shear cartilage and underlying bone from its medial articular surface, producing a loose fragment. This is the leading explanation for the acute dislocation followed by locking and a palpable loose body; the supplied radiographs alone do not reliably establish the fragment's origin.
symptoms_in_common: Tenderness around the medial patellofemoral ligament
Palpable loose body beneath the patella
Generalized joint laxity predisposing to patellar instability
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic fatigue syndrome is not a characteristic feature

data.diagnosis: Osteochondral fracture of the lateral femoral condyle
data.description: A fragment of cartilage and underlying bone can detach from the lateral femoral condyle when the patella strikes it during dislocation or reduction. The resulting intra-articular loose body can cause persistent effusion and mechanical locking.
symptoms_in_common: Acute lateral patellar dislocation as a potential injury mechanism
Acute knee pain and inability to bear weight
symptoms_not_in_common: Medial patellofemoral ligament tenderness reflects the associated patellar injury rather than the condylar fracture itself
Generalized joint laxity is not a characteristic manifestation of a condylar fracture
Chronic fatigue syndrome is not a characteristic feature

data.diagnosis: Juvenile osteochondritis dissecans with an unstable or detached fragment
data.description: A disorder of subchondral bone in adolescents that can destabilize the overlying cartilage and release an osteochondral loose body, causing swelling and mechanical symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset with a witnessed lateral patellar dislocation is less typical than a preceding history of activity-related pain
Medial patellofemoral ligament tenderness is not characteristic
Generalized joint laxity is not a characteristic manifestation
Chronic fatigue syndrome is not a characteristic feature

data.description: A torn meniscal fragment, particularly a bucket-handle tear, can become displaced within the joint and cause painful locking, swelling, and loss of motion.
symptoms_not_in_common: Visible lateral patellar dislocation is not explained by an isolated meniscal tear
A palpable loose body beneath the patella is atypical for a meniscal tear
Tenderness localized to the medial patellofemoral ligament rather than the joint line
Chronic fatigue syndrome is not a characteristic feature

data.diagnosis: Medial patellofemoral ligament tear associated with acute patellar instability
data.description: Disruption of the main soft-tissue restraint to lateral patellar displacement commonly accompanies a first-time lateral dislocation. Generalized laxity increases susceptibility, but an isolated ligament tear does not explain a true loose body.
symptoms_in_common: Acute pain and inability to bear weight
Beighton score of 6 indicating generalized joint laxity
symptoms_not_in_common: Palpable loose body suggests an additional osteochondral injury
Intermittent mechanical locking is atypical for an isolated ligament tear
Chronic fatigue syndrome is not a characteristic feature

data.diagnosis: Acute lateral patellar dislocation with osteochondral fracture and intra-articular loose body
data.description: Traumatic or low-energy lateral displacement of the patella, often tearing the medial patellofemoral ligament and shearing an osteochondral fragment from the medial patellar facet or lateral femoral condyle; the fragment then acts as a loose body.
symptoms_in_common: Knee 'wobble' and giving way followed by a fall
Pain on palpation around the medial patellofemoral ligament
Palpable loose body under the patella
Joint laxity (Beighton score 6) as a predisposing factor
symptoms_not_in_common: Very low-energy mechanism (carrying a tray) rather than a twisting sports injury
No history of prior dislocations
Chronic fatigue syndrome is unrelated

data.diagnosis: Hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome / hypermobility spectrum disorder with patellar instability
data.description: Heritable connective tissue disorder with generalised joint hypermobility, predisposing to joint subluxations and dislocations after minimal trauma, and often associated with chronic fatigue and pain.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic fatigue syndrome (fatigue is commonly associated)
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of previous joint dislocations
Palpable loose body and mechanical locking are not explained by laxity alone
No reported skin hyperextensibility, abnormal scarring or family history
Acute effusion suggests structural injury rather than laxity alone

data.diagnosis: Osteochondritis dissecans of the knee with unstable or detached fragment
data.description: Focal disorder of subchondral bone in adolescents in which a bone and cartilage fragment can separate and become a loose body, causing pain, effusion and locking.
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden onset with no preceding chronic activity-related knee pain
Frank lateral patellar dislocation on examination
Tenderness over the medial patellofemoral ligament
Loose body appearing only after the acute dislocation event

data.diagnosis: Meniscal tear (including bucket-handle tear or discoid meniscus tear)
data.description: Tear of the fibrocartilaginous meniscus, typically from a twisting injury, causing joint line pain, effusion, locking and giving way.
symptoms_in_common: Reduced range of movement with an extension deficit
symptoms_not_in_common: Laterally dislocated patella
Tenderness over the medial patellofemoral ligament rather than the joint line
Palpable loose body under the patella
No twisting mechanism described
Unremarkable ligamentous and provocative tests

data.description: Tear of the main anterior stabiliser of the knee, usually from a pivoting injury, causing acute haemarthrosis, instability and giving way; it may be accompanied by meniscal or osteochondral injury.
symptoms_in_common: Knee 'wobble' and giving way with a fall
symptoms_not_in_common: Ligamentous tests unremarkable
Laterally dislocated patella
Tenderness localised to the medial patellofemoral ligament
Palpable loose body under the patella
Low-energy, non-pivoting mechanism

data.description: 52-year-old man with 2 weeks of exertional chest fullness in the center of the chest without radiation and associated dyspnea; symptoms absent at rest. Prior screening echocardiogram 3 years earlier showed mild left ventricular hypertrophy with otherwise normal cardiac structure and function. Exam: afebrile, BP 146/70 mmHg, HR 70/min, RR 14/min, BMI 36.2, normal JVP, regular rhythm without murmurs/rubs/gallops, normal lung and abdominal exam, no edema, warm legs with symmetric distal pulses. Labs: WBC 10,900/mm³, creatinine 1.6 mg/dL (baseline 1.0), BUN 15 mg/dL, potassium 5.4 mmol/L, normal INR, sodium, thyrotropin, and troponin I.

ECG evidence suggestive of advanced atrioventricular block

Myocardial biopsy showing giant cells and extensive inflammation

Giant cells and inflammation in myocardial tissue

data.description: Inflammation and injury of cardiac muscle, often associated with viral infection or immune activation, which can produce chest discomfort, arrhythmias, conduction abnormalities, and heart failure.

Normal troponin I, compatible with angina without infarction

data.description: Rare, rapidly progressive, likely autoimmune myocarditis characterized by diffuse myocardial inflammation with multinucleated giant cells and myocyte necrosis, often presenting with heart failure, ventricular arrhythmias and heart block in middle-aged adults.

Wall thickening previously read as mild left ventricular hypertrophy

data.description: Atherosclerotic narrowing of coronary arteries producing exertional myocardial ischemia; may cause ischemic arrhythmias and conduction disturbances.

data.description: Cardiac involvement by Borrelia burgdorferi, typically causing fluctuating AV block that can progress rapidly to complete heart block, sometimes with myopericarditis.

data.description: 34-year-old man in Scotland presented with an expanding itchy rash on the right flank that persisted for three months. data.description: An inflammatory skin reaction producing slowly expanding rings or arcs, sometimes associated with infection, medication, or another trigger. A fine trailing scale may occur inside the advancing edge.

The very large solitary ring is less typical than smaller eczematous patches

data.description: Cutaneous manifestation of Borrelia burgdorferi sensu lato infection transmitted by Ixodes ticks, presenting as a slowly expanding annular erythematous lesion with central clearing. data.description: Superficial dermatophyte infection of the skin producing annular, pruritic plaques with an active, raised, scaly border and central clearing that expand centrifugally.

Very large single lesion with a smooth, flat erythematous band
Exposure history in a tick-endemic area points elsewhere

data.description: A 20-year-old woman with a history of asthma presented to the emergency department with shortness of breath and sharp pains in her chest and neck. The pain worsened on deep inspiration. She had a cough producing small amounts of whitish sputum. She had experienced several previous asthma exacerbations and had not been using her inhalers regularly. On examination, her airway was patent with a generalized moderate wheeze in her chest, but no other obvious clinical signs. She could speak in full sentences and had normal oxygen saturations and temperature. She was mildly tachycardic and appeared slightly anxious. Blood tests showed a mild neutrophilia and elevated C reactive protein.

Air escapes from ruptured alveoli into the mediastinum, often following coughing or an asthma exacerbation. This is the leading consideration: the radiograph appears to show air outlining mediastinal structures and extending into the neck, although formal radiologic confirmation is needed.

Apparent mediastinal and cervical air on the radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated C-reactive protein and neutrophilia are nonspecific rather than defining findings

data.description: An episode of increased airway inflammation and narrowing causing wheezing, cough, and breathlessness. It may coexist with, and precipitate, pneumomediastinum.

symptoms_not_in_common: Sharp pleuritic chest pain is less typical than chest tightness
Neck pain is not characteristic of uncomplicated asthma
Apparent mediastinal and cervical air suggests an additional complication

data.description: Air enters the pleural space and partially or completely collapses a lung. It can cause acute pleuritic pain and breathlessness, but a definite pleural air collection is not evident on the supplied radiograph.

data.description: Inflammation of the larger airways, usually caused by a viral infection, producing cough and sometimes triggering an asthma exacerbation.

data.description: 48-year-old male presented with 1-week history of jaundice, dark brown urine, pale stools, and nausea. Medical history and physical exam were unremarkable. Elevated conjugated bilirubin and cholestatic enzymes

diagnoses.name: Primary pancreatic T-cell/histiocyte-rich large B-cell lymphoma
diagnoses.title: T-cell/histiocyte rich large B-cell lymphoma

External compression of the laryngeal region from behind

data.description: 62-year-old man with hypertension treated with amlodipine presented with 4 episodes of palpitations over 1 week, described as fast heartbeat and shortness of breath; two episodes followed alcohol intake. data.description: Autonomous aldosterone overproduction from an adrenal adenoma or hyperplasia causing hypertension, often with hypokalemia; associated with a markedly higher risk of atrial fibrillation than essential hypertension.
symptoms_in_common: Hypertension uncontrolled despite amlodipine (160/90 mm Hg)
Frequent supraventricular ectopy (potentially promoted by hypokalemia and atrial fibrosis)
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported muscle weakness, cramps, polyuria or documented hypokalemia
Hypertension on only one drug, not clearly resistant
Alcohol association of episodes

data.description: Excess thyroid hormone increases adrenergic sensitivity and atrial automaticity, commonly causing atrial fibrillation and supraventricular ectopy, particularly in older patients who may have few other symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Relatively high average heart rate on Holter (99 bpm)
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss, tremor, heat intolerance, sweating or goiter reported
Resting pulse 82 beats/min and regular at examination
Diastolic hypertension rather than wide pulse pressure
Alcohol association of episodes

data.description: Catecholamine-secreting tumor of the adrenal medulla causing sustained or paroxysmal hypertension with episodic palpitations, headache and sweating; can provoke atrial tachyarrhythmias, and attacks may be triggered by alcohol.
symptoms_in_common: Paroxysmal episodes of palpitations with fast heartbeat
Atrial tachyarrhythmias and frequent supraventricular ectopy
symptoms_not_in_common: No headache, sweating, pallor or anxiety during episodes
No documented paroxysmal blood pressure surges or orthostatic hypotension
Rare condition; arrhythmia alone is an uncommon presentation

data.description: 8-year-5-month-old male with severe motor and cognitive developmental delay: never achieved head control or unsupported sitting, began turning over at age 5, and cannot speak or communicate. Born at term to consanguineous parents by vaginal delivery, birth weight 2.5 kg. Examination showed myopathic facies, high-arched palate, nystagmus, generalized muscle weakness, marked hypotonia, absent deep tendon reflexes, knee and ankle contractures, and positive right Babinski sign with possible left Babinski positivity. Serum CK was 1514 U/L.

An autosomal recessive dystroglycanopathy, often associated with POMGNT1 variants, that combines congenital muscular dystrophy, developmental brain abnormalities, and ocular disease. This is a strong diagnostic consideration, but genetic and ophthalmologic confirmation is needed.
symptoms_in_common: Profound motor and cognitive developmental delay
Absent speech and inability to sit unsupported
Generalized weakness, marked hypotonia, and absent tendon reflexes
Myopathic facies and elevated CK of 1514 U/L
Nystagmus and apparently abnormal fundus photographs
MRI showing ventricular enlargement and white-matter signal abnormalities
Babinski sign suggesting central nervous system involvement
Parental consanguinity supporting autosomal recessive inheritance
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly discordant reported feature; however, characteristic cortical and cerebellar malformations are not confidently established from the supplied images

data.description: An autosomal recessive FKTN-related dystroglycanopathy causing early muscular weakness, intellectual disability, and developmental brain abnormalities, often including cortical dysplasia.
symptoms_in_common: Severe early-onset muscle weakness and hypotonia
Severe cognitive impairment and absent speech
Ventricular enlargement and white-matter abnormalities on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Complete failure to achieve head control is more severe than in many classic cases
Nystagmus and prominent structural ocular abnormalities are less characteristic than in muscle-eye-brain disease

data.description: A severe autosomal recessive dystroglycanopathy characterized by congenital muscular dystrophy, major brain malformations, and ocular abnormalities. It usually has a more severe, life-limiting course than other dystroglycanopathies.
symptoms_in_common: Failure to achieve head control or unsupported sitting
Nystagmus and apparently abnormal fundus findings
symptoms_not_in_common: Survival to age 8 years is less typical of classic Walker-Warburg syndrome
The supplied MRI does not clearly establish the extensive cortical, brainstem, and cerebellar malformations usually associated with classic disease

data.description: An autosomal recessive muscular dystrophy caused by laminin-alpha-2 deficiency, producing severe early weakness, contractures, elevated CK, and characteristic cerebral white-matter abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound cognitive impairment and complete absence of communication are not typical of uncomplicated LAMA2-related disease
Nystagmus and apparent ocular structural abnormalities are not characteristic
Marked ventricular enlargement is less characteristic than the white-matter abnormalities

data.diagnosis: POMT2-related congenital muscular dystrophy with intellectual disability
data.description: An autosomal recessive dystroglycanopathy caused by POMT2 variants, with a spectrum ranging from muscular dystrophy with intellectual disability to severe muscle-eye-brain phenotypes.
symptoms_in_common: Severe motor and cognitive developmental delay
Absent tendon reflexes and joint contractures
Possible combined brain and ocular involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent ocular abnormalities and marked ventricular enlargement are less typical of the milder intellectual-disability phenotype, although compatible with the severe end of the POMT2 spectrum
Failure to achieve head control represents an unusually severe presentation for milder POMT2-related disease

data.diagnosis: Muscle-eye-brain disease (congenital muscular dystrophy-dystroglycanopathy type A3, e.g., POMGNT1-related)
data.description: Autosomal recessive alpha-dystroglycanopathy causing congenital muscular dystrophy with structural eye abnormalities (retinal dysplasia/detachment, myopia, optic atrophy) and brain malformations (pachygyria/polymicrogyria, ventriculomegaly, white matter changes, brainstem and cerebellar hypoplasia). Survival into childhood is common.
symptoms_in_common: Severe motor and cognitive developmental delay
Generalized muscle weakness and marked hypotonia
Nystagmus with abnormal fundus/retinal findings on imaging
Ventriculomegaly, white matter signal abnormalities and cortical malformation on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No seizures reported, although these are common in this disease
Never achieving head control is at the severe end of the spectrum

data.description: The most severe alpha-dystroglycanopathy (POMT1, POMT2, FKRP, FKTN, LARGE and other genes), with cobblestone lissencephaly, hydrocephalus, cerebellar and brainstem malformations, severe eye malformations and congenital muscular dystrophy. It is usually lethal within the first 1-3 years.
symptoms_in_common: Severe hypotonia and weakness from birth
Profound developmental delay with no milestones such as head control or sitting
Ventriculomegaly/hydrocephalus and cortical malformation on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Survival to more than 8 years (usually fatal in infancy)
Learned to turn over at age 5
No reported occipital encephalocele or complete agyria
No reported microphthalmia or congenital glaucoma

data.description: Autosomal recessive FKTN-related dystroglycanopathy, most common in Japan, with congenital muscular dystrophy, cobblestone cortical dysplasia, intellectual disability, seizures and milder eye involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Hypotonia and generalized weakness from infancy
Cortical malformation and white matter changes on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe retinal/eye abnormalities are less typical (eye involvement is usually mild)
Marked ventriculomegaly is less common
Most patients achieve head control and sitting
No seizures reported
Rare outside Japanese ancestry

data.description: Autosomal recessive congenital muscular dystrophy due to laminin-alpha2 deficiency, with severe hypotonia, weakness, contractures, raised CK and diffuse white matter signal abnormality on MRI, usually with normal cognition.
symptoms_in_common: White matter signal abnormalities on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe cognitive impairment and absent speech (cognition is usually normal)
Retinal abnormalities and nystagmus
Ventriculomegaly and cortical malformation
Babinski sign
Never achieving head control or sitting (most achieve sitting)

data.diagnosis: Congenital muscular dystrophy with intellectual disability due to other dystroglycanopathy genes (e.g., FKRP/LARGE-related, MDC1C/MDC1D)
data.description: Intermediate alpha-dystroglycanopathy phenotypes with congenital muscular dystrophy, intellectual disability and variable structural brain abnormalities (cerebellar cysts, white matter changes, pachygyria), with or without eye involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Severe intellectual disability and absent speech
White matter and structural brain abnormalities on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent retinal abnormalities are more typical of muscle-eye-brain disease
Marked ventriculomegaly is less common
CK is often much higher in FKRP-related disease
No reported muscle hypertrophy (calves, tongue)

data.description: A 22 year old man presented to the emergency department with abdominal pain, jaundice, itching, and fever. His urine was dark and stools pale. Physical examination revealed temperature of 38.7°C, icterus, abdominal tenderness worst in the right upper quadrant with negative Murphy's sign, impalpable gall bladder, inflamed oropharynx with cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy. Laboratory tests showed liver function abnormalities with alkaline phosphatase 327, aspartate aminotransferase 358, and bilirubin 109 suggesting cholestasis. White cell count was elevated at 20.8, C reactive protein was raised at 17, and platelets were low at 168. Monospot test was positive for Epstein Barr virus, confirmed by positive Epstein Barr virus serology. Hepatitis A, B, and C serology were negative.

Gallbladder inflammation without gallstones, occasionally complicating acute Epstein–Barr virus infection. The supplied images appear to show gallbladder wall thickening and edema without an obvious stone, making this a leading possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Fever and right upper quadrant abdominal tenderness
Jaundice, itching, dark urine, and pale stools
Elevated alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, and AST
Inflamed oropharynx and cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Positive Monospot and Epstein–Barr virus serology
Apparent gallbladder wall thickening and edema on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative Murphy's sign is less typical of acute cholecystitis, although it does not exclude it

data.diagnosis: Epstein–Barr virus-associated cholestatic hepatitis with reactive gallbladder edema
data.description: Acute Epstein–Barr virus infection can cause hepatic inflammation and intrahepatic cholestasis. Associated gallbladder wall edema can mimic cholecystitis without primary gallbladder inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Fever, inflamed oropharynx, and generalized lymphadenopathy
Positive Monospot and Epstein–Barr virus serology
Jaundice, itching, dark urine, and pale stools
Elevated AST, alkaline phosphatase, and bilirubin
Abdominal discomfort and right upper quadrant tenderness
Apparent gallbladder wall edema and splenic enlargement on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked focal right upper quadrant tenderness is less typical of uncomplicated hepatitis and raises concern for associated gallbladder inflammation

data.description: Infection of the bile ducts, usually caused by biliary obstruction. Fever, jaundice, and right upper quadrant pain form the classic clinical triad, but obstruction is not established by the supplied images.
symptoms_in_common: Jaundice and right upper quadrant abdominal pain
Dark urine, pale stools, and itching
symptoms_not_in_common: Inflamed oropharynx with cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Positive Monospot and Epstein–Barr virus serology suggest an alternative cause
Apparent splenic enlargement is not typical of isolated acute cholangitis

data.description: A stone in the common bile duct can obstruct bile flow, causing pain and cholestatic jaundice. No definite ductal stone is demonstrated in the supplied images, so this is a less supported alternative.
symptoms_in_common: Jaundice, itching, dark urine, and pale stools
symptoms_not_in_common: High fever and marked leukocytosis are not typical of uncomplicated obstruction and would suggest superimposed infection
Inflamed oropharynx and generalized lymphadenopathy
Positive Monospot and Epstein–Barr virus serology

data.description: Gallbladder inflammation caused by a stone obstructing the cystic duct. Gallbladder wall thickening, fever, and localized tenderness fit, but no obvious gallstone is visible in the supplied images.
symptoms_in_common: Right upper quadrant abdominal pain and tenderness
Apparent gallbladder wall thickening and edema on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative Murphy's sign
Prominent jaundice, itching, dark urine, and pale stools are less typical without additional bile duct obstruction
Inflamed oropharynx and cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Positive Monospot and Epstein–Barr virus serology

data.diagnosis: Epstein-Barr virus infectious mononucleosis with cholestatic hepatitis and acalculous gallbladder involvement
data.description: Acute EBV infection causing pharyngitis, lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly; it can uncommonly cause cholestatic hepatitis with jaundice and reactive gallbladder wall thickening/oedema (acalculous cholecystitis) without biliary obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Jaundice with dark urine and pale stools
Right upper quadrant pain and tenderness
Raised AST, alkaline phosphatase and bilirubin
Negative hepatitis A, B and C serology
Gallbladder wall thickening/oedema on ultrasound and MRI without an obvious obstructing stone
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked cholestatic jaundice with pruritus is uncommon in EBV (most cases have only mild transaminitis)
Pale stools are unusual

data.description: Inflammation of the gallbladder, usually from a stone obstructing the cystic duct, causing right upper quadrant pain, fever and leukocytosis.
symptoms_in_common: Right upper quadrant pain and tenderness
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative Murphy's sign
Marked jaundice, itching, pale stools and dark urine
Pharyngitis
Cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Positive EBV tests
No obvious gallstones on imaging
Splenomegaly
Young male with no stated risk factors

data.description: Obstruction of the common bile duct by a stone with secondary bacterial infection of the biliary tree, classically giving Charcot's triad of fever, jaundice and right upper quadrant pain.
symptoms_not_in_common: Inflamed oropharynx
Cervical and axillary lymphadenopathy
Positive Monospot and EBV serology
No obvious duct stone or biliary dilatation on imaging
Splenomegaly
Young age

data.diagnosis: Acute viral hepatitis from another virus (e.g. cytomegalovirus, hepatitis E)
data.description: Acute hepatocellular inflammation from a hepatotropic or systemic virus, causing fever, jaundice, right upper quadrant discomfort and raised transaminases; reactive gallbladder wall thickening can occur. CMV can also produce a mononucleosis-like illness.
symptoms_in_common: Negative hepatitis A, B and C serology
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive Monospot (heterophile antibody) and confirmatory EBV serology
Prominent exudative-type pharyngitis is less typical of CMV
Marked leukocytosis
Predominantly cholestatic picture with pruritus and pale stools

data.diagnosis: Lymphoma (e.g. Hodgkin lymphoma) with hepatic or biliary involvement
data.description: Lymphoid malignancy that can present in young adults with fever, lymphadenopathy and splenomegaly; jaundice may result from liver infiltration, porta hepatis nodal compression of the bile duct, or paraneoplastic cholestasis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute onset
Inflamed oropharynx
Positive Monospot and EBV serology explaining the picture
Acute right upper quadrant tenderness with gallbladder wall oedema
No mass or biliary dilatation on imaging
Markedly raised AST

data.description: A 65-year-old man with a 40 pack-year smoking history presented with a one-month history of worsening breathlessness and chest discomfort on walking. He came to hospital following a collapse that occurred after self-administering sublingual glyceryl trinitrate to relieve his symptoms. He reported no history of cough or coryza, had not lost weight, and experienced no haemoptysis. Laboratory testing revealed a raised serum D-dimer level.

data.diagnosis: Bronchogenic carcinoma with pulmonary lymphangitic carcinomatosis
data.description: Lung cancer spreading through pulmonary lymphatic vessels causes septal and peribronchovascular thickening. The apparent right hilar/mediastinal soft-tissue abnormality, predominantly right-sided septal thickening, and small right pleural effusion make this an important possibility, although tissue diagnosis is required.
symptoms_in_common: Older age and substantial smoking history
Right-sided interstitial abnormalities and apparent hilar/mediastinal soft-tissue enlargement on imaging
Raised D-dimer, which can occur with malignancy
symptoms_not_in_common: Collapse immediately after glyceryl trinitrate is not a characteristic manifestation
No weight loss, cough, or haemoptysis, although their absence does not exclude lung cancer

data.diagnosis: Mediastinal lymphoma with pulmonary lymphatic involvement
data.description: A lymphoid malignancy can produce bulky mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy, obstruct lymphatic drainage, and cause pulmonary interstitial thickening and pleural effusion.
symptoms_in_common: Septal thickening and a small right pleural effusion
Raised D-dimer, a nonspecific finding that may accompany malignancy
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported weight loss
Collapse following glyceryl trinitrate is not typical
A heavy smoking history is not a characteristic lymphoma risk factor

data.description: Obstruction of pulmonary arteries by thrombus can cause breathlessness, chest pain, and syncope. The elevated D-dimer supports investigating this urgent possibility but is not diagnostic; the supplied lung-window image cannot establish or exclude embolism.
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly unilateral septal thickening with apparent bulky hilar/mediastinal soft tissue is not typical of uncomplicated pulmonary embolism
Gradual worsening over one month is less typical of a single acute embolic event
The immediate association of collapse with glyceryl trinitrate suggests a possible additional hypotensive mechanism

data.diagnosis: Unilateral pulmonary edema from pulmonary venous obstruction
data.description: Impaired drainage of a pulmonary vein, potentially from compression by a hilar or mediastinal lesion, can produce unilateral interstitial edema with septal thickening and pleural effusion.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent adjacent hilar/mediastinal soft-tissue abnormality that could cause vascular compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Raised D-dimer is not specific for pulmonary venous obstruction
Collapse after glyceryl trinitrate is not a characteristic feature

data.description: An uncommon fibroinflammatory process in the mediastinum can encase pulmonary vessels and airways, causing venous or lymphatic obstruction and asymmetric pulmonary interstitial changes.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral septal thickening compatible with impaired venous or lymphatic drainage
symptoms_not_in_common: Raised D-dimer is not a characteristic diagnostic finding
Collapse after glyceryl trinitrate is not typical
Heavy smoking is not a characteristic risk factor
No cough or haemoptysis, which may occur with airway or vascular involvement

data.diagnosis: Lymphangitis carcinomatosa secondary to primary lung carcinoma
data.description: Spread of tumour through the pulmonary lymphatics, usually from a central bronchogenic carcinoma, causing unilateral interlobular septal and peribronchovascular thickening with progressive breathlessness.
symptoms_in_common: unilateral right-sided reticular/septal thickening on chest X-ray
CT showing right hilar/mediastinal soft tissue mass with smooth and nodular interlobular septal thickening confined to the right lung
symptoms_not_in_common: no weight loss
no haemoptysis
no cough
collapse after glyceryl trinitrate

data.description: Obstruction of the pulmonary arteries by thrombus, causing breathlessness, chest pain, syncope and raised D-dimer; malignancy is a major risk factor.
symptoms_in_common: possible underlying malignancy as a prothrombotic state
symptoms_not_in_common: one-month subacute course
unilateral interlobular septal thickening on CT
right hilar soft tissue mass
no haemoptysis
collapse temporally related to glyceryl trinitrate rather than spontaneous

data.diagnosis: Ischaemic heart disease with unilateral pulmonary oedema (heart failure)
data.description: Coronary artery disease causing exertional angina and left ventricular dysfunction; pulmonary oedema produces septal thickening, though it is usually bilateral.
symptoms_in_common: heavy smoking history and age as risk factors
use of glyceryl trinitrate for symptoms
D-dimer can be mildly raised in heart failure
symptoms_not_in_common: strictly unilateral right-sided changes
right hilar/mediastinal soft tissue mass
nodular septal thickening
no clear cardiomegaly or pleural effusions

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary veno-occlusion or pulmonary artery obstruction by central tumour
data.description: Compression or invasion of the pulmonary veins or artery by a hilar mass, causing unilateral venous congestion with septal thickening, reduced preload and exertional symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: no haemoptysis
no pleural effusion evident
nodular pattern of septal thickening favours lymphatic tumour spread rather than pure congestion

data.diagnosis: Lymphoma or sarcoidosis with lymphatic involvement
