data.description: Lymphoproliferative or granulomatous disease causing hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy with perilymphatic interstitial infiltration and septal thickening.
symptoms_in_common: absence of infective symptoms (no cough or coryza)
symptoms_not_in_common: strictly unilateral distribution (sarcoidosis is usually bilateral and symmetrical)
older age and heavy smoking history favour carcinoma
no weight loss, fever or night sweats
exertional chest discomfort
collapse after glyceryl trinitrate

data.description: A 50-year-old man presented with a 3-week history of back pain and a skull mass that had been growing slowly for 7 months. Physical examination revealed a smooth, firm, and non-tender mass on his skull that gave him the appearance of having a high domed forehead. Laboratory investigations showed renal impairment, hypercalcaemia, anaemia, and immunoparesis. Lambda light chains were detected in both urine and serum. Bone marrow aspirate showed a low level infiltration of plasma cells, though the patient could not tolerate a bone marrow biopsy. A biopsy of the thoracic lesion revealed a monomorphic population of plasma cells that were strongly positive for CD138 and lambda light chain restricted.

data.diagnosis: Lambda light-chain multiple myeloma with bulky osseous plasmacytomas
data.description: A malignant plasma-cell disorder producing monoclonal lambda light chains and causing bone lesions, renal injury, hypercalcaemia and anaemia. This is the leading diagnosis; limited marrow involvement on aspirate does not exclude patchy disease.
symptoms_in_common: Back pain with a thoracic lesion
Slowly enlarging, firm skull mass consistent with a bulky calvarial plasmacytoma
Lambda light chains in serum and urine
Thoracic biopsy showing CD138-positive, lambda-restricted plasma cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Low plasma-cell infiltration on marrow aspirate is less typical of conventional diffuse marrow disease
An exceptionally large, slowly growing skull mass is an unusual presentation

data.diagnosis: Multifocal osseous plasmacytoma with minimal marrow involvement
data.description: A plasma-cell neoplasm forming multiple localized bone tumors despite relatively little marrow involvement. Myeloma-related systemic organ damage would favor classification as multiple myeloma rather than localized plasmacytoma disease.
symptoms_in_common: Back pain and a separate thoracic lesion
Low-level plasma-cell infiltration on marrow aspirate
CD138-positive, lambda-restricted plasma cells in the thoracic lesion
Monoclonal lambda light chains in serum and urine
symptoms_not_in_common: Renal impairment attributable to the plasma-cell disorder
Hypercalcaemia
Anaemia
Marked systemic findings and immunoparesis favor multiple myeloma over localized plasmacytoma disease

data.description: An aggressive lymphoma with plasma-cell differentiation that can express CD138 and show light-chain restriction. It is a less likely pathological mimic requiring assessment of cell morphology, proliferation rate, Epstein–Barr virus status and additional immunophenotyping.
symptoms_in_common: Possible involvement of bone and other extranodal sites
symptoms_not_in_common: Slow skull-mass growth over seven months is less typical of an aggressive lymphoma
The combination of hypercalcaemia, renal impairment and monoclonal urinary light chains strongly favors myeloma
Immunoparesis is more characteristic of a plasma-cell disorder
The biopsy describes plasma cells rather than explicitly plasmablastic morphology

data.description: An indolent B-cell lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation, usually associated with an IgM monoclonal protein. Rare non-IgM or light-chain-producing forms can resemble plasma-cell neoplasms.
symptoms_in_common: Possible renal impairment related to a monoclonal protein
A clonal plasma-cell component can express CD138
symptoms_not_in_common: Bulky skull and thoracic bone lesions are unusual
Hypercalcaemia is uncommon
A monomorphic plasma-cell tumor without a reported lymphoid component favors a plasma-cell neoplasm
The overall combination of bone lesions, immunoparesis and lambda light chains is more typical of myeloma

data.diagnosis: Metastatic carcinoma involving the skull and spine
data.description: A solid-organ cancer spreading to bone can produce an enlarging calvarial mass, spinal pain and malignancy-associated hypercalcaemia. This is an imaging-based alternative but is strongly contradicted by the reported biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Back pain with a thoracic lesion
Renal impairment, potentially worsened by hypercalcaemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Monomorphic, CD138-positive, lambda-restricted plasma cells indicate a plasma-cell neoplasm rather than carcinoma
Lambda light chains in both serum and urine
Immunoparesis
Clonal plasma-cell findings are not explained by ordinary bone metastases

data.diagnosis: Lambda light chain multiple myeloma with calvarial and thoracic plasmacytomas
data.description: Malignant clonal plasma cell disorder producing monoclonal light chains, causing bone destruction, hypercalcaemia, renal impairment, anaemia and immunoparesis; may present with large bone-based plasmacytomas with soft-tissue extension.
symptoms_in_common: Lambda light chains in serum and urine
Plasma cell infiltration of bone marrow
Thoracic lesion biopsy showing monomorphic CD138-positive, lambda-restricted plasma cells
Large enhancing, vascular calvarial mass on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Only low-level marrow plasma cell infiltration on aspirate (may reflect patchy disease or sampling)
Such a large skull mass is an unusual presentation

data.diagnosis: Solitary plasmacytoma of bone with minimal marrow involvement
data.description: Localized clonal plasma cell tumour of bone without systemic myeloma-defining end-organ damage, with absent or minimal marrow plasmacytosis.
symptoms_in_common: Biopsy showing monoclonal CD138-positive, lambda-restricted plasma cells
symptoms_not_in_common: More than one lesion (skull and thoracic)
Hypercalcaemia
Renal impairment
Anaemia
Immunoparesis

data.diagnosis: Metastatic carcinoma to bone (e.g. renal cell, thyroid, lung or prostate)
data.description: Haematogenous spread of a solid tumour to bone, producing lytic or hypervascular lesions of the skull and spine, often with hypercalcaemia of malignancy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lambda light chains in serum and urine
Immunoparesis
Biopsy showing monoclonal plasma cells rather than carcinoma
No known primary tumour
Slow growth over 7 months

data.diagnosis: Lymphoma with plasmacytic differentiation involving bone (e.g. plasmablastic lymphoma or lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma)
data.description: B-cell lymphomas that can express plasma cell markers and light chain restriction, may secrete paraprotein, and can form bone and soft-tissue masses.
symptoms_not_in_common: Monomorphic mature plasma cell morphology
Hypercalcaemia and light chain-related renal impairment are more typical of myeloma
Slow, indolent growth over 7 months (plasmablastic lymphoma is aggressive)
No lymphadenopathy or B symptoms reported
No immunodeficiency reported

data.diagnosis: Intraosseous or en plaque meningioma with extracranial extension
data.description: Usually benign meningothelial tumour that can invade the calvarium and form a slowly growing, enhancing, vascular scalp and skull mass.
symptoms_in_common: Avidly enhancing, vascular calvarial lesion on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Back pain with thoracic lesion
Hypercalcaemia
Renal impairment
Anaemia
Immunoparesis
Lambda light chains in serum and urine
Plasma cell histology on biopsy

data.description: A 59-year-old woman was admitted to the hospital with a 9-day history of stiffness, swelling, and severe pain beginning in the metacarpophalangeal joint of the right thumb, followed by bilateral ankle involvement 3 days later. She had a history of stroke, glaucoma, and total abdominal hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy 7 years prior. The patient lived in New England, worked in health care, and reported unprotected vaginal intercourse 2 weeks before presentation. Physical examination showed the right thumb metacarpophalangeal joint was erythematous, warm, and painful with movement. Both ankles showed effusion and warmth without erythema, with pain on all range of motion. No fever, chills, night sweats, or systemic symptoms were reported. Joint stiffness was not worse in the morning and did not improve throughout the day. Symptoms had not improved despite 4 days of methylprednisolone therapy.

data.diagnosis: Disseminated gonococcal infection with septic arthritis
data.description: Dissemination of Neisseria gonorrhoeae from a mucosal infection can cause migratory joint inflammation or purulent arthritis. This is the leading consideration given the recent sexual exposure and apparent diplococci in the supplied microbiology images, although organism identification requires laboratory confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Acute severe joint pain, warmth, swelling, and restricted movement
Sequential involvement of the thumb joint and both ankles
Absence of systemic symptoms does not exclude gonococcal arthritis
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported fever, rash, or tenosynovitis, which can accompany disseminated infection
Presentation at age 59 is less common than in younger sexually active adults

data.diagnosis: Nongonococcal bacterial septic arthritis, particularly Staphylococcus aureus
data.description: Bacterial infection of joints can rapidly damage cartilage and requires urgent synovial fluid testing and treatment. Staphylococcus aureus is a common cause, although the apparent diplococcal morphology in the image is less characteristic of this organism.
symptoms_in_common: Pain throughout passive or active range of motion
Failure to improve with corticosteroid therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: Sequential involvement of three joints is less typical than a single infected joint
No fever or systemic illness, although these can be absent
Recent sexual exposure is more suggestive of gonococcal infection

data.description: A sterile inflammatory arthritis that develops after a genitourinary infection, often Chlamydia trachomatis. It commonly affects lower-extremity joints; confirmed bacteria in synovial fluid would argue against this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral ankle pain, swelling, and effusions
Onset within weeks of a possible infectious exposure
Absence of fever or systemic symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Initial thumb metacarpophalangeal involvement is less characteristic
No reported urethritis, conjunctivitis, enthesitis, or mucocutaneous lesions
Stiffness does not improve with activity
No improvement with methylprednisolone

data.description: A late manifestation of Borrelia burgdorferi infection causing intermittent or persistent inflammation of one or a few joints, usually the knee. Residence in New England increases exposure plausibility, but the joint distribution and microbiology are less supportive.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of fever or systemic symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Initial thumb metacarpophalangeal inflammation is unusual
Severe pain is less typical than prominent swelling with relatively modest pain
Rapid sequential involvement of the thumb and both ankles is less characteristic
No reported knee involvement

data.description: Calcium pyrophosphate crystals can provoke abrupt, painful inflammatory arthritis in older adults, sometimes involving multiple joints. Synovial fluid crystal analysis is needed, and crystals do not exclude concurrent infection.
symptoms_in_common: Abrupt severe joint pain and swelling
Metacarpophalangeal and ankle involvement can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Sequential thumb and bilateral ankle involvement is less typical than knee or wrist involvement
Recent sexual exposure is not explained
Failure to improve with methylprednisolone is less supportive
Stiffness without morning predominance or improvement during the day is nonspecific

data.description: Hematogenous spread of Neisseria gonorrhoeae from a mucosal site causing migratory polyarthritis, tenosynovitis and/or purulent arthritis; organism is a gram-negative diplococcus that grows on blood and chocolate agar.
symptoms_in_common: Acute asymmetric additive/migratory oligoarthritis (thumb MCP then both ankles)
Severe pain, swelling, warmth, erythema of joints
Unprotected vaginal intercourse 2 weeks before onset
Culture growth on blood and chocolate agar with gram-negative diplococci on Gram stain
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or chills
No reported skin pustules or dermatitis
No reported genitourinary symptoms
Age 59 is older than typical

data.description: Septic or immune-mediated arthritis due to Neisseria meningitidis, a gram-negative diplococcus that can cause oligo- or polyarthritis with or without meningitis or sepsis.
symptoms_in_common: Gram-negative diplococci growing on blood and chocolate agar
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, rash, or petechiae
No meningitis or sepsis features
Recent sexual exposure points more to gonococcus
Subacute 9-day course without systemic illness

data.description: Sterile inflammatory arthritis occurring 1-4 weeks after genitourinary (e.g., Chlamydia) or enteric infection, typically asymmetric oligoarthritis of the lower limbs.
symptoms_in_common: Onset about 2 weeks after unprotected intercourse
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive culture with organisms (reactive arthritis is sterile)
No urethritis/cervicitis, conjunctivitis, or enthesitis reported
Lack of improvement with glucocorticoids
Stiffness not worse in the morning

data.diagnosis: Crystal-induced arthritis (gout or calcium pyrophosphate deposition disease)
data.description: Acute inflammatory arthritis from monosodium urate or CPPD crystal deposition, causing sudden painful, red, swollen joints, common in older adults.
symptoms_in_common: Acute severe pain, erythema, warmth of thumb MCP joint
symptoms_not_in_common: No improvement after 4 days of methylprednisolone
Organisms seen on Gram stain and culture
Additive polyarticular spread over days
No prior attacks or known hyperuricemia

data.description: Late manifestation of Borrelia burgdorferi infection endemic in New England, usually causing mono- or oligoarthritis of large joints, especially the knee, with large effusions.
symptoms_in_common: Ankle effusions with warmth and little erythema
symptoms_not_in_common: Small joint (thumb MCP) involvement
Severe pain (Lyme effusions are typically less painful)
No knee involvement
No known tick bite or erythema migrans
Culture growing gram-negative diplococci on routine media

data.description: A 57-year-old male patient presented with a three-month history of fatigue, recurrent sore throats, and a persistent 'cold sore.' The patient had no relevant medical history, drank little alcohol, and was a non-smoker.

A malignancy of mature lymphocytes that can cause fatigue, enlarged lymph nodes, and impaired immunity with recurrent infections. Confirmation requires blood counts, a blood smear, and flow cytometry.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent cold-sore-like lesion, potentially reflecting impaired immunity
Possible cervical or submandibular swelling indicated in the photograph
symptoms_not_in_common: A solitary crusted ulcer at the mouth corner is not a direct or characteristic manifestation; it would more likely represent a secondary infection or another condition

data.description: A malignancy of immature myeloid blood cells that can cause anemia and neutropenia, leading to fatigue, recurrent infections, and poorly healing oral ulcers. Evaluation requires urgent blood counts and, if indicated, bone marrow testing.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent sore throats, potentially associated with neutropenia
Persistent ulcerated mouth-corner lesion, potentially associated with infection or impaired healing
symptoms_not_in_common: A localized cold-sore-like lesion is nonspecific rather than a characteristic manifestation
Possible isolated cervical swelling is less characteristic than in lymphoid malignancies

data.diagnosis: HIV infection with chronic mucocutaneous herpes simplex
data.description: HIV can impair cellular immunity, allowing herpes simplex lesions to become prolonged or atypical and increasing susceptibility to other infections. Neither HIV nor herpes can be established from photographs alone.
symptoms_in_common: Cold-sore-like ulcer persisting for approximately three months
symptoms_not_in_common: The solitary crusted lesion is not specific for HIV and could have an unrelated cause

data.diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lip or oral commissure
data.description: A malignant tumor of squamous epithelial cells that may present as a persistent ulcerated or crusted lip lesion and spread to regional lymph nodes. A nonhealing lesion requires clinical assessment and consideration of biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Possible regional cervical or submandibular swelling
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent sore throats are not typical of a small localized lip carcinoma
Fatigue is not usually an early feature of localized disease

data.description: Herpes simplex virus infection can produce lip vesicles that ulcerate and crust. Ordinary episodes usually heal within one to two weeks; prolonged lesions warrant viral testing and assessment for impaired immunity or an alternative diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Crusted ulcer at the mouth corner
Possible reactive regional lymph node swelling
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistence for three months is atypical in an immunocompetent person
Sustained fatigue is not typical of an isolated recurrent cold sore
Recurrent sore throats over several months are not adequately explained by localized herpes labialis

diagnoses.name: Perioral lesion with plasma cell rich infiltrate
diagnoses.title: Plasma cell neoplasms

data.description: Sexually transmitted infection caused by Treponema pallidum; the primary chancre can occur at the lip or oral commissure as an indurated, crusted ulcer with regional lymphadenopathy, and may overlap with secondary-stage systemic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent ulcerated, crusted lesion at the lip commissure mistaken for a cold sore
Recurrent sore throats (possible pharyngeal involvement or secondary syphilis)
No tobacco or alcohol risk factors for carcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Three-month duration is longer than a typical chancre (usually heals in 3-8 weeks)
No reported rash or genital lesion
No reported sexual exposure history

data.diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lip
data.description: Malignant epithelial tumour of the lip or oral commissure presenting as a persistent, indurated, crusted non-healing ulcer that may metastasise to submandibular or cervical lymph nodes.
symptoms_in_common: Non-healing crusted ulcer for three months
symptoms_not_in_common: Non-smoker with little alcohol intake
Recurrent sore throats
Commissure location is less typical than the sun-exposed lower lip vermilion
Relatively small lesion with early nodal swelling

data.diagnosis: Chronic herpes simplex labialis in an immunocompromised host (e.g., underlying HIV infection)
data.description: Reactivation of HSV-1 normally heals within 2 weeks; in immunosuppressed patients lesions can become chronic, ulcerative and crusted, accompanied by systemic symptoms of the underlying immune deficiency.
symptoms_in_common: Lesion resembling a cold sore at the lip
Recurrent sore throats suggesting recurrent infection or immune compromise
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistence for three months is very atypical for HSV
No vesicles or reported prodromal tingling or pain
No known immunosuppression
Marked induration

data.diagnosis: Angular cheilitis with secondary infection (candidal or staphylococcal)
data.description: Inflammation and fissuring of the oral commissure caused by Candida and/or Staphylococcus, often associated with nutritional deficiency, anaemia, or immune compromise.
symptoms_in_common: Lesion located at the oral commissure
symptoms_not_in_common: Unilateral lesion (usually bilateral)
Indurated ulcer with dark crust
Prominent submandibular lymphadenopathy
No dentures or other predisposing factors mentioned

data.diagnosis: Haematological malignancy (leukaemia or lymphoma) with oral manifestation
data.description: Malignancies of blood or lymphoid cells cause immune dysfunction, recurrent infections, fatigue, lymphadenopathy, and non-healing oral or perioral ulcers.
symptoms_in_common: Lymph node swelling in the neck
symptoms_not_in_common: Single localised indurated lesion at the commissure
No reported bruising, bleeding, gingival swelling, fever, night sweats or weight loss
Unilateral localised rather than generalised lymphadenopathy

data.description: A 44-year-old man with a 17-year history of tobacco and cannabis use presented with acute dyspnoea and left-sided pleuritic chest pain. He had no other medical conditions and took no regular medications. On examination, he was thin and hypoxic, with a silent, hyper-resonant left hemithorax. Laboratory results showed normal α-1 antitrypsin concentration (1.4 g/L), normal immunoglobulins, and specific IgE for Aspergillus. Spirometry revealed severe obstruction with FVC of 2.95 L (57% predicted), FEV1 of 1.37 L (34% predicted), and FEV1/FVC ratio of 59% predicted.

Large emphysematous bullae replace and compress functioning lung, causing airflow obstruction and sometimes mimicking pneumothorax. Tobacco and cannabis exposure are associated risk factors. The supplied images strongly favor giant left-sided bullae.
symptoms_in_common: Long history of tobacco and cannabis use
Large, thin-walled air spaces occupying much of the left hemithorax on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt pleuritic chest pain is less typical of uncomplicated bullous emphysema and raises concern for an acute complication

data.description: Air enters the pleural space, often following rupture of an emphysematous bulla. This is an important acute differential, although giant bullae can mimic pneumothorax and the supplied images do not clearly establish pleural air.
symptoms_in_common: Absent breath sounds and hyper-resonance over the left hemithorax
Smoking history and underlying bullous lung abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe persistent airflow obstruction requires underlying lung disease rather than pneumothorax alone
Internal walls within the large left-sided air spaces favor bullae rather than a simple pleural air collection

data.description: A smoking-associated lung disorder characterized by bronchiolocentric nodules and irregular cysts, which can cause airflow obstruction and spontaneous pneumothorax.
symptoms_in_common: Acute pleuritic pain potentially associated with pneumothorax
symptoms_not_in_common: Dominant giant left-sided bullae are less typical than bilateral irregular cysts
The supplied images do not demonstrate the characteristic combination of upper-lung nodules and cysts

data.description: An inherited deficiency of a protective antiprotease causes premature emphysema, often with lower-lung predominance and accelerated progression in smokers.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal alpha-1 antitrypsin concentration substantially argues against clinically significant deficiency
Markedly asymmetric giant bullae are less characteristic than bilateral panacinar emphysema
Acute pleuritic pain is not typical without a complication such as pneumothorax

data.description: An inherited FLCN-associated disorder causing pulmonary cysts and spontaneous pneumothorax, sometimes accompanied by characteristic skin lesions and renal tumors.
symptoms_in_common: Adult presentation with cystic lung abnormalities
Acute dyspnoea and pleuritic chest pain potentially indicating pneumothorax
Large air-filled spaces involving the lower left lung
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe airflow obstruction is unusual because lung function is often relatively preserved
Dominant giant emphysematous bullae are less typical than multiple bilateral basilar and medial cysts
No associated skin lesions, renal tumors, or family history are reported

data.diagnosis: Cannabis- and tobacco-related giant bullous emphysema ("bong lung" / vanishing lung syndrome)
data.description: Severe premature bullous lung disease in young to middle-aged heavy cannabis and tobacco smokers, with large bullae that compress adjacent lung and may rupture, causing secondary pneumothorax.
symptoms_in_common: 17-year history of cannabis and tobacco use
relatively young age (44) for severe emphysema
giant bullae with thin septa on CT
hyperlucent left hemithorax on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: specific IgE for Aspergillus
cystic/honeycomb-like changes at the right lung base on CT

data.diagnosis: Secondary spontaneous pneumothorax (possibly under tension) from ruptured bulla
data.description: Air in the pleural space caused by rupture of a bulla or bleb in a patient with underlying lung disease, producing acute breathlessness and pleuritic pain.
symptoms_not_in_common: thin septations crossing the air spaces on CT suggest bullae rather than free pleural air
severe obstructive spirometry reflects chronic disease rather than pneumothorax itself
specific IgE for Aspergillus

data.diagnosis: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (smoking-related emphysema) with acute complication
data.description: Progressive, incompletely reversible airflow obstruction due to smoking-induced airway disease and parenchymal destruction; may be complicated by bullae and pneumothorax.
symptoms_in_common: severe obstruction on spirometry (reduced FEV1 and FEV1/FVC)
symptoms_not_in_common: young age for such severe disease
abrupt onset with pleuritic chest pain
unilateral silent hyper-resonant hemithorax
giant bullae occupying most of a hemithorax
specific IgE for Aspergillus

data.description: Inherited deficiency of a protease inhibitor leading to early-onset panlobular, basal-predominant emphysema, accelerated by smoking.
symptoms_not_in_common: normal alpha-1 antitrypsin concentration (1.4 g/L)
acute pleuritic chest pain
unilateral silent hyper-resonant hemithorax
specific IgE for Aspergillus
no reported liver disease or family history

data.diagnosis: Allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis / Aspergillus-related lung disease (possibly from contaminated cannabis)
data.description: Hypersensitivity reaction to Aspergillus colonising the airways, causing obstruction, central bronchiectasis and mucus plugging; cannabis is commonly contaminated with Aspergillus spores, and cystic bronchiectasis can occasionally lead to pneumothorax.
symptoms_in_common: cannabis use (a source of Aspergillus exposure)
cystic changes at the right lung base on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: no history of asthma or cystic fibrosis
normal immunoglobulins (total IgE not reported as elevated)
no reported wheeze, productive cough or mucus plugs
acute pleuritic chest pain
silent hyper-resonant left hemithorax
giant bullae rather than central bronchiectasis or fleeting infiltrates

data.description: A 26-year-old woman presented with a one-year history of rash on her lower legs, abdomen, and arms, accompanied by a six-month history of paraesthesia in her right hand and left foot. She had no history of fatigue, weight loss, fever, or arthralgia. Neurological examination showed reduced sensation to light touch in the right ring and little fingers, the lateral palmar and dorsal hand, the left lateral calf, and the dorsum of the left foot. She experienced clumsiness in her right hand causing difficulty with writing, but no weakness was noted. Blood tests, including a full autoimmune screen, were normal. Electromyography demonstrated sensory damage in the right ulnar nerve and asymmetrical superficial sensory damage in the peroneal nerve, with greater involvement on the left side.

A skin-predominant necrotizing vasculitis of small and medium muscular arteries that can cause livedoid skin changes and peripheral neuropathy. The apparent arterial wall injury and surrounding inflammation in the biopsy support this possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic mottled, livedoid-appearing rash on the legs, abdomen, and arms
Asymmetric sensory neuropathy affecting the right ulnar and left superficial peroneal nerve territories
Absence of constitutional symptoms and normal autoimmune screening, compatible with skin-predominant disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported painful subcutaneous nodules, ulceration, or skin tenderness
Neuropathy is sensory without demonstrated motor weakness, although this does not exclude the diagnosis

data.description: An uncommon cutaneous arteritis characterized by persistent macular or livedoid lesions and lymphocyte-predominant inflammation around dermal arteries, often with a fibrin ring in the vessel wall. The chronic rash and apparent biopsy pattern make this an important consideration.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent macular, reticulated rash involving the limbs and trunk
Normal blood tests and autoimmune screening
Absence of fever, fatigue, weight loss, and arthralgia
Apparent inflammatory cuff and prominent eosinophilic ring around an artery in the biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Multifocal peripheral sensory neuropathy is uncommon in this usually skin-limited disorder
Hand clumsiness associated with nerve dysfunction is not a usual manifestation

data.description: A necrotizing small-vessel vasculitis that can involve the skin and peripheral nerves, often alongside kidney or lung disease. Negative autoimmune testing does not completely exclude it.
symptoms_in_common: Asymmetric involvement of separate peripheral nerves, suggesting a mononeuritis multiplex pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic livedoid macules are less characteristic than palpable purpura
No reported constitutional, renal, or respiratory manifestations
Normal blood tests and autoimmune screening make active systemic disease less typical

data.description: An immune-complex small-vessel vasculitis associated with circulating cryoglobulins, sometimes related to hepatitis C, autoimmune disease, or a blood disorder. Skin lesions and peripheral neuropathy are common manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic rash involving the lower legs
symptoms_not_in_common: The rash appears predominantly livedoid rather than typical palpable purpura
No fatigue or arthralgia
Normal reported laboratory studies, although specific cryoglobulin and complement results are not provided
The apparent arterial biopsy pattern is less typical than small-vessel leukocytoclastic vasculitis

data.description: A chronic infection caused by Mycobacterium leprae or Mycobacterium lepromatosis that affects skin and peripheral nerves, producing skin lesions and asymmetric sensory impairment.
symptoms_in_common: Long-standing rash accompanied by peripheral sensory changes
Asymmetric sensory loss in the hand and foot
Absence of systemic symptoms and normal routine blood tests
symptoms_not_in_common: The rash appears livedoid rather than consisting of typical anesthetic patches, plaques, or nodules
Sensory loss within the skin lesions and enlarged peripheral nerves are not reported
The supplied biopsy appears centered on an inflamed artery rather than showing characteristic nerve-associated inflammation or demonstrable organisms

data.description: Necrotizing vasculitis of small and medium-sized arteries confined mainly to the skin, typically with livedo racemosa, nodules or ulcers, and often associated with mononeuritis multiplex in the affected limbs, without systemic organ involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic (one-year) net-like, broken livedo racemosa rash on lower legs, abdomen and arms
Asymmetric sensory mononeuritis multiplex (right ulnar and left-predominant superficial peroneal nerves) on electromyography
Paraesthesia in right hand and left foot
Biopsy showing a medium-sized vessel with a fibrinoid necrosis ring and dense perivascular inflammatory infiltrate
No fever, weight loss, fatigue or arthralgia
Normal blood tests and negative autoimmune screen (ANCA-negative)
symptoms_not_in_common: No painful subcutaneous nodules or ulcers described
Involvement of the abdomen and arms (disease is usually predominant on the lower legs)
Hand clumsiness without motor weakness

data.description: Systemic necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries affecting skin, peripheral nerves, kidneys, gut and other organs; ANCA-negative and sometimes associated with hepatitis B.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, weight loss or fatigue
No arthralgia or myalgia
No reported renal, gastrointestinal or hypertensive involvement
Normal blood tests (inflammatory markers would usually be raised)
Indolent one-year course without systemic progression

data.description: Autosomal recessive autoinflammatory disorder caused by ADA2 mutations, producing a polyarteritis nodosa-like vasculopathy with livedo, neuropathy, early-onset strokes and sometimes immunodeficiency or cytopenias.
symptoms_in_common: Livedo racemosa in a young patient
Polyarteritis nodosa-like medium-vessel necrotizing vasculitis on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset in adulthood rather than childhood
No history of stroke
No recurrent fevers
No cytopenias or immunodeficiency evident (normal blood tests)
No family history mentioned

data.description: Non-inflammatory thrombotic vasculopathy of small and medium arteries causing generalized livedo racemosa and cerebrovascular events, frequently associated with antiphospholipid antibodies.
symptoms_in_common: Widespread, persistent livedo racemosa on trunk and limbs
symptoms_not_in_common: Neurological deficit is peripheral (mononeuritis multiplex), not central (stroke or transient ischaemic attack)
Biopsy shows inflammatory fibrinoid necrotizing vasculitis rather than bland thrombosis or intimal proliferation
Normal autoimmune screen (antiphospholipid antibodies presumably negative)
No history of thrombosis, miscarriage or headache

data.diagnosis: ANCA-associated vasculitis (e.g., eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis or microscopic polyangiitis)
data.description: Small-to-medium vessel necrotizing vasculitides that frequently cause mononeuritis multiplex and skin lesions, usually with ANCA positivity and systemic organ involvement (lungs, kidneys, sinuses; asthma and eosinophilia in EGPA).
symptoms_in_common: Necrotizing vasculitis with fibrinoid necrosis on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative autoimmune screen (ANCA-negative)
Normal blood tests (no eosinophilia, no renal impairment)
No asthma, sinus, pulmonary or renal symptoms
No fever, weight loss, fatigue or arthralgia
Livedo racemosa rather than palpable purpura
Biopsy shows medium-sized vessel involvement rather than predominantly small vessels

data.description: A 44-year-old woman with cerebral palsy and multiple sclerosis (diagnosed at age 16) presented to the emergency department with four days of acute constipation and vomiting. She had a history of chronic constipation due to neurogenic bowel dysfunction secondary to her underlying conditions, initially managed with laxatives. Her constipation had become severe enough to warrant insertion of a sacral anterior root stimulator in the last year. On examination, her abdomen was markedly distended, diffusely tender, with absent bowel sounds. There was no guarding, rigidity, or previous incisions, and all hernia orifices were intact. Vital signs showed tachycardia (140 beats/min), tachypnea, normal blood pressure (130/60 mmHg), and oxygen saturation of 98% on room air. Laboratory findings revealed normal pH of 7.36, hypocapnea (PCO2 29mmHg), hyperlactataemia (20 mg/dL), normal PO2 (), white blood cell count of 10,500 cells/mm3 (73% neutrophils), and elevated C-reactive protein of 3.25 mg/dL.
An impacted stool mass obstructs evacuation and causes marked upstream colonic dilation. The substantial pelvic stool burden and massively dilated colon make this a leading possibility.
symptoms_in_common: Longstanding severe constipation from neurogenic bowel dysfunction
Four days of acute constipation and vomiting
Marked abdominal distension and diffuse tenderness
Imaging shows substantial distal stool burden and severe colonic dilation
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked tachycardia and elevated inflammatory markers are concerning for a complication rather than uncomplicated impaction
Possible gas within the bowel wall on CT is not typical of uncomplicated fecal impaction

data.description: Severe colonic dilation without a fixed mechanical blockage, caused by impaired autonomic regulation of colonic motility. Underlying neurologic disease increases susceptibility, but mechanical obstruction must be excluded.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple sclerosis and cerebral palsy with neurogenic bowel dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Substantial impacted distal stool suggests an alternative or additional obstructive mechanism
Possible bowel-wall gas and systemic inflammatory findings are not typical of uncomplicated pseudo-obstruction

data.diagnosis: Stercoral colitis with possible pressure-related ischemia
data.description: Impacted stool creates pressure on the colonic wall, causing inflammation and potentially ischemia or perforation. CT assessment for wall thickening, surrounding inflammation, and abnormal bowel-wall gas is important.
symptoms_in_common: Severe chronic constipation and neurologic impairment
Substantial pelvic stool burden on CT
Vomiting and acute failure to pass stool
Possible bowel-wall gas on CT raises concern for ischemic injury
symptoms_not_in_common: No guarding or rigidity, which would be more concerning for perforation or advanced peritonitis
Normal blood pressure and near-normal blood pH do not suggest advanced circulatory compromise

data.description: Twisting of an elongated sigmoid colon causes large-bowel obstruction and can compromise its blood supply. Chronic constipation and neurologic disability are risk factors, although the supplied images do not establish a characteristic twist.
symptoms_in_common: Severely dilated colon with air-fluid levels
symptoms_not_in_common: Substantial distal pelvic stool burden is less typical of a complete sigmoid volvulus with an empty distal rectum
Diffuse absent bowel sounds are less typical of early mechanical obstruction, although they can occur later

data.description: Failure of intestinal propulsion produces bowel dilation without a mechanical obstruction. Neurologic dysfunction, medications, electrolyte disturbances, or systemic illness may precipitate it.
symptoms_not_in_common: Predominantly massive colonic dilation with substantial distal stool burden favors a colonic evacuation disorder over generalized ileus
Possible bowel-wall gas is not typical of uncomplicated ileus
Marked tachycardia and elevated inflammatory markers warrant consideration of obstruction or bowel injury

data.diagnosis: Sigmoid volvulus (with possible early bowel ischemia)
data.description: Torsion of a redundant sigmoid colon around its mesentery causing closed-loop large bowel obstruction; common in patients with chronic constipation and neurological disease, and can progress to ischemia and perforation.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic constipation from neurogenic bowel (cerebral palsy, multiple sclerosis) as a predisposing factor
Marked abdominal distension with diffuse tenderness
No previous incisions and intact hernia orifices (adhesions and hernia unlikely)
Elevated lactate and CRP suggesting bowel compromise
Imaging showing a massively dilated gas-filled colonic loop extending to the upper abdomen with air-fluid levels and a fecal-loaded distal colon
Possible intramural gas on CT suggesting ischemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Relatively young age and female sex (more typical in elderly men)
Absent bowel sounds (early obstruction usually gives hyperactive sounds, though absent sounds occur late or with ischemia)
No guarding or rigidity despite suspected ischemia
Near-normal white cell count

data.description: Torsion of a mobile cecum and ascending colon around the mesentery causing closed-loop obstruction, typically in somewhat younger patients than sigmoid volvulus, with risk of ischemia.
symptoms_in_common: Age in the 40s and female sex
Chronic constipation and colonic distension as risk factors
Massively dilated gas-filled bowel loop on imaging with air-fluid levels
symptoms_not_in_common: Dilated loop appears to be in continuity with a fecal-loaded pelvic colon, favoring a sigmoid origin
Distal colon is not collapsed as would be expected in cecal volvulus
Absent bowel sounds
Near-normal white cell count

data.description: Massive colonic dilatation without mechanical obstruction, caused by autonomic dysregulation; seen in patients with neurological disease, immobility or severe illness.
symptoms_in_common: Underlying neurological disease (multiple sclerosis, cerebral palsy) with neurogenic bowel
Massive gaseous colonic dilatation on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Absent bowel sounds (usually present in pseudo-obstruction)
Elevated lactate and marked tachycardia suggest ischemia or closed-loop obstruction
Imaging suggests a single disproportionately dilated loop rather than diffuse colonic dilatation
Possible intramural gas on CT

data.diagnosis: Fecal impaction with obstruction / stercoral colitis
data.description: Large bowel obstruction from a hard impacted fecal mass in the rectosigmoid, which can cause pressure necrosis of the bowel wall, ischemia and perforation; common in chronic neurogenic constipation.
symptoms_in_common: Long-standing severe constipation needing laxatives and a sacral anterior root stimulator
Heavy fecal loading of the rectosigmoid on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Massive, predominantly gas-filled dilated loop reaching the diaphragm is more typical of volvulus
Absent bowel sounds
No guarding or rigidity if stercoral perforation were present
Degree of tachycardia and tachypnea is out of proportion to simple impaction

data.diagnosis: Toxic megacolon / ischemic colitis with colonic necrosis
data.description: Acute non-obstructive colonic dilatation with systemic toxicity due to severe colitis (infectious, inflammatory or ischemic), with risk of necrosis and perforation.
symptoms_not_in_common: No diarrhea or bloody stools; presentation is constipation
No fever reported
Normal blood pressure
Near-normal white cell count
No history of inflammatory bowel disease, recent antibiotics or vascular disease
No guarding or rigidity

data.description: A 64-year-old man presented with 5 months of cough with thin yellow sputum, exertional dyspnea, chest tightness, and wheezing, followed by 10 days of lethargy, myalgias, chills, headaches, anorexia, and night sweats. On presentation he had fever, tachycardia, bitemporal bandlike headaches, neck stiffness, photophobia, inspiratory crackles in both lungs, and mild synovial thickening in the hands. He worked in a healthcare facility and had recent travel to Florida and to Europe/Caribbean. Past history included fibromyalgia, L5 radiculopathy with foot drop, carpal tunnel syndrome, osteoarthritis of the knees and neck, cervical spondylosis, sleep apnea, and peptic ulcer disease. Initial labs showed leukocytosis with neutrophilia, elevated ESR, mild hyponatremia, and microscopic hematuria.

An ANCA-associated small-vessel vasculitis that can involve the lungs, kidneys, joints, and occasionally the meninges. The pulmonary abnormalities and microscopic hematuria make this an important possibility. The fluorescence image may represent ANCA testing, but its pattern and antigen specificity require laboratory confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral inspiratory crackles with patchy pulmonary abnormalities on CT
Microscopic hematuria suggesting possible renal involvement
Fever, night sweats, anorexia, and elevated ESR
Headache, neck stiffness, and photophobia, potentially from uncommon meningeal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Thin yellow sputum is nonspecific and may suggest respiratory infection
Prominent wheezing is less characteristic than other pulmonary manifestations
Meningeal symptoms are uncommon compared with respiratory and renal manifestations

data.description: An ANCA-associated small-vessel vasculitis commonly causing glomerulonephritis and pulmonary capillaritis. It can produce systemic inflammation, pulmonary infiltrates, and microscopic hematuria.
symptoms_in_common: Cough, exertional dyspnea, and bilateral crackles
Fever, lethargy, myalgias, and elevated ESR
Joint inflammation suggested by hand synovial thickening
symptoms_not_in_common: Headache with neck stiffness and photophobia is an unusual manifestation
Wheezing and chest tightness are not defining features
A prolonged productive cough is less characteristic than pulmonary hemorrhage or interstitial lung involvement

data.description: A small-vessel vasculitis associated with asthma, eosinophilia, and pulmonary infiltrates, sometimes affecting peripheral nerves and kidneys. It is less supported here because eosinophilia and established asthma are not reported.
symptoms_in_common: Microscopic hematuria, which can occur with renal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Neutrophilic leukocytosis rather than reported eosinophilia
Headache, neck stiffness, and photophobia are uncommon
Yellow sputum is not a characteristic feature
The previously attributed radiculopathy and foot drop do not establish vasculitic neuropathy

data.diagnosis: Disseminated cryptococcosis with pulmonary infection and meningitis
data.description: A fungal infection that can involve both the lungs and central nervous system, producing chronic respiratory symptoms followed by meningitis. It can occur without recognized immunosuppression.
symptoms_in_common: Months of cough and exertional dyspnea
Fever, lethargy, anorexia, and night sweats
symptoms_not_in_common: Microscopic hematuria is not typical
Hand synovial thickening is not a usual manifestation
Prominent wheezing and chest tightness are less characteristic
Marked neutrophilic inflammation is less characteristic of indolent cryptococcal infection

data.diagnosis: Tuberculosis with pulmonary and meningeal involvement
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can cause chronic pulmonary disease and disseminate to the meninges. Healthcare exposure, persistent cough, and constitutional symptoms justify consideration, although the CT findings shown are nonspecific.
symptoms_in_common: Fever, night sweats, anorexia, and lethargy
Mild hyponatremia, which can accompany tuberculous meningitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Wheezing and chest tightness are not typical dominant features
Microscopic hematuria would require additional renal or genitourinary involvement
Hand synovial thickening is not typical of uncomplicated pulmonary or meningeal tuberculosis
Neutrophilic leukocytosis is less characteristic than in acute bacterial infection

data.description: ANCA-associated small-vessel vasculitis (often perinuclear/MPO-ANCA) characterized by adult-onset asthma, eosinophilia, migratory pulmonary opacities, mononeuritis multiplex, and systemic vasculitis affecting kidneys, joints, and nervous system.
symptoms_in_common: Months of cough, wheezing, chest tightness and exertional dyspnea (asthma-like prodrome)
Patchy ground-glass and peribronchial opacities on CT
Foot drop and carpal tunnel syndrome (possible mononeuritis multiplex)
Immunofluorescence image suggestive of positive ANCA with perinuclear pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: Neck stiffness and photophobia (meningeal involvement is rare)
Neutrophilia rather than documented eosinophilia
Mild hyponatremia
No reported sinusitis or nasal polyps
Foot drop and carpal tunnel previously attributed to mechanical causes

data.description: MPO-ANCA (p-ANCA) associated necrotizing small-vessel vasculitis without granulomas, typically causing glomerulonephritis, pulmonary capillaritis or interstitial lung disease, neuropathy, and constitutional symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Fever, night sweats, myalgias, anorexia, lethargy
Bilateral crackles with ground-glass and basal lung opacities
Headache and meningism (possible pachymeningitis, seen with MPO-ANCA)
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent wheezing and asthma-like symptoms for 5 months
No hemoptysis
Photophobia and neck stiffness are uncommon
Hyponatremia not typical

data.description: ANCA-associated (usually c-ANCA/PR3) granulomatous vasculitis involving upper and lower airways and kidneys; may cause tracheobronchial disease, pulmonary nodules or infiltrates, and hypertrophic pachymeningitis.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic cough, sputum, dyspnea, wheezing (airway involvement)
symptoms_not_in_common: No sinusitis, epistaxis or nasal crusting reported
No cavitary nodules on CT
Immunofluorescence pattern appears perinuclear rather than cytoplasmic
Asthma-like wheezing is less typical

data.diagnosis: Legionella or other atypical/community-acquired pneumonia with meningoencephalitic features
data.description: Infection with Legionella pneumophila (or Mycoplasma/Chlamydia) causing pneumonia with systemic features such as headache, hyponatremia, hematuria, and confusion; associated with travel and healthcare water exposure.
symptoms_in_common: Fever, chills, myalgias, headache, anorexia, lethargy
Cough with sputum and bilateral crackles
Patchy ground-glass and tree-in-bud type opacities
Recent travel and healthcare facility work
symptoms_not_in_common: 5-month course of respiratory symptoms is too long
Synovial thickening of hands
Frank neck stiffness and photophobia
Positive ANCA-pattern immunofluorescence
No diarrhea reported

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection causing chronic pulmonary disease with possible dissemination to the meninges, producing subacute meningitis, constitutional symptoms and hyponatremia (SIADH).
symptoms_in_common: Chronic cough with sputum for months
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent wheezing and chest tightness
Lower-lobe predominant disease without cavitation
Synovial thickening of hands
Neutrophilic leukocytosis
ANCA-pattern immunofluorescence
No weight loss or hemoptysis reported

data.description: A 7-month-old female infant presented with a 2-month history of brown macules on the back and thighs, without prodromal erythema or trauma. Her birth history was unremarkable, and her growth and development were normal. Family history was unremarkable. Physical examination revealed 7 sharply marginated, irregularly shaped, polymorphic hyperpigmented macules of 10 to 15 mm in diameter, without scales, on the back and thighs. The hyperpigmented macules were of orange hue, with unevenness of the pigmentation. Vital signs were normal. There was no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory test results, including complete blood cell count, liver function tests, and renal function, were normal.

An accumulation of mast cells in the skin that produces tan to orange-brown lesions, often beginning in infancy. Lesions may become swollen and red after rubbing (Darier sign). This is the leading consideration, but examination and potentially skin biopsy are needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple orange-brown, nonscaling lesions on the back and thighs
Variable lesion shapes and uneven pigmentation
Apparent localized swelling and surrounding redness in the close-up photograph, potentially consistent with Darier sign if elicited by rubbing
Normal growth, laboratory results, and absence of organ enlargement are compatible with skin-limited disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly atypical findings; itching, flushing, and a confirmed response to rubbing were not reported

data.description: Benign, flat areas of increased skin pigmentation that can appear in infancy. Six or more lesions larger than 5 mm in a prepubertal child warrant evaluation for associated conditions such as neurofibromatosis type 1, but do not establish that diagnosis alone.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of scale or preceding inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Orange hue rather than a typically uniform tan-brown color
Uneven pigmentation within lesions
Apparent swelling and surrounding erythema in the close-up photograph

data.description: A usually benign childhood disorder involving dermal histiocytes, typically producing yellow-orange or reddish-brown papules and nodules that often regress spontaneously.
symptoms_in_common: Normal general health and laboratory results
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions described as flat macules rather than firm papules or nodules
Irregular, polymorphic outlines rather than predominantly rounded lesions
Uneven brown pigmentation rather than a typical yellow-orange papulonodular appearance

data.diagnosis: Small congenital or early-onset melanocytic nevi
data.description: Benign collections of pigment-producing cells that are present at birth or become apparent early in life, appearing as brown macules or raised lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Some variation in pigmentation and shape
No preceding trauma or inflammatory eruption
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions first noticed several months after birth, which is less typical of clearly congenital nevi
Orange coloration
Apparent localized swelling and surrounding redness in the close-up photograph

data.description: A rare, benign pigmentary disorder producing asymptomatic brown macules without preceding inflammation or an identifiable trigger. It is more commonly described in older children and adolescents.
symptoms_in_common: Acquired brown macules on the trunk and thighs
Absence of preceding erythema or trauma
Normal growth, development, and laboratory results
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset in a 5-month-old infant is unusually early
Orange hue and uneven pigmentation
Apparent swelling and erythema in the close-up photograph, which are not characteristic of a purely pigmentary disorder

data.description: Clonal accumulation of mast cells in the skin, most often presenting in infancy as yellow-brown to orange-brown macules or papules on the trunk that urticate (wheal and flare) when rubbed (Darier sign). Usually limited to skin in children with a benign course.
symptoms_in_common: Onset in infancy (around 5 months of age)
Multiple brown macules with orange hue on back and thighs
Second image showing wheal with surrounding erythema in a lesion, consistent with positive Darier sign
Normal blood count and liver function (skin-limited disease)
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported pruritus, flushing, or blistering
No systemic mast cell mediator symptoms such as diarrhea or wheezing

data.description: Uniformly pigmented light-brown macules due to increased epidermal melanin, present at birth or appearing in early childhood; six or more macules larger than 5 mm in a prepubertal child suggest neurofibromatosis type 1.
symptoms_not_in_common: Orange hue
Uneven pigmentation (café-au-lait macules are homogeneous)
Wheal and erythema of lesion on rubbing
Negative family history
No axillary or inguinal freckling described

data.description: Acquired excess melanin deposition following cutaneous inflammation or injury (e.g., eczema, insect bites, infections), producing brown macules at sites of prior lesions that fade over time.
symptoms_not_in_common: No prodromal erythema, rash, or trauma
Sharply marginated lesions with orange hue
Urtication of lesion on rubbing
Persistence for 2 months without fading

data.description: Benign non-Langerhans cell histiocytosis of infancy and early childhood presenting as one or several yellow-orange to red-brown papules or nodules, usually on the head, neck, and trunk, which regress spontaneously.
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesions are flat macules rather than dome-shaped papules or nodules
Lesion size and irregular polymorphic shape
Wheal and flare on rubbing
No head and neck involvement

data.description: Clonal proliferation of Langerhans cells that in infants often involves skin with red-brown crusted or scaly papules, petechiae, and seborrheic dermatitis-like eruption on scalp, trunk, and flexures, with possible bone, liver, spleen, and marrow involvement.
symptoms_not_in_common: Non-scaly, non-crusted flat macules
No petechiae or purpura
No scalp or flexural involvement
No lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly
Normal blood count and liver function
Wheal and flare on rubbing

data.description: A 65-year-old man presented with bilateral leg swelling that had worsened over six weeks. He reported vague abdominal discomfort and tiredness. Physical examination revealed bilateral pitting edema up to the groin, without erythema, tenderness, or warmth. The patient was systemically well with normal heart sounds and clear chest examination. No palpable masses or lymphadenopathy were found in the abdomen. Laboratory testing showed normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 95 g/L; normal range 130-180), elevated C-reactive protein of 33.0 mg/L (normal range 0-5.0), and raised IgG4 level (3.55 g/L; normal range 0.08-1.4). Doppler ultrasound showed no deep vein thrombosis.

An immune-mediated fibroinflammatory disease that forms tissue around the abdominal aorta and adjacent structures. Venous compression can cause bilateral leg edema. The apparent periaortic soft-tissue cuff on CT and elevated IgG4 favor this diagnosis, although serum IgG4 alone is not diagnostic.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive bilateral pitting edema extending to the groin, potentially from iliac vein or inferior vena cava compression
Apparent periaortic soft-tissue thickening on CT
Negative leg Doppler despite substantial edema, compatible with more proximal venous compression

data.description: A nonmalignant fibrotic inflammatory process surrounding the abdominal aorta and iliac vessels, sometimes obstructing veins or ureters. This is an alternative if IgG4-related disease is not confirmed.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent periaortic soft-tissue cuff on CT
Bilateral leg edema consistent with proximal venous compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Raised serum IgG4 favors an IgG4-related subtype rather than non-IgG4 idiopathic fibrosis

data.description: A malignancy of lymphoid cells that can produce retroperitoneal soft tissue encasing major vessels and impairing venous drainage. Imaging and tissue sampling may be needed to distinguish it from fibrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Retroperitoneal soft tissue around the aorta on CT
Progressive bilateral leg edema from possible central venous compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Raised serum IgG4 is not a characteristic lymphoma marker
No palpable lymphadenopathy, although this does not exclude deep retroperitoneal disease
Systemically well presentation without reported fever, night sweats, or weight loss is less suggestive of symptomatic lymphoma

data.description: Retroperitoneal infiltration or a fibrotic reaction associated with an underlying cancer, which can mimic benign retroperitoneal fibrosis and compress major veins.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive bilateral pitting edema suggesting proximal venous obstruction
Retroperitoneal periaortic soft tissue on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Raised serum IgG4 more strongly supports an immune-mediated process
No palpable abdominal mass or lymphadenopathy
No reported weight loss or other clear systemic features of malignancy

data.description: A rare non-Langerhans-cell histiocytic disorder that can cause periaortic and retroperitoneal infiltration, occasionally producing vascular or urinary obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent periaortic soft-tissue infiltration on CT
Bilateral leg edema potentially related to retroperitoneal vascular compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Raised serum IgG4 is not a defining feature
No reported long-bone pain, a common clinical clue
No reported diabetes insipidus or orbital symptoms
No characteristic perirenal infiltration is clearly established by the supplied images

data.description: Fibroinflammatory condition in which IgG4-positive plasma cell-rich tissue forms a soft-tissue mantle around the abdominal aorta and adjacent retroperitoneal structures, which can encase and compress the inferior vena cava, lymphatics and ureters.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral pitting leg edema up to the groin (IVC/lymphatic compression)
CT showing periaortic soft-tissue cuff around the abdominal aorta
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported flank or back pain
No reported evidence of ureteric obstruction or renal impairment
No other organ involvement described (pancreas, salivary glands)

data.description: Chronic periaortic fibroinflammatory disease of unknown cause producing a retroperitoneal soft-tissue mass around the infrarenal aorta, often entrapping the ureters and IVC.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral leg edema from venous/lymphatic compression
symptoms_not_in_common: Markedly raised serum IgG4 favors the IgG4-related form
No back or flank pain reported
No hydronephrosis or renal dysfunction reported

data.description: Malignant lymphoid proliferation (typically non-Hodgkin lymphoma) forming confluent retroperitoneal nodal masses that can surround the aorta and compress the IVC.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral leg edema from IVC/lymphatic obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No palpable lymphadenopathy or abdominal mass
No fever, night sweats or weight loss reported
Raised IgG4 is more typical of IgG4-related disease
Lymphoma typically lifts the aorta off the spine and is bulkier and lobulated rather than a smooth cuff
Systemically well

data.diagnosis: Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm / chronic periaortitis
data.description: Aneurysmal dilatation of the abdominal aorta with a thickened inflammatory wall and perianeurysmal fibrosis that can adhere to and compress adjacent structures; part of the chronic periaortitis spectrum.
symptoms_in_common: Leg edema possible if IVC is involved
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear aneurysmal dilatation of the aorta described
No pulsatile abdominal mass on examination
No back pain reported
Raised IgG4 points to a specific IgG4-related etiology

data.diagnosis: Retroperitoneal malignancy (metastatic disease or sarcoma with IVC compression)
data.description: Metastatic retroperitoneal infiltration (e.g., from gastrointestinal, urological or testicular primaries) or a primary retroperitoneal sarcoma that encases or compresses the great vessels and lymphatics.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral leg edema from IVC/lymphatic obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No known primary tumor
No palpable mass or lymphadenopathy
No reported weight loss
Raised IgG4 not explained by malignancy
Smooth symmetric periaortic cuff is more typical of fibrosis than tumor

data.description: 41-year-old woman with chest pain. One year earlier, she had transient left-sided chest and shoulder tightness. Five days before presentation, she developed acute substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders with dyspnea while packing for a flight; it lasted 1 hour and resolved spontaneously. The day before presentation, similar pain recurred after walking, accompanied by light-headedness and dyspnea. History includes laparoscopy for ovarian cyst and miscarriage 1 month prior. She exercised regularly, did not smoke, and drank two alcoholic drinks weekly. Family history was notable for hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in her mother, brother, and sister, and a maternal second cousin who died of cerebral aneurysm at age 51. On examination, she was diaphoretic with normal temperature, heart rate 68 bpm, blood pressure 143/87 mmHg bilaterally, respiratory rate 18/min, oxygen saturation 100%, and no cardiac murmurs, rubs, or gallops.

Nontraumatic separation or bleeding within a coronary artery wall, reducing myocardial blood flow and causing acute coronary syndrome. This is the leading possibility given the clinical presentation and coronary angiographic appearance.
symptoms_in_common: Acute substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders
Recent pregnancy loss, a possible hormonal context
Coronary angiography appears to show segmental narrowing and distal contrast retention, findings suggestive of dissection
symptoms_not_in_common: Transient chest and shoulder tightness one year earlier is not clearly explained by a single acute dissection

data.description: A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory arterial disorder causing stenoses, aneurysms, and dissections. It frequently affects renal arteries and is associated with spontaneous coronary artery dissection.
symptoms_in_common: Middle-aged woman without prominent conventional atherosclerotic risk factors
Chest pain compatible with associated coronary dissection
Renal arterial images appear to show multifocal caliber irregularity suggestive of beading
Renal cortical indentations may reflect prior ischemic injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Jaw-radiating chest pain, dyspnea, and diaphoresis are not typical of isolated renal fibromuscular dysplasia and would require associated coronary disease

data.description: An inherited connective-tissue disorder, usually related to COL3A1 variants, that causes arterial fragility and spontaneous dissections or ruptures. Family history of hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome does not establish this distinct subtype.
symptoms_in_common: Possible spontaneous coronary dissection at a relatively young age
Extended family history of fatal cerebral aneurysm
Possible abnormalities in multiple arterial territories
symptoms_not_in_common: Exertional chest pain is not a defining manifestation without an arterial complication
Renal arterial beading is more characteristic of fibromuscular dysplasia than vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome

data.description: Transient coronary artery spasm causes episodic myocardial ischemia, often at rest, with spontaneous resolution of chest pain.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent substernal pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders
Spontaneous resolution of the initial episode
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrence after walking is less typical than the usual resting pattern
An episode lasting approximately one hour is longer than many uncomplicated vasospastic attacks
Distal coronary contrast retention and renal arterial irregularities are not explained by isolated coronary spasm

data.description: Coronary plaque disruption and thrombosis cause unstable angina or myocardial infarction. Troponin measurements and serial ECGs are needed to determine whether myocardial injury is present.
symptoms_in_common: Substernal chest pain radiating to the jaw and shoulders
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age, regular exercise, and absence of smoking make typical atherosclerotic disease less likely
Coronary angiographic abnormalities appear more suggestive of dissection than focal plaque-related obstruction
Renal arterial beading and family connective-tissue history are not typical features of atherosclerotic acute coronary syndrome

data.diagnosis: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) associated with fibromuscular dysplasia
data.description: Non-atherosclerotic tear or intramural hematoma of a coronary artery causing acute coronary syndrome, typically in young to middle-aged women with few risk factors. Often associated with fibromuscular dysplasia of extracoronary arteries (e.g., renal arteries) and with recent pregnancy.
symptoms_in_common: Woman aged 41 with no conventional atherosclerotic risk factors
Acute substernal chest pain radiating to jaw and shoulders with dyspnea
Recurrent pain with exertion, light-headedness, diaphoresis
Angiography showing smooth tapered narrowing of a coronary branch with distal contrast staining/occlusion, without atherosclerotic plaque elsewhere
Renal artery irregularity/beading and cortical notches suggesting renal infarcts on CT angiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Episode of chest tightness one year earlier is not fully explained
Family history of hypermobile Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is not a recognised association of fibromuscular dysplasia
ECG without marked ST elevation

data.diagnosis: Vascular Ehlers-Danlos syndrome (COL3A1) with coronary dissection
data.description: Autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder from defective type III collagen, causing arterial fragility with dissections, aneurysms and rupture of medium-sized arteries, as well as organ rupture and pregnancy complications.
symptoms_in_common: Family history of Ehlers-Danlos syndrome in mother, brother and sister
Relative who died of cerebral aneurysm
Coronary artery dissection appearance on angiography
Renal artery abnormalities and renal infarcts on CT
Young age without atherosclerotic risk factors
Recent pregnancy as a vascular stressor
symptoms_not_in_common: Family diagnosis is the hypermobile type, not the vascular type
No reported thin translucent skin, easy bruising, characteristic facial features or prior organ rupture
Affected relative with aneurysm is distant (second cousin)
Beaded renal artery appearance is more typical of fibromuscular dysplasia

data.diagnosis: Atherosclerotic acute coronary syndrome (plaque rupture NSTEMI/unstable angina)
data.description: Rupture or erosion of atherosclerotic coronary plaque with thrombus formation causing myocardial ischemia or infarction; the most common cause of acute coronary syndrome overall.
symptoms_in_common: Substernal chest pain radiating to jaw and shoulders
Prior episode of chest tightness a year earlier
symptoms_not_in_common: Young premenopausal woman who exercises and does not smoke
No diabetes, dyslipidemia or family history of premature coronary disease reported
Angiogram shows smooth long tapering without diffuse atherosclerotic plaque
Renal artery beading and renal infarcts point to a non-atherosclerotic arteriopathy

data.diagnosis: Coronary embolism (e.g., paradoxical embolism or hypercoagulable state after pregnancy)
data.description: Occlusion of a distal coronary artery by thrombus originating from the heart or venous system (via a patent foramen ovale), sometimes with emboli to other organs such as the kidneys. Pregnancy and the postpartum/post-miscarriage period are prothrombotic.
symptoms_in_common: Symptom onset around planned air travel
Distal coronary branch cut-off on angiography
Renal cortical defects compatible with infarcts in more than one vascular territory
symptoms_not_in_common: No atrial fibrillation, valve disease, murmur or known intracardiac shunt
No signs of deep vein thrombosis
Renal arteries show beading/irregularity rather than discrete filling defects
Coronary lesion appears as long smooth tapering rather than an abrupt embolic cut-off
Family history of connective tissue disease and aneurysm is not explained

data.description: Transient intense constriction of an epicardial coronary artery causing episodic ischemic chest pain, often at rest, with spontaneous resolution; can cause infarction if prolonged.
symptoms_in_common: Episodic chest pain that resolved spontaneously after about an hour
Similar transient episode one year earlier
Young woman without atherosclerotic risk factors
Radiation to jaw and shoulders with dyspnea and diaphoresis
symptoms_not_in_common: Episodes occurred with activity rather than at rest or at night
Non-smoker
Fixed distal vessel occlusion/contrast staining on angiography rather than reversible spasm
Renal artery abnormalities and renal infarcts are not explained
No documented transient ST elevation

data.description: 50-year-old postmenopausal woman with 1 year of menopause presented with abdominal distention, anorexia, and exertional dyspnoea. Examination showed a markedly distended abdomen. CT/MRI revealed gross ascites and a heterogeneous left adnexal/pelvic mass with enhancing solid components and thick septa, small calcifications, and no lymphadenopathy or peritoneal dissemination. CA 125 was markedly elevated at 1237 U/ml; CEA, CA 19-9, and SCC were normal. Repeated ascitic fluid cytology showed benign mesothelial cells without malignant cells. Thyroid function tests were normal, and there were no symptoms or signs of thyroid hormone imbalance.

An ovarian teratoma composed predominantly of thyroid tissue that can cause benign ascites and pleural effusion, sometimes with striking CA 125 elevation. Most patients have normal thyroid function; confirmation requires histopathology.
symptoms_in_common: Complex unilateral adnexal mass with enhancing solid components, thick septa, and small calcifications
Gross ascites and marked abdominal distention
Right pleural effusion visible on the chest image, consistent with exertional dyspnoea
Markedly elevated CA 125 despite repeatedly negative ascitic cytology
Normal thyroid function and absence of thyroid hormone imbalance, which do not exclude struma ovarii
symptoms_not_in_common: CA 125 of 1237 U/ml is unusual for an uncomplicated struma ovarii, although reported with pseudo-Meigs syndrome

data.diagnosis: Ovarian fibroma or fibrothecoma with Meigs syndrome
data.description: A benign ovarian stromal tumor associated with ascites and pleural effusion that resolve after tumor removal. Serosal irritation can markedly elevate CA 125.
symptoms_in_common: Postmenopausal presentation with an adnexal mass
Right pleural effusion and exertional dyspnoea
Absence of lymphadenopathy or peritoneal dissemination
symptoms_not_in_common: A prominently heterogeneous, septated solid-cystic mass is less typical than the predominantly solid appearance of a fibroma
Very high CA 125 is uncommon, although possible in Meigs syndrome

data.description: A malignant epithelial ovarian tumor, particularly a serous carcinoma, that can produce a complex adnexal mass, ascites, pleural effusion, and elevated CA 125.
symptoms_in_common: Complex adnexal mass with enhancing solid components and thick septa
Right pleural effusion and exertional dyspnoea
symptoms_not_in_common: No peritoneal dissemination or lymphadenopathy despite extensive fluid accumulation
Repeated ascitic cytology without malignant cells, although negative cytology does not exclude carcinoma

data.description: An epithelial ovarian tumor with atypical proliferation but no destructive stromal invasion. It may appear as a complex cystic-solid mass and occasionally cause ascites and elevated CA 125.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral complex adnexal mass with enhancing solid tissue and thick septa
symptoms_not_in_common: Gross ascites and a large pleural effusion are less typical without extraovarian implants
CA 125 of 1237 U/ml is less typical of a localized borderline tumor

data.diagnosis: Mature cystic ovarian teratoma with pseudo-Meigs syndrome
data.description: A benign ovarian germ-cell tumor containing mature tissues that can rarely provoke ascites, pleural effusion, and reactive CA 125 elevation.
symptoms_in_common: Heterogeneous adnexal mass with solid components and calcifications
Right pleural effusion and exertional dyspnoea
symptoms_not_in_common: No characteristic macroscopic fat or fat-fluid level is described
Thick enhancing septa and prominent enhancing solid tissue are less typical of a conventional dermoid cyst
Massive ascites and markedly elevated CA 125 are rare in an uncomplicated mature cystic teratoma

data.description: A monodermal ovarian teratoma composed predominantly of thyroid tissue; it can rarely present with ascites, pleural effusion and elevated CA 125, mimicking ovarian cancer, and resolves after tumor removal.
symptoms_in_common: Heterogeneous adnexal mass with enhancing solid components and thick septa
High-attenuation areas on unenhanced CT and T2 low-signal areas suggesting thyroid colloid
Right pleural effusion on chest X-ray with exertional dyspnoea
Only mild FDG uptake on PET
Normal thyroid function (most cases are euthyroid)
symptoms_not_in_common: CA 125 above 1000 U/ml is unusual for a benign tumor
Postmenopausal age is slightly older than the typical presentation
No signs of hyperthyroidism (present only in a minority of cases)

data.description: The most common malignant ovarian tumor in postmenopausal women, typically presenting with a complex adnexal mass, ascites and raised CA 125.
symptoms_in_common: Complex adnexal mass with enhancing solid components and thick septa
symptoms_not_in_common: Repeated ascitic cytology negative for malignant cells
No peritoneal dissemination despite massive ascites
No lymphadenopathy
Only mild FDG uptake on PET
Unilateral, relatively small mass

data.description: A benign sex cord-stromal tumor classically associated with ascites and right-sided pleural effusion that resolve after resection; CA 125 may be elevated.
symptoms_not_in_common: Multilocular appearance with thick septa is atypical; fibromas are usually homogeneous solid masses
Avidly enhancing solid components (fibromas enhance poorly)
CA 125 at this level is uncommon

data.description: Peritoneal and tubo-ovarian infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that classically mimics advanced ovarian cancer with ascites, adnexal mass and high CA 125.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, night sweats or weight loss reported
No peritoneal thickening, nodularity or omental caking
No lymphadenopathy
Well-defined multiloculated mass with enhancing solid components
No lymphocytic predominance in ascitic fluid reported

data.diagnosis: Adult granulosa cell tumor of the ovary
data.description: A low-grade malignant sex cord-stromal tumor of peri- and postmenopausal women, appearing as a solid and multicystic mass, often estrogen-producing.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral heterogeneous solid-cystic adnexal mass with thick septa
Absence of peritoneal spread or lymphadenopathy
symptoms_not_in_common: No postmenopausal bleeding or estrogenic effects
Markedly elevated CA 125 is not typical
Calcifications are uncommon
Massive ascites with pleural effusion is unusual

data.description: 24-year-old man presented with a 2-day history of swelling on the left side of neck and fever. Past medical history included two similar neck abscesses 2 years and 6 years ago, which were treated with antibiotics and drainage. Physical examination showed a 2 cm diameter swelling at the level of thyroid cartilage.

data.diagnosis: Pyriform sinus fistula associated with a third or fourth branchial pouch anomaly
data.description: A congenital tract connecting the pyriform sinus to neck tissues, usually on the left, that can cause recurrent neck abscesses. This is the leading consideration; the apparent tract near the left pyriform sinus on the provided image supports it but requires confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent left-sided neck abscesses over several years
Swelling at the level of the thyroid cartilage
Apparent tract extending from the left hypopharyngeal region on imaging

data.description: A congenital lateral neck cyst that can become infected, producing fever and swelling, and recur after drainage if the cyst remains.
symptoms_in_common: Young adult with a lateral neck swelling
Recurrent abscesses treated with antibiotics and drainage
symptoms_not_in_common: The relatively low location at the thyroid cartilage is less characteristic than an upper lateral neck mass
An apparent connection to the pyriform sinus is not typical of a second branchial cleft cyst

data.diagnosis: Acute suppurative thyroiditis with thyroid abscess
data.description: A bacterial infection of the thyroid that can form an abscess. Recurrent left-sided episodes in a young person can occur because of an underlying pyriform sinus fistula; thyroid involvement would need confirmation.
symptoms_not_in_common: A discrete swelling at thyroid cartilage level rather than clearly within the thyroid gland is less typical
The apparent hypopharyngeal tract suggests an underlying congenital cause rather than an isolated thyroid infection

data.description: An infected congenital remnant along the thyroid's embryologic descent pathway, generally producing a midline neck mass near the hyoid bone.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent neck swelling and abscess formation
