symptoms_not_in_common: Consistently left-sided lateral swelling rather than a midline mass
An apparent pyriform sinus connection is not typical

data.description: A bacterial infection of cervical lymph nodes that can progress to a localized abscess.
symptoms_in_common: A localized approximately 2 cm neck mass
Previous improvement after antibiotics and drainage
symptoms_not_in_common: Repeated abscesses in the same location over several years are less typical without a persistent underlying source
An apparent tract near the pyriform sinus is not explained by uncomplicated lymph node infection

data.diagnosis: Pyriform sinus fistula (third/fourth branchial pouch anomaly)
data.description: Congenital sinus tract running from the apex of the pyriform sinus toward the perithyroid space, almost always on the left side, causing recurrent lower neck abscesses or suppurative thyroiditis. Barium swallow or CT with oral contrast shows a contrast-filled tract arising from the pyriform fossa.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent neck abscesses at the same site over several years
Previous episodes needing antibiotics and drainage
Swelling at the level of the thyroid cartilage
CT showing a contrast-filled tract extending from the left pyriform sinus region into the neck soft tissues
symptoms_not_in_common: First presentation is more often in childhood, though adult presentation is well described
No reported thyroid pain or thyroid dysfunction

data.description: Congenital remnant of the second branchial apparatus presenting as a lateral neck mass along the anterior border of the sternocleidomastoid, which may become infected repeatedly; any internal opening is in the tonsillar fossa.
symptoms_not_in_common: Tract on CT arises from the pyriform sinus region rather than the tonsillar fossa
Usually located higher, near the angle of the mandible
Strong left-sided predilection is not characteristic

data.description: Rare bacterial infection of the thyroid gland, often secondary to an underlying pyriform sinus fistula, presenting with painful anterior neck swelling and fever, usually affecting the left lobe.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent episodes (when an underlying fistula is present)
symptoms_not_in_common: Swelling is at the level of the thyroid cartilage rather than over the thyroid gland itself
No reported dysphagia, thyroid tenderness or thyroid function abnormality
Does not by itself explain the contrast-filled tract on imaging

data.description: Congenital remnant of the thyroglossal duct presenting as a neck mass near the hyoid that moves with swallowing and tongue protrusion; it may become infected and form recurrent abscesses or fistulae.
symptoms_in_common: Neck swelling near the level of the thyroid cartilage
symptoms_not_in_common: Swelling is clearly lateral (left-sided) rather than midline or paramedian
No reported movement with tongue protrusion
Tract on CT communicates with the pyriform sinus region, not the hyoid or tongue base

data.diagnosis: Tuberculous cervical lymphadenitis (scrofula) with cold abscess
data.description: Mycobacterial infection of the cervical lymph nodes causing chronic or recurrent neck swelling that may suppurate, point through the skin and form draining sinuses.
symptoms_in_common: Neck swelling with abscess formation pointing at the skin
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset over 2 days is too acute; scrofula is usually indolent
Marked acute inflammation rather than a cold abscess
Usually multiple matted nodes in the posterior triangle or supraclavicular region
No reported weight loss, night sweats or pulmonary symptoms
Does not explain a tract from the pyriform sinus on CT

data.description: 54-year-old man with a history of polysubstance abuse and treatment-naïve hepatitis C presented with altered mental status. He was afebrile, drowsy, and hypertensive (172/110 mmHg), with distended jugular veins and bibasilar crackles. Labs showed severe renal dysfunction (creatinine 16.0 mg/dL, BUN 99 mg/dL), mild anemia (hemoglobin 11.3 g/dL), proteinuria, random urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 1.9, elevated LDH, rare schistocytes on blood film, and low C3 with normal C4; C3 hypocomplementemia persisted during hospitalization. Urine toxicology was positive for cocaine metabolites. Blood and urine cultures were negative, HIV testing was negative, and ultrasound showed echogenic kidneys measuring 9.8 cm and 10.3 cm. Family history included a sister with renal failure of unknown cause requiring dialysis at age 45.

data.diagnosis: Complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome)
data.description: Alternative complement pathway dysregulation causes small-vessel endothelial injury, often predominantly affecting the kidneys. The biopsy images appear to show vascular narrowing and concentric remodeling compatible with thrombotic microangiopathy, although these findings do not establish its cause.
symptoms_in_common: Severe renal dysfunction with creatinine 16.0 mg/dL
Persistent low C3 with normal C4, suggesting alternative complement pathway activation
Elevated LDH, anemia, and rare schistocytes
Family history of relatively early kidney failure
Biopsy appearances compatible with chronic vascular endothelial injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Only rare schistocytes and mild anemia are less typical of pronounced systemic microangiopathic hemolysis, although kidney-limited disease can occur
Cocaine exposure provides an alternative or additional trigger for vascular injury

data.description: Severe hypertension can injure renal arterioles, causing endothelial damage, concentric intimal thickening, ischemia, and microangiopathic hemolysis.
symptoms_in_common: Jugular venous distension and bibasilar crackles consistent with volume overload
Concentric vascular thickening and luminal narrowing visible in the biopsy images
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent isolated C3 hypocomplementemia is not typical of hypertension alone
Family history of early kidney failure raises concern for an underlying inherited disorder
The recorded blood pressure is lower than often encountered in classic malignant hypertension

data.description: Cocaine can cause intense vasoconstriction, hypertension, and endothelial injury, producing renal ischemia and thrombotic microangiopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Positive urine testing for cocaine metabolites
Elevated LDH, anemia, and rare schistocytes
Biopsy appearances compatible with small-vessel injury
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent low C3 with normal C4 is not characteristic of uncomplicated cocaine-related vascular injury
Family history of early kidney failure is not explained by cocaine exposure
Echogenic kidneys suggest chronic disease that an isolated acute exposure would not fully explain

data.description: An alternative complement pathway disorder characterized by predominant C3 deposition in glomeruli, causing proteinuria and progressive kidney dysfunction. Confirmation requires immunofluorescence and electron microscopy.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent low C3 with normal C4
Family history of kidney failure, potentially suggesting inherited complement dysregulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Rare schistocytes and elevated LDH suggest microangiopathic injury rather than isolated glomerular disease
The supplied images emphasize vascular remodeling rather than diagnostic glomerular C3 deposition
Cocaine exposure is not a characteristic feature

data.description: Chronic hepatitis C can generate circulating immune complexes and cryoglobulins that cause glomerular inflammation, commonly with a membranoproliferative pattern.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal C4 with persistently low C3 is atypical; cryoglobulinemia more commonly produces marked C4 reduction
Schistocytes and elevated LDH are more suggestive of thrombotic microangiopathy
The supplied biopsy images show predominantly vascular lesions rather than a characteristic immune-complex glomerular pattern
Family history of early kidney failure is not explained by acquired hepatitis C-associated disease

data.diagnosis: Complement-mediated (atypical) hemolytic uremic syndrome / thrombotic microangiopathy, possibly cocaine-triggered
data.description: Thrombotic microangiopathy caused by dysregulation of the alternative complement pathway (often genetic mutations in CFH, CFI, MCP, C3), frequently unmasked by triggers such as cocaine or severe hypertension. It produces renal failure, microangiopathic hemolysis and arteriolar lesions such as intimal mucoid edema and onion-skinning.
symptoms_in_common: Persistently low C3 with normal C4, suggesting alternative pathway activation
Sister with unexplained renal failure requiring dialysis at age 45, suggesting a hereditary complement defect
Biopsy showing arteriolar intimal edema/mucoid thickening and concentric onion-skin lesions with luminal narrowing
symptoms_not_in_common: Only rare schistocytes and mild anemia (hematologic features subtle)
Thrombocytopenia not documented
Echogenic kidneys suggesting some chronicity
Altered mental status more likely due to uremia or hypertension

data.diagnosis: Malignant hypertension (hypertensive emergency) with malignant nephrosclerosis
data.description: Severe hypertension causing acute end-organ damage, with renal arteriolar fibrinoid necrosis and hyperplastic (onion-skin) arteriolosclerosis producing a secondary thrombotic microangiopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Volume overload with distended jugular veins and crackles
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistently low C3
Family history of early renal failure in sister
Blood pressure only moderately elevated for the degree of renal injury

data.description: Cocaine causes intense vasoconstriction, endothelial injury and accelerated hypertension, leading to renal thrombotic microangiopathy, arteriolar sclerosis and acute or chronic kidney injury.
symptoms_in_common: Urine toxicology positive for cocaine metabolites
Arteriolar onion-skinning and intimal thickening on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent C3 hypocomplementemia not explained by cocaine alone
Family history of renal failure in sister

data.description: Immune complex–mediated glomerulonephritis associated with chronic HCV and mixed cryoglobulinemia, presenting with proteinuria, hematuria, hypertension, renal impairment and hypocomplementemia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal C4 (cryoglobulinemia typically causes markedly low C4)
Schistocytes and elevated LDH
Biopsy dominated by vascular onion-skin lesions rather than proliferative glomerular changes
No purpura, arthralgia or neuropathy reported
Family history of renal failure

data.diagnosis: C3 glomerulopathy (C3 glomerulonephritis / dense deposit disease)
data.description: Glomerular disease caused by alternative complement pathway dysregulation with dominant C3 deposition, causing proteinuria, hematuria, hypertension and progressive renal failure; it may be familial and can overlap with complement-mediated thrombotic microangiopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Persistently low C3 with normal C4
Family history of renal failure in sister
symptoms_not_in_common: Schistocytes and elevated LDH
Biopsy showing arteriolar thrombotic microangiopathy-type lesions rather than glomerular proliferative changes
Cocaine-related onset
Altered mental status

data.description: A 13-month-old male infant presented to the Department of Dermatology with a single asymptomatic plaque on the lower back that was first noticed by parents at approximately 4 months of age. During observation, the lesion gradually became larger and firmer, and intermittent sweating on the surface was noticed.

A rare benign malformation containing increased eccrine sweat glands and vascular structures. It often appears in childhood as a plaque or nodule and can cause localized sweating. Histopathologic confirmation is needed.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent sweating confined to the lesion
Localized increased hair visible in the clinical photograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Lower-back location is less typical than an extremity location

data.description: A benign developmental overgrowth of smooth muscle in the skin, usually presenting in infancy as a skin-colored or pigmented, sometimes hairy plaque on the trunk or lower back.
symptoms_in_common: Localized increased hair visible in the clinical photograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent localized sweating is not a characteristic feature

data.description: A rare benign hamartoma involving increased numbers or size of eccrine sweat glands. Localized excessive sweating may be its principal manifestation.
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive development of a firm, prominent plaque is less typical
Localized increased hair is not characteristic

data.description: A benign soft-tissue tumor of infancy composed of fibrous tissue, mature fat, and primitive mesenchymal tissue. It commonly presents as a painless, enlarging subcutaneous mass.
symptoms_in_common: Onset within the first year of life
symptoms_not_in_common: Sweating confined to the lesion is not characteristic
A superficial plaque is less typical than a subcutaneous mass
Localized increased hair is not a usual feature

data.description: A benign hamartoma involving dermal collagen, elastin, or other connective-tissue components. It can present as a firm, skin-colored plaque, including on the lower back.
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent localized sweating is not characteristic
Localized increased hair is not a typical defining feature

data.description: Rare benign myofibroblastic proliferation of infancy presenting as a slowly enlarging, firm plaque, most often on the lower back, with fascicles of spindle cells filling the dermis and extending into the subcutis.
symptoms_in_common: Onset in early infancy (noticed at 4 months)
Single asymptomatic plaque on the lower back
Histology showing spindle cell fascicles in the deep dermis and subcutis around adnexal structures
Imaging showing a lesion confined to skin and subcutis without spinal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Intermittent localized sweating is not a classic feature, though it has been reported

data.description: Benign hamartoma made up of increased eccrine glands and small vessels, usually presenting in childhood as a solitary plaque or nodule with localized hyperhidrosis and sometimes hypertrichosis.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent sweating on the lesion surface
Eccrine structures seen in the deep dermis on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Usually found on the extremities rather than the lower back
Often painful, whereas this lesion is asymptomatic
Progressive firmness is unusual
Biopsy appears dominated by spindle cell fascicles rather than vascular and eccrine proliferation

data.description: Benign proliferation of arrector pili-type smooth muscle bundles in the dermis, presenting as a skin-coloured or slightly pigmented plaque with hypertrichosis, commonly on the lumbosacral trunk.
symptoms_in_common: Spindle cell bundles in the dermis on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Usually present at birth and grows only in proportion to the child rather than progressively enlarging and hardening
Sweating is not typical
Pseudo-Darier sign (transient induration on rubbing) is not described
Extension deep into the subcutis is unusual

data.description: Benign soft tissue tumour of the first two years of life with a triphasic histology of fibrous trabeculae, immature mesenchymal cells and mature fat; may show overlying hypertrichosis and hyperhidrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Overlying hair growth and sweating are reported
Fibrous fascicles mixed with fat in the deep dermis and subcutis
symptoms_not_in_common: Usually a subcutaneous nodule or mass rather than a plaque
Typical sites are the axilla, shoulder, upper arm and groin rather than the lower back
Primitive mesenchymal component is not evident

data.description: The most common fibrous tumour of infancy, a benign myofibroblastic proliferation presenting as a firm dermal or subcutaneous nodule, typically with biphasic histology and a haemangiopericytoma-like vascular pattern.
symptoms_in_common: Myofibroblastic spindle cell proliferation on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Usually a nodule rather than a broad plaque
Hypertrichosis and sweating are not typical
Often regresses rather than steadily enlarging
Biphasic pattern with central haemangiopericytoma-like vessels is not apparent

data.description: A 58-year-old overweight African American male presented with a 5-year history of a slightly pruritic and painful rash that worsened during summers, and blisters sometimes developed. Emollients were unhelpful. The patient was otherwise healthy, performed indoor manual labor as a maintenance engineer, and had no significant sun exposure. His sister had diabetes mellitus and a similar rash in her axillae. Physical examination revealed irregularly thickened skin containing hyperpigmentation, hypopigmentation, multiple acrochordons (skin tags), malodorous crust, and areas of maceration and erosion. Further examination showed pseudofolliculitis barbae in the submental and mandibular regions bilaterally. The nails, oral cavity, and mucosal membranes appeared normal.

An inherited skin disorder causing recurrent fragile blisters and painful erosions in skin folds, often triggered by heat, sweating, and friction. This is the leading possibility; the biopsy image appears to show extensive epidermal acantholysis consistent with this disease.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic, recurrent rash involving the axilla and neck folds
Pain, mild itching, and occasional blisters
Sister with a similar axillary rash
Normal oral cavity and mucosal membranes
Apparent epidermal acantholysis in the biopsy image
symptoms_not_in_common: Numerous skin tags are not a defining feature
Pseudofolliculitis barbae is likely a separate condition

data.description: An inherited disorder of epidermal adhesion and keratinization that produces crusted, keratotic papules, sometimes with prominent involvement of skin folds. Biopsy typically shows acantholysis with dyskeratosis.
symptoms_in_common: Family history of a similar rash
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal nails, without characteristic notching or longitudinal streaks
Normal oral cavity, without characteristic mucosal papules
Recurrent blistering and broad macerated erosions are more characteristic of Hailey-Hailey disease
Numerous skin tags are not characteristic

data.description: A rare autoimmune pemphigus variant causing blisters that evolve into thickened, vegetating plaques, particularly in flexural areas. Diagnosis generally requires biopsy and direct immunofluorescence.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal oral mucosa, whereas oral involvement is common
A sister with a similar localized rash is less supportive of an acquired autoimmune disease
Consistent summer exacerbations are less characteristic
Numerous skin tags are not a typical feature

data.description: Inflammation and Candida overgrowth in moist skin folds, promoted by sweating, friction, and excess weight. It can also complicate an underlying blistering disorder.
symptoms_not_in_common: Extensive thickened, papillomatous plaques with numerous skin tags are not typical primary findings
Recurrent blisters and a familial pattern suggest an underlying inherited disorder
Apparent extensive epidermal acantholysis is not characteristic of candidal intertrigo
Mixed hyperpigmentation and hypopigmentation are not defining features

data.description: A disorder producing velvety, thickened, hyperpigmented skin in folds, often associated with obesity and insulin resistance. Secondary irritation or infection can cause odor and erosions.
symptoms_in_common: Thickened, hyperpigmented neck and axillary skin
Maceration and odor potentially attributable to secondary intertrigo
symptoms_not_in_common: Recurrent blistering is not typical
Painful erosions and heavy crusting are not typical without a secondary process
Hypopigmented areas are not characteristic
Apparent epidermal acantholysis is not consistent with uncomplicated acanthosis nigricans

data.description: Autosomal dominant acantholytic disorder caused by ATP2C1 mutation, producing recurrent blisters, erosions and macerated, malodorous plaques in intertriginous areas, worsened by heat, sweat and friction. Histology shows suprabasal and widespread acantholysis ('dilapidated brick wall') with little dyskeratosis.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic 5-year intertriginous rash of axillae and neck
Normal nails, oral cavity and mucosae
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset in the sixth decade is later than the usual third to fourth decade
Multiple acrochordons
Marked thickened papillomatous skin with hyper- and hypopigmentation
Pseudofolliculitis barbae (unrelated)

data.description: Autosomal dominant ATP2A2 disorder with greasy, crusted, malodorous keratotic papules in seborrheic and flexural areas, exacerbated by heat, sweat and sun. Histology shows acantholysis with prominent dyskeratosis (corps ronds and grains).
symptoms_in_common: Occasional blisters can occur in the vesiculobullous variant
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal nails (no red/white longitudinal bands or V-shaped nicks)
Normal oral mucosa
Late onset rather than adolescence
Purely intertriginous distribution without seborrheic area involvement
Prominent maceration and erosions
Acrochordons

data.description: Velvety hyperpigmented thickening of flexural skin associated with obesity, insulin resistance and diabetes, often accompanied by skin tags.
symptoms_in_common: Thickened hyperpigmented skin of axillae and neck
symptoms_not_in_common: Blisters
Erosions and maceration
Malodorous crust
Pain
Seasonal summer worsening
Hypopigmentation
Acantholysis on histology

data.description: Rare variant of pemphigus vulgaris with autoantibodies to desmogleins, producing vegetating, eroded, malodorous plaques in intertriginous areas with suprabasal acantholysis.
symptoms_in_common: Thickened vegetating plaques in axillae and neck
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal oral mucosa (oral lesions are usual)
Family history of similar rash
Stable 5-year course with seasonal variation
Otherwise healthy
No eosinophilic abscesses evident
Acrochordons

data.description: Inflammatory dermatosis of skin folds caused by friction, moisture and heat, frequently secondarily infected with Candida or bacteria; common in overweight and diabetic patients.
symptoms_not_in_common: True blisters
Family history of similar rash
Markedly thickened papillomatous plaques
No satellite pustules described
Acantholysis on histology
5-year persistent course

data.description: 44-year-old Chinese woman with no significant prior history presented with 7 weeks of progressively worsening nausea and vomiting with 13 kg weight loss. She denied abdominal pain, distension, or diarrhea. Initial treatment with antidepressants, prokinetics, and anti-emetics for 3 weeks was ineffective. Eight days after admission, she developed metabolic alkalosis, acute respiratory failure, and neurological deficits. Examination showed right-sided limb paralysis, horizontal nystagmus, absent pharyngeal reflex, absent right tendon reflexes, and bilateral Babinski signs. Prior gastroscopy and abdominal CT were normal. Laboratory studies, including liver, kidney, thyroid, autoimmune, and glucose testing, were unremarkable; serum AQP4-IgG was negative, but cerebrospinal fluid AQP4-IgG was positive.

data.diagnosis: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder with area postrema syndrome
data.description: An inflammatory astrocyte disorder associated with AQP4-IgG. Involvement of the dorsal medulla and area postrema can cause prolonged vomiting, followed by brainstem dysfunction. This is the leading diagnosis; isolated cerebrospinal fluid AQP4-IgG positivity should be confirmed with validated testing.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent, progressive nausea and vomiting despite antiemetic treatment
Severe weight loss with normal gastrointestinal investigations
Apparent medullary signal abnormality on the supplied MRI images
Horizontal nystagmus and absent pharyngeal reflex
Right-sided paralysis and bilateral Babinski signs
Acute respiratory failure consistent with severe medullary involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative serum AQP4-IgG despite positive cerebrospinal fluid testing is unusual
Absent right tendon reflexes are less typical than brisk reflexes in central motor pathway disease

data.description: An inflammatory demyelinating disorder that can affect the brainstem, optic nerves, or spinal cord. Brainstem involvement can occasionally produce an area postrema-like presentation.
symptoms_in_common: Nausea and vomiting with brainstem neurological deficits
Right-sided paralysis and bilateral Babinski signs
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive cerebrospinal fluid AQP4-IgG favors neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder instead
Seven weeks of isolated refractory vomiting is an uncommon presentation
Absent right tendon reflexes are not typical of isolated central demyelination

data.description: A central nervous system demyelinating disease that may cause focal brainstem lesions, eye movement abnormalities, weakness, and pyramidal signs.
symptoms_in_common: Absent pharyngeal reflex from possible bulbar pathway involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Prolonged isolated intractable vomiting with profound weight loss is uncommon
Positive cerebrospinal fluid AQP4-IgG argues against multiple sclerosis
Acute respiratory failure is unusual
Absent right tendon reflexes are atypical for central motor pathway lesions

data.description: An infiltrative brainstem tumor that can cause progressive medullary dysfunction, including vomiting, bulbar weakness, motor deficits, and impaired respiratory control.
symptoms_in_common: Horizontal nystagmus and absent pharyngeal reflex
Right-sided paralysis and bilateral Babinski signs
symptoms_not_in_common: Positive cerebrospinal fluid AQP4-IgG favors an inflammatory rather than neoplastic disorder
Abrupt neurological deterioration after a predominantly vomiting-related illness is less typical
Absent right tendon reflexes are not typical of an isolated brainstem tumor

data.description: Inflammation of the brainstem and cerebellum, potentially infectious or autoimmune, that can cause cranial nerve dysfunction, asymmetric weakness, and respiratory compromise.
symptoms_not_in_common: Seven weeks of predominantly isolated vomiting is less typical of infectious rhombencephalitis
Positive cerebrospinal fluid AQP4-IgG favors neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder
Otherwise unremarkable laboratory studies provide limited support for systemic infection

data.diagnosis: Neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (area postrema syndrome)
data.description: Autoimmune astrocytopathy mediated by AQP4-IgG that targets the optic nerves, spinal cord and brainstem. Involvement of the area postrema in the dorsal medulla causes intractable nausea and vomiting, and lesions can extend into the medulla and cervical cord.
symptoms_in_common: 7 weeks of intractable nausea and vomiting unresponsive to anti-emetics and prokinetics
dorsal medulla/cervicomedullary lesion on sagittal MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: serum AQP4-IgG negative (serum is usually more sensitive than CSF)
no optic neuritis reported
absent right tendon reflexes (may reflect acute phase)
metabolic alkalosis (secondary to vomiting rather than the disease itself)

data.description: Acute thiamine deficiency affecting periventricular and brainstem structures, classically after prolonged vomiting or malnutrition, causing ophthalmoplegia/nystagmus, ataxia and confusion.
symptoms_in_common: prolonged vomiting with 13 kg weight loss as a risk factor
neurological deterioration after weeks of poor intake
possible dorsal medullary signal change on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: right-sided limb paralysis
bilateral Babinski signs
absent pharyngeal reflex
acute respiratory failure
no confusion described
CSF AQP4-IgG positive
does not explain the initial vomiting

data.diagnosis: Brainstem (medullary) glioma or other medullary tumour
data.description: Infiltrating neoplasm of the medulla or cervicomedullary junction that causes progressive vomiting, lower cranial nerve palsies and long-tract signs.
symptoms_in_common: progressive nausea and vomiting over weeks
symptoms_not_in_common: abrupt neurological deterioration over days
CSF AQP4-IgG positive
no clear mass effect described
absent right tendon reflexes

data.diagnosis: Multiple sclerosis or MOG antibody-associated disease with brainstem involvement
data.description: Inflammatory demyelinating diseases of the central nervous system that can produce brainstem and spinal cord lesions with relapsing or monophasic deficits.
symptoms_in_common: woman in a typical age range
intractable vomiting can occur with area postrema lesions (particularly in MOGAD)
symptoms_not_in_common: weeks of isolated intractable vomiting as the sole presentation is unusual for MS
acute respiratory failure
CSF AQP4-IgG positive
absent right tendon reflexes
metabolic alkalosis

data.description: Non-inflammatory demyelination of the brainstem caused by rapid correction of electrolyte disturbances, typically in malnourished patients or after prolonged vomiting.
symptoms_in_common: prolonged vomiting and malnutrition with metabolic alkalosis and likely electrolyte derangement
neurological deterioration 8 days after admission (after probable fluid/electrolyte correction)
bulbar dysfunction with absent pharyngeal reflex
symptoms_not_in_common: lesion centred on the medulla rather than the central pons
CSF AQP4-IgG positive
does not explain the initial 7 weeks of vomiting
unilateral rather than symmetric limb weakness
no documented hyponatraemia or rapid sodium correction

data.description: 60-year-old Japanese woman presented with a black nodule on the right postauricular area. Initial staging after radical resection and sentinel node biopsy was pT3aN0M0 stage IIA. At 19 months post-surgery, imaging detected right jugular lymph node and lung metastases. Seven courses of pembrolizumab treatment later, evaluation showed further lung metastasis and new liver metastasis. Tumor harbored BRAF V600E mutation. Thirteen days after starting dabrafenib/trametinib, patient developed fever and hepatosplenomegaly. Laboratory findings showed pancytopenia, hyperferritinemia, increased liver enzyme levels, and coagulation abnormalities.

A potentially life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by excessive immune activation. The onset after dabrafenib/trametinib suggests a treatment-associated trigger, potentially influenced by prior pembrolizumab. The marrow image appears suggestive of hemophagocytosis, although this finding alone does not establish HLH.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent hemophagocytosis in the supplied marrow image
symptoms_not_in_common: The original black skin nodule and established melanoma metastases reflect the underlying malignancy rather than HLH itself

data.diagnosis: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)
data.description: A severe systemic drug hypersensitivity reaction that can cause fever, rash, hematologic abnormalities, and internal-organ injury. The supplied skin photograph appears to show an erythematous eruption, but eosinophilia and other diagnostic features are not reported.
symptoms_in_common: Fever after introduction of new medications
symptoms_not_in_common: Pancytopenia rather than the more characteristic eosinophilia or atypical lymphocytosis
Marked hyperferritinemia with splenomegaly is more suggestive of HLH
Apparent marrow hemophagocytosis is not a defining feature of uncomplicated DRESS
Onset after 13 days is shorter than the usual first-exposure latency

data.description: Severe infection can produce systemic inflammation, liver dysfunction, cytopenias, and consumptive coagulation abnormalities. Infection can also trigger secondary HLH.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent hepatosplenomegaly is less typical of uncomplicated acute sepsis
Apparent marrow hemophagocytosis with hyperferritinemia favors an associated hyperinflammatory syndrome
The close temporal relationship to dabrafenib/trametinib suggests a possible medication-related trigger

data.diagnosis: Dabrafenib/trametinib-associated pyrexia syndrome with systemic toxicity
data.description: BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy commonly causes fever and can produce rash, inflammatory symptoms, and liver-test abnormalities. Severe cases require distinction from infection and HLH.
symptoms_in_common: Fever beginning 13 days after dabrafenib/trametinib initiation
symptoms_not_in_common: Hepatosplenomegaly
Pancytopenia
Hyperferritinemia
Coagulation abnormalities
Apparent marrow hemophagocytosis

data.diagnosis: Progressive metastatic melanoma with bone marrow and hepatic involvement
data.description: Disseminated melanoma can infiltrate the marrow and liver, causing cytopenias, liver dysfunction, and systemic symptoms. The patient has established BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic melanoma, but additional marrow involvement has not been demonstrated.
symptoms_in_common: Documented jugular lymph node, lung, and liver metastases
Pancytopenia, if marrow infiltration is present
Possible malignancy-associated fever and coagulation abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt febrile deterioration shortly after starting targeted therapy
Hyperferritinemia with splenomegaly is more suggestive of HLH than direct tumor infiltration alone
The supplied marrow image appears to show hemophagocytosis rather than clear melanoma infiltration

data.diagnosis: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) induced by dabrafenib/trametinib after anti-PD-1 therapy
data.description: Life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by uncontrolled activation of macrophages and T cells, which can be triggered by BRAF/MEK inhibitors, particularly when given sequentially after immune checkpoint inhibitors.
symptoms_in_common: Hemophagocytosis by macrophages on bone marrow smear
symptoms_not_in_common: Skin biopsy shows nonspecific interface/perivascular lymphocytic dermatitis rather than an HLH-specific finding

data.diagnosis: Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS) / drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome
data.description: Severe delayed drug hypersensitivity reaction with fever, widespread rash, hematologic abnormalities and internal organ involvement, typically 2-8 weeks after drug initiation.
symptoms_in_common: Onset about 2 weeks after a new drug
Perivascular lymphocytic infiltrate with interface change on skin biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: Pancytopenia rather than leukocytosis with eosinophilia
Marked hyperferritinemia
Coagulation abnormalities
Hemophagocytosis in bone marrow
No facial edema or prominent lymphadenopathy described

data.diagnosis: Dabrafenib/trametinib-associated pyrexia syndrome with drug eruption
data.description: Common adverse event of BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy featuring recurrent fever, sometimes with rash, chills, and mild liver enzyme elevation, usually resolving with drug interruption.
symptoms_in_common: Onset within the first weeks of dabrafenib/trametinib
symptoms_not_in_common: Hepatosplenomegaly
Pancytopenia
Hyperferritinemia
Coagulation abnormalities
Hemophagocytosis in bone marrow

data.diagnosis: Delayed immune-related adverse event / cytokine release syndrome from pembrolizumab
data.description: Immune checkpoint inhibitors can cause delayed systemic immune activation including hepatitis, hematologic toxicity, rash, and cytokine release syndrome, sometimes unmasked by subsequent targeted therapy.
symptoms_in_common: Maculopapular rash with lymphocytic interface dermatitis
symptoms_not_in_common: Close temporal relation to starting dabrafenib/trametinib rather than to pembrolizumab dosing
Hepatosplenomegaly
Bone marrow hemophagocytosis points to full HLH rather than isolated immune-related adverse event
No prominent hypotension or hypoxia described

data.diagnosis: Sepsis with disseminated intravascular coagulation / infection-associated hemophagocytic syndrome (e.g., EBV or CMV)
data.description: Severe systemic infection causing fever, cytopenias, liver dysfunction and coagulopathy; viral infections can also trigger secondary hemophagocytosis in cancer patients.
symptoms_not_in_common: No infectious focus or positive microbiology described
Clear temporal association with initiation of dabrafenib/trametinib
No hypotension or shock described
Patient not reported to be neutropenic or on cytotoxic chemotherapy beforehand

data.description: A 58-year-old man presented with a six-week history of muscle weakness, dysphagia, and a symmetrical widespread rash on the face, torso, and limbs. Laboratory testing revealed elevated creatine kinase of 7070 u/L (reference range 30-175). An oesophagogastroduodenoscopy was performed and showed abnormal findings, and a PET CT scan was arranged.

data.diagnosis: Cancer-associated dermatomyositis, potentially associated with oesophageal carcinoma
data.description: An inflammatory muscle disease with characteristic skin lesions that can occur as a paraneoplastic syndrome. The abnormal endoscopy and focal thoracic PET uptake raise concern for an oesophageal malignancy, but biopsy is needed to establish its presence and type.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated creatine kinase of 7070 U/L
Symmetrical rash involving the face, torso, and limbs
Dorsal hand lesions over the finger joints consistent with Gottron papules
Abnormal upper gastrointestinal endoscopy and focal thoracic PET uptake suggesting a possible underlying malignancy

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory myopathy causing muscle weakness and characteristic rashes, including Gottron papules. Dysphagia can result from involvement of swallowing muscles.
symptoms_in_common: Joint-centered erythematous, scaly lesions on the dorsal hand
symptoms_not_in_common: Focal thoracic PET uptake and abnormal endoscopy are not explained by idiopathic dermatomyositis alone and require investigation for associated disease

data.diagnosis: Overlap myositis associated with a connective tissue disease
data.description: Inflammatory muscle disease occurring alongside another autoimmune connective tissue disorder, such as systemic sclerosis or mixed connective tissue disease. It may include dermatomyositis-like skin findings and oesophageal dysfunction.
symptoms_not_in_common: The characteristic joint-centered hand rash more specifically favors dermatomyositis
Focal thoracic PET uptake is not a typical manifestation of uncomplicated overlap myositis

data.description: An inflammatory myopathy characterized by muscle weakness and elevated muscle enzymes, sometimes with swallowing muscle involvement. It generally lacks the characteristic skin lesions of dermatomyositis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Widespread symmetrical rash
Gottron-like lesions over the finger joints
Focal thoracic PET uptake and abnormal endoscopy are not explained by polymyositis itself

data.description: An autoimmune muscle disease causing prominent muscle injury, substantial creatine kinase elevation, and weakness. It may be associated with anti-SRP or anti-HMGCR antibodies, statin exposure, or occasionally malignancy.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated creatine kinase of 7070 U/L
symptoms_not_in_common: Widespread symmetrical inflammatory rash
Gottron-like dorsal hand lesions are characteristic of dermatomyositis rather than necrotizing myopathy
Focal thoracic PET uptake and abnormal endoscopy require a separate explanation

data.diagnosis: Paraneoplastic dermatomyositis secondary to oesophageal carcinoma
data.description: Idiopathic inflammatory myopathy with characteristic skin findings (Gottron's papules, heliotrope rash) occurring as a paraneoplastic phenomenon; in adults over 50 it is frequently associated with an underlying malignancy, here suggested by an FDG-avid oesophageal/mediastinal lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute muscle weakness over six weeks
Symmetrical widespread rash on face, torso and limbs
Erythematous scaly plaques over the knuckles and interphalangeal joints (Gottron's papules/sign)
Focal FDG-avid lesion in the region of the oesophagus on PET CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss or other constitutional symptoms reported
Dysphagia could be due to myopathy alone rather than tumour

data.description: Autoimmune inflammatory myopathy with proximal muscle weakness and pathognomonic skin changes, without an associated malignancy.
symptoms_in_common: Symmetrical rash on face, torso and limbs
Gottron's papules on the dorsal hands
symptoms_not_in_common: Abnormal endoscopy findings
Focal FDG-avid mediastinal/oesophageal lesion on PET CT suggesting malignancy

data.description: Autoimmune myositis associated with antisynthetase antibodies (e.g. anti-Jo-1) or overlapping connective tissue disease, featuring myositis, interstitial lung disease, arthritis, Raynaud's phenomenon and mechanic's hands.
symptoms_not_in_common: No interstitial lung disease, arthritis, fever or Raynaud's reported
Rash is over the knuckles and widespread rather than mechanic's hands on the lateral fingers
Focal FDG-avid oesophageal lesion
Abnormal endoscopy findings

data.description: Multisystem autoimmune disease that can cause photosensitive facial and body rash and, less commonly, inflammatory myositis.
symptoms_in_common: Symmetrical rash involving face, torso and limbs
Erythematous rash on the dorsal hands
symptoms_not_in_common: Hand rash in lupus typically spares the knuckles and affects the skin between the joints, whereas here the knuckles are involved
Creatine kinase this high is unusual
Prominent dysphagia
Older male patient
Focal FDG-avid oesophageal lesion and abnormal endoscopy
No arthritis, serositis, renal or haematological features reported

data.description: Severe inflammatory myopathy (anti-SRP or anti-HMGCR antibody associated, sometimes statin-triggered or paraneoplastic) with rapidly progressive weakness and very high creatine kinase.
symptoms_not_in_common: Widespread symmetrical rash on face, torso and limbs
Gottron's papules on the hands (skin involvement is not typical)
No statin exposure reported

data.description: 28-year-old male who suddenly went into coma for 9 hours preceded by tonic-clonic seizures lasting 10 minutes. No fever, vomiting or micturition. No focal neurological signs. Past medical history was unremarkable. Neurological examination revealed normal cranial nerves, normal power and reflexes. Routine laboratory tests were normal.

A malignant astrocytic brain tumor that can cause seizures and intratumoral hemorrhage. The frontal lesion and apparent GFAP and OLIG2 staining favor a glial tumor, but definitive classification requires formal pathology and molecular testing.
symptoms_in_common: Prolonged loss of consciousness following the seizure
Left frontal mass with ring enhancement and surrounding edema
Hyperdense lesion on CT, suggesting a possible hemorrhagic component
Normal routine laboratory tests and absence of fever
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt presentation without preceding progressive neurological symptoms
Normal strength, reflexes and cranial nerve examination despite a sizable lesion

data.description: An aggressive diffuse glioma that commonly produces an enhancing mass with necrosis, edema and sometimes hemorrhage. The imaging is compatible, but the supplied images alone cannot establish the required histological or molecular criteria.
symptoms_in_common: Ring-enhancing frontal mass with surrounding edema
Apparent glial-marker positivity in the pathology panels
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 28 is younger than the usual presentation
No preceding progressive focal neurological symptoms
Normal neurological examination after recovery

data.description: A diffuse glioma frequently arising in the frontal lobes and presenting with seizures in younger adults. Higher-grade tumors may enhance or bleed; diagnosis requires an IDH mutation and combined 1p/19q deletion.
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden prolonged coma is less typical than an isolated seizure presentation
Prominent ring enhancement and extensive edema are less typical of lower-grade oligodendroglioma
The supplied pathology does not establish the required molecular alterations

data.description: A low-flow vascular malformation that can cause seizures and intracerebral bleeding and may not be visible on angiography. A hemorrhagic lesion can occasionally resemble a tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden seizure and loss of consciousness
Hyperdense frontal lesion compatible with blood
No obvious vascular malformation on the supplied angiographic views
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent ring enhancement with substantial surrounding edema is less characteristic of an uncomplicated cavernous malformation
The supplied pathology appears to favor a glial neoplasm rather than malformed vascular channels

data.description: A localized intracerebral bacterial infection that can produce a ring-enhancing mass, edema and seizures. Diffusion-weighted MRI and microbiological evaluation are important for distinguishing it from a necrotic tumor.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever
Normal routine laboratory tests
No reported infectious source or relevant medical history
Hyperdense, potentially hemorrhagic lesion is less typical
The supplied pathology appears more consistent with a glial tumor than suppurative infection

data.diagnosis: Glioblastoma (WHO grade IV) with intratumoral hemorrhage
data.description: Highly malignant astrocytic tumor that may present acutely with hemorrhage (tumor apoplexy) mimicking spontaneous intracerebral hematoma; typically shows ring enhancement, perilesional edema, and GFAP/Olig2 positivity with high p53 and Ki-67 (MIB-1) labeling.
symptoms_in_common: Sudden onset tonic-clonic seizure followed by coma
Left frontal hyperdense hemorrhagic mass on CT with surrounding edema
Ring-enhancing lesion on contrast MRI with marked perilesional edema and mass effect
CTA without aneurysm or vascular malformation
Histology showing pleomorphic, atypical glial cells with mitotic activity
GFAP and Olig2 positive, strong p53 expression, high MIB-1 proliferation index
No fever and normal laboratory tests
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age (28 years) is less typical for glioblastoma
No prior headache or progressive neurological deficit
No focal neurological signs despite a large frontal lesion
Fairly smooth, regular rim of enhancement rather than a thick irregular nodular rim

data.diagnosis: Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage from a vascular malformation (cavernous malformation or AVM)
data.description: Bleeding from a congenital vascular lesion, the most common cause of lobar hemorrhage in young adults, often presenting with seizures; a subacute hematoma can show peripheral rim enhancement.
symptoms_in_common: Young adult with unremarkable past history
Sudden onset seizure and loss of consciousness
Hyperdense lobar frontal hematoma on CT
T2 hypointense core consistent with blood products
Rim enhancement can occur in subacute hematoma
symptoms_not_in_common: CTA shows no nidus, draining veins or abnormal vessels
Extensive vasogenic edema disproportionate to an acute hematoma
Histology shows neoplastic glial cells rather than vascular channels
High p53 and MIB-1 labeling indicates a neoplasm

data.description: Focal encapsulated intracerebral infection that appears as a smooth, thin ring-enhancing lesion with a T2 hypointense capsule and marked surrounding edema; often presents with seizures and headache.
symptoms_in_common: Marked perilesional vasogenic edema with mass effect
Fever may be absent in up to half of cases
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, no source of infection, no immunosuppression
Normal routine laboratory tests (no leukocytosis)
Hyperdense hemorrhagic center on CT rather than hypodense pus
T2 hypointense core rather than T2 hyperintense liquid content
Gross specimen is hemorrhagic tissue, histology shows glial tumor rather than pus and inflammatory cells

data.description: Secondary tumor deposit (e.g., melanoma, choriocarcinoma/germ cell tumor, renal or lung carcinoma) that frequently bleeds, shows ring enhancement and disproportionate vasogenic edema.
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age with no known primary malignancy
Solitary lesion
Normal laboratory tests and unremarkable history
GFAP and Olig2 positivity indicates glial origin rather than metastatic tumor

data.diagnosis: Anaplastic astrocytoma / IDH-mutant astrocytoma (WHO grade III–IV) with hemorrhage
data.description: Diffusely infiltrating high-grade astrocytoma more common in young adults, typically frontal, often IDH-mutant with ATRX loss and p53 overexpression; presents commonly with seizures.
symptoms_in_common: GFAP and Olig2 positive glial tumor
Strong p53 expression and elevated MIB-1 index
symptoms_not_in_common: Massive intratumoral hemorrhage is uncommon
Ring enhancement with central necrosis/hemorrhage suggests grade IV rather than grade III
IDH-1 staining appears weak/equivocal and ATRX appears retained, not the classic IDH-mutant profile
Sudden apoplectic onset without prior symptoms

data.description: 40-year-old woman with 10 months of progressive lower-extremity edema, starting as episodic pain and swelling in the feet and ankles after prolonged standing and advancing to the lower legs and thighs, with abdominal distention and pain. Five months before evaluation, she developed left back and flank pain. Past history includes hypothyroidism, latent tuberculosis, two vaginal deliveries, ectopic pregnancy, hysterectomy for fibroids, and appendectomy. Examination showed 2+ edema of the lower and upper legs, jugular venous pressure of 8 cm H2O, and a distended, mildly tender abdomen. Labs showed hypoalbuminemia and low total protein, marked proteinuria, microscopic hematuria, low calcium, and mildly elevated TSH with low free thyroxine.

A glomerular disease that causes heavy urinary protein loss, hypoalbuminemia, and edema. Associated hypercoagulability can cause renal vein or inferior vena cava thrombosis; the CT appearance raises concern for venous thrombosis but requires formal radiologic confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Flank pain potentially related to renal vein thrombosis
Low total calcium potentially related to hypoalbuminemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Flank and abdominal pain are not typical of uncomplicated membranous nephropathy
Hypothyroidism is not a defining feature, although urinary thyroid-binding protein loss can worsen it

data.diagnosis: Renal vein thrombosis with inferior vena cava involvement
data.description: Clot formation in the renal veins, potentially extending into the inferior vena cava, can cause renal venous congestion and impaired lower-body venous drainage. It may complicate nephrotic syndrome rather than explain the underlying protein-losing kidney disease.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive swelling involving both lower legs and thighs
CT findings concerning for central venous filling defects and surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound hypoalbuminemia and marked proteinuria suggest an underlying glomerular disease rather than isolated venous thrombosis
Abnormal thyroid function is not directly explained by venous thrombosis
Low calcium is not a characteristic direct manifestation

data.diagnosis: Lupus nephritis, particularly class V membranous lupus nephritis
data.description: Autoimmune kidney inflammation associated with systemic lupus erythematosus. Class V disease can cause nephrotic syndrome, while other classes or mixed disease may produce substantial hematuria.
symptoms_in_common: Adult woman in a typical demographic group
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent flank pain is not typical unless a complication such as thrombosis occurs
Abnormal thyroid function is not a characteristic manifestation of lupus nephritis

data.description: Scarring affecting portions of some kidney glomeruli, causing proteinuria and sometimes nephrotic syndrome. Diagnosis generally requires kidney biopsy and assessment for primary or secondary causes.
symptoms_not_in_common: Back and flank pain are not typical of uncomplicated focal segmental glomerulosclerosis
Abdominal pain is not a characteristic direct manifestation
Hypothyroidism is not a defining feature

data.description: Deposition of abnormal amyloid proteins in the kidneys can cause heavy proteinuria and nephrotic syndrome. It may arise from a plasma-cell disorder or chronic inflammatory disease; a history of latent tuberculosis alone does not establish an inflammatory cause.
symptoms_not_in_common: Microscopic hematuria is less characteristic than proteinuria
Localized back and flank pain is not typical of uncomplicated renal amyloidosis
Abnormal thyroid function is not a usual presenting feature of renal amyloidosis

diagnoses.name: Membranous nephropathy
diagnoses.title: Glomerular disease associated with thin basement membrane nephropathy

data.diagnosis: Membranous nephropathy (primary, PLA2R-associated) with nephrotic syndrome
data.description: Immune-complex podocytopathy that is the most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in non-diabetic adults; slow onset of edema and a high risk of venous thrombosis, including renal vein thrombosis.
symptoms_in_common: abdominal distention with ascites and anasarca on imaging
back and flank pain possibly from renal vein thrombosis
low total calcium due to low albumin
abnormal thyroid tests from urinary loss of thyroid hormone and binding proteins
perinephric and mesenteric edema on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: abdominal pain is not typical unless complicated by thrombosis or bowel wall edema
jugular venous pressure of 8 cm H2O is not explained by the disease itself

data.diagnosis: Lupus nephritis (class V membranous or mixed)
data.description: Immune-complex glomerulonephritis due to systemic lupus erythematosus, commonly affecting women of reproductive age and presenting with nephrotic-range proteinuria and hematuria.
symptoms_in_common: ascites and abdominal pain possibly from serositis
symptoms_not_in_common: no rash, arthritis, oral ulcers or cytopenias described
no fever or other systemic features
10-month indolent course without extrarenal manifestations

data.description: Podocyte injury pattern, primary or secondary, causing nephrotic syndrome in adults, often with microscopic hematuria and progressive loss of kidney function.
symptoms_not_in_common: back and flank pain
primary form usually has more abrupt onset than a 10-month gradual course
abdominal pain

data.description: Deposition of amyloid fibrils in glomeruli causing heavy proteinuria; AL arises from a plasma cell clone, AA from chronic inflammation or infection such as tuberculosis.
symptoms_in_common: history of tuberculosis infection as a possible chronic inflammatory source
kidneys of preserved or enlarged size on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: microscopic hematuria is uncommon
relatively young age for AL amyloidosis
latent rather than active tuberculosis makes AA unlikely
no macroglossia, neuropathy, hepatomegaly or cardiac involvement described
back and flank pain

data.diagnosis: Renal vein thrombosis complicating nephrotic syndrome
data.description: Thrombosis of the renal vein (sometimes extending to the inferior vena cava) due to the hypercoagulable state of nephrotic syndrome, especially membranous nephropathy; causes flank pain, hematuria and worsening proteinuria.
symptoms_in_common: back and flank pain developing 5 months before evaluation
worsening leg edema extending to the thighs
severe hypoalbuminemia as a risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: does not by itself explain 5 months of edema before the pain began
bilateral symmetric edema and ascites are better explained by the underlying nephrotic syndrome
thyroid test abnormalities

data.description: A 25-year-old man was referred to the oncology unit with a three-week history of a progressively enlarging neck lump and atypical lymphoid cells found on fine needle aspiration cytology. He reported mild exertional dyspnea and drenching night sweats, but denied weight loss, occupational exposure to harmful substances, recent travel, or high-risk sexual behavior. He had a smoking history since age 16. On physical examination, a palpable right supraclavicular lymph node measuring 3 cm in diameter was found. Chest radiography revealed a widened mediastinum but no lung lesions. Core biopsy of the lymph node showed partial effacement of nodal architecture by scattered large cells in a background of reactive lymphocytes, eosinophils, and plasma cells with some collagen fibrosis. These large cells stained positive for CD15 and CD30 and negative for CD45.

data.diagnosis: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, likely nodular sclerosis subtype
data.description: The most likely diagnosis. This lymphoma commonly affects young adults and involves mediastinal and cervical lymph nodes. Scattered Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells typically express CD15 and CD30 but lack CD45; fibrosis favors the nodular sclerosis subtype.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively enlarging right supraclavicular lymph node
Widened mediastinum and anterior mediastinal soft-tissue mass on imaging
Scattered large atypical cells in a reactive background containing eosinophils and plasma cells
Large cells positive for CD15 and CD30 and negative for CD45

data.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma occurring predominantly in young adults, often presenting as an anterior mediastinal mass with fibrosis. The reported cellular pattern and immunophenotype favor classical Hodgkin lymphoma instead.
symptoms_in_common: Anterior mediastinal mass and widened mediastinum
CD30 expression, which can occur in this lymphoma
symptoms_not_in_common: CD15 positivity with CD45 negativity is atypical
Scattered large cells in a predominantly reactive inflammatory background rather than a diffuse proliferation of large B cells

data.description: A rare lymphoma with overlapping features of classical Hodgkin lymphoma and primary mediastinal large B-cell lymphoma. Diagnosis requires additional tissue assessment and B-cell marker testing.
symptoms_in_common: Young adult man with an anterior mediastinal mass
Large atypical cells with CD30 and possible CD15 expression
symptoms_not_in_common: The reported scattered-cell inflammatory pattern and CD15-positive, CD30-positive, CD45-negative phenotype fit classical Hodgkin lymphoma more directly
No discordant morphology or strong B-cell marker expression is reported to establish gray zone lymphoma

data.description: A CD30-positive T-cell lymphoma that often affects young people and can cause rapidly enlarging lymph nodes and systemic symptoms. ALK testing and additional lineage markers would help distinguish it from Hodgkin lymphoma.
symptoms_in_common: Possible mediastinal lymph node involvement with dyspnea
symptoms_not_in_common: CD15 positivity is unusual
CD45 negativity is less typical, although expression can vary
Scattered large cells within an eosinophil-rich reactive background with fibrosis are more characteristic of classical Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: An aggressive precursor T-cell lymphoma that commonly affects adolescent and young adult men and often produces a large anterior mediastinal mass. Its usual blast morphology and immunophenotype differ substantially from the reported biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Anterior mediastinal mass and widened mediastinum
symptoms_not_in_common: Scattered large atypical cells rather than a relatively uniform population of lymphoblasts
Reactive eosinophils and plasma cells with collagen fibrosis
CD15-positive and CD30-positive large cells are not the typical immunophenotype

data.description: B-cell derived lymphoma characterized by scattered Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells (CD15+, CD30+, CD45-) in a mixed inflammatory background with collagen fibrosis; commonly presents in young adults with cervical/supraclavicular nodes and an anterior mediastinal mass.
symptoms_in_common: Mild exertional dyspnea from mediastinal mass
Widened mediastinum on radiograph and anterior mediastinal mass on CT
Scattered large cells in a background of reactive lymphocytes, eosinophils and plasma cells
Large cells CD15+ and CD30+, CD45-
symptoms_not_in_common: No weight loss (may be absent)
Short three-week history is somewhat rapid

data.description: Aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma arising from thymic B cells, presenting in young adults as a rapidly growing anterior mediastinal mass, often with sclerosis.
symptoms_in_common: Anterior mediastinal mass with widened mediastinum
symptoms_not_in_common: CD45 negative (PMBCL is CD45+)
CD15 positive (usually negative)
Scattered large cells rather than sheets of large cells
Prominent eosinophil and plasma cell inflammatory background
More common in young women

data.description: CD30-positive mature T-cell lymphoma (ALK+ form common in young males) composed of large pleomorphic 'hallmark' cells, presenting with lymphadenopathy and B symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: CD15 positive (usually negative in ALCL)
Scattered tumor cells rather than cohesive sheets or sinusoidal growth
Eosinophil/plasma cell-rich background with collagen fibrosis more typical of Hodgkin lymphoma
No extranodal or skin involvement

data.diagnosis: Mediastinal germ cell tumor (e.g., seminoma or embryonal carcinoma)
data.description: Extragonadal germ cell tumor arising in the anterior mediastinum of young men; may metastasize to supraclavicular nodes. Embryonal carcinoma is CD30+ and CD45-.
symptoms_in_common: Large cells CD30+ and CD45- (embryonal carcinoma)
Lymphocyte-rich background with fibrous septa can be seen in seminoma
symptoms_not_in_common: CD15 positivity
Drenching night sweats (uncommon)
Eosinophil and plasma cell-rich background
Scattered rather than cohesive tumor cells
Fine needle aspiration showed atypical lymphoid cells
No testicular abnormality reported

data.description: Epithelial tumor of the thymus presenting as an anterior mediastinal mass with a variable lymphocytic component; thymic carcinoma may spread to lymph nodes.
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age (typically 40-60 years)
Supraclavicular lymphadenopathy is uncommon in thymoma
Drenching night sweats
CD15 and CD30 positivity of the large cells
Eosinophils and plasma cells in background
No paraneoplastic features such as myasthenia gravis

data.description: A 36-year-old man, sexually active with men, presented to the emergency department with a 2-week history of fever, headache, drowsiness, and photophobia. He was previously healthy. Physical examination revealed a temperature of 38.3°C and neck stiffness. CT of the head was normal. Lumbar puncture showed an opening pressure of 29 cm of water (ref: <20 cm). CSF analysis revealed: cell count 340 cells/µL (90% mononuclear cells, predominantly lymphocytes), glucose 46 mg/dL, and protein 0.80 g/L. HIV antibody test was positive with viral load 300,000 copies/mL and CD4+ count of 7 cells/µL.

An opportunistic fungal infection of the meninges, usually caused by Cryptococcus neoformans in advanced HIV. This is the leading diagnosis; the supplied microscopy shows round yeast-like organisms with prominent clear capsules, strongly supporting Cryptococcus.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute fever and headache over two weeks
Elevated CSF opening pressure of 29 cm H2O
Lymphocyte-predominant CSF inflammation and elevated protein
Profound HIV-associated immunosuppression with CD4 count of 7 cells/µL
Encapsulated yeast-like organisms on supplied microscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: CSF cell count of 340 cells/µL is higher than often seen in cryptococcal meningitis with profound immunosuppression, although it does not exclude the diagnosis

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the meninges, producing subacute meningitis with lymphocytic inflammation, elevated protein, and frequently low CSF glucose. Advanced HIV increases susceptibility.
symptoms_in_common: Two-week history of fever and headache
symptoms_not_in_common: Encapsulated yeast-like organisms on microscopy are not explained by tuberculosis
CSF glucose of 46 mg/dL is not markedly reduced, although interpretation requires a paired blood glucose

data.description: An opportunistic viral infection of the central nervous system, typically occurring in people with HIV and CD4 counts below 50 cells/µL.
symptoms_in_common: Profound immunosuppression with CD4 count of 7 cells/µL
symptoms_not_in_common: Encapsulated yeast-like organisms on microscopy are incompatible with CMV as the explanation for that finding
Prominent elevated intracranial pressure is less characteristic than in cryptococcal meningitis

data.description: Treponema pallidum infection of the meninges can cause headache, fever, meningismus, and lymphocytic CSF inflammation. HIV coinfection increases clinical concern.
symptoms_in_common: Sexual exposure context that warrants syphilis testing
Headache, fever, photophobia, and neck stiffness
symptoms_not_in_common: Encapsulated yeast-like organisms on microscopy are not a feature of neurosyphilis
Markedly elevated opening pressure and drowsiness are less characteristic of uncomplicated syphilitic meningitis

data.description: HSV infection of the meninges and brain can cause fever, headache, meningismus, altered consciousness, and lymphocytic CSF inflammation. Early CT imaging may be normal.
symptoms_in_common: Normal CT does not exclude the disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Encapsulated yeast-like organisms on microscopy are not explained by HSV infection
A subacute two-week course with elevated opening pressure in profound HIV-associated immunosuppression is more characteristic of cryptococcal meningitis

data.description: Opportunistic fungal meningoencephalitis caused by an encapsulated yeast, typically in advanced HIV with CD4 <100 cells/µL; presents subacutely with raised intracranial pressure. CSF microscopy shows round encapsulated yeasts with clear halos (capsules) and narrow-based budding.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute 2-week course of fever and headache
Advanced HIV with CD4+ count of 7 cells/µL
Elevated opening pressure (29 cm of water)
Lymphocytic CSF pleocytosis with elevated protein
CSF microscopy showing round yeast cells surrounded by clear halos consistent with encapsulated yeasts
symptoms_not_in_common: CSF cell count of 340 cells/µL is higher than usual for HIV-associated cryptococcal meningitis (often low or near-normal cell count)
CSF glucose only mildly reduced or normal
Prominent meningism is less common in severely immunosuppressed patients

data.description: Subacute to chronic meningitis caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, common in HIV-infected patients, with basal meningeal inflammation, lymphocytic CSF, high protein and low glucose.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute 2-week course of fever and headache
symptoms_not_in_common: Encapsulated yeast forms seen on CSF microscopy
CSF glucose not markedly low
CSF protein only modestly elevated
Normal head CT without hydrocephalus or basal enhancement
No cranial nerve palsies or reported pulmonary symptoms

data.description: CNS infection by Treponema pallidum, more frequent and more aggressive in HIV-positive men who have sex with men; can present as subacute lymphocytic meningitis.
symptoms_in_common: Man who has sex with men with HIV infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Encapsulated yeast forms seen on CSF microscopy
Markedly elevated opening pressure is less typical
Fever and drowsiness are less prominent in syphilitic meningitis
No rash, chancre, cranial nerve palsies, or ocular/otologic involvement described

data.diagnosis: Viral (aseptic) meningitis, including HSV-2/VZV/enterovirus or HIV-associated meningitis
data.description: Meningeal inflammation due to viral infection, producing lymphocytic pleocytosis with normal or slightly low glucose and mildly elevated protein; usually self-limited.
symptoms_in_common: Near-normal CSF glucose with mildly elevated protein
symptoms_not_in_common: Encapsulated yeast forms seen on CSF microscopy
2-week subacute duration is longer than typical
Markedly raised opening pressure
Drowsiness (altered sensorium) is unusual for uncomplicated viral meningitis
CD4 count of 7 is not consistent with HIV seroconversion meningitis

data.description: Reactivation of Toxoplasma gondii in advanced HIV (CD4 <100 cells/µL), usually causing multiple ring-enhancing brain abscesses with headache, fever, altered mental status and focal neurological deficits.
symptoms_in_common: Advanced HIV with CD4+ count <100 cells/µL
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal head CT (no ring-enhancing or mass lesions)
Prominent meningism (neck stiffness, photophobia)
CSF pleocytosis of 340 cells/µL
Encapsulated yeast forms seen on CSF microscopy
No focal neurological deficits or seizures

data.description: 31-year-old man with sleep apnea and newly diagnosed severe hypertension (170/128 mm Hg initially, persistent readings 164/110 and 173/110). He reported 6 months of lethargy and intermittent headaches. History included ex-smoking (20 pack-years). On examination, he was tachycardic (106 bpm) with BMI 34; otherwise no cushingoid features, hyperpigmentation, renal or carotid bruits, or tremor. Blood counts, urea, electrolytes, and renal artery Doppler were normal. Hormonal testing showed elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio, normal urinary metanephrines, mildly elevated 24-hour urinary cortisol, normal post-dexamethasone cortisol, and low ACTH.

Excess aldosterone production, often from an adrenal adenoma or bilateral adrenal hyperplasia, causes secondary hypertension. This is a leading possibility, although an elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio requires interpretation and usually confirmatory testing.
symptoms_in_common: Severe, persistent hypertension at a young age
Normal potassium does not exclude this diagnosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Tachycardia is not a characteristic feature
Low ACTH and mildly elevated urinary cortisol are not explained by isolated aldosterone excess

data.description: Repeated upper-airway obstruction during sleep can increase sympathetic activity, contribute to severe hypertension, and cause daytime fatigue.
symptoms_in_common: Tachycardia, potentially related to sympathetic activation
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio warrants evaluation for an additional cause of hypertension
Low ACTH is not a characteristic finding

data.description: Hypertension without a single identifiable secondary cause, associated with factors such as obesity and sleep apnea. It could coexist with another endocrine disorder.
symptoms_in_common: Normal renal function and renal artery Doppler
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked hypertension at age 31 raises concern for a secondary cause
Elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio suggests possible primary aldosteronism
Low ACTH and mildly elevated urinary cortisol are not characteristic

data.description: Adrenal cortisol production independent of pituitary ACTH can cause hypertension and metabolic abnormalities, sometimes without obvious cushingoid features. Normal cortisol suppression after dexamethasone makes this diagnosis less likely.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal post-dexamethasone cortisol argues against autonomous cortisol secretion
Elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio is not explained by isolated cortisol excess
No cushingoid features, although these may be absent in mild disease

data.description: A catecholamine-secreting adrenal tumor that can cause sustained or episodic hypertension, headaches, and tachycardia. Normal urinary metanephrines substantially reduce its likelihood.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal urinary metanephrines argue strongly against this diagnosis
Elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio is not characteristic
Low ACTH and mildly elevated urinary cortisol are not characteristic
No tremor

data.diagnosis: Primary aldosteronism (aldosterone-producing adrenal adenoma, Conn syndrome)
data.description: Autonomous aldosterone secretion from an adrenal adenoma or bilateral adrenal hyperplasia, causing renin-suppressed hypertension. It is often seen in young patients with severe or resistant hypertension and is strongly associated with sleep apnea.
symptoms_in_common: Severe hypertension at a young age
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal electrolytes (no hypokalemia, although normokalemia is common)
Mildly elevated 24-hour urinary cortisol
Low ACTH
Tachycardia

data.diagnosis: Aldosterone and cortisol co-secreting adrenal adenoma (Connshing syndrome)
data.description: An adrenal cortical tumor that autonomously secretes both aldosterone and cortisol, producing primary aldosteronism together with mild or subclinical ACTH-independent hypercortisolism.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of overt cushingoid features (consistent with subclinical hypercortisolism)
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal post-dexamethasone cortisol (autonomous cortisol secretion usually fails to suppress)
Normal electrolytes
Tachycardia

data.diagnosis: ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome (cortisol-secreting adrenal adenoma or subclinical Cushing)
data.description: Autonomous adrenal cortisol overproduction that suppresses pituitary ACTH, causing hypertension, central obesity and metabolic complications.
symptoms_not_in_common: No cushingoid features
Normal post-dexamethasone cortisol
Elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio
Normal electrolytes and blood counts
Tachycardia

data.diagnosis: Adrenocortical carcinoma with mixed hormone secretion
data.description: A rare malignant tumor of the adrenal cortex that often secretes several steroid hormones (cortisol, aldosterone, androgens or precursors), and can present with rapidly developing severe hypertension.
symptoms_in_common: Severe new-onset hypertension in a young adult
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal or flank pain or mass
No weight loss
No hypokalemia
No cushingoid or virilizing features
Normal post-dexamethasone cortisol
Tachycardia

data.diagnosis: Essential hypertension with obstructive sleep apnea and obesity (pseudo-Cushing state)
data.description: Primary hypertension worsened by obesity and obstructive sleep apnea, which cause sympathetic overactivity. Obesity and sleep apnea can also mildly raise urinary cortisol without true Cushing syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Mildly elevated urinary cortisol with normal dexamethasone suppression
Normal renal artery Doppler and metanephrines
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated aldosterone-to-renin ratio
Low ACTH
Very severe hypertension at age 31

data.description: 22-year-old athletic male presented with swelling and locking of the left knee. He had no recent trauma but had several football injuries as a child. Two years prior, he had experienced disabling knee pain.

data.diagnosis: Osteochondritis dissecans of the femoral condyle
data.description: A focal disorder of subchondral bone that can cause the overlying cartilage and bone to separate, producing an unstable fragment or loose body. The apparent femoral condylar defect on these radiographs makes this a leading possibility; MRI would help assess stability.
symptoms_in_common: Mechanical locking, potentially caused by an unstable fragment
Previous episode of disabling knee pain

data.diagnosis: Chronic post-traumatic osteochondral injury with an intra-articular loose body
data.description: An old injury can detach a fragment of cartilage and underlying bone, leaving an articular defect and a loose body that intermittently obstructs knee movement.
symptoms_in_common: Possible osteochondral defect on the radiographs
symptoms_not_in_common: No recent trauma, which argues against an acute osteochondral fracture but not a chronic injury

data.description: A displaced longitudinal meniscal tear can physically block knee movement and cause recurrent pain and swelling. MRI is needed because meniscal tears are not directly visible on plain radiographs.
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent femoral condylar bony defect is not explained by an isolated meniscal tear
No recent twisting injury, although a chronic tear remains possible

data.description: A usually benign synovial disorder that produces cartilage nodules, which can detach and form intra-articular loose bodies, sometimes becoming calcified or ossified.
symptoms_not_in_common: A focal femoral condylar defect is less characteristic than multiple intra-articular nodules
Numerous mineralized loose bodies are not clearly demonstrated on the supplied radiographs

data.diagnosis: Tenosynovial giant cell tumor of the knee
data.description: A proliferative synovial disorder, historically called pigmented villonodular synovitis in its diffuse form, that can cause chronic pain, swelling, and occasional mechanical symptoms. MRI is more informative than radiographs.
symptoms_not_in_common: True mechanical locking is less typical than persistent swelling and stiffness
An apparent osteochondral fragment or focal articular defect is less typical than synovial thickening or pressure erosions

data.diagnosis: Osteochondritis dissecans with intra-articular loose body
data.description: Focal injury of subchondral bone and overlying cartilage, usually of the femoral condyle, in young athletes; the fragment can become unstable and detach, forming a loose body that causes mechanical symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Episode of disabling knee pain two years earlier
Radiographs suggesting an ossified fragment in the suprapatellar region/possible femoral condylar defect
symptoms_not_in_common: Lesion most often becomes symptomatic in adolescence rather than at 22
Condylar donor site not clearly defined on plain films

data.description: Tear of the fibrocartilaginous meniscus, with a displaced fragment that blocks joint motion; common in athletes and may be chronic or degenerative on top of old injuries.
symptoms_in_common: Previous episode of severe knee pain
symptoms_not_in_common: No recent twisting injury
Ossified intra-articular body on radiograph is not explained by a meniscal tear
Meniscal tears are not visible on plain radiographs

data.diagnosis: Osteochondral fracture with loose fragment (e.g., after prior patellar dislocation)
data.description: Shear fracture of cartilage and subchondral bone from the patella or femoral condyle, often after transient patellar dislocation, leaving an osteochondral fragment free in the joint.
symptoms_in_common: Disabling knee pain episode two years ago (possible index injury)
symptoms_not_in_common: No recent trauma
No reported history of patellar dislocation or instability
No acute haemarthrosis described

data.description: Benign metaplastic proliferation of the synovium producing multiple cartilaginous nodules that may calcify or ossify and become loose bodies; the knee is the most common site.
symptoms_not_in_common: Typically presents in the 3rd to 5th decade
Usually multiple, uniformly sized loose bodies rather than a single fragment
History of repeated sports injuries points more to a traumatic/osteochondral cause

data.diagnosis: Pigmented villonodular synovitis (tenosynovial giant cell tumour)
data.description: Benign but locally aggressive proliferation of the synovium with haemosiderin deposition, most often affecting the knee of young adults and causing recurrent effusions.
symptoms_in_common: Possible mechanical symptoms such as locking (localised form)
symptoms_not_in_common: Does not calcify or produce ossified loose bodies
Usually causes recurrent haemorrhagic effusions, which are not described
Radiographs usually show soft-tissue swelling or erosions rather than a bony fragment

data.description: 67-year-old previously healthy male with a 4-month history of dry cough, wheezing, and mild dyspnea, worsening despite inhaled bronchodilators and corticosteroids. No smoking history and no significant past medical history.
