On examination, he required 1 L nasal cannula oxygen (SaO2 96%) and had decreased breath sounds with fine crackles in the right lower lung field; no JVP elevation, murmurs, gallop, or peripheral edema. Chest x-ray showed right-sided ground-glass opacities, and high-resolution CT showed ground-glass opacities with surrounding consolidation in the right lower lung field. Laboratory findings included marked eosinophilia, elevated CRP, and mild anemia.

data.diagnosis: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia, not otherwise specified
data.description: A clonal myeloid malignancy with persistent eosinophilia and possible eosinophil-mediated organ injury. The depicted dysplastic marrow cells and apparent chromosomal abnormalities strongly warrant investigation, but diagnosis requires formal marrow, cytogenetic, and molecular testing.
symptoms_in_common: Eosinophilic precursors and abnormal granulocyte morphology in the supplied marrow images
Apparent abnormal karyotype in the supplied image
Persistent cough, wheezing, and dyspnea compatible with pulmonary eosinophilic involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Isolated unilateral lower-lung involvement is less characteristic than more widespread pulmonary involvement

data.description: A clonal bone marrow disorder causing ineffective blood-cell production and cellular dysplasia; some cases feature prominent eosinophilia. The patient's age, anemia, marrow morphology, and apparent cytogenetic abnormalities support consideration.
symptoms_in_common: Megaloblastoid cells and irregular hypersegmented neutrophils depicted in the marrow images
Eosinophilia, which can occur in a subset of cases
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked eosinophilia with dominant respiratory symptoms is not a usual presentation
Wheezing and focal ground-glass opacities with consolidation are not direct hallmark manifestations

data.description: A syndrome of sustained hypereosinophilia associated with eosinophil-related organ damage. Pulmonary involvement can cause cough, wheezing, and infiltrates; a clonal underlying cause must be assessed in this case.
symptoms_in_common: Four months of persistent respiratory symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Marrow dysplasia and apparent chromosomal abnormalities argue against an idiopathic form
Unilateral focal pulmonary disease is less characteristic than multifocal involvement

data.description: An eosinophilic inflammatory lung disease causing respiratory symptoms over weeks to months, blood or lung eosinophilia, and pulmonary consolidation. It is a diagnosis of exclusion, particularly when clonal marrow abnormalities are suspected.
symptoms_in_common: Four-month history of dry cough and dyspnea
Fine crackles and supplemental oxygen requirement
symptoms_not_in_common: Unilateral right lower-lung disease rather than the more typical bilateral peripheral, often upper-lung opacities
Dysplastic marrow morphology and apparent cytogenetic abnormalities are not explained by this disease

data.description: An eosinophil-rich small-vessel vasculitis typically associated with asthma, sinonasal disease, and systemic organ involvement. Pulmonary eosinophilic infiltrates may precede overt vasculitis.
symptoms_not_in_common: No established history of asthma or sinonasal disease is reported
No neuropathy, skin lesions, or renal involvement is reported
Marrow dysplasia and apparent chromosomal abnormalities favor a clonal hematologic process rather than vasculitis

data.diagnosis: Myelodysplastic syndrome with eosinophilia and der(1;7)(q10;p10), with eosinophilic pulmonary infiltration
data.description: Clonal hematopoietic stem cell disorder with dysplastic hematopoiesis. The unbalanced translocation der(1;7) produces trisomy 1q and monosomy 7q; it may rarely present with marked eosinophilia and eosinophilic lung infiltrates.
symptoms_in_common: Dysplastic marrow/blood findings (irregular hypersegmented neutrophils, megaloblastoid change)
Left-shifted eosinophil precursors (eosinophilic myelocytes, metamyelocytes, bands)
Karyotype showing an extra derivative chromosome 1 and loss of one chromosome 7
Ground-glass opacities with consolidation consistent with eosinophilic lung infiltration
Cough and dyspnea refractory to inhaled therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: Respiratory symptoms as the presenting feature are unusual for MDS
Wheezing
Only mild cytopenia
No history of prior chemotherapy or toxin exposure

data.diagnosis: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia, not otherwise specified
data.description: Myeloproliferative neoplasm with clonal eosinophil proliferation, persistent eosinophilia and organ damage from eosinophil infiltration, defined by a clonal cytogenetic abnormality or increased blasts without PDGFRA/PDGFRB/FGFR1 rearrangements.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary infiltrates with cough and dyspnea
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent multilineage dysplasia (hypersegmented neutrophils, megaloblastoid erythroid cells) favors MDS
der(1;7) is more characteristic of MDS
No reported splenomegaly
No cardiac or skin involvement

data.description: Idiopathic eosinophilic infiltration of the alveoli and interstitium with subacute respiratory symptoms, typically peripheral consolidations, blood eosinophilia and rapid response to systemic steroids.
symptoms_in_common: Months-long dry cough, wheeze and dyspnea
No response to inhaled bronchodilators/inhaled steroids
symptoms_not_in_common: Unilateral lower-lobe disease (usually bilateral, peripheral, upper-zone predominant)
Dysplastic blood cells and immature eosinophil precursors
Clonal chromosomal abnormality
No prior asthma or atopy
Male sex (more common in women)
Anemia

data.description: Small-to-medium vessel necrotizing vasculitis with asthma, eosinophilia and eosinophil-rich granulomatous inflammation affecting the lungs, nerves, skin, heart and sinuses.
symptoms_not_in_common: No sinusitis or nasal polyps
No neuropathy, purpura, renal or cardiac involvement
Infiltrates fixed and unilateral rather than migratory
Dysplastic hematopoiesis and immature eosinophils
Clonal karyotype abnormality
Poor response to steroids-based inhaled therapy with no long-standing asthma history

data.diagnosis: Parasitic or fungal eosinophilic lung disease (e.g., strongyloidiasis, toxocariasis, allergic bronchopulmonary aspergillosis)
data.description: Reactive eosinophilia with pulmonary infiltrates caused by helminth larval migration or hypersensitivity to Aspergillus colonizing the airways.
symptoms_not_in_common: No travel, exposure or gastrointestinal/skin symptoms reported
No history of asthma or cystic fibrosis, and no central bronchiectasis or mucus plugging (against ABPA)
Persistent fixed unilateral infiltrate rather than fleeting
Dysplastic neutrophils and megaloblastoid cells
Clonal chromosomal abnormality
Anemia

data.description: A 19-year-old previously healthy gravida 3 para 2002 female presented at 28 weeks' gestation after emigrating to the U.S. at 25 weeks of gestation. During the 20th week of gestation, she experienced a maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, fever, and headache. She and her spouse had unprotected intercourse through the first and second trimester. The patient's initial fetal ultrasound with neurosonography revealed cerebral ventriculomegaly (20-25 mm) with dangling choroid, prominent 3rd ventricle, and a widened cavum septum pellucidum. Amniocentesis showed negative NAT for ZIKV with no evidence of chromosomal variations by CMA; TORCH panel was negative.

Prenatal Zika infection can disrupt fetal brain development and cause ventriculomegaly and other cerebral abnormalities, even without microcephaly. The maternal illness, residence in an endemic area, and positive maternal serum NAT results shown in the timeline strongly support this diagnosis; negative amniotic-fluid NAT does not exclude fetal infection.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, fever, and headache at 20 weeks
Residence in a Zika-endemic area during pregnancy
Possible sexual exposure through an affected spouse
Severe bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly measuring 20–25 mm
Abnormal cavum septum pellucidum and prominent third ventricle
Positive maternal serum Zika NAT results depicted in the timeline
symptoms_not_in_common: No microcephaly documented, although it is not required for congenital Zika infection
Negative amniotic-fluid Zika NAT, which is discordant but does not exclude infection

data.description: Transplacental cytomegalovirus infection can cause fetal brain injury, ventriculomegaly, cortical abnormalities, and periventricular calcifications. A negative TORCH panel lowers suspicion, although exclusion depends on the specific tests and their timing.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal fever and headache during pregnancy
Abnormal fetal cerebral development suggested by septal findings
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal conjunctivitis and maculopapular rash are less characteristic
Negative TORCH panel
Positive maternal Zika NAT results favor another infection

data.description: Fetal infection with Toxoplasma gondii can cause hydrocephalus, intracranial calcifications, and ocular disease. Maternal infection may be asymptomatic or produce a nonspecific febrile illness.
symptoms_in_common: Marked fetal ventricular enlargement compatible with hydrocephalus
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal maculopapular rash and conjunctivitis are not characteristic
Negative TORCH panel
Positive maternal Zika NAT results favor another infection

data.description: Narrowing or obstruction of the cerebral aqueduct impairs cerebrospinal-fluid flow, typically enlarging the lateral and third ventricles. It may occur sporadically or from genetic causes not detectable by chromosomal microarray.
symptoms_in_common: Dangling choroid plexus associated with marked ventricular enlargement
Normal chromosomal microarray does not exclude this condition
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal rash, conjunctivitis, fever, and headache are not explained by isolated aqueductal stenosis
Positive maternal Zika NAT results suggest an infectious explanation
Dysplastic cavum septum pellucidum may indicate broader developmental injury rather than isolated obstruction

data.description: Incomplete or abnormal development of the corpus callosum can accompany ventriculomegaly, altered ventricular configuration, and abnormalities of the cavum septum pellucidum. Targeted fetal MRI is needed to establish the callosal anatomy.
symptoms_in_common: Widened or dysplastic cavum septum pellucidum
Normal chromosomal microarray does not exclude an isolated or single-gene developmental abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal rash, conjunctivitis, fever, and headache are not explained by isolated callosal dysgenesis
Positive maternal Zika NAT results suggest an infectious cause
Severe diffuse ventricular enlargement is less specific than the characteristic ventricular configuration of callosal agenesis

data.diagnosis: Congenital Zika syndrome (maternal Zika virus infection with fetal brain injury)
data.description: Flavivirus infection transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes or sexually; maternal infection in pregnancy can cause fetal neural progenitor destruction leading to ventriculomegaly, cortical thinning, callosal/septal anomalies, calcifications and often (but not always) microcephaly.
symptoms_in_common: Maternal maculopapular rash, conjunctivitis, fever and headache at 20 weeks
Residence in endemic area during first and second trimester
Symptomatic partner and unprotected intercourse (possible sexual transmission)
Positive maternal serum NAT with prolonged viremia and positive urine NAT/IgM on timeline
Severe bilateral fetal ventriculomegaly with dangling choroid
Dysplastic/widened cavum septum pellucidum and prominent third ventricle
Negative TORCH panel and normal chromosomal microarray
symptoms_not_in_common: Amniotic fluid NAT negative for ZIKV
No microcephaly
Infection occurred in second trimester rather than the higher-risk first trimester

data.description: Most common congenital viral infection; can cause ventriculomegaly, periventricular calcifications, cortical malformations, microcephaly and growth restriction.
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative TORCH panel
Maternal conjunctivitis and maculopapular rash are uncommon in CMV
Partner with the same illness and endemic arbovirus exposure
Positive Zika NAT
No microcephaly or described periventricular calcifications

data.description: Transplacental Toxoplasma gondii infection causing hydrocephalus from aqueductal obstruction, intracranial calcifications and chorioretinitis.
symptoms_in_common: Marked fetal ventriculomegaly with prominent third ventricle
symptoms_not_in_common: Negative TORCH panel
Maternal rash and conjunctivitis are atypical
Symptomatic partner
Positive Zika NAT
No scattered parenchymal calcifications described

data.diagnosis: Congenital aqueductal stenosis (obstructive hydrocephalus, including X-linked L1CAM type)
data.description: Narrowing of the cerebral aqueduct causing dilatation of the lateral and third ventricles with severe ventriculomegaly and a dangling choroid; may be genetic, post-infectious or post-hemorrhagic.
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal rash, fever, conjunctivitis and headache
Positive maternal Zika testing
Widened/dysplastic cavum septum pellucidum (usually the septum is disrupted or absent in severe hydrocephalus)
Endemic exposure and symptomatic partner

data.diagnosis: Midline brain malformation (agenesis/dysgenesis of the corpus callosum or septo-optic dysplasia spectrum)
data.description: Developmental anomalies of midline structures producing abnormal cavum septum pellucidum, colpocephaly/ventriculomegaly and variable associated cortical anomalies.
symptoms_not_in_common: Maternal febrile rash illness with conjunctivitis
Positive Zika NAT and IgM
Normal chromosomal microarray (though it does not exclude this)
Ventriculomegaly more severe than typical colpocephaly
Thinned cortical mantle

data.description: A 58-year-old man presented with a 3-month history of abdominal pain, diarrhea, and weight loss. He also experienced urinary symptoms including frequency, urgency, and dysuria. Initial colonoscopy revealed prominent congestion and edema, loss of vascular pattern, and multiple moth-eaten ulcers with purulent exudates involving the entire colon. A repeat colonoscopy showed scattered irregular ulcers with with granular background mucosa and 'fuzzy' vasculature. The ileum appeared normal.

Chronic inflammatory bowel disease affecting the colonic mucosa, potentially throughout the entire colon. The diffuse inflammation and loss of vascular markings are compatible, but biopsy interpretation and exclusion of infection are required.
symptoms_in_common: Congestion and edema involving the entire colon
Loss of vascular pattern and granular mucosa
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency, urgency, and dysuria are not typical direct manifestations
Scattered irregular, moth-eaten ulcers are less characteristic than continuous superficial inflammation

data.diagnosis: Crohn disease limited to the colon
data.description: Chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can produce patchy ulceration and inflammation confined to the colon. Transmural disease may occasionally cause urinary complications through an intestinal-bladder fistula.
symptoms_in_common: Urinary symptoms could occur with a fistula or adjacent inflammation, although neither is established here
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse pancolonic congestion and loss of vascular pattern are more suggestive of ulcerative colitis
Granular background mucosa without reported deep linear ulcers or cobblestoning is less characteristic

data.description: Infection of the colon by Entamoeba histolytica, causing ulcerative inflammation that can mimic inflammatory bowel disease. Stool testing and examination of biopsies for trophozoites are needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Ulcers covered by inflammatory or purulent exudates
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency, urgency, and dysuria are not typical
Diffuse granular inflammation throughout the colon is less characteristic than discrete ulcers with relatively preserved intervening mucosa

data.description: Viral infection causing colonic inflammation and ulceration, most often in immunocompromised patients or those with underlying inflammatory bowel disease. Confirmation requires appropriate biopsy findings or viral testing.
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary frequency, urgency, and dysuria are not typical manifestations of isolated colitis
Diffuse granular mucosa with fuzzy vascular markings is nonspecific and less characteristic than discrete deep ulcers

data.description: A lymphoid malignancy involving the colon that can occasionally resemble inflammatory colitis. The dense cellular infiltrates in the supplied histology warrant specialist review, but unlabeled immunostains cannot establish lymphoma or its subtype.
symptoms_in_common: Dense mucosal cellular infiltrates in the supplied biopsy images
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse congestion, edema, and loss of vascular markings without a reported mass or nodular lesions are less typical
Urinary frequency, urgency, and dysuria would generally require additional urinary involvement or a separate condition

data.diagnosis: Indolent T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder of the gastrointestinal tract
data.description: A rare clonal, low-grade T-cell proliferation confined mainly to the mucosa of the GI tract, with a chronic relapsing course that mimics inflammatory bowel disease. Biopsies show a dense, non-destructive lamina propria infiltrate of small monotonous lymphocytes positive for T-cell markers, with a low proliferation index.
symptoms_in_common: granular mucosa with fuzzy or lost vascular pattern
dense small lymphoid infiltrate expanding the lamina propria with preserved crypts on histology
diffuse immunostain positivity consistent with a T-cell population
symptoms_not_in_common: urinary frequency, urgency and dysuria
purulent exudates on ulcers
normal ileum (small bowel is often involved)

data.description: A chronic idiopathic inflammatory bowel disease causing continuous mucosal inflammation extending proximally from the rectum, with a relapsing and remitting course.
symptoms_not_in_common: urinary frequency, urgency and dysuria
moth-eaten and scattered irregular ulcers rather than continuous disease
monotonous dense lymphoid infiltrate without prominent cryptitis or crypt abscesses
no rectal bleeding reported

data.description: A chronic transmural granulomatous inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the GI tract, typically with discontinuous lesions, and may be complicated by fistulae, including enterovesical fistulae.
symptoms_in_common: urinary symptoms (could reflect an enterovesical fistula or adjacent inflammation)
symptoms_not_in_common: normal ileum
diffuse involvement of the entire colon on first colonoscopy
no granulomas, strictures or cobblestoning described
monotonous lymphoid infiltrate on histology

data.diagnosis: Monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal T-cell lymphoma or other aggressive intestinal T-cell lymphoma
data.description: Aggressive primary intestinal T-cell lymphomas that cause ulcerating lesions, often with perforation or obstruction and rapid clinical decline. They show destructive infiltrates with epitheliotropism and a high proliferation index.
symptoms_in_common: dense lymphoid infiltrate with T-cell marker positivity
symptoms_not_in_common: urinary frequency, urgency and dysuria
relatively indolent 3-month course without perforation, obstruction or mass
small bland lymphocytes with preserved crypts rather than destructive infiltrate
normal ileum (small bowel usually affected)
diffuse superficial pancolonic involvement

data.diagnosis: Infectious colitis (intestinal tuberculosis, amoebic or cytomegalovirus colitis)
data.description: Infection of the colon by bacteria, parasites or viruses, producing ulcerating colitis with exudates. Tuberculosis in particular can involve both the bowel and the genitourinary tract.
symptoms_in_common: urinary frequency, urgency and dysuria (possible genitourinary tuberculosis)
symptoms_not_in_common: normal ileum (tuberculosis favours the ileocecal region)
no granulomas, trophozoites or viral inclusions on histology
monotonous lymphoid infiltrate with diffuse immunostain positivity
persistence on repeat colonoscopy
no fever reported

data.description: 7-year-old girl with no past medical history, presenting with intermittent abdominal pain for 1 month, unrelieved by anti-inflammatory treatment. CT showed peritoneal effusion and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy; ultrasound revealed multiple enlarged abdominal and retroperitoneal hypoechoic lymph nodes. Serum AFP was elevated at 1,210 ng/mL. At surgery, a 4 cm full-thickness jejunal mass was found with a gray-white cut surface. Histology showed an infiltrative tumor with microcystic, reticular, macrocystic, papillary, solid, and tubule-glandular patterns, marked nuclear pleomorphism, and abundant mitotic activity. Lymph nodes showed reactive hyperplasia.

A rare extragonadal malignant germ cell tumor with yolk sac differentiation. This is the leading possibility given the marked AFP elevation and varied reticular, microcystic, and glandular architecture; confirmation requires immunohistochemistry and exclusion of a primary tumor elsewhere.
symptoms_in_common: Microcystic, reticular, macrocystic, papillary, solid, and tubule-glandular histologic patterns
Marked nuclear pleomorphism and abundant mitotic activity
symptoms_not_in_common: A primary jejunal location is exceptionally rare
Enlarged lymph nodes showed reactive hyperplasia rather than tumor involvement

data.diagnosis: Mixed malignant germ cell tumor with a yolk sac component
data.description: A malignant tumor containing multiple germ cell tumor components. A yolk sac component can produce substantial AFP elevation, although distinct additional components must be demonstrated histologically.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal pain and an infiltrative abdominal mass
Marked nuclear pleomorphism and abundant mitotic activity
symptoms_not_in_common: No distinct second germ cell tumor component is described
Primary involvement of the jejunum is exceptionally unusual
Reactive lymph node hyperplasia does not establish metastatic spread

data.description: An aggressive malignant germ cell tumor that can display primitive pleomorphic cells in solid, glandular, and papillary arrangements. AFP elevation is more suggestive of an accompanying yolk sac component than pure embryonal carcinoma.
symptoms_in_common: Solid, papillary, and tubule-glandular histologic patterns
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent microcystic and reticular architecture favors yolk sac tumor
Marked AFP elevation is less characteristic of pure embryonal carcinoma
A primary jejunal tumor in a 7-year-old girl is highly unusual

data.diagnosis: AFP-producing jejunal adenocarcinoma with hepatoid or enteroblastic differentiation
data.description: A rare intestinal epithelial malignancy that may produce AFP and resemble hepatic or primitive fetal intestinal tissue. Histology and a defined immunohistochemical panel are needed to distinguish it from yolk sac tumor.
symptoms_in_common: Marked nuclear pleomorphism and abundant mitotic activity
symptoms_not_in_common: Intestinal adenocarcinoma is exceptionally rare at age 7
Extensive reticular and microcystic patterns favor yolk sac differentiation
Characteristic hepatocyte-like morphology or an associated conventional adenocarcinoma component is not described

data.description: An aggressive B-cell lymphoma that commonly presents in children with an abdominal or intestinal mass and rapid cellular proliferation. It is an important clinical differential but is poorly supported by the AFP level and described tumor architecture.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked AFP elevation is not characteristic
Reticular, microcystic, papillary, and tubule-glandular architecture is not typical of lymphoma
Marked nuclear pleomorphism is less typical than the relatively uniform cells of Burkitt lymphoma
Sampled enlarged lymph nodes showed reactive hyperplasia rather than lymphoma

diagnoses.name: Primary yolk sac tumor of intestine
diagnoses.title: Yolk sac tumour, unspecified site, female

data.diagnosis: Primary extragonadal yolk sac tumor of the jejunum
data.description: A malignant germ cell tumor arising outside the gonads, here in the small intestine. It typically secretes AFP and shows varied histologic patterns (microcystic, reticular, macrocystic, papillary, solid, glandular), with immunostaining usually positive for SALL4, AFP and glypican-3.
symptoms_in_common: 4 cm full-thickness jejunal mass with gray-white cut surface
Microcystic, reticular, macrocystic, papillary, solid and tubule-glandular patterns
Marked nuclear pleomorphism and abundant mitoses
FDG-avid focal abdominal lesion on PET/CT
Tumor positive for nuclear and cytoplasmic immunostains while adjacent mucosa is negative
symptoms_not_in_common: Intestinal primary site is extremely rare (most arise in gonads, sacrococcygeal region or mediastinum)
Enlarged lymph nodes showed only reactive hyperplasia rather than metastasis

data.diagnosis: Metastatic yolk sac tumor from an occult ovarian (gonadal) primary
data.description: Ovarian yolk sac tumor is a common malignant germ cell tumor in girls. It secretes AFP and can spread to the peritoneum, bowel serosa and retroperitoneal nodes.
symptoms_in_common: Histology typical of yolk sac tumor
symptoms_not_in_common: No ovarian or pelvic mass described on CT, ultrasound or at surgery
Solitary full-thickness jejunal mass suggests a primary intestinal lesion rather than serosal implant
Lymph nodes were reactive, not metastatic

data.diagnosis: AFP-producing adenocarcinoma of the small intestine (hepatoid/enteroblastic type)
data.description: A rare aggressive intestinal carcinoma with hepatoid or fetal gut-like differentiation that secretes AFP and forms glandular, papillary and solid structures.
symptoms_in_common: Nuclear pleomorphism and high mitotic activity
symptoms_not_in_common: Extremely unusual at age 7 (typically older adults)
Microcystic and reticular patterns favor yolk sac tumor
No predisposing condition such as polyposis or inflammatory bowel disease
No nodal or liver metastases despite usual early spread

data.diagnosis: Burkitt lymphoma of the small intestine
data.description: A highly aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma and the most common small bowel malignancy in children. It often presents with an abdominal mass, pain, intussusception, ascites and lymphadenopathy.
symptoms_in_common: Small bowel mass with gray-white cut surface
Abdominal and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated AFP
Microcystic, reticular, papillary and glandular architecture rather than diffuse sheets of lymphoid cells with starry-sky pattern
Jejunal site (ileocecal region is more typical)
Lymph nodes showed reactive hyperplasia only

data.diagnosis: Malignant mixed germ cell tumor / immature teratoma with yolk sac component
data.description: Germ cell tumors containing more than one element (e.g., yolk sac tumor, embryonal carcinoma, teratoma). They can arise extragonadally in children and raise AFP when a yolk sac component is present.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple histologic patterns including cystic, glandular and solid areas
symptoms_not_in_common: No teratomatous tissues (cartilage, neuroepithelium, skin elements) described
No embryonal carcinoma or other germ cell component reported
No calcification or fat on imaging
Jejunal wall location is highly unusual

data.description: 71-year-old woman with hematuria and bruising, with a long history of easy skin bruising that worsened at age 66. Past history included nephrolithiasis at age 41 and osteoporosis (T-score -2.6 at the left femoral neck). Physical examination showed bruising on the lower extremities. Serial testing at a tertiary center showed elevated late-night serum cortisol and abnormal Dex-CRH testing.

An ACTH-independent cause of Cushing syndrome involving small cortisol-producing nodules in both adrenal glands. The marked adrenal regions appear relatively small without an obvious large mass, which can fit micronodular disease, but the image alone cannot establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Longstanding easy bruising that has worsened
Abnormal Dex-CRH testing consistent with endogenous hypercortisolism
History of nephrolithiasis, potentially associated with cortisol-related hypercalciuria
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria is not a typical direct manifestation
Recognition at age 71 is less typical than presentation in younger patients

data.description: Bilateral adrenal nodules that produce cortisol independently of pituitary ACTH, often causing slowly progressive Cushing syndrome in older adults. Typical enlarged, macronodular adrenal glands are not clearly demonstrated in the supplied image.
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria is not a typical direct manifestation
Remote nephrolithiasis is nonspecific and does not establish this diagnosis

data.description: A benign adrenal tumor that autonomously secretes cortisol, producing ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome. Confirmation requires ACTH measurement and dedicated adrenal imaging; no definite dominant adrenal mass can be established from the supplied image.
symptoms_in_common: Nephrolithiasis can occur with cortisol-related hypercalciuria
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria is not a typical direct manifestation
A very long history of bruising is less characteristic of a newly developed solitary adenoma

data.description: A pituitary tumor that secretes ACTH and stimulates excess adrenal cortisol production. Cortisol results support consideration of Cushing syndrome but do not establish a pituitary source.
symptoms_in_common: History of nephrolithiasis, which may accompany hypercortisolism
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria is not a typical direct manifestation
New recognition in the eighth decade is less typical, although possible

data.description: ACTH secretion by a nonpituitary tumor, such as a pulmonary neuroendocrine tumor, causing endogenous Cushing syndrome. Indolent tumors can produce a prolonged course, but ACTH testing and tumor localization are needed.
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria is not a typical direct manifestation
The longstanding, slowly progressive bruising is less typical of aggressive ectopic ACTH-producing tumors
Remote nephrolithiasis is nonspecific

data.description: ACTH-dependent hypercortisolism from a pituitary corticotroph adenoma, causing bilateral adrenal hyperplasia/thickening, skin fragility, bone loss and kidney stones. May be mild or cyclic in older patients.
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset/diagnosis at 71 years is older than typical
No described central obesity, striae, proximal myopathy, hypertension or diabetes
Very long indolent course

data.diagnosis: Primary bilateral macronodular adrenal hyperplasia (ACTH-independent Cushing's syndrome)
data.description: Bilateral adrenal nodular enlargement with autonomous cortisol secretion, usually presenting in the 5th-7th decade with slowly progressive, often mild or subclinical hypercortisolism.
symptoms_not_in_common: Adrenals on CT appear only mildly thickened rather than markedly macronodular
Abnormal Dex-CRH test is more suggestive of ACTH-dependent disease
Hematuria not directly explained

data.diagnosis: Ectopic ACTH syndrome (e.g., occult neuroendocrine tumor)
data.description: ACTH secretion from a non-pituitary tumor (bronchial carcinoid, thymic, pancreatic NET) causing hypercortisolism and bilateral adrenal hyperplasia; indolent carcinoids can mimic Cushing's disease.
symptoms_not_in_common: Very long, mild course rather than rapid onset
No reported hypokalemia, severe weakness, hyperpigmentation or weight loss
No known primary tumor

data.diagnosis: Autonomous cortisol secretion from adrenal adenoma(s) (mild/subclinical Cushing's syndrome)
data.description: Benign adrenocortical adenoma producing low-grade cortisol excess, commonly found in older adults and associated with osteoporosis, skin fragility and metabolic complications.
symptoms_not_in_common: Findings are bilateral rather than a single discrete adenoma
Abnormal Dex-CRH test typically points toward ACTH-dependent disease
Nephrolithiasis and hematuria less characteristic

data.diagnosis: Primary hyperparathyroidism with non-neoplastic hypercortisolism (pseudo-Cushing state)
data.description: Parathyroid hormone excess causing hypercalcemia, kidney stones and bone loss; coexisting physiological HPA axis activation (age, illness, depression, alcohol) can produce mildly abnormal cortisol tests. Could also raise consideration of MEN1 if both endocrine disorders coexist.
symptoms_in_common: Mildly elevated late-night cortisol can occur in pseudo-Cushing states
symptoms_not_in_common: Easy bruising and skin fragility not explained by hyperparathyroidism
Abnormal Dex-CRH test argues for true Cushing's syndrome rather than pseudo-Cushing
Bilateral adrenal changes on CT
No calcium or PTH values reported

data.description: 26-year-old Chinese female with a 2-year history of progressive lower-limb weakness and scissoring gait beginning at age 24, followed by dysphagia and severe cognitive impairment (MMSE 16/30). Exam showed severe spasticity in the lower extremities, mild spasticity in the upper extremities, and left patellar clonus. Birth history and developmental milestones were normal. Genetic testing later showed compound heterozygous mutations consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

An autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder caused by biallelic SPG11 variants, producing progressive spastic paraplegia, cognitive decline, and often a thin corpus callosum. This is the strongest diagnosis because the supplied pedigree labels compound heterozygous SPG11 variants, and the MRI appears to show callosal thinning and periventricular white-matter abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive lower-limb weakness beginning in young adulthood
Severe lower-extremity spasticity with milder upper-extremity involvement
Normal early development followed by progressive neurological decline
Compound heterozygous variants consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance

data.description: An autosomal recessive disorder caused by biallelic ZFYVE26 variants that can closely resemble SPG11 disease, with progressive spastic paraplegia, cognitive impairment, and thinning of the corpus callosum.
symptoms_in_common: Young-adult onset of progressive lower-limb weakness
Apparent corpus callosum thinning on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No clearly discordant clinical symptom; however, the supplied SPG11 variant labels favor SPG11 rather than SPG15

data.description: An autosomal recessive lysosomal disorder, usually caused by ARSA deficiency, that damages central and peripheral myelin. Adult presentations may include cognitive decline, progressive spastic weakness, and white-matter abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Upper motor neuron signs including clonus
symptoms_not_in_common: Motor-predominant onset before cognitive symptoms is less characteristic of adult presentations
Marked lower-limb-predominant spasticity with apparent callosal thinning more strongly suggests complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia

data.description: An autosomal recessive CYP27A1-related disorder of bile-acid synthesis that causes cholestanol accumulation and potentially treatable progressive neurological dysfunction.
symptoms_not_in_common: A predominantly scissoring, spastic gait without reported cerebellar features is less characteristic of the usual mixed neurological presentation
The apparent thin-corpus-callosum MRI pattern is less characteristic than the cerebellar and dentate-region abnormalities often associated with this disorder

data.description: An autosomal recessive leukodystrophy caused by GALC deficiency. Late-onset disease can cause progressive corticospinal tract dysfunction, spastic paraparesis, and cerebral white-matter abnormalities.
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe cognitive impairment relatively early in the motor disease course is less typical of adult-onset presentations
Apparent corpus callosum thinning with frontal periventricular abnormalities is more suggestive of SPG11-related disease than the usual late-onset Krabbe imaging pattern

diagnoses.name: Complex hereditary spastic paraplegia
diagnoses.title: Autosomal recessive complex hereditary spastic paraplegia

data.diagnosis: Hereditary spastic paraplegia type 11 (SPG11) with thin corpus callosum
data.description: Autosomal recessive complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by biallelic SPG11 (spatacsin) mutations, characterized by progressive spastic paraparesis, cognitive decline, thin corpus callosum and periventricular white matter changes ('ears of the lynx' sign), often with bulbar involvement.
symptoms_in_common: Thin corpus callosum on sagittal MRI
Periventricular/frontal horn white matter hyperintensities (ears of the lynx)
Compound heterozygous SPG11 frameshift mutations (p.M245fs, p.F2343fs) with heterozygous carrier parents, autosomal recessive inheritance
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset at age 24 is somewhat later than the typical childhood/adolescent onset
No reported peripheral neuropathy or amyotrophy

data.description: Autosomal recessive complicated spastic paraplegia clinically and radiologically nearly indistinguishable from SPG11, with thin corpus callosum, cognitive decline, white matter changes and sometimes pigmentary retinopathy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Mutations identified in SPG11 rather than ZFYVE26
No pigmentary maculopathy/retinal changes reported
Onset later than the typical adolescent onset

data.diagnosis: Juvenile amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS5, SPG11-related) / juvenile primary lateral sclerosis
data.description: Slowly progressive young-onset motor neuron disease, autosomal recessive forms of which may be caused by SPG11 or ALS2 mutations, with upper motor neuron signs and bulbar dysfunction, with or without lower motor neuron signs.
symptoms_in_common: Clonus and upper motor neuron signs in upper and lower limbs
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe cognitive impairment
Thin corpus callosum
Periventricular white matter lesions
No lower motor neuron signs such as wasting or fasciculations reported

data.diagnosis: Adult-onset leukodystrophy (e.g., metachromatic leukodystrophy or Krabbe disease)
data.description: Autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorders causing demyelination; adult forms present with cognitive/psychiatric decline and progressive spastic gait with confluent white matter abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive spastic paraparesis in a young adult
symptoms_not_in_common: White matter changes are limited and focal rather than diffuse and confluent
Marked thinning of the corpus callosum is more typical of SPG11/SPG15
SPG11 mutations rather than ARSA/GALC mutations
No peripheral neuropathy reported

data.description: Immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the CNS that can present in young women with progressive spastic paraparesis, cognitive impairment and periventricular white matter lesions with callosal atrophy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Symmetric, ill-defined frontal horn lesions rather than ovoid, asymmetric plaques
Uniformly thin corpus callosum without focal lesions
Severe early dementia is unusual
No sensory, visual or sphincter symptoms reported
Biallelic pathogenic SPG11 mutations indicate a genetic cause

data.description: A previously healthy 58-year-old male presented with two weeks of lumbar pain and fever, accompanied by asthenia, anorexia, and recent weight loss of 3kg. He was a non-smoker with no drug abuse, recent travel, or animal contact history. On examination, he had a fever of 39.3°C with hemodynamic stability, bilateral painless swollen legs, and respiratory crackles on the right side. Laboratory tests showed hemoglobin 116 g/l, leukocyte count 33.3*109 cells/l, C-reactive protein 114.6mg/l, creatinine 56 μmol/l, elevated liver enzymes (AST 174 U/l, ALT 209 U/l, ALP 406 U/l, GGT 517 U/l), total bilirubin 76 μmol/l, conjugated bilirubin 66 μmol/l, and INR 1.38. Serology for hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV were negative. Urinary sediment was unremarkable.

A bacterial infection producing an abscess within the iliopsoas muscle. The apparent left iliopsoas enlargement and low-attenuation areas on the supplied CT raise this possibility, although full imaging review is needed.
symptoms_in_common: Marked leukocytosis and elevated C-reactive protein
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral painless leg swelling is not a usual primary manifestation
Right-sided respiratory crackles are not directly explained
Marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and cholestatic liver abnormalities are not typical, although severe infection can cause cholestasis

data.diagnosis: Pyogenic lumbar spondylodiscitis with secondary iliopsoas abscess
data.description: Bacterial infection of a lumbar intervertebral disc and adjacent vertebral bodies, potentially extending into the iliopsoas muscles. The lower lumbar disc-endplate region and adjacent soft tissues warrant dedicated MRI assessment.
symptoms_in_common: Marked leukocytosis and elevated C-reactive protein
Possible lower lumbar disc-endplate and adjacent iliopsoas abnormalities on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral painless leg edema is not typical without an additional vascular or systemic complication
Right-sided respiratory crackles are not a characteristic manifestation
Pronounced cholestatic liver abnormalities are not a usual direct feature

data.diagnosis: Secondary iliopsoas abscess from a perforated colonic process
data.description: Retroperitoneal spread of infection from bowel disease, such as perforated diverticulitis or an occult colonic tumor, can produce an iliopsoas abscess. A bowel source is not established by the supplied image.
symptoms_in_common: Lumbar pain associated with a possible retroperitoneal collection
Marked leukocytosis and elevated C-reactive protein
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral painless leg swelling is not typical of an uncomplicated colonic infection
Right-sided respiratory crackles are not directly explained
Marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia is not a characteristic primary manifestation

data.description: Infected thrombosis of the iliac veins or inferior vena cava, potentially associated with adjacent retroperitoneal infection. This could explain fever and bilateral leg edema, but venous thrombosis cannot be confirmed from the supplied CT slice.
symptoms_in_common: High fever and marked inflammatory response
Respiratory findings could reflect pulmonary complications, although crackles alone are nonspecific
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent iliopsoas collection would suggest an associated infectious source rather than isolated thrombophlebitis
Marked cholestatic liver abnormalities are not typical unless there is systemic infection or another complication
Weight loss and anorexia are nonspecific rather than characteristic features

data.description: Tuberculosis of the spine can extend into the iliopsoas compartment and produce a paraspinal or psoas abscess. It is an alternative to pyogenic infection, but the acute, intensely inflammatory presentation is less typical.
symptoms_in_common: Possible spinal and iliopsoas abnormalities on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: A two-week presentation with fever of 39.3°C is less typical than an indolent course
Leukocyte count of 33.3 × 10^9/L more strongly favors pyogenic infection
Bilateral painless leg edema is not a usual manifestation
Marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia and cholestatic liver abnormalities are not typical of isolated spinal tuberculosis

data.diagnosis: Pyogenic spondylodiscitis with psoas abscess and septic iliac/caval vein thrombophlebitis (likely Staphylococcus aureus bacteremia with septic pulmonary emboli)
data.description: Bacterial infection of the lumbosacral disc and adjacent vertebrae with contiguous spread to the psoas muscle; adjacent iliac veins/inferior vena cava may develop septic thrombosis, causing leg swelling and septic emboli to the lungs. Sepsis can cause cholestatic liver dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: CT: abnormal iliac vessel suggesting thrombosis
cholestatic liver tests and conjugated hyperbilirubinemia (sepsis-associated cholestasis)
symptoms_not_in_common: no obvious risk factors (previously healthy, no drug abuse, no known portal of entry)
degree of transaminase and ALP/GGT elevation is more marked than usual for sepsis alone
leg swelling is painless rather than painful

data.diagnosis: Infective endocarditis with metastatic septic foci
data.description: Infection of the cardiac valves producing sustained bacteremia with embolic and metastatic infections, commonly including spondylodiscitis, psoas abscess and pulmonary or systemic septic emboli.
symptoms_in_common: lumbar pain (spondylodiscitis is a frequent complication)
right-sided crackles (septic emboli or heart failure)
symptoms_not_in_common: no known valvular disease or intravenous drug use
no murmur or peripheral stigmata reported
unremarkable urinary sediment (no hematuria of embolic/immune glomerulonephritis)
hemodynamically stable
marked conjugated hyperbilirubinemia is unusual

data.diagnosis: Tuberculous spondylodiscitis (Pott disease) with psoas cold abscess
data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection of the spine, typically subacute/chronic, often with large paravertebral or psoas abscesses, constitutional symptoms and possible pulmonary or hepatic (granulomatous) involvement.
symptoms_not_in_common: short course of only two weeks
very high leukocytosis (33.3 x10^9/l)
high fever of 39.3°C (usually low grade)
no TB exposure, travel or immunosuppression
venous thrombosis and bilateral leg swelling are not typical
marked jaundice is unusual

data.diagnosis: Pyogenic liver abscess / ascending cholangitis with bacteremia and metastatic infection (e.g., Klebsiella pneumoniae invasive syndrome)
data.description: Hepatobiliary bacterial infection causing fever, cholestasis and bacteremia, which may seed distant sites such as the spine, psoas muscle and lungs.
symptoms_in_common: right-sided crackles (reactive effusion or metastatic pulmonary infection)
psoas abscess and spondylodiscitis as metastatic foci
symptoms_not_in_common: no right upper quadrant abdominal pain reported
lumbar pain as the leading symptom
no known diabetes or biliary disease
bilateral leg swelling and iliac vein abnormality not directly explained
no clear focal liver lesion evident on the provided image

data.diagnosis: Malignancy with retroperitoneal, vertebral and hepatic involvement (lymphoma or metastatic carcinoma) with venous thrombosis
data.description: Neoplastic infiltration of retroperitoneum/psoas, spine and liver can cause back pain, B symptoms, cholestasis and compression or paraneoplastic thrombosis of the iliac veins/inferior vena cava.
symptoms_in_common: bilateral painless leg swelling (venous compression or thrombosis)
cholestatic liver enzymes and jaundice (hepatic infiltration or biliary obstruction)
symptoms_not_in_common: acute two-week course
very high fever of 39.3°C
extreme leukocytosis (33.3 x10^9/l) more suggestive of infection
disc-centered lesion (tumors usually spare the disc)
hypodense fluid-like psoas collection favors abscess

data.description: 28-year-old male patient admitted on November 27, 2013, complaining of diarrhea (loose stool, three to five times per day) for over 10 years and hematochezia for about 1 month. Had been diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia 5 months after birth, with hemoglobin level remaining 70-80 g/L (normal range 110-150 g/L) for most of the time. On admission, albumin level was 26 g/L (normal range 35-52 g/L). Liver and renal function were otherwise normal. Patient reported recurrent arthralgia in the knee and ankle joints.
A rare inherited disorder causing chronic small-intestinal ulceration, gastrointestinal blood loss, and protein loss. It is a diagnostic consideration when severe anemia begins early in life.
symptoms_in_common: Severe, longstanding iron deficiency anemia beginning in infancy
Hypoalbuminemia consistent with intestinal protein loss
Apparent intestinal ulceration and narrowing in the supplied images
Arthralgia, which can accompany associated bone and joint manifestations
symptoms_not_in_common: Overt hematochezia is less characteristic than chronic occult gastrointestinal bleeding

data.description: A rare small-intestinal disorder characterized by recurrent superficial ulcers and multiple strictures, often causing chronic bleeding and anemia. Diagnosis requires exclusion of other causes of intestinal ulceration.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent ulceration and intestinal narrowing in the supplied images
symptoms_not_in_common: Anemia beginning at 5 months of age is unusually early
Recurrent knee and ankle arthralgia is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: A chronic inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any gastrointestinal segment and cause intestinal ulcers, strictures, bleeding, and extraintestinal joint inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent intestinal ulceration and narrowing in the supplied images
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe anemia beginning in infancy, long before the reported diarrhea, is atypical for conventional Crohn disease

data.description: An inflammatory disorder that can cause gastrointestinal ulcers, particularly in the ileocecal region, along with joint inflammation. Recurrent oral or genital ulcers and ocular disease are important supporting features but are not reported here.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent intestinal ulceration in the supplied images
symptoms_not_in_common: Iron deficiency anemia beginning in infancy is highly atypical
A decade-long course dominated by diarrhea and severe anemia is less characteristic than episodic inflammatory gastrointestinal disease

data.description: A systemic infection caused by Tropheryma whipplei that can produce intestinal malabsorption, chronic diarrhea, anemia, hypoalbuminemia, and recurrent arthralgia.
symptoms_not_in_common: Iron deficiency anemia beginning in infancy is inconsistent with the usual acquired adult presentation
Hematochezia is uncommon
Ulcerative intestinal narrowing is less typical than diffuse malabsorptive mucosal disease

data.diagnosis: Chronic enteropathy associated with SLCO2A1 gene (CEAS) / Chronic nonspecific multiple ulcers of the small intestine (CNSU)
data.description: Rare autosomal recessive enteropathy caused by SLCO2A1 mutations (prostaglandin transporter), producing multiple shallow circumferential or oblique small bowel ulcers and strictures with chronic occult blood loss and protein loss starting in childhood. It may overlap with primary hypertrophic osteoarthropathy.
symptoms_in_common: Iron deficiency anemia since infancy with persistently low hemoglobin (70-80 g/L)
Shallow small bowel ulcers on capsule endoscopy
Segmental small bowel wall thickening with dilated loops on CT
Arthralgia of knees and ankles (possible associated hypertrophic osteoarthropathy)
symptoms_not_in_common: Overt hematochezia (bleeding is usually occult)
Prominent chronic diarrhea is less typical
Possible gastric/colonic involvement (disease is usually confined to the ileum/small bowel)

data.description: Chronic transmural granulomatous inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract, with skip lesions, ulcers, strictures and extraintestinal manifestations such as arthritis.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic diarrhea for more than 10 years
Recurrent arthralgia of large joints (knee, ankle)
Segmental bowel wall thickening and strictures on CT
Ulcers and luminal narrowing on endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Anemia beginning at 5 months of age (very early onset is unusual)
Shallow ulcers with thin diaphragm-like strictures rather than deep longitudinal ulcers or cobblestoning
No fistula, abscess or perianal disease reported
No fever, abdominal pain or weight loss reported

data.description: Rare idiopathic disease (some cases linked to PLA2G4A mutations) characterised by multiple short superficial small bowel ulcers and fibrous strictures, with a chronic relapsing course of anemia, protein loss and obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Short concentric strictures with dilated bowel loops
symptoms_not_in_common: Onset in infancy (usually presents in adolescence or adulthood)
Chronic diarrhea (intermittent obstructive symptoms are more typical)
Overt hematochezia
No clear episodes of bowel obstruction reported

data.description: Small bowel mucosal injury from non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, causing erosions, ulcers and thin concentric diaphragm-like strictures, with occult bleeding and protein loss.
symptoms_in_common: Shallow ulcers and diaphragm-like concentric strictures
Arthralgia (a plausible reason for NSAID use)
symptoms_not_in_common: Anemia since 5 months of age, long before any plausible NSAID exposure
No NSAID use documented
Diarrhea lasting more than 10 years
Lifelong course

data.description: Systemic variable-vessel vasculitis with gastrointestinal involvement, typically causing deep, round or oval punched-out ulcers in the ileocecal region, along with oral/genital ulcers, skin and eye lesions and arthritis.
symptoms_not_in_common: No recurrent oral or genital ulcers reported
No skin or eye lesions reported
Anemia since infancy
Shallow ulcers with concentric strictures rather than deep punched-out ileocecal ulcers
Multiple strictures are uncommon

data.description: 54-year-old woman without comorbidities presented to emergency department with 12-hour history of redness and painful swelling in left gluteal region. Denied trauma. At admission: afebrile (36.2°C), normal blood pressure (109/65 mmHg), heart rate 89 bpm, mild peripheral oxygen desaturation (92% on room air) without respiratory distress. Rest of physical exam normal.
Bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue. The diffuse redness and apparent subcutaneous edema on ultrasound favor this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse erythema visible in the photographs
Fever may be absent in localized infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Oxygen saturation of 92% without respiratory distress is not explained by uncomplicated cellulitis

data.description: A rapidly progressive infection causing tissue destruction along fascial planes. This is an urgent exclusion in rapidly developing painful swelling; normal temperature and stable vital signs do not exclude early disease. The supplied images alone cannot establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Painful gluteal swelling developing over 12 hours
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported systemic toxicity, hypotension, or tachycardia
No reported pain out of proportion to examination
No visible bullae or skin necrosis
Isolated mild oxygen desaturation is nonspecific

data.description: A localized collection of pus in gluteal soft tissue, often accompanied by surrounding skin infection. A collection may be deep or not yet organized early in the course.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of fever does not exclude a localized abscess
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse rather than clearly focal swelling
No reported fluctuance or purulent drainage
No clearly defined fluid collection identifiable in the supplied ultrasound images
Mild oxygen desaturation is not typical

data.description: A superficial bacterial infection involving the upper dermis and lymphatic vessels, usually producing a tender, raised, sharply demarcated red plaque.
symptoms_in_common: Broad erythematous area visible in the photographs
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion does not appear clearly raised or sharply demarcated
Afebrile presentation is less characteristic, although possible
Mild oxygen desaturation is not typical

data.description: Bacterial infection of gluteal skeletal muscle, sometimes progressing to an intramuscular abscess. Deep imaging would be needed to distinguish it from a superficial infection.
symptoms_in_common: No trauma is required for the disease to occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Very short reported symptom duration
No reported deep muscle pain or limitation of hip movement
No fever or systemic illness
The supplied ultrasound images do not demonstrate a definite intramuscular abnormality
Mild oxygen desaturation is not typical

data.diagnosis: Necrotizing fasciitis (necrotizing soft tissue infection) of the gluteal region
data.description: Rapidly progressive, life-threatening bacterial infection of the subcutaneous tissue and fascia. Early skin findings can be mild, and fever may be absent. Ultrasound may show subcutaneous thickening, fluid along the fascia and hyperechoic foci of gas with dirty shadowing.
symptoms_in_common: Painful swelling and erythema of the left gluteal region
Violaceous/purpuric discoloration at the centre of the lesion
Ultrasound showing abnormal subcutaneous tissue with hyperechoic foci suggestive of gas and loss of normal architecture compared with the normal side
Mild hypoxemia (92% on room air) as a possible early sign of systemic involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Afebrile
Normal blood pressure and heart rate
No comorbidities such as diabetes or immunosuppression
No bullae, crepitus or frank skin necrosis described

data.description: Acute bacterial infection of the dermis and subcutaneous tissue, usually streptococcal or staphylococcal, causing a spreading, warm, tender area of erythema and swelling.
symptoms_in_common: Redness of the left gluteal region
Subcutaneous thickening and increased echogenicity on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: Hyperechoic foci suggestive of subcutaneous gas on ultrasound
Violaceous/purpuric central discoloration
Hypoxemia (92% on room air)
Afebrile
No evident portal of entry

data.description: Localized collection of pus in the perianal, ischiorectal or gluteal soft tissues, often arising from an anal gland infection or after an injection. It can extend into the buttock and may progress to necrotizing infection.
symptoms_in_common: Painful swelling and redness of the buttock close to the gluteal cleft
Gas-like echogenic foci possible with gas-forming organisms
symptoms_not_in_common: No discrete hypoechoic fluid collection seen on ultrasound
No fluctuance or purulent discharge described
Afebrile
Diffuse rather than localized erythema
Hypoxemia not explained

data.description: Fulminant infection of muscle by gas-forming Clostridium species. It can occur spontaneously (e.g., C. septicum) and causes severe pain, swelling, tissue gas and rapid systemic toxicity.
symptoms_in_common: Ultrasound findings suggestive of soft tissue gas
Mild hypoxemia possibly reflecting early systemic toxicity
symptoms_not_in_common: Afebrile
No tachycardia or hypotension
No crepitus, bullae or foul discharge described
No known malignancy, neutropenia or other predisposing condition

data.description: Bacterial infection of skeletal muscle, usually Staphylococcus aureus, often with intramuscular abscess formation. It presents with localized pain and swelling and sometimes overlying erythema.
symptoms_in_common: Painful swelling of the gluteal region
Stable vital signs in early stage
symptoms_not_in_common: Very acute onset (usually subacute over days to weeks)
Prominent skin changes with violaceous discoloration
Ultrasound changes mainly in subcutaneous tissue with gas-like foci rather than an intramuscular collection
Afebrile
Hypoxemia

data.description: 3.5-year-old male. Proteinuria, hematuria, and glycosuria were noted in the early neonatal period. He had a urinary tract infection at 12 months and bronchopneumonia at 3 years with elevated creatinine. Ongoing findings included persistent proteinuria, glycosuria, hematuria, reduced eGFR (30.56 ml/min/1.73 m²), elevated creatinine, uric acid, urea, cholesterol, and triglycerides. Renal ultrasound showed increased cortical echogenicity and decreased corticomedullary differentiation. Family history was unremarkable, and karyotype was normal (46,XY). Physical findings included dolichocephaly, craniosynostosis, frontal bossing, full cheeks, broad nasal bridge, long philtrum, low-set/protruding ears, narrow chest with pectus excavatum, short ribs, rhizomelic limb shortening, short humeri and fibulae, flattened epiphyses, brachydactyly, overlapping toes, joint laxity, fine sparse hair, small teeth, thin/short nails, and protuberant abdomen. Ophthalmologic findings included hyperopia, strabismus, and nystagmus. Motor development was normal.

A rare inherited ciliopathy combining craniosynostosis, skeletal abnormalities, ectodermal defects, and progressive kidney disease. This is the strongest overall fit, although genetic testing is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Frontal bossing, broad nasal bridge, and low-set ears
Narrow chest, short ribs, and rhizomelic limb shortening
Fine sparse hair, small teeth, and thin or short nails
Progressive kidney dysfunction with increased cortical echogenicity and reduced corticomedullary differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: Neonatal proteinuria, hematuria, and glycosuria are less typical than the later tubulointerstitial kidney disease usually described
Marked hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia are not defining features

data.description: An inherited skeletal ciliopathy characterized by a narrow thorax, short ribs, shortened limbs, and possible progressive renal, hepatic, or retinal disease.
symptoms_in_common: Bronchopneumonia in the setting of a small thorax
symptoms_not_in_common: Craniosynostosis and dolichocephaly are not characteristic
Sparse hair, small teeth, and abnormal nails are less typical

data.description: A skeletal ciliopathy featuring renal disease, cone-shaped phalangeal epiphyses, and retinal dystrophy, with variable thoracic and other skeletal abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal renal echogenicity and corticomedullary differentiation
Nystagmus, which can accompany retinal disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Craniosynostosis is not characteristic
Sparse hair, small teeth, and thin nails are not core features
Flattened epiphyses are less characteristic than cone-shaped phalangeal epiphyses
Hyperopia and strabismus do not establish the characteristic retinal dystrophy
Neonatal glycosuria and hematuria are not typical

data.description: A rare inherited disorder causing skeletal dysplasia, proteinuric kidney disease, and variable T-cell immunodeficiency.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent proteinuria and progressive renal failure
Elevated cholesterol and triglycerides, potentially accompanying substantial protein loss
Urinary tract infection and bronchopneumonia, which could occur with immune dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Craniosynostosis and dolichocephaly are not characteristic
Rhizomelic shortening is less typical than the characteristic short-trunk spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia
Glycosuria is not a defining renal feature
Sparse hair, small teeth, and thin nails are not characteristic
Hyperopia, strabismus, and nystagmus are not core manifestations

data.description: An X-linked disorder in boys characterized by ocular abnormalities, proximal renal tubular dysfunction, and neurologic involvement, with possible progressive kidney failure.
symptoms_in_common: Neonatal proteinuria and glycosuria suggesting proximal tubular dysfunction
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal motor development contrasts with the usual hypotonia and developmental delay
Hyperopia without reported congenital cataracts is not the classic ocular presentation
Craniosynostosis and dolichocephaly are not characteristic
Short ribs and congenital rhizomelic limb shortening are not typical
Sparse hair, small teeth, and thin nails are not defining features
Hematuria is not a hallmark

data.description: Autosomal recessive skeletal ciliopathy (IFT122, WDR35, IFT43, WDR19 and related genes) with sagittal craniosynostosis and dolichocephaly, ectodermal abnormalities, narrow thorax, rhizomelic limb shortening, brachydactyly, and progressive tubulointerstitial nephropathy (nephronophthisis) leading to early renal failure.
symptoms_in_common: chronic kidney disease with reduced eGFR and elevated creatinine
increased cortical echogenicity and decreased corticomedullary differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: neonatal onset of proteinuria, hematuria and glycosuria (renal disease usually presents later with polyuria)
prominent hematuria
hypercholesterolemia and hypertriglyceridemia
unremarkable family history (compatible with recessive inheritance but not supportive)

data.diagnosis: Jeune asphyxiating thoracic dystrophy (short-rib thoracic dysplasia)
data.description: Autosomal recessive skeletal ciliopathy with a narrow thorax and short ribs, short limbs, brachydactyly, and variable renal (nephronophthisis-like), hepatic and retinal involvement.
symptoms_in_common: chronic kidney disease with echogenic kidneys
symptoms_not_in_common: craniosynostosis and dolichocephaly
fine sparse hair
small teeth
thin/short nails
joint laxity
glycosuria
hematuria

craniosynostosis and dolichocephaly
rhizomelic rather than the typical acromesomelic shortening

strabismus and nystagmus
joint laxity

symptoms_in_common: early chronic kidney disease with reduced eGFR
increased renal echogenicity and loss of corticomedullary differentiation
nystagmus, strabismus and hyperopia (possible retinal dystrophy)
symptoms_not_in_common: fine sparse hair
small teeth

joint laxity

symptoms_in_common: chronic kidney disease with echogenic kidneys
full cheeks and protuberant abdomen (truncal adiposity)
symptoms_not_in_common: craniosynostosis and dolichocephaly
narrow chest with short ribs
rhizomelic limb shortening
fine sparse hair

normal development

data.description: A 31-year-old Caucasian man with multiple sclerosis who had received 24 natalizumab infusions and was switched to fingolimod due to persistent high anti-JCPyV antibody index (3.61). After 40 days of fingolimod treatment, he developed seizures and visual field defects. Neurological examination revealed lateral nystagmus to the left, homonymous hemianopia, distal tremor and spasm of the upper limbs. He presented with leukopenia (0.83 × 10^9/L) at hospital admission.

JC polyomavirus infection causing demyelination of the central nervous system in immunocompromised patients. This is overwhelmingly favored by prior natalizumab exposure, a high anti-JCPyV antibody index, and the reported CSF JCPyV DNA level of 1.62 × 10^6 IU/mL.
symptoms_in_common: Homonymous hemianopia and visual field defects
Seizures, which can occur with cortical or juxtacortical involvement
Marked leukopenia in the setting of immunomodulatory treatment
Mildly elevated CSF protein with few CSF cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Upper-limb spasms are nonspecific and may also reflect underlying multiple sclerosis
Leukopenia is a predisposing treatment-related finding rather than a direct manifestation of PML

data.description: An inflammatory worsening of JC virus-associated brain disease as immune surveillance recovers after withdrawal of immunosuppression. Recent natalizumab discontinuation makes this possible, although confirmation requires evidence of immune recovery and inflammatory brain lesions.
symptoms_in_common: CSF evidence of JC polyomavirus infection
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked leukopenia suggests ongoing immunosuppression rather than clearly established immune recovery
Minimal CSF cellular inflammation does not strongly support an inflammatory syndrome
No brain imaging evidence of enhancement, edema, or mass effect is provided

data.diagnosis: Rebound multiple sclerosis activity after natalizumab withdrawal
data.description: Renewed or unusually severe inflammatory demyelination after stopping natalizumab, potentially occurring during transition to another disease-modifying therapy.
symptoms_not_in_common: The very high CSF JCPyV DNA concentration is not explained by an MS relapse
Seizures are less typical than other manifestations of MS relapse
Marked leukopenia is not caused by MS inflammatory activity

data.description: A syndrome of vasogenic brain edema, often involving posterior cerebral regions, associated with endothelial dysfunction, hypertension, or certain medications. Fingolimod exposure makes it a less likely medication-associated alternative.
symptoms_not_in_common: High CSF JCPyV DNA concentration strongly favors JC virus disease instead
Nystagmus, distal tremor, and upper-limb spasms are not characteristic core features
Marked leukopenia is not a typical direct manifestation
No hypertension or characteristic posterior vasogenic edema is documented

data.description: A viral infection of the brain, usually affecting temporal and frontal regions, that can produce seizures and focal neurological deficits. Immunosuppression can lead to atypical presentations.
symptoms_in_common: Focal neurological deficits, including visual field loss
symptoms_not_in_common: High CSF JCPyV DNA concentration supports a different viral cause
Only 5 CSF cells/µL is less typical of classic HSV encephalitis, although possible in immunocompromised patients
No fever, headache, confusion, or behavioral change is reported
Nystagmus and upper-limb spasms are not characteristic presenting features

data.diagnosis: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML), natalizumab-associated (carry-over after switch to fingolimod)
data.description: Demyelinating opportunistic brain infection caused by JC polyomavirus reactivation in immunosuppressed patients, particularly after prolonged natalizumab therapy with a high anti-JCPyV antibody index.
symptoms_in_common: CSF JCPyV-DNA strongly positive (1.62 x 10^6 IU/mL)
tremor and motor signs of upper limbs
HIV negative with natalizumab as risk factor
symptoms_not_in_common: nystagmus is less common unless posterior fossa is involved
very high CSF protein (569 mg/L is mildly elevated; PML CSF is usually bland)

data.diagnosis: Multiple sclerosis relapse / rebound after natalizumab discontinuation
data.description: Return or rebound of inflammatory demyelinating disease activity, typically 2-6 months after stopping natalizumab.
symptoms_not_in_common: seizures are uncommon
homonymous hemianopia is unusual in MS
high JCPyV-DNA load in CSF
leukopenia not explained by relapse

data.description: Inflammatory worsening of PML lesions as immune surveillance recovers after natalizumab washout, causing paradoxical clinical deterioration.
symptoms_in_common: natalizumab stopped about 40 days or more before onset
symptoms_not_in_common: ongoing fingolimod-induced lymphopenia/leukopenia argues against immune reconstitution
low CD4/CD8 ratio
CSF cell count not elevated

data.description: Vasogenic oedema syndrome predominantly affecting parieto-occipital regions, reported rarely with fingolimod, presenting with seizures, visual disturbance and headache.
symptoms_not_in_common: CSF JCPyV-DNA positivity
no reported hypertension, headache or encephalopathy
nystagmus and limb tremor/spasm
leukopenia

data.diagnosis: Opportunistic viral encephalitis (herpes simplex / varicella-zoster) under fingolimod
data.description: Herpesvirus CNS infection, a recognised risk under fingolimod-induced lymphopenia, causing seizures and focal neurological deficits.
symptoms_not_in_common: no fever or altered consciousness reported
no CSF pleocytosis (5 cells/µl)
CSF positive for JCPyV rather than herpesviruses
homonymous hemianopia and nystagmus less typical

data.description: 8-month-old male with two prior admissions for bronchitis at 3 and 6 months of age, including one episode of severe neutropenia that resolved without treatment, born at term with no relevant family history. Presented with respiratory distress, fever, and fatigue. Examination showed no palpable lymph nodes or tonsillar tissue, bilateral lung crackles, and diminished breath sounds. Chest X-ray revealed bilateral infiltrates without pleural effusion, consistent with acute bilateral pneumonia.

BTK-related failure of B-cell maturation causes profound antibody deficiency and recurrent infections in male infants. This is strongly favored by the supplied BTK c.494G>A (p.C165Y) result and markedly reduced patient monocyte BTK expression; low-level maternal mosaicism explains the negative family history.
symptoms_in_common: Male infant with recurrent respiratory infections
Absent palpable lymph nodes and tonsillar tissue
Transient severe neutropenia, which can accompany presentation
Fever, fatigue, and respiratory distress from pneumonia
Bilateral crackles, diminished breath sounds, and bilateral pulmonary infiltrates

data.description: Defects in genes involved in early B-cell development can cause profound antibody deficiency resembling Bruton disease. This is a clinical alternative, but the supplied BTK mutation and expression findings favor X-linked agammaglobulinemia instead.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent respiratory infections beginning in infancy
Absent tonsillar tissue and nonpalpable lymph nodes
Acute bilateral pneumonia with fever and respiratory distress
symptoms_not_in_common: Transient severe neutropenia is less characteristic

data.description: Severe defects in T-cell immunity, often accompanied by B-cell dysfunction, cause life-threatening infections in infancy. Lymphocyte counts and subsets would help evaluate this alternative; the BTK findings favor an isolated B-cell maturation disorder.
symptoms_in_common: Absent or poorly developed lymphoid tissue
Pneumonia with bilateral infiltrates, respiratory distress, and fever
symptoms_not_in_common: An isolated episode of severe neutropenia that resolved spontaneously is not a characteristic defining feature

data.description: Defective CD40 ligand signaling prevents normal antibody class switching and impairs antimicrobial defenses, causing bacterial and opportunistic infections in young boys. The supplied BTK findings argue against this alternative.
symptoms_in_common: Male infant with recurrent respiratory infections
Pneumonia with fever, respiratory distress, and bilateral infiltrates
symptoms_not_in_common: Complete absence of tonsillar tissue and nonpalpable lymph nodes is less characteristic than in agammaglobulinemia

data.description: Delayed maturation of antibody production can cause recurrent respiratory infections in infants, generally with preserved B-cell numbers and later spontaneous normalization of immunoglobulins. The absent lymphoid tissue and supplied BTK findings make this substantially less likely.
symptoms_in_common: Pneumonia with fever, fatigue, and respiratory distress
symptoms_not_in_common: Absent tonsillar tissue and nonpalpable lymph nodes
Severe neutropenia
Repeated hospitalizations for significant respiratory infections are less typical of its usually milder course

data.description: X-linked primary immunodeficiency caused by BTK mutations that block B-cell maturation, leading to absent B cells, very low immunoglobulins, and recurrent bacterial sinopulmonary infections once maternal IgG wanes after about 6 months of age.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent respiratory infections starting at 3-6 months (two bronchitis admissions)
Acute bilateral pneumonia with fever and respiratory distress
No palpable lymph nodes or tonsillar tissue
Episode of severe neutropenia (reported in a minority of XLA patients)
Hemizygous BTK c.494G>A / p.C165Y mutation on sequencing
Absent BTK protein expression in patient monocytes on flow cytometry (overlaps isotype control)
Mother shown to be a low-level somatic mosaic carrier (2.3-5.4% mutant reads across tissues), explaining the negative family history
symptoms_not_in_common: No relevant family history (explained here by maternal mosaicism / near de novo mutation)
First infection at 3 months is slightly early, as maternal IgG usually still protects

data.diagnosis: Autosomal recessive agammaglobulinemia (e.g., mu heavy chain/IGHM, BLNK, CD79A deficiency)
data.description: Group of rare autosomal recessive defects in pre-B-cell receptor signalling that produce a clinical picture identical to XLA, with absent B cells and agammaglobulinemia.
symptoms_in_common: No palpable lymph nodes or tonsillar tissue
No family history (consistent with recessive inheritance)
symptoms_not_in_common: Identified pathogenic BTK mutation
Absent BTK protein expression in monocytes (BTK expression is normal in autosomal recessive forms)
Maternal mosaic carrier status for the BTK variant

data.description: Group of genetic disorders with profound T-cell deficiency, with or without B- and NK-cell deficiency, causing severe, opportunistic and recurrent infections in the first months of life.
symptoms_in_common: Male infant (X-linked SCID is the most common form)
Recurrent respiratory infections from 3 months of age
Absent lymphoid tissue (no lymph nodes or tonsils)
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported failure to thrive, chronic diarrhea, or persistent candidiasis
No opportunistic infections described
BTK mutation and absent BTK protein expression point to an isolated B-cell defect
Transient severe neutropenia is not typical (except in reticular dysgenesis)

data.description: X-linked combined immunodeficiency due to CD40LG mutations with defective class-switch recombination, giving low IgG/IgA with normal or high IgM, recurrent sinopulmonary and opportunistic infections, and frequent neutropenia.
symptoms_in_common: Recurrent respiratory infections in the first year of life
Bilateral pneumonia with bilateral infiltrates (can resemble Pneumocystis pneumonia)
Episode of severe neutropenia (common in this disorder)
symptoms_not_in_common: Absent lymph nodes and tonsillar tissue (lymphoid tissue is usually present or even enlarged)
BTK mutation with absent BTK protein expression
No relevant family history

data.diagnosis: Severe congenital neutropenia (e.g., ELANE- or HAX1-related)
data.description: Inherited bone marrow disorder with maturation arrest of myeloid precursors and persistently very low neutrophil counts, causing early, recurrent, severe bacterial infections.
symptoms_in_common: No family history (many cases are de novo)
symptoms_not_in_common: Neutropenia resolved spontaneously without treatment (it is persistent in congenital neutropenia)
Absent lymph nodes and tonsillar tissue
No skin abscesses, omphalitis, oral ulcers, or gingivitis reported
BTK mutation with absent BTK protein expression

data.description: 54-year-old female with hypertension and hyperlipidemia presented to cardiology clinic for follow-up 20 months since her most recent office visit. She was being evaluated for follow-up of cardiac risk factors and medication management. The patient was in her usual state of health and asymptomatic without changes in her exercise tolerance, weight, or energy levels. She did not have any gross hematuria or flank pain.
