A rare bacterial infection with a strong association with aortic valve endocarditis, sometimes following animal or fish exposure. The supplied pattern of low penicillin MIC and very high vancomycin MIC is suggestive, but organism identification is required.
symptoms_in_common: Two-month history of fever and malaise
Aortic diastolic murmur consistent with aortic regurgitation
Echocardiographic findings concerning for aortic valve disease

data.description: An uncommon infection of the heart valves caused by Lactobacillus species, often in patients with structural heart disease. Intrinsic vancomycin resistance and variable beta-lactam susceptibility can resemble the supplied susceptibility profile.
symptoms_in_common: Aortic diastolic murmur suggesting valve dysfunction
Possible aortic valve abnormality on echocardiography

data.description: A rare cause of bloodstream infection and endocarditis. Leuconostoc species are intrinsically resistant to vancomycin; the clinical syndrome is compatible, although microbiological confirmation is necessary.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent or intermittent fever over two months

data.description: A bacterial infection of the aortic valve that can produce a prolonged constitutional illness and aortic regurgitation. Enterococci are intrinsically resistant to cephalosporins, and some strains are vancomycin-resistant, making this a microbiological alternative.
symptoms_in_common: Echocardiographic concern for aortic valve pathology

data.diagnosis: Viridans group streptococcal aortic valve endocarditis
data.description: A common cause of subacute endocarditis in patients with abnormal heart valves. The clinical presentation fits, but the extremely high vancomycin and cephalosporin MICs are atypical and make this less likely than the preceding alternatives.
symptoms_in_common: Two-month course of fever and malaise
Possible aortic valve involvement on echocardiography

data.diagnosis: Subacute infective endocarditis of the aortic valve due to Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae
data.description: Zoonotic gram-positive bacillus infection that typically causes subacute endocarditis of the aortic valve in middle-aged men; the organism is intrinsically resistant to vancomycin and susceptible to penicillin.
symptoms_in_common: 2-month subacute course of fever, headache, myalgia, arthralgia and malaise
aortic valve diastolic murmur suggesting aortic regurgitation
regurgitant jet on color Doppler echocardiography
isolate with vancomycin MIC >256 and low penicillin, ampicillin and imipenem MICs
inflammatory infiltrate with granulation tissue on histology of resected tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: no reported animal, fish or meat exposure
no erysipeloid skin lesion described
cephalosporin MICs >256 are unusual, as Erysipelothrix is usually cephalosporin-susceptible
only low-grade fever (37.3°C) on admission

data.diagnosis: Infective endocarditis due to vancomycin-resistant Lactobacillus species
data.description: Rare endocarditis caused by gram-positive rods of the oral and gut flora, usually in patients with structural heart disease; many species are intrinsically vancomycin-resistant, with variable cephalosporin resistance and penicillin susceptibility.
symptoms_in_common: subacute fever, malaise, myalgia and arthralgia
aortic valve diastolic murmur with regurgitation on echocardiography
symptoms_not_in_common: no reported dental procedure, probiotic use or immunosuppression
headache is non-specific
meropenem MIC of 16 is not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Infective endocarditis due to Leuconostoc, Pediococcus or Weissella species
data.description: Rare opportunistic infections by intrinsically vancomycin-resistant gram-positive cocci or coccobacilli that can cause endocarditis and are usually susceptible to penicillin and ampicillin.
symptoms_in_common: aortic regurgitation murmur and echocardiographic valve involvement
high-level vancomycin resistance with penicillin and ampicillin susceptibility
symptoms_not_in_common: no immunosuppression, central venous catheter, prior vancomycin exposure or gastrointestinal disease reported
usually healthcare-associated rather than community-acquired
very rare cause of native valve endocarditis

data.description: Endocarditis caused by enterococci with acquired vancomycin resistance; enterococci are intrinsically resistant to cephalosporins and often cause subacute left-sided endocarditis in men.
symptoms_in_common: subacute fever, malaise and musculoskeletal symptoms
aortic valve involvement with diastolic murmur
symptoms_not_in_common: no healthcare exposure, urinary or gastrointestinal source reported
community-acquired vancomycin-resistant enterococcal infection in a 47-year-old is uncommon
typically affects older patients

data.diagnosis: Non-infectious aortitis or aortic valvulitis with aortic root dilatation (e.g., Takayasu or giant cell arteritis, syphilitic aortitis)
data.description: Inflammatory disease of the aortic wall causing aortic root dilatation and secondary aortic regurgitation, with systemic symptoms such as fever, malaise, myalgia and arthralgia.
symptoms_in_common: prolonged low-grade fever, malaise, myalgia, arthralgia and headache
aortic root measurement of 3.94 cm on echocardiography, upper normal to mildly dilated
chronic inflammatory infiltrate with neovascularization on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: a cultured organism with an antibiogram points to infection
no pulse deficits, limb claudication or blood pressure asymmetry reported
male sex and age are atypical for Takayasu arteritis and too young for giant cell arteritis
no history of syphilis reported

data.description: A male full-term neonate was admitted to the hospital 4 hours after birth for ecchymosis and petechiae. The infant was delivered by cesarean section at 40+5 weeks gestation due to failed induction, with birth weight 4000g and Apgar scores of 10. Physical examination revealed stable vital signs, weight 3850g, length 52cm, head circumference 35cm. The infant was alert and responsive with no special facial features. Skin examination showed large areas of ecchymosis on the chest, back, and upper limbs, with ecchymosis at the hepatitis B vaccine and vitamin K1 injection sites, and scattered pinpoint hemorrhages on the buttocks and lower limbs. The umbilical cord ligation site showed no bleeding, and cardiac, pulmonary, abdominal, and neurological examinations were normal.

data.description: 19-year-old woman with 3 weeks of right shoulder and right flank pain, followed 2 weeks later by exertional dyspnea and nonproductive cough that progressively worsened over an 8-day cruise to severe dyspnea with minimal walking and need for a wheelchair. On presentation she was ill-appearing with increased work of breathing, tachycardia (132 bpm), tachypnea (>40/min), and hypoxemia (88% on room air); a cardiac murmur was noted. She also had visible chest pulsations and labored breathing during sleep for 2 weeks. History included intermittent back pain for 6 months, asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection 2 months earlier, dental cleaning 5 weeks earlier, two episodes of diarrhea during the cruise, anxiety, and anemia. Labs showed microcytic anemia, leukocytosis, thrombocytosis, hypoalbuminemia, and markedly elevated inflammatory markers.

data.description: 15-year-old girl with 6 weeks of lower abdominal pain, initially midline then shifting to the right within 24 hours, sharp and crampy, worse with movement and relieved by lying down. At first evaluation she had mild bilateral lower abdominal tenderness (right greater than left), soft nondistended abdomen, normal bowel sounds, and no rebound or guarding; labs showed leukocytosis, anemia, and elevated C-reactive protein. She was discharged, then returned 6 weeks later with recurrent similar pain, missed school, and 2 weeks of increased waist size with difficulty fitting into pants. She denied fever, chills, night sweats, gastrointestinal or urinary symptoms, and vaginal bleeding/discharge. She had no significant medical history, took no medications, and had normal growth and development; menarche had not occurred. On exam, she had a firm, distended right lower abdomen with mild tenderness and Tanner stage 4 pubertal development. Repeat labs showed worsening leukocytosis, anemia, and higher C-reactive protein.

Following extubation from mechanical ventilation on day 6, the patient developed recurrent inspiratory dyspnea and stridor. data.description: 29-year-old woman with 7 weeks of progressive generalized pruritus, nausea, bloating, and watery mustard-colored diarrhea beginning after eating sushi. Three weeks later she developed jaundice, right upper quadrant discomfort, decreased appetite, and amber urine. Initial urgent care treatment with methylprednisolone, hydroxyzine, and diphenoxylate-atropine did not help. Prior labs showed elevated ALT 327 U/L, AST 104 U/L, total bilirubin 5.8 mg/dL, and CA 19-9 73 U/mL. Past history: anxiety and depression; no medications or drug allergies. On exam she was thin, jaundiced with scleral icterus and diffuse excoriations. Vital signs were stable.

A malignant pancreatic glandular tumor that can obstruct the distal bile duct. The images appear to show a pancreatic-head lesion with biliary and pancreatic duct dilation; the supplied histology shows irregular glands in fibrous stroma, concerning for adenocarcinoma.

data.description: 60-year-old man with 1 year of progressive exertional dyspnea, worse over the past 4 months, accompanied by persistent nonproductive cough. He also had a 5-day history of sore throat, orthopnea, and swelling of the neck and both arms, with facial flushing noted by family. He was transferred for evaluation of new dyspnea, cough, neck swelling, and a lung mass. At the outside hospital, he was afebrile with normal oxygen saturation; exam showed flushed face, swollen neck, and absent breath sounds in the right lung fields. Past history includes heavy tobacco use (2 packs/day for 40 years), occasional marijuana use, and regular alcohol intake. Family history notable for pancreatic cancer in his mother.

data.diagnosis: Squamous cell carcinoma of the lung with superior vena cava syndrome
data.description: A smoking-associated lung cancer that often arises centrally and can obstruct a main bronchus and compress or invade the superior vena cava. The images suggest a bulky right hilar/mediastinal tumor with airway and venous obstruction; tissue staining is needed to establish the subtype.

symptoms_not_in_common: Acute sore throat is nonspecific rather than a characteristic symptom

data.diagnosis: Small cell lung carcinoma with superior vena cava syndrome
data.description: An aggressive, strongly smoking-associated neuroendocrine cancer that commonly produces a central lung mass and bulky mediastinal disease. It frequently causes superior vena cava obstruction, although the supplied tissue images appear less typical of classic small cell morphology.
symptoms_in_common: Absent right-sided breath sounds from possible bronchial obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: A year-long progressive course is less typical of this rapidly growing cancer

data.diagnosis: Lung adenocarcinoma with mediastinal involvement and superior vena cava syndrome
data.description: A malignant gland-forming lung tumor that can spread to mediastinal lymph nodes and distant organs. symptoms_not_in_common: Acute sore throat is nonspecific

data.diagnosis: Large cell carcinoma of the lung with superior vena cava syndrome

symptoms_not_in_common: Acute sore throat is not characteristic

data.description: 27-year-old man with 3 days of progressive bilateral leg myalgias followed by acute inability to lift his legs, stand, or move in bed on the day of presentation, with associated arm weakness. For several months আগে, he had insomnia, loose stools, ~5 kg weight loss, and hand tremors. He had started an herbal stress supplement 4 days before presentation. On exam: conjunctival injection, fine hand tremor, hyperreflexia (3+ patellar reflexes), and proximal weakness (4/5 upper extremities, 3/5 lower extremities). Labs showed severe hypokalemia (1.8 mmol/L), mild transaminitis and cholestatic enzyme elevation, mild hyperbilirubinemia, elevated creatine kinase and aldolase, and venous blood gas pH 7.29.

data.diagnosis: Graves disease with thyrotoxic hypokalemic periodic paralysis
data.description: Autoimmune hyperthyroidism can cause an intracellular potassium shift producing sudden severe weakness, particularly in young men. The diffusely enlarged, hypervascular thyroid and areas of follicular epithelial hyperplasia on the supplied images support this possibility, although thyroid hormone and antibody testing are needed.
symptoms_in_common: Acute severe proximal weakness affecting the legs more than the arms
Months of weight loss, loose stools, insomnia, and fine hand tremor
Conjunctival injection, potentially associated with thyroid eye disease
Elevated muscle enzymes and abnormal liver tests
symptoms_not_in_common: Venous acidemia is not typical of uncomplicated thyrotoxic periodic paralysis
Progressive painful myalgias over three days are less typical than abrupt painless weakness
Prominent thyroid lymphoid aggregates suggest possible overlapping autoimmune thyroiditis

data.description: Autoimmune lymphocytic thyroiditis can produce a transient hyperthyroid phase through release of stored thyroid hormones. The prominent lymphocytic infiltrates and lymphoid follicles in the supplied histology support autoimmune thyroiditis; associated hypokalemic paralysis is uncommon.

Thyroid histology showing substantial lymphocytic infiltration and lymphoid aggregates
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked diffuse thyroid hypervascularity is more characteristic of Graves disease
Hypokalemic periodic paralysis is a rare manifestation of destructive thyroiditis
Conjunctival injection is not a characteristic manifestation of Hashimoto thyroiditis
Venous acidemia is not explained by uncomplicated hashitoxicosis

data.description: Some herbal supplements contain thyroid hormone, iodine, or ingredients capable of provoking thyroid dysfunction. A supplement could precipitate paralysis in someone with preexisting thyrotoxicosis, although its contents and thyroid studies would need investigation.

Severe hypokalemia with sudden generalized proximal weakness
Tremor, insomnia, loose stools, and weight loss consistent with excess thyroid hormone

Lymphoid thyroid infiltrates indicate an underlying autoimmune process rather than isolated supplement toxicity
Venous acidemia is not typical of uncomplicated supplement-induced thyrotoxicosis

data.description: An inherited skeletal-muscle ion-channel disorder causes episodic weakness associated with potassium shifting into cells. It can present in young adults but would not independently explain the evidence of thyroid disease.

Proximal weakness involving both legs and arms

data.diagnosis: Renal tubular acidosis causing hypokalemic paralysis

data.diagnosis: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis due to Graves' disease

Ultrasound shows a diffusely enlarged, heterogeneous, hypervascular thyroid; histology shows papillary hyperplasia with scalloped colloid and lymphoid aggregates.

months of insomnia, loose stools, weight loss, and hand tremor

recent herbal supplement as possible trigger

mild transaminitis, cholestatic enzyme elevation and hyperbilirubinemia

data.description: Autosomal dominant channelopathy (CACNA1S or SCN4A) causing episodic flaccid weakness with low serum potassium, usually beginning in adolescence, triggered by rest after exercise, carbohydrate meals, or stress.

data.description: Male infant, 22 hours old, admitted for repeated right-sided limb clonic seizures for 16 hours. Born at 40+6 weeks by cesarean section after fetal heart monitoring showed frequent variable decelerations; amniotic fluid was reduced and grade I turbid. Apgar scores were 10 at 1, 5, and 10 minutes; birth weight 3380 g. Seizures began 6 hours after birth, were right-sided limb clonic, without loss of consciousness or cyanosis, self-resolving, occurring 4 times. On admission, vital signs were stable. Physical examination showed an alert infant with normal skin color, flat anterior fontanelle, equal reactive pupils, coarse breath sounds without rales, normal heart exam, soft abdomen without masses, normal limb activity and muscle tone, and normal primitive reflexes.

data.diagnosis: Perinatal arterial ischemic stroke, likely involving the left middle cerebral artery territory

Seizure onset within the first day of life
Alertness and a normal neurological examination between seizures
Apparent focal diffusion restriction in the left lateral cerebral cortex

data.description: 33-year-old male with a 20-day history of cough and small amounts of yellow-white sputum after a cold. No hemoptysis, fever, chills, chest pain, or dyspnea initially. He received unspecified intravenous treatment at a local clinic without improvement. Seven days before admission, the cough worsened, especially at night causing sleep disturbance, sometimes with right-sided chest pain. Past history was unremarkable; he smoked about 10 cigarettes daily for over 10 years and did not drink alcohol. Physical exam: T 36.2℃, P 112/min, R 19/min, BP 126/85 mmHg; chest symmetric with normal expansion and vocal fremitus, clear percussion, coarse breath sounds bilaterally, and a small amount of wet rales in the right lung.

A fungal lung infection caused by Cryptococcus that can occur even in otherwise healthy adults. It may cause nodules, consolidation, and cavitation. The supplied tissue images suggest inflammation but cannot establish the organism without special stains and microbiologic testing.

Right lower lobe consolidation with multiple cavities on CT
Biopsy showing necrotic material with inflammatory cell infiltrate
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or night sweats reported
No hemoptysis
No weight loss reported
Lower lobe location less typical than upper lobe/apical segment
Short course

data.description: Suppurative bacterial infection (anaerobes, Staphylococcus aureus, Klebsiella) causing lung tissue necrosis and cavity formation, with neutrophil-rich exudate on histology.
symptoms_in_common: Cough with purulent yellow-white sputum after a cold
Right lower lobe consolidation with multiple cavities
Neutrophil-rich inflammatory exudate and necrosis on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or chills
Only small amount of sputum, not copious foul-smelling
No aspiration risk factors such as alcohol use
No improvement with intravenous treatment
No clear air-fluid level in a single thick-walled cavity

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary fungal infection (e.g., aspergillosis, cryptococcosis or mucormycosis)
data.description: Fungal infection of the lung producing consolidation, nodules and cavitation with necrosis; does not respond to antibacterial therapy and is diagnosed by histology/culture.
symptoms_in_common: Failure of empirical intravenous (likely antibiotic) therapy
Consolidation with multiple cavities on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No known immunosuppression, diabetes or structural lung disease
No hemoptysis
No fever
No obvious halo or air-crescent sign

data.description: ANCA-associated necrotizing granulomatous vasculitis affecting the respiratory tract and kidneys; lung involvement shows cavitating nodules or consolidations with necrosis and neutrophilic infiltrate.
symptoms_in_common: Necrosis with neutrophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: No sinusitis, nasal crusting or epistaxis
No hemoptysis
No renal involvement reported
Unilateral single-lobe disease rather than bilateral multiple nodules
No systemic features such as arthralgia or rash

data.diagnosis: Cavitating lung cancer (e.g., squamous cell carcinoma or invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma) with obstructive pneumonia
data.description: Primary lung malignancy that can present as non-resolving consolidation or cavitating mass, often in smokers, mimicking pneumonia.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent cough not improving with treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age (33 years)
Short history following a cold
No hemoptysis or weight loss
Biopsy shows inflammatory cells and necrosis rather than obvious malignant cells
Multiple small cavities within consolidation rather than a single thick-walled irregular cavity

data.description: 16-year-old girl with 4 weeks of intermittent severe sharp abdominal pain, worsening over 2 weeks from every few days to twice daily; episodes lasted minutes to 15 minutes, were worst in the epigastrium and upper quadrants, and sometimes woke her from sleep. Two weeks before admission she developed nausea and vomiting, with progressive decreased appetite, fatigue, dizziness, generalized weakness, constipation, and missed school. Pain was not related to menstruation, position, time, or food; ibuprofen worsened it, and vomiting briefly relieved it. Past history includes iron-deficiency anemia, anxiety disorder, and pica in early childhood; medications included iron, oral contraception, and famotidine. Exam at initial evaluation showed dry mucous membranes and diffuse abdominal tenderness with guarding in the epigastrium and upper quadrants. Initial labs showed leukocytosis, mild anemia, and thrombocytosis; urinalysis and abdominal/pelvic ultrasound were unremarkable.

data.diagnosis: Gastric trichobezoar with possible distal extension or a satellite intestinal bezoar
data.description: An accumulation of swallowed hair in the stomach that can cause mucosal injury and intermittent obstruction. The visible hair-containing gastric mass and extracted specimen strongly support this diagnosis. Rapunzel syndrome requires confirmation of a continuous extension into the small bowel.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent severe epigastric and upper-quadrant pain
Nausea and vomiting with temporary pain relief after vomiting
Hair-containing mass on endoscopy and a gastric intraluminal mass on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported hair ingestion or hair pulling, although these behaviors may be undisclosed
Leukocytosis and guarding are less typical of an uncomplicated bezoar and suggest associated inflammation or obstruction

data.diagnosis: Intermittent partial small-bowel obstruction from a migrated bezoar
data.description: A bezoar fragment can migrate into the small intestine and intermittently obstruct its lumen. The possible additional pelvic intraluminal mass on CT makes this a potential complication of the gastric trichobezoar.
symptoms_in_common: Brief recurrent episodes of severe abdominal pain
Possible distal intraluminal mass on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain predominantly localized to the epigastrium and upper quadrants
No reported abdominal distension
No reported complete inability to pass stool or gas
Iron-deficiency anemia is not directly explained by uncomplicated obstruction

data.diagnosis: Peptic ulcer disease or erosive gastritis
data.description: Inflammation or ulceration of the stomach or duodenum can cause epigastric pain, vomiting, and anemia. It could coexist with a bezoar through pressure injury or be aggravated by ibuprofen.
symptoms_in_common: Pain sometimes waking her from sleep
symptoms_not_in_common: Hair-containing intragastric mass is not explained by primary peptic disease
Possible distal bowel mass on CT
Constipation
Very brief, intermittent severe pain episodes
No consistent relationship between pain and food

data.description: An intragastric collection of indigestible plant fibers or mixed material can cause pain, vomiting, and impaired gastric emptying. This is an alternative bezoar composition, although the clearly visible hair strongly favors a trichobezoar.
symptoms_not_in_common: Visible strands of hair in the endoscopic mass and extracted specimen favor a trichobezoar rather than a pure phytobezoar
No reported gastric surgery or known gastric motility disorder
Iron-deficiency anemia is not typical unless mucosal injury is present

data.description: A rare inherited disorder of heme synthesis that can cause episodic severe abdominal pain, constipation, vomiting, and neurologic or psychiatric symptoms. It is a much weaker alternative because it does not explain the demonstrated hair-containing mass.
symptoms_in_common: Adolescent female taking oral contraception, a possible trigger in susceptible individuals
symptoms_not_in_common: Hair-containing gastric mass and possible distal bezoar
Prominent localized upper-abdominal tenderness with guarding
Iron-deficiency anemia and thrombocytosis
No reported dark urine, hyponatremia, tachycardia, hypertension, or objective neuropathy

data.description: A mass of ingested hair that accumulates in the stomach, sometimes with a tail extending into the small bowel, causing intermittent gastric outlet or small-bowel obstruction, mucosal irritation and nutritional deficiencies. It is typically seen in adolescent girls with anxiety, pica or hair-pulling behaviours.
symptoms_in_common: History of anxiety disorder and childhood pica
Intermittent severe epigastric and upper abdominal pain
Nausea and vomiting, with vomiting briefly relieving pain
Endoscopy showing a hair-ball mass in the stomach
CT showing a mottled intragastric mass with trapped air, with a second finding in the distal bowel that may be a separate fragment or tail
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported hair pulling, alopecia or hair eating in the history
No palpable epigastric mass noted
Pain worsened by ibuprofen is not specifically explained by a bezoar

data.diagnosis: Peptic ulcer disease / NSAID- or H. pylori-associated gastritis
data.description: Mucosal inflammation or ulceration of the stomach or duodenum caused by acid, H. pylori infection or NSAIDs, producing epigastric pain, nausea and sometimes bleeding with anemia.
symptoms_in_common: Nocturnal pain waking her from sleep
Already on famotidine, suggesting suspected acid-related disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain unrelated to food
Brief sharp episodes of minutes rather than sustained burning pain
Constipation
Leukocytosis and thrombocytosis
Intragastric hair mass on endoscopy and CT is not explained
No hematemesis or melena reported

data.diagnosis: Intermittent small-bowel obstruction (e.g., intussusception or bezoar fragment)
data.description: Partial or intermittent mechanical blockage of the small intestine causing colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, constipation and dehydration. In adolescents it usually has a lead point such as a bezoar fragment, polyp or Meckel diverticulum.
symptoms_in_common: Intermittent, severe, colicky pain lasting minutes
Nausea and vomiting with temporary relief after vomiting
Possible distal bowel finding on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Pain localized to epigastrium and upper quadrants rather than diffuse or periumbilical
No marked abdominal distension described
Four-week course is long for an unrelieved obstruction
Unremarkable ultrasound
Does not by itself explain the gastric mass

data.description: Chronic transmural inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract, often presenting in adolescents with abdominal pain, weight loss, fatigue, anemia and raised inflammatory markers.
symptoms_in_common: Several weeks of recurrent abdominal pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Constipation rather than diarrhea
No bloody stools, fever, perianal disease or growth failure reported
Pain predominantly epigastric rather than right lower quadrant
Very brief pain episodes
Endoscopy and CT show an intragastric foreign mass rather than bowel wall inflammation

data.description: Gallstones intermittently obstructing the cystic duct, causing episodic epigastric or right upper quadrant pain with nausea and vomiting. Risk is increased in females and with estrogen-containing contraceptives.
symptoms_in_common: Episodic severe epigastric and upper quadrant pain
symptoms_not_in_common: Episodes last only minutes (biliary colic usually lasts 30 minutes to hours)
No relation to food, especially fatty meals
Normal abdominal ultrasound with no gallstones
Constipation
Anemia and thrombocytosis
Pain worsened by ibuprofen
Intragastric hair mass on imaging and endoscopy

data.description: A 69-year-old male patient presented with lower abdominal pain. Physical examination revealed a flat abdomen without varicose veins, soft abdomen, with a palpable 3 cm×4 cm hard mass in the left lower abdomen, positive lower abdominal tenderness without rebound tenderness. Bowel sounds were normal at 4 times per minute. The patient had a history of cataracts for over one year, denied history of coronary heart disease, diabetes, hypertension, hepatitis, tuberculosis, or other acute or chronic infectious diseases. He denied food or drug allergies, trauma, blood transfusion history, or other surgical history.

A rare malignancy arising from the urachal remnant above the bladder dome. The apparent supravesical mass with calcification and mucin-associated glandular tissue makes this a leading possibility, but its origin requires confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: CT appearance of a mass near the bladder dome with apparent calcification
Histology appearing to show epithelial clusters in mucin and gland-forming tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Left-sided palpable mass rather than the more typical midline location
Cataracts are unrelated to this disease

data.diagnosis: Primary adenocarcinoma of the urinary bladder
data.description: An uncommon bladder cancer with glandular differentiation, sometimes producing abundant mucin. Distinguishing it from urachal cancer or secondary gastrointestinal involvement requires anatomical assessment and pathology review.
symptoms_in_common: Glandular and possibly mucinous features in the supplied histology
symptoms_not_in_common: An apparently predominantly supravesical mass is less typical than a bladder-wall-centered lesion
Cataracts are unrelated to this disease

data.diagnosis: Sigmoid colorectal adenocarcinoma with bladder involvement
data.description: A gland-forming cancer of the sigmoid colon that can invade adjacent pelvic structures, including the bladder. A mucinous subtype could account for the mucin-rich microscopic appearance.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable hard left lower abdominal mass
Pelvic mass close to bowel and bladder
symptoms_not_in_common: An apparently bladder-dome-centered calcified lesion is less typical of a primary sigmoid tumor
Cataracts are unrelated to this disease

data.diagnosis: Appendiceal mucinous neoplasm with pelvic spread
data.description: A mucin-producing appendiceal tumor that may spread mucin and tumor cells into the peritoneum, sometimes forming pelvic deposits or causing pseudomyxoma peritonei.
symptoms_in_common: Possible mucin pools containing epithelial clusters in the supplied histology
Possible calcification within a mucinous pelvic lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: A solitary apparent bladder-dome mass is less typical than an appendiceal lesion or distributed peritoneal disease
Flat, nondistended abdomen is less typical of advanced pseudomyxoma peritonei
Cataracts are unrelated to this disease

data.diagnosis: Infected urachal cyst with inflammatory mass
data.description: Infection of a persistent urachal cyst can produce a tender mass above the bladder and resemble a tumor on imaging. The apparent glandular and mucinous pathology makes this less likely than malignancy.
symptoms_not_in_common: Left-sided hard mass rather than a typical midline inflammatory swelling
Apparent mucin-associated epithelial clusters and complex glands are not typical of a simple infected cyst
Cataracts are unrelated to this disease

diagnoses.name: Bladder invasion
diagnoses.title: Mucinous cystic neoplasm with associated invasive carcinoma of other or unspecified parts of biliary tract[Gallbladder]

data.diagnosis: Sigmoid colon adenocarcinoma invading the urinary bladder (possible colovesical fistula)
data.description: Malignant glandular tumor of the sigmoid colon that can directly invade the bladder dome; malignant columnar cells may be shed into urine, and histology shows intestinal-type glands, typically CK20/CDX2 positive and CK7 negative.
symptoms_in_common: Hard 3x4 cm palpable mass in left lower abdomen
CT showing a gas-containing mass between bowel and bladder with protrusion into the bladder wall
Urine cytology with atypical columnar cell clusters
Histology showing adenocarcinoma with intestinal-type glands and strong immunostaining
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported change in bowel habits, hematochezia or weight loss
No reported pneumaturia or fecaluria
Normal bowel sounds without obstruction

data.description: Rare adenocarcinoma arising from urachal remnants at the bladder dome, often enteric-type, frequently with calcifications and extravesical growth.
symptoms_in_common: Mass at the bladder dome with small calcification on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Mass is in the left lower abdomen rather than midline/supravesical toward the umbilicus
Gas within the mass suggests bowel communication
No reported hematuria or mucusuria

data.diagnosis: Primary adenocarcinoma of the urinary bladder
data.description: Uncommon primary bladder malignancy with glandular differentiation, histologically similar to colorectal adenocarcinoma; diagnosed after excluding secondary spread.
symptoms_in_common: Mass projecting into the bladder on CT
Glandular malignant cells on cytology and adenocarcinoma on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: Bulk of the mass appears extravesical and bowel-centered with gas
Palpable left lower quadrant mass
No reported hematuria or irritative voiding symptoms
No history of exstrophy or chronic bladder irritation

data.diagnosis: Urothelial carcinoma of the bladder with glandular differentiation
data.description: Most common bladder cancer; may show glandular differentiation and invade through the wall into adjacent structures.
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology shows pure gland-forming adenocarcinoma rather than urothelial morphology
Gas-containing mass centered on bowel
No reported gross hematuria
Palpable left lower abdominal hard mass is unusual

data.diagnosis: Complicated sigmoid diverticulitis with inflammatory mass and colovesical fistula
data.description: Inflammation or perforation of sigmoid diverticula forming a phlegmon or abscess that can adhere to and fistulize into the bladder; the most common benign cause of colovesical fistula.
symptoms_in_common: Left lower abdominal pain and tenderness
Gas-containing mass adjacent to the bladder on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Hard mass without reported fever or leukocytosis
No rebound tenderness
Malignant glandular cells on cytology
Histology confirming adenocarcinoma

data.description: 39-year-old man with 4 days of fever with shaking chills, diffuse headache, fatigue, lower back pain, weakness, anorexia, decreased urine output with dark urine, and blurry vision during fever episodes after returning from a 2-week trip to East Africa (Tanzania). During the trip he had mosquito bites and later developed nausea, vomiting, and nonbloody diarrhea. Past history: degenerative knee disease with prior glucocorticoid injections. On examination: temperature 38.9°C, facial flushing, mild scleral icterus, and dark brown urine. Initial labs showed thrombocytopenia, elevated creatinine, elevated AST/ALT, hyperbilirubinemia, and low haptoglobin.

data.diagnosis: Severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria with hemoglobinuria and acute kidney injury
data.description: A mosquito-transmitted parasitic infection that can cause extensive red-cell destruction and multiorgan injury. This is the leading diagnosis: the supplied rapid test appears positive for falciparum antigen, and the blood smear shows numerous delicate intraerythrocytic ring forms. Suspected severe malaria requires emergency treatment.
symptoms_in_common: Fever with shaking chills after travel to Tanzania and mosquito exposure
Diffuse headache, fatigue, weakness, and anorexia
Dark brown urine and low haptoglobin consistent with intravascular hemolysis
Decreased urine output and elevated creatinine
Scleral icterus, hyperbilirubinemia, and elevated AST/ALT
symptoms_not_in_common: Facial flushing is nonspecific rather than a characteristic finding
Blurry vision confined to fever episodes is not a classic diagnostic feature

data.description: A bacterial infection acquired through water or soil contaminated by animal urine; severe disease can produce jaundice, acute kidney injury, and thrombocytopenia. It is a clinical alternative, but does not explain the apparent malaria-positive test and intraerythrocytic parasites.
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked intravascular hemolysis with low haptoglobin and dark brown urine is less typical
Blurry vision restricted to fever episodes is not characteristic

data.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection that can cause fever, thrombocytopenia, hepatitis, and occasionally acute kidney injury. The hemolytic findings and supplied malaria testing strongly favor malaria instead.
symptoms_not_in_common: Low haptoglobin suggesting substantial intravascular hemolysis
Dark brown urine consistent with hemoglobinuria
Jaundice and pronounced oliguric kidney injury are less typical unless disease is severe
Blurry vision during fever episodes is not characteristic

data.description: An intraerythrocytic protozoal infection, usually transmitted by ticks, that can cause hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, and renal injury. It can resemble malaria on a blood smear, but Tanzania travel, mosquito exposure, and the apparent falciparum-positive rapid test make it substantially less likely.
symptoms_in_common: Low haptoglobin and dark urine from hemolysis
Elevated creatinine and decreased urine output
symptoms_not_in_common: Facial flushing is not characteristic
Nonbloody diarrhea is less characteristic
Blurry vision during fever episodes is not typical

data.description: A thrombotic microangiopathy characterized by red-cell fragmentation, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury, sometimes following diarrheal illness. The supplied smear instead appears to show malaria parasites, making this a less likely alternative.
symptoms_in_common: Decreased urine output and elevated creatinine
symptoms_not_in_common: High fever with prominent shaking chills is less characteristic
Lower back pain and facial flushing are not typical
Elevated AST/ALT and scleral icterus are not defining features

data.description: Mosquito-borne protozoal infection of red blood cells causing cyclical fever, hemolysis, and in severe cases multi-organ dysfunction (acute kidney injury, jaundice, hyperparasitemia, blackwater fever). The rapid antigen test shows control, T1 and T2 lines (P. falciparum or mixed infection), and the blood smear shows a high density of intraerythrocytic ring forms, including double chromatin dot and appliqué forms and a pigment-containing trophozoite.
symptoms_in_common: travel to East Africa with mosquito bites
dark brown urine and decreased urine output
positive rapid antigen test for P. falciparum
numerous ring-form parasites on blood smear
clear chest radiograph and no focal liver lesion on ultrasound, consistent with a non-focal systemic infection
symptoms_not_in_common: blurry vision during fever episodes is uncommon, though it can occur with malarial retinopathy or severe illness
facial flushing is nonspecific

data.description: Spirochetal zoonosis acquired from fresh water or soil contaminated with animal urine; the severe form causes jaundice, acute kidney injury, and bleeding tendency.
symptoms_in_common: lower back pain and myalgia-like weakness
decreased urine output with elevated creatinine
symptoms_not_in_common: low haptoglobin (hemolysis is not prominent)
positive malaria rapid antigen test
intraerythrocytic parasites on smear
no reported freshwater or animal exposure
no conjunctival suffusion described

data.description: Aedes mosquito-borne flavivirus infection causing acute fever, severe headache, myalgia and back pain, thrombocytopenia, and transaminitis; severe forms cause plasma leakage and hemorrhage.
symptoms_in_common: mosquito bites during travel to an endemic region
symptoms_not_in_common: hemolysis with low haptoglobin
scleral icterus and hyperbilirubinemia
dark brown urine
acute kidney injury is uncommon
positive malaria antigen test and parasites on smear
no rash or retro-orbital pain reported

data.description: Systemic infection with Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi or Paratyphi acquired from contaminated food or water, causing sustained fever, headache, abdominal symptoms, and mild hepatitis.
symptoms_not_in_common: shaking chills with paroxysmal fever
hemolysis with low haptoglobin
dark brown urine
acute kidney injury
scleral icterus is uncommon
positive malaria antigen test and parasites on smear

data.description: Mosquito-borne flavivirus hemorrhagic fever endemic to sub-Saharan Africa, causing fever, back pain, and headache, with a toxic phase of jaundice, renal failure, and bleeding in severe cases.
symptoms_in_common: acute kidney injury with decreased urine output
symptoms_not_in_common: low haptoglobin (hemolysis is not typical)
positive malaria antigen test and parasites on smear
no hemorrhagic manifestations
transaminases are usually markedly elevated
travelers are usually vaccinated (status not stated)

data.description: Newborn girl admitted to the NICU after cardiorespiratory arrest at delivery. Pregnancy was complicated by maternal hepatitis C infection, treated urogenital Chlamydia trachomatis infection, gestational hypertension, and prenatal right urinary tract dilatation on ultrasound. At 40 weeks’ gestation, after prolonged labor and cesarean delivery for nonreassuring fetal status with meconium-stained fluid, she was born in breech position with limp tone and no respiratory effort. She required 16 minutes of resuscitation, including intubation, CPR, epinephrine, and saline boluses, before spontaneous circulation returned. Apgar scores were 1, 0, 0, 1, and 3 at 1, 5, 10, 15, and 20 minutes. On NICU arrival, she was hypothermic (34.9°C) with heart rate 141 bpm, blood pressure 84/59 mm Hg, and oxygen saturation 97% on mechanical ventilation; therapeutic hypothermia was started.

A congenital region of abnormal lung tissue supplied by a systemic artery rather than the pulmonary circulation. The apparent artery arising from the descending aorta and supplying the left basal lung strongly suggests sequestration, possibly with a coexisting congenital pulmonary airway malformation.
symptoms_in_common: Left basal lung abnormality on chest imaging
Apparent systemic arterial supply from the descending aorta on Doppler ultrasound and CT
Severe neonatal respiratory compromise requiring mechanical ventilation
symptoms_not_in_common: Profound cardiorespiratory arrest at delivery is not typical of a small isolated sequestration
Bilateral pleural air collections are not a usual primary feature
Prenatal right urinary tract dilatation is not directly explained

data.description: A developmental malformation producing abnormal cystic or solid lung tissue that can cause neonatal respiratory distress. Cystic changes at the left lung base could represent this condition; systemic arterial supply would favor a hybrid lesion with sequestration.
symptoms_in_common: Cystic-appearing abnormalities at the left lung base on CT
Requirement for intubation and mechanical ventilation
symptoms_not_in_common: An artery arising from the descending aorta is not typical of an isolated pulmonary airway malformation
Profound birth depression and prolonged cardiac arrest are not specific to this condition
Prenatal right urinary tract dilatation is not directly explained

data.description: Air in the pleural space, often related to positive-pressure ventilation or underlying lung disease. The radiographs suggest bilateral pneumothoraces, with a larger left-sided collection and possible pressure-related mediastinal displacement.
symptoms_in_common: Peripheral pleural lucencies and apparent pleural lines on chest radiographs
Prominent left-sided hyperlucency with apparent mediastinal displacement
Exposure to prolonged resuscitation and mechanical ventilation
symptoms_not_in_common: Systemic arterial supply to a left basal lung lesion is not explained
Persistent cystic abnormalities within the left basal lung are not explained by pleural air alone
Absent respiratory effort before resuscitation suggests an additional underlying cause

data.description: Respiratory disease caused by aspiration of meconium around delivery, producing airway obstruction, inflammation, and sometimes pneumothorax or pulmonary hypertension.
symptoms_in_common: Term delivery with nonreassuring fetal status
Pulmonary air leaks suggested on radiographs
symptoms_not_in_common: A focal left basal lesion supplied by a systemic artery is not characteristic
Localized congenital-appearing cystic lung changes are not typical
The images do not show a clearly dominant diffuse coarse, patchy infiltrative pattern

data.description: Neonatal brain dysfunction caused by inadequate oxygen delivery and blood flow around birth. The profound birth depression and prolonged resuscitation raise strong concern, although neurological examination and additional testing are needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Nonreassuring fetal status after prolonged labor
Limp tone and absent respiratory effort at birth
Cardiorespiratory arrest requiring 16 minutes of resuscitation
symptoms_not_in_common: A systemic artery supplying abnormal left basal lung tissue is not explained
Cystic lung abnormalities are not a feature
Pneumothoraces are not a direct manifestation
Prenatal right urinary tract dilatation is unrelated

data.diagnosis: Bronchopulmonary sequestration (likely extralobar, left lower lobe)
data.description: Congenital mass of nonfunctioning lung tissue with no normal connection to the tracheobronchial tree, supplied by an anomalous systemic artery, usually from the aorta. It is often associated with other congenital anomalies, including renal anomalies.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent left lower/retrocardiac opacity on serial chest radiographs
Echogenic left basal mass on ultrasound with a systemic feeding artery arising from the aorta on Doppler
CT angiography showing an anomalous artery from the aorta supplying the left lower lobe lesion
Associated congenital urinary tract anomaly (prenatal right urinary tract dilatation, cystic right renal lesion on CT)
symptoms_not_in_common: Cardiorespiratory arrest at delivery with very low Apgar scores (better explained by perinatal asphyxia)
Meconium-stained fluid
Pneumothoraces on early radiographs (more likely resuscitation/ventilation related)
Lesion not detected on prenatal ultrasound

data.diagnosis: Hybrid lesion: congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) with systemic arterial supply
data.description: Developmental hamartomatous cystic/solid lung lesion. Hybrid lesions combine CPAM histology with the systemic arterial supply of a sequestration.
symptoms_in_common: Focal left lower lobe mass-like opacity
Systemic arterial feeder from the aorta (seen in hybrid lesions)
Associated renal anomaly can occur (especially type 2 CPAM)
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear air-filled cysts within the lesion on radiographs or CT
Pure CPAM normally has pulmonary rather than systemic arterial supply
Cardiorespiratory arrest at birth not explained by a small lesion
No mediastinal shift from mass effect

data.description: Defect or weakness of the diaphragm allowing abdominal contents to enter the chest, causing pulmonary hypoplasia and respiratory failure at birth.
symptoms_in_common: Severe respiratory failure at birth requiring intubation
Left basal opacity on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Diaphragm appears intact on CT
No bowel loops or abdominal organs in the chest
Systemic feeding artery from the aorta to the lesion is not a feature
Solid echogenic lung-like tissue on ultrasound
No scaphoid abdomen or marked mediastinal shift described

data.diagnosis: Meconium aspiration syndrome with air leak and hypoxic-ischemic injury
data.description: Aspiration of meconium-stained amniotic fluid causing airway obstruction, chemical pneumonitis, atelectasis, air leak and persistent pulmonary hypertension, usually in term or post-term infants with fetal distress.
symptoms_in_common: Term infant with nonreassuring fetal status and prolonged labor
Respiratory failure at birth requiring intubation and resuscitation
symptoms_not_in_common: Opacity is focal and persistent in the left lower lobe rather than diffuse, patchy and bilateral
Systemic arterial supply from the aorta to the lesion
Solid echogenic mass on ultrasound
Urinary tract anomaly not explained

data.diagnosis: Congenital/neonatal pneumonia with lobar consolidation or atelectasis
data.description: Early-onset lung infection acquired in utero or during delivery (e.g., group B streptococcus, Chlamydia trachomatis), or lobar collapse in a ventilated neonate, producing focal lung opacity and respiratory distress.
symptoms_in_common: Left lower lobe opacity on chest radiographs
Maternal infection history (Chlamydia trachomatis, hepatitis C)
Prolonged labor as a risk factor for perinatal infection
Hypothermia can be a sign of neonatal sepsis
symptoms_not_in_common: Anomalous systemic artery from the aorta supplying the lesion
Persistent, well-defined mass-like lesion that does not resolve
Maternal chlamydia was treated, and chlamydial pneumonia typically presents at 2-12 weeks rather than at birth
Hypothermia on arrival is more likely due to resuscitation/asphyxia
Renal anomaly not explained

data.description: 57-year-old woman with resected stage IIIC cutaneous melanoma. Four months before admission, she developed bleeding from a right scalp lesion; biopsy showed ulcerated melanoma with positive margins. Three months before admission, she underwent wide local excision and neck lymph-node dissection, which showed metastatic melanoma in 2 of 26 nodes; BRAF V600E mutation was identified. One month before admission, she started adjuvant dabrafenib and trametinib. Fever and nausea began one day after starting therapy, improved after temporary discontinuation and antipyretics, then fever recurred two weeks before admission. On presentation, she had fever to 40.2°C, hypotension (85/53 mm Hg), tachycardia (108 beats/min), diaphoresis, ill appearance, and mild right upper quadrant tenderness, without rash.

data.diagnosis: Dabrafenib–trametinib-associated systemic drug reaction with granulomatous hepatitis
data.description: BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy can cause severe recurrent pyrexia and, less commonly, inflammatory liver injury. This is a leading possibility given the treatment timing and apparent hepatic granulomas.
symptoms_in_common: Fever and nausea beginning one day after treatment initiation
Initial improvement after temporary treatment discontinuation
Liver biopsy images suggestive of granulomatous inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Hepatic and splenic imaging abnormalities are not typical of uncomplicated treatment-associated pyrexia
Pulmonary septal thickening and pleural effusions suggest involvement beyond an isolated febrile reaction

data.diagnosis: Acute Q fever with granulomatous hepatitis
data.description: Coxiella burnetii infection can cause high fever, hepatitis, and characteristic fibrin-ring granulomas. Exposure history, serology, and molecular testing would be needed to establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Hepatic granulomas with possible ring-like morphology on the supplied biopsy images
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever beginning immediately after dabrafenib and trametinib initiation
Initial improvement associated with withholding anticancer therapy
Profound hypotension is less typical of uncomplicated acute Q fever

data.description: Targeted melanoma treatments can rarely trigger a multisystem granulomatous reaction resembling sarcoidosis, potentially affecting the liver, spleen, and lungs.
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt fever beginning one day after treatment initiation
Fever as high as 40.2°C with profound hypotension
Pleural effusions are less characteristic than other thoracic manifestations

data.description: Disseminated Histoplasma infection can cause systemic illness with granulomatous involvement of the liver, spleen, and lungs. Confirmation requires fungal testing and appropriate interpretation of tissue stains.
symptoms_in_common: Possible hepatic, splenic, and pulmonary abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Close temporal relationship between fever onset and targeted therapy
Initial improvement after treatment interruption
No fungal organisms can be confidently identified from the supplied images alone

data.description: Gallbladder inflammation, with or without gallstones, can cause fever, right upper quadrant pain, and sepsis. The gallbladder ultrasound warrants assessment for a calculus and inflammatory changes.
symptoms_in_common: Possible echogenic gallbladder focus on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: Only mild right upper quadrant tenderness despite marked systemic illness
Recurrent fever linked to initiation and interruption of targeted therapy
Hepatic granulomas are not typical of uncomplicated cholecystitis
Splenic lesions and pulmonary interstitial abnormalities are not explained by a localized gallbladder infection

data.diagnosis: Drug-induced sarcoid-like granulomatous reaction with pyrexia syndrome due to dabrafenib-trametinib (BRAF/MEK inhibitor toxicity)
data.description: BRAF/MEK inhibitors commonly cause a cytokine-mediated pyrexia syndrome that can be severe, with hypotension, and can induce sarcoid-like noncaseating granulomatous inflammation in the liver, lungs and lymph nodes, with granulomatous hepatitis and negative stains for organisms.
symptoms_in_common: Fever starting one day after beginning dabrafenib and trametinib
Improvement after temporary discontinuation of therapy, then recurrence of fever
High fever to 40.2°C with hypotension, tachycardia and diaphoresis
Liver biopsy appearing to show granulomas with what look like negative special stains for organisms
Chest CT appearing to show interlobular septal and peribronchial thickening with small pleural effusions
Imaging suggesting hepatosplenomegaly and periportal/gallbladder-region changes
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of rash, which often accompanies drug reactions
Severity with shock-like hypotension is at the extreme end of the spectrum
Whether fever recurred on or off drug two weeks before admission is not stated

data.diagnosis: Sepsis from biliary source (acute cholecystitis or cholangitis)
data.description: Bacterial infection of the gallbladder or biliary tree, often related to gallstones, causing fever, right upper quadrant pain and septic shock.
symptoms_in_common: Ultrasound appearing to show an echogenic focus in the gallbladder, possibly a stone
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever began one day after starting targeted therapy and improved when it was stopped
Only mild tenderness; jaundice not described
Granulomas on liver biopsy
Pulmonary septal thickening and pleural effusions
Month-long relapsing course

data.diagnosis: Disseminated granulomatous infection (miliary tuberculosis, histoplasmosis or Q fever)
data.description: Systemic infection with mycobacteria, fungi or Coxiella that seeds the liver, spleen and lungs, causing prolonged fever and granulomatous hepatitis.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary abnormalities and pleural effusions on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Close temporal link of fever to drug initiation and improvement on stopping it
Special stains for acid-fast bacilli and fungi appear negative
No exposure history or profound immunosuppression described
No miliary nodules or cavitary lesions evident
Acute hypotension is unusual

data.description: Hyperinflammatory syndrome of uncontrolled macrophage and T-cell activation, triggered by malignancy, infection or drugs, causing high fever, hepatosplenomegaly, cytopenias, liver dysfunction and shock.
symptoms_in_common: Liver involvement with right upper quadrant tenderness
Possible trigger from melanoma or targeted therapy
symptoms_not_in_common: No cytopenias, hyperferritinemia or coagulopathy described
Biopsy shows well-formed granulomas rather than hemophagocytosis
No rash
Fever improved simply with holding the drug and antipyretics

data.diagnosis: Metastatic melanoma progression (hepatic and pulmonary lymphangitic involvement with tumor fever)
data.description: Recurrence and spread of high-risk stage IIIC melanoma to the liver, lungs and lymphatics, which can cause tumor fever, hepatomegaly and lymphangitic septal thickening.
symptoms_in_common: Known stage IIIC melanoma with nodal metastases and ulcerated primary
Right upper quadrant tenderness with apparent hepatomegaly
Interlobular septal thickening and pleural effusions that could mimic lymphangitic spread
symptoms_not_in_common: Liver biopsy shows granulomatous inflammation without apparent melanoma cells
No discrete liver or lung masses evident
Fever timed to drug initiation and improved off drug
Very high fever with hypotension is atypical for tumor fever
Progression is unlikely so soon after resection on active BRAF/MEK therapy

data.description: A 71-year-old woman presented with a 3-day history of headache and fatigue, followed by sudden onset of confusion and language production difficulties while typing at work. The confusion resolved briefly but recurred later that evening. She had a history of myasthenia gravis (diagnosed 18 years prior, treated with mycophenolate mofetil for 7 years), vitamin B12 deficiency, and hypertension. Past surgical history included supracervical hysterectomy with bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (31 years prior), transsternal thymectomy and wedge resection of right upper lobe for cortical thymoma (22 years prior), and sigmoid colectomy for recurrent diverticulitis (7 years prior). On examination at the current hospital, she had severe expressive aphasia, followed commands intermittently, disconjugate gaze at rest, motor strength 5/5 in left extremities and 4/5 in right extremities. Blood phosphorus was 2.2 mg/dL (reference range 2.6-4.5); other routine labs were normal.

An uncommon bacterial infection causing focal suppurative brain lesions, particularly in older or immunosuppressed adults. The multiloculated enhancing left frontal lesion, inflammatory histology, and apparent short bacterial rods make this a leading possibility; microbiologic identification is required.
symptoms_in_common: Headache and fatigue preceding neurological deterioration
Confusion and intermittent difficulty following commands
Right-sided weakness consistent with a left frontal lesion
Long-term mycophenolate treatment increasing susceptibility to invasive infection
Enhancing brain lesion with surrounding edema and areas of restricted diffusion
symptoms_not_in_common: Brief resolution followed by recurrence of confusion is less characteristic of an established abscess, although associated seizures could explain it
Disconjugate gaze is not readily explained by an isolated left frontal abscess
Mild hypophosphatemia is not a characteristic finding

data.description: An opportunistic infection caused by Nocardia species that can produce multiloculated brain abscesses in immunosuppressed patients. Confirmation requires demonstration or culture of branching, weakly acid-fast organisms.
symptoms_in_common: Multiloculated enhancing brain lesion with surrounding edema
Suppurative inflammatory appearance of the tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden, fluctuating symptom onset is less typical than a subacute progressive course
Disconjugate gaze is not typical of an isolated frontal abscess
Mild hypophosphatemia is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: An opportunistic infection caused by Toxoplasma gondii, usually producing necrotizing, ring-enhancing brain lesions in markedly immunocompromised patients. The apparent bacterial rods in the supplied images would argue against this diagnosis if confirmed.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing brain lesion with surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt onset with transient improvement is less typical than progressive neurological deterioration
Disconjugate gaze is less typical with a solitary frontal lesion
Mild hypophosphatemia is not characteristic

data.description: A lymphoma confined to the central nervous system that can cause enhancing brain masses and focal neurological deficits. Immunosuppression increases risk, but suppurative tissue and apparent bacteria favor infection instead.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing intracerebral lesion with edema and restricted diffusion
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden onset and brief spontaneous resolution are less typical than steadily progressive deficits
Disconjugate gaze is not readily explained by a solitary frontal mass
Mild hypophosphatemia is not a characteristic finding

data.description: An aggressive primary brain tumor commonly occurring in older adults and producing irregular enhancement, necrosis, and surrounding edema. The apparent suppurative inflammation and bacterial organisms make it less likely than a brain abscess.
symptoms_in_common: Expressive aphasia from involvement of the dominant frontal lobe
Irregular enhancing left frontal lesion with extensive surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Abrupt neurological onset with temporary resolution is less typical than progressive decline, although tumor-associated seizures can fluctuate
Disconjugate gaze is not typical of an isolated frontal tumor
Mild hypophosphatemia is not a characteristic manifestation

data.description: Focal suppurative CNS infection caused by Listeria monocytogenes, a gram-positive rod, occurring mainly in older or immunosuppressed patients (e.g., on mycophenolate); it produces irregular, multiloculated or 'worm-like' ring-enhancing lesions with surrounding edema and is confirmed by culture and MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry.
symptoms_in_common: Subacute headache and fatigue followed by confusion
Expressive aphasia and right-sided weakness from a left frontal lesion
Clustered ring-enhancing lesions with extensive vasogenic edema and tract-like enhancement on MRI
Short rods on Gram stain with organism identified from culture by mass spectrometry
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or meningismus reported
Normal routine labs without leukocytosis
Fluctuating, sudden stroke-like onset
Disconjugate gaze without other brainstem signs
Hemorrhagic component within the lesion is uncommon
Hypophosphatemia is nonspecific

data.description: CNS infection by Nocardia species, branching gram-positive, weakly acid-fast bacilli, typically in immunosuppressed hosts and often spreading from a pulmonary focus; it causes multiloculated ring-enhancing abscesses.
symptoms_in_common: Headache, confusion and focal deficits (aphasia, right hemiparesis)
symptoms_not_in_common: Organisms appear as short rods rather than long, beaded, branching filaments
No pulmonary or skin lesions described
Rapid growth in culture is atypical for Nocardia
No fever

data.description: Focal collection of pus in brain parenchyma from contiguous (sinus, ear, dental) or haematogenous spread, commonly due to Streptococcus anginosus group, anaerobes or staphylococci; it classically shows a smooth ring-enhancing lesion with central restricted diffusion.
symptoms_in_common: Headache and fatigue progressing to confusion
symptoms_not_in_common: No identified source (sinusitis, otitis, dental infection, endocarditis)
Gram stain shows rods rather than cocci in chains or clusters
Irregular clustered rim pattern rather than a single smooth-walled cavity
No fever or leukocytosis

data.description: Most common malignant primary brain tumour in adults, appearing as an irregular, heterogeneously ring-enhancing mass with central necrosis, haemorrhage and surrounding edema.
symptoms_in_common: Headache with progressive focal deficits (aphasia, right hemiparesis)
Irregular heterogeneously enhancing left frontal mass with extensive FLAIR hyperintensity
Fluctuating confusion and speech arrest could reflect tumour-related seizures
symptoms_not_in_common: Very short 3-day history
Biopsy shows sheets of neutrophils rather than pleomorphic glial tumour cells with necrosis and microvascular proliferation
Bacteria seen on Gram stain and grown in culture
Immunosuppression is not a specific risk factor

data.description: Extranodal non-Hodgkin B-cell lymphoma confined to the CNS, with increased incidence in immunosuppressed patients (including those on mycophenolate, often EBV-driven), in whom lesions may be ring-enhancing, necrotic or haemorrhagic.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing lesion with surrounding edema and restricted diffusion
Ring enhancement and haemorrhage can occur in immunosuppressed hosts
symptoms_not_in_common: Acute 3-day onset
Pathology shows neutrophils rather than atypical perivascular lymphoid cells
Organisms identified on Gram stain and culture
Lesion is not periventricular or homogeneously enhancing

data.description: 27-year-old man with 2-year history of recurrent convulsive episodes. Events began with shaking of the trunk, arms, and legs lasting 4–5 minutes, often preceded by occipital pain radiating to the neck, blurred vision, palpitations, nausea, and difficulty concentrating. Four months before admission, an episode occurred with sudden body stiffening, fall backward, shaking for 5–8 minutes, and urinary incontinence. Despite levetiracetam, seizures continued about weekly; one month before admission he was found on the floor with shaking and clenching movements lasting about 2 minutes. On examination, he was awake and alert but nonverbal, with a stiff body and intermittent nonrhythmic tremulous movements of the trunk and limbs. He had extensive burn scars on the face, trunk, back, arms, and legs. Past history included febrile seizure in childhood, several concussions, asthma, major depressive disorder, chronic PTSD, and panic disorder with agoraphobia. Basic labs were normal except mildly elevated lactate and creatine kinase.

Involuntary seizure-like episodes caused by functional neurological dysfunction rather than epileptic discharges. This is the leading consideration: the supplied EEG appears dominated by movement artifacts with some preserved posterior activity rather than a clearly evolving ictal pattern. Confirmation requires clinical correlation and video-EEG capture of typical events.
symptoms_in_common: Prolonged, recurrent shaking episodes lasting 4–8 minutes
Intermittent nonrhythmic trunk and limb movements
Alertness despite nonverbal behavior and abnormal movements
History of PTSD, depression, and panic disorder
Stiffening, falls, and urinary incontinence can also occur in functional seizures
symptoms_not_in_common: Occipital pain radiating into the neck is not a characteristic feature
Childhood febrile seizure and concussions raise the possibility of coexisting epilepsy rather than specifically supporting functional seizures

data.diagnosis: Focal epilepsy with focal-to-bilateral tonic-clonic seizures
data.description: Epileptic activity beginning in one brain region and spreading bilaterally can produce autonomic or visual auras followed by stiffening and convulsions. A single artifact-contaminated EEG image cannot exclude epilepsy.
symptoms_in_common: Visual disturbance, nausea, and palpitations before episodes
Sudden body stiffening followed by generalized shaking
Mild lactate and creatine kinase elevations after motor activity
History of childhood febrile seizure and several concussions
symptoms_not_in_common: Alertness during ongoing nonrhythmic generalized movements
Repeated convulsive episodes lasting 5–8 minutes are atypically prolonged and would require urgent assessment if epileptic
The supplied EEG does not show a clearly identifiable evolving epileptic discharge
Persistent nonverbal behavior with intermittent tremulous movements is not a typical tonic-clonic seizure pattern

data.description: Transient reduction in cerebral blood flow, from reflex fainting or a cardiac rhythm disturbance, can cause collapse with brief stiffening and jerking.
symptoms_in_common: Blurred vision, nausea, and difficulty concentrating before collapse
symptoms_not_in_common: Shaking lasting 4–8 minutes is much longer than typical syncopal jerking
Alertness during ongoing generalized abnormal movements
Persistent nonverbal behavior and intermittent nonrhythmic tremors
Occipital pain radiating to the neck is not a characteristic syncopal prodrome

data.description: Episodes of intense autonomic arousal can produce palpitations, nausea, visual disturbance, shaking, and dissociation. Panic may also precipitate functional seizures, but does not alone explain every convulsive feature.
symptoms_not_in_common: Sudden tonic stiffening with a backward fall
Urinary incontinence
Prolonged generalized convulsive movements
Sustained nonverbal behavior with marked bodily stiffness

data.description: A psychomotor syndrome associated with psychiatric or medical illness that can cause mutism, rigidity, abnormal posturing, and episodes of agitation. It could explain some examination findings but is less convincing as the cause of the recurrent convulsive spells.
symptoms_not_in_common: Discrete recurrent convulsive episodes with sudden falls
Urinary incontinence during an episode
Prodromal palpitations, blurred vision, and nausea
Occipital pain radiating to the neck
No additional defining catatonic signs, such as negativism or waxy flexibility, are reported

data.diagnosis: Functional (psychogenic nonepileptic) seizures / functional neurological disorder
data.description: Paroxysmal events resembling epileptic seizures but without epileptiform EEG correlate, arising from altered brain network function and strongly associated with trauma, PTSD, depression and anxiety.
symptoms_in_common: Long episodes (4–8 minutes) of shaking of trunk and limbs
Awake and alert yet nonverbal during bilateral motor activity
Refractory to levetiracetam with weekly events
Prodrome of palpitations, nausea, blurred vision, difficulty concentrating (panic-like)
History of chronic PTSD, major depression, panic disorder, severe burn trauma
EEG showing eye-blink/eye-movement and muscle artifact with preserved background rather than an evolving epileptiform discharge
symptoms_not_in_common: Urinary incontinence (can occur but less typical)
Sudden stiffening with backward fall
Mildly elevated lactate and creatine kinase
Childhood febrile seizure

data.diagnosis: Epilepsy with focal to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures (e.g., post-traumatic or temporal/occipital lobe)
data.description: Recurrent unprovoked seizures from abnormal synchronous cortical discharges; may follow head trauma or febrile seizures and can be drug-resistant.
symptoms_in_common: Body stiffening with fall and shaking
Aura-like symptoms (blurred vision, nausea, occipital pain)
History of febrile seizure and multiple concussions
Mildly elevated lactate and creatine kinase
symptoms_not_in_common: Episodes lasting 5–8 minutes
Preserved awareness with bilateral movements
Nonrhythmic tremulous movements
No response to levetiracetam
EEG during the event without clear ictal epileptiform evolution

data.diagnosis: Panic attacks (panic disorder) with dissociative features
data.description: Sudden surges of intense fear with autonomic symptoms; may include trembling, derealization and hyperventilation-induced tetany or stiffness.
symptoms_in_common: Known panic disorder with agoraphobia and PTSD
symptoms_not_in_common: Falls with whole-body stiffening
Urinary incontinence
Being found on the floor with clenching movements
Nonverbal state with stiff body
Elevated creatine kinase

data.description: Transient cerebral hypoperfusion causing loss of consciousness, sometimes with brief myoclonic jerks or stiffening and incontinence.
symptoms_not_in_common: Shaking lasting several minutes (syncopal jerks last seconds)
Weekly frequency over two years
Awake and alert during movements
ECG channel without an evident causal arrhythmia
Elevated creatine kinase

data.diagnosis: Migraine with brainstem aura / occipital-onset migraine-related events
data.description: Migraine variant with occipital headache and visual and brainstem symptoms, occasionally with altered consciousness; migraine can rarely trigger seizures.
symptoms_in_common: Occipital pain radiating to the neck
symptoms_not_in_common: Convulsive shaking of trunk and limbs
Body stiffening and falls
Urinary incontinence
Nonverbal state with tremulous movements
Elevated lactate and creatine kinase

data.description: 36-year-old man with 18 days of fever up to 39.5°C preceded by throat swelling sensation. Symptoms persisted despite amoxicillin-clavulanic acid given for presumed streptococcal pharyngitis; associated headache, fatigue, and lower neck swelling/discomfort with neck movement. He denied dysphagia, odynophagia, rhinorrhea, and rash. Past history notable for seasonal allergies. Recent travel to the southwestern United States with his wife 2 weeks before symptom onset; wife had transient fever and sore throat. On exam: afebrile, tachycardic, normal oropharynx without tonsillar exudates, no lymphadenopathy, and firm, nontender thyroid tissue palpable in the anterior neck.

An inflammatory thyroid disorder, often following a viral illness, that can cause fever, thyroid enlargement, and transient thyrotoxicosis. This is the leading consideration; the supplied CT appears to show an enlarged, relatively low-attenuation thyroid, compatible with thyroid inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Lower anterior neck swelling and discomfort with neck movement
symptoms_not_in_common: The thyroid is nontender, whereas appreciable thyroid tenderness is typical

data.description: A rare bacterial infection of the thyroid that can produce high fever, neck swelling, and occasionally an abscess. Imaging and microbiological testing are needed to distinguish it from noninfectious thyroid inflammation.
symptoms_not_in_common: Nontender thyroid rather than marked focal tenderness
No dysphagia or odynophagia
No improvement with amoxicillin-clavulanic acid, although resistant infection or an undrained abscess could still explain this

data.description: A usually autoimmune, destructive thyroid inflammation that releases stored thyroid hormone, causing temporary thyrotoxicosis without substantial thyroid pain.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prolonged high fever is unusual
Neck discomfort with movement is less typical
A prominent preceding throat illness is less characteristic than in subacute granulomatous thyroiditis

data.description: Autoimmune thyroid inflammation that commonly produces a firm, painless goiter and can occasionally cause temporary thyroid hormone excess before hypothyroidism develops.
symptoms_in_common: Tachycardia if a transient thyrotoxic phase is present
symptoms_not_in_common: Persistent fever up to 39.5°C is distinctly atypical
Acute onset following throat symptoms is less typical
Neck discomfort with movement is not characteristic

data.description: An autoimmune disorder causing increased thyroid hormone production and usually diffuse thyroid enlargement. Thyroid function tests and TSH-receptor antibodies would help distinguish it from destructive thyroiditis.
symptoms_not_in_common: Prolonged high fever is unusual in uncomplicated Graves disease
Neck discomfort with movement is atypical
A preceding throat illness is not characteristic
The relatively low-attenuation thyroid appearance on the supplied CT favors inflammatory thyroiditis over typical Graves disease

data.description: Self-limited post-viral inflammatory disorder of the thyroid causing gland destruction with release of preformed hormone (thyrotoxic phase), fever, and neck discomfort; CT shows an enlarged, heterogeneous, hypoattenuating thyroid.
symptoms_in_common: Sick contact (wife) with transient fever and sore throat
Lower neck swelling and discomfort with neck movement
CT showing hypoattenuating, ill-defined thyroid lobe
symptoms_not_in_common: Thyroid is nontender (classically exquisitely tender)
Male sex (more common in women)
Fever as high as 39.5°C for 18 days is somewhat pronounced

data.description: Rare bacterial (or occasionally fungal) infection of the thyroid, sometimes linked to a piriform sinus fistula, causing fever, neck pain, and a focal hypodense collection on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Hypoattenuating area in the thyroid on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Nontender thyroid (usually exquisitely tender with erythema/warmth)
No dysphagia or odynophagia
No improvement on amoxicillin-clavulanic acid
Subacute 18-day course without toxic deterioration
Immunocompetent adult (more common in children or immunocompromised)
No discrete rim-enhancing abscess described

data.description: Endemic fungal infection of the southwestern United States caused by Coccidioides, typically presenting 1–3 weeks after exposure with fever, fatigue, and headache; rarely disseminates to extrapulmonary sites such as the thyroid.
symptoms_in_common: Travel to the southwestern United States 2 weeks before onset
Wife also had a febrile illness after the same trip
symptoms_not_in_common: No cough, chest pain, or other respiratory symptoms
No rash (erythema nodosum/multiforme) or arthralgias
Thyroid involvement is very rare and usually occurs in disseminated disease or immunocompromised hosts
Wife's illness was transient sore throat, more suggestive of a viral infection

data.description: Autoimmune hyperthyroidism caused by TSH-receptor stimulating antibodies, producing diffuse goiter, tachycardia, and hypermetabolic symptoms.
symptoms_not_in_common: High fever to 39.5°C for 18 days (unusual unless thyroid storm)
Neck discomfort with movement
Acute onset after pharyngitis-like prodrome
No ophthalmopathy, tremor, or weight loss reported
Focal hypoattenuation on CT rather than diffuse homogeneous enlargement
Male sex (less common)

data.diagnosis: Thyroid lymphoma or anaplastic thyroid carcinoma
data.description: Aggressive thyroid malignancies presenting as a firm, enlarging thyroid mass, sometimes with systemic B symptoms (fever, fatigue) and hypodense infiltrative appearance on CT.
symptoms_in_common: Hypoattenuating infiltrative thyroid lesion on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Young age (typically older patients, lymphoma often with underlying Hashimoto thyroiditis)
Acute onset following pharyngitis-like illness and sick contact
No cervical lymphadenopathy
No compressive symptoms (dysphagia, hoarseness, stridor)
High spiking fever is atypical
No weight loss or night sweats reported

data.description: 47-year-old female with an incidentally discovered right adrenal mass found 3 years ago, initially about 2.2 × 3.1 cm and untreated. Recent enhanced CT 10 days ago showed enlargement to about 5.8 × 4.7 cm. She remained asymptomatic throughout. Past history negative for hypertension, diabetes, cardiac, pulmonary, or cerebrovascular disease; no smoking or alcohol use. Menstrual flow was reduced. Physical examination was unremarkable, with normal vital signs, normal cardiopulmonary findings, soft non-tender abdomen, and no palpable mass or renal percussion pain.

A rare adrenal cortical tumor composed of cells with abundant granular eosinophilic cytoplasm. Often nonfunctioning and discovered incidentally; benign versus malignant potential requires formal histopathologic assessment.
symptoms_in_common: Asymptomatic course with normal vital signs
No clinical hypertension or overt hormone-excess syndrome
Provided histology appears to show cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm, compatible with an oncocytic tumor
