symptoms_not_in_common: Reduced menstrual flow is not characteristic of a nonfunctioning oncocytoma

data.description: A benign adrenal cortical tumor that does not produce clinically apparent excess hormones. Imaging characterization and biochemical testing are needed to establish this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Absence of pain or constitutional symptoms
Normal blood pressure and physical examination
No overt clinical manifestations of cortisol or aldosterone excess
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked interval enlargement to approximately 5.8 cm is less typical of an ordinary adenoma
Reduced menstrual flow is not characteristic of a nonfunctioning adenoma

data.description: A malignant adrenal cortical tumor that may be functioning or nonfunctioning. Increasing size and a diameter above 4 cm raise concern, but malignancy cannot be established from size alone.
symptoms_in_common: Substantial interval growth of an adrenal mass
Current maximum dimension of approximately 5.8 cm
A nonfunctioning carcinoma can lack overt endocrine symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Remaining entirely asymptomatic for three years is less typical of aggressive carcinoma
No abdominal pain, palpable mass, or reported constitutional symptoms
Reduced menstrual flow alone is not a characteristic presentation

data.description: An adrenal medullary tumor that commonly produces catecholamines. Some tumors are discovered incidentally in normotensive patients; biochemical testing is necessary even without classic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: An asymptomatic, normotensive presentation is possible
Eosinophilic tumor cells on the supplied histology can overlap with this diagnosis
symptoms_not_in_common: No hypertension or episodic blood-pressure abnormalities
No reported headaches, palpitations, or sweating
Reduced menstrual flow is not characteristic

data.description: A rare, usually benign nerve-sheath tumor arising in or near the adrenal gland. It is typically nonfunctioning and may enlarge slowly without symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Normal vital signs and unremarkable physical examination
symptoms_not_in_common: Reduced menstrual flow is not characteristic
The supplied histology appears predominantly polygonal and eosinophilic rather than showing the spindle-cell pattern expected in schwannoma

data.description: Rare, usually benign and non-functioning adrenocortical tumor composed of large polygonal cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm rich in mitochondria; often discovered incidentally as a large, well-circumscribed mass, more often in women.
symptoms_in_common: Large well-circumscribed encapsulated mass (5.8 x 4.7 cm)
Normal blood pressure and no signs of hormone excess
Histology showing sheets of large cells with abundant eosinophilic granular cytoplasm
Heterogeneous enhancement on CT and contrast ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: Reduced menstrual flow (tumor usually non-functional)
Progressive enlargement raises concern for borderline or malignant potential

data.description: Rare aggressive malignancy of the adrenal cortex, typically larger than 4-6 cm, heterogeneous with necrosis or hemorrhage; about half secrete cortisol and/or androgens.
symptoms_in_common: Reduced menstrual flow could reflect androgen or cortisol excess
symptoms_not_in_common: Slow growth over 3 years (carcinoma usually grows faster)
Completely asymptomatic with no pain or weight loss
No Cushingoid features or virilization
Well-defined capsule without invasion or metastasis
No hypertension or diabetes
Histology without marked atypia, necrosis or frequent mitoses

data.description: Catecholamine-producing tumor of the adrenal medulla; may be clinically silent and found incidentally; typically a large, avidly and heterogeneously enhancing mass with cystic or necrotic areas.
symptoms_in_common: Heterogeneous enhancement with possible cystic/necrotic areas
symptoms_not_in_common: No hypertension
No paroxysmal headache, palpitations or sweating
Normal vital signs
No diabetes or glucose intolerance
Histology shows diffuse eosinophilic cells rather than the classic nested (Zellballen) pattern
Reduced menstrual flow not explained

data.description: Most common adrenal incidentaloma; benign cortical tumor, usually small, homogeneous and lipid-rich; may show mild autonomous cortisol secretion.
symptoms_in_common: Reduced menstrual flow could reflect subtle cortisol excess
symptoms_not_in_common: Significant growth to nearly 6 cm (adenomas are usually stable and under 4 cm)
Heterogeneous appearance
Histology with eosinophilic rather than lipid-rich clear cells

data.diagnosis: Adrenal metastasis or tumor from an adjacent organ (e.g., hepatocellular carcinoma, renal cell carcinoma)
data.description: The adrenal gland is a common site of metastasis (lung, breast, kidney, melanoma), and exophytic liver or upper-pole renal tumors can mimic a right adrenal mass; eosinophilic tumor cells may resemble hepatoid or renal oncocytic neoplasms.
symptoms_in_common: Mass closely abutting liver and upper pole of the kidney
symptoms_not_in_common: No known primary malignancy
Slow growth over 3 years
No smoking history or systemic symptoms
Unilateral solitary encapsulated lesion
No liver disease history or renal findings
Reduced menstrual flow not explained

data.description: 72-year-old man with a history of well-controlled gastroesophageal reflux disease on daily omeprazole developed recurrent heartburn 11 months before admission, followed by postprandial nausea and early satiety. Over the next 9 months, symptoms progressively worsened, with gradual dietary restriction from solid foods to soft solids, then blended foods, and finally liquids. Two months before admission, EGD was limited by a large amount of retained gastric food despite 24 hours of fasting; no intraluminal mass was seen. He later became unable to tolerate liquids and presented to the emergency department. On examination, he was thin, mildly tachycardic, with mild epigastric tenderness; the abdomen was flat, soft, and nondistended.

data.diagnosis: Diffuse-type gastric adenocarcinoma with infiltrative gastric outlet obstruction
data.description: A gastric cancer that can infiltrate the stomach wall without forming a discrete intraluminal mass. Antral or pyloric involvement can obstruct gastric emptying. This is the leading consideration given the progressive course and apparent infiltrative atypical cells in the supplied histology; confirmation requires formal pathology review.
symptoms_in_common: Progressively worsening early satiety and postprandial nausea
Progressive intolerance of solids and eventually liquids
Retained gastric food despite 24 hours of fasting
Thin appearance and mild epigastric tenderness
Marked gastric dilation and apparent antral-pyloric wall thickening on CT
Absence of a discrete intraluminal mass does not exclude infiltrative cancer
symptoms_not_in_common: A flat, nondistended abdomen is less typical of advanced gastric retention, although it does not exclude it

data.description: A lymphoid malignancy involving the stomach that can produce thickened folds, mural infiltration, early satiety, and occasionally gastric outlet obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent gastric wall thickening and prominent nodular folds
symptoms_not_in_common: The supplied histology appears more suggestive of infiltrating epithelial malignancy than a predominantly lymphoid tumor
Severe progressive outlet obstruction is less characteristic than in an obstructing gastric adenocarcinoma

data.diagnosis: Peptic ulcer disease with benign pyloric stenosis
data.description: Chronic ulceration near the pylorus can cause inflammation and scarring that narrow the gastric outlet, leading to retained food and progressive feeding intolerance.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive intolerance of solids followed by liquids
Marked gastric dilation without a discrete intraluminal mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent nodular gastric folds are not typical of uncomplicated peptic scarring
Apparent infiltrative atypical cells in the supplied histology are not explained by benign pyloric stenosis
Progression despite daily omeprazole is less typical of acid-mediated inflammation alone

data.description: Delayed gastric emptying without mechanical obstruction, caused by impaired gastric neuromuscular function. It can be idiopathic or associated with diabetes, medications, or other disorders.
symptoms_in_common: Retained gastric food despite 24 hours of fasting
Poor oral intake and thin appearance
No intraluminal mass seen during the limited initial endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent focal antral-pyloric thickening suggests a structural outlet lesion rather than isolated dysmotility
Prominent nodular folds are not explained by uncomplicated gastroparesis
Apparent infiltrative atypical cells in the supplied histology are inconsistent with a purely motility-related disorder

data.description: A rare hypertrophic gastropathy characterized by enlarged gastric folds and protein loss. It can cause nausea, epigastric discomfort, early satiety, and nutritional decline.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent enlarged or nodular gastric folds on endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe progressive gastric outlet obstruction is unusual
Apparent antral-pyloric involvement is less typical because Ménétrier disease usually predominantly affects the body and fundus
Marked retained food and gastric dilation are not its usual dominant manifestations
Apparent infiltrative atypical cells in the supplied histology are not characteristic

data.diagnosis: Diffuse-type (signet-ring cell) gastric adenocarcinoma with linitis plastica causing gastric outlet obstruction
data.description: Poorly cohesive carcinoma that infiltrates the submucosa and muscularis propria of the stomach wall, often without a discrete intraluminal mass. It produces wall thickening, rigidity and pyloric/antral stenosis, and mucosal biopsies may be falsely negative.
symptoms_in_common: Older man with progressive heartburn, postprandial nausea and early satiety over 11 months
Stepwise progression from solids to soft foods to liquids, then intolerance of liquids
Retained gastric food despite 24 hours of fasting
No intraluminal mass on EGD, consistent with an infiltrative submucosal process
CT showing a markedly distended fluid-filled stomach with wall thickening and enhancement at the antrum/pylorus
Thickened, edematous gastric folds on endoscopy
Endoscopic ultrasound showing circumferential wall thickening with loss of normal layering
Biopsy showing poorly cohesive atypical cells, some with vacuoles, infiltrating muscularis propria, apparently highlighted by an immunostain (likely keratin)
Tumor cells apparently on the serosal/peritoneal surface next to fat
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported overt GI bleeding or anemia
Relatively long 11-month course
No discrete mass seen at endoscopy
Flat, nondistended abdomen without ascites or palpable mass

data.diagnosis: Pancreatic or periampullary adenocarcinoma invading the duodenum/pylorus
data.description: Malignancy of the pancreatic head or periampullary region that can encase or invade the duodenum or distal stomach, causing malignant gastric outlet obstruction without an intragastric mass.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive gastric outlet obstruction with nausea and early satiety
No intraluminal gastric mass on EGD
Retained gastric food and markedly distended stomach
Infiltrating malignant cells on biopsy could represent extension from an adjacent adenocarcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: No jaundice or biliary obstruction described
No back pain
No evident pancreatic mass or ductal dilatation described on imaging
Diffusely thickened gastric folds and gastric wall on endoscopy and EUS point to a primary gastric process

data.diagnosis: Gastric lymphoma (e.g., diffuse large B-cell or MALT lymphoma)
data.description: Lymphoid malignancy of the stomach that can cause diffuse wall thickening and enlarged folds, and occasionally outlet obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Gastric wall thickening on CT and endoscopic ultrasound
Early satiety, nausea and epigastric discomfort
symptoms_not_in_common: Lymphoma usually keeps the wall pliable, so severe gastric outlet obstruction is uncommon
No fever, night sweats or bulky lymphadenopathy reported
Histology shows poorly cohesive epithelioid cells with vacuoles rather than sheets of lymphoid cells
Staining pattern appears to be that of an epithelial (keratin) marker rather than a lymphoid one

data.diagnosis: Peptic ulcer disease with benign pyloric stenosis
data.description: Chronic pyloric channel or duodenal ulceration, often related to H. pylori or NSAIDs, leading to scarring and fibrotic narrowing of the gastric outlet.
symptoms_in_common: Long history of acid-related disease (GERD) and heartburn
Progressive gastric outlet obstruction with retained food
symptoms_not_in_common: Developed despite daily proton pump inhibitor therapy
No reported NSAID use, ulcer history or GI bleeding
Diffusely thickened gastric folds and wall thickening on EUS
Biopsy showing atypical infiltrating cells in muscularis propria rather than fibrosis
Relentless progression in an elderly patient favors malignancy

data.description: Delayed gastric emptying without mechanical obstruction, due to impaired gastric neuromuscular function; commonly diabetic, postsurgical, drug-related or idiopathic.
symptoms_in_common: Retained gastric food after prolonged fasting
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of diabetes, gastric surgery or causative medications given
Steady progression to complete intolerance of liquids is unusual; liquids are usually tolerated better than solids
Thickened gastric wall and folds on CT, endoscopy and EUS indicate a structural lesion
Biopsy showing infiltrating atypical cells
New onset at age 72 with apparent weight loss

data.description: A 56-year-old female patient presented with low-back and hip pain radiating down to her left leg for 12 months. She did not respond to initial management with conservative therapy of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications.

data.diagnosis: Aggressive vertebral hemangioma with epidural and paravertebral extension
data.description: A benign vascular vertebral tumor that can behave locally aggressively and compress nerve roots. The apparent L3 vertebral involvement, coarse trabecular pattern, and enhancing epidural and paravertebral extension make this a leading imaging consideration, although the supplied images alone are not definitive.
symptoms_in_common: Pain radiating down the left leg
Persistent pain despite non-steroidal anti-inflammatory treatment

data.description: Cancer spreading to a vertebra can replace bone marrow and extend into the spinal canal or adjacent soft tissues, causing pain and nerve compression. It is an important alternative for a vertebral lesion with extraosseous extension.
symptoms_in_common: Left-leg radiating pain from possible nerve compression
Failure to improve with conservative treatment

data.description: A localized plasma-cell tumor that commonly involves the spine and may produce an expansile vertebral lesion with an epidural or paravertebral mass. Confirmation requires tissue diagnosis and evaluation for systemic plasma-cell disease.
symptoms_in_common: Pain radiating into the left leg
Poor response to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medications

data.description: Lymphoma can infiltrate vertebral marrow and form enhancing epidural or paravertebral soft tissue, sometimes with relatively limited bone destruction. It can cause chronic back pain and radicular symptoms.

A usually benign nerve-sheath tumor that can extend through a neural foramen and cause radicular pain. Large lesions may remodel adjacent bone, although the apparent vertebral-centered involvement and trabecular pattern are less typical than for a vascular vertebral lesion.
symptoms_in_common: Pain radiating down the left leg
Lack of improvement with anti-inflammatory treatment

data.description: Slow-growing, locally aggressive malignant tumor of notochordal remnants; in the mobile spine it typically involves the vertebral body with a large T2-hyperintense lobulated paravertebral soft tissue mass, may span adjacent vertebrae while sparing the discs.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic progressive low-back and hip pain over 12 months
Vertebral body lesion, T1 hypointense and markedly T2/STIR hyperintense
Large lobulated, septated prevertebral/paravertebral soft tissue mass
Involvement of adjacent vertebrae with preserved intervertebral discs
symptoms_not_in_common: Lumbar location less common than sacrococcygeal or clival
Slightly more common in males
No bowel or bladder dysfunction reported

data.description: Most common malignant lesion of the spine in adults over 50; hematogenous spread from primaries such as breast, lung, kidney or thyroid, causing marrow replacement, paravertebral and epidural extension.
symptoms_in_common: Persistent back pain unresponsive to conservative therapy
T1 hypointense marrow replacement of vertebral body
Paravertebral and epidural soft tissue extension
symptoms_not_in_common: No known primary malignancy
Long 12-month indolent course
Contiguous rather than scattered multifocal lesions
Very high T2 signal lobulated septated mass is unusual
No weight loss or systemic symptoms reported

data.description: Plasma cell neoplasm producing lytic vertebral body lesions, often with soft tissue extension and nerve compression; commonly in patients over 50.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic back pain with radicular symptoms
Vertebral body marrow replacement, T1 hypointense
Soft tissue extension with epidural component
symptoms_not_in_common: Typically intermediate rather than very bright T2 signal
Large lobulated septated prevertebral mass is atypical
No reported anemia, hypercalcemia, renal dysfunction or paraprotein
No characteristic 'mini-brain' appearance

data.description: Chronic granulomatous infection of the spine with vertebral destruction, subligamentous spread across levels and large paravertebral or psoas cold abscesses, with relative disc preservation early on.
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, night sweats or weight loss reported
No known TB exposure or pulmonary disease
Mass appears solid, lobulated and septated rather than a thin rim-enhancing abscess
No marked vertebral collapse or gibbus deformity

data.description: Malignant cartilage-forming tumor that can arise in vertebral body or posterior elements; shows lobulated, very high T2 signal with septal and peripheral enhancement and soft tissue extension.
symptoms_in_common: Slowly progressive pain with nerve root symptoms
Paravertebral soft tissue extension and bone destruction
symptoms_not_in_common: More often arises from posterior elements
More common in the thoracic spine and in males
Chondroid matrix calcification (rings and arcs) not demonstrated
Multi-level vertebral body involvement with disc sparing is less typical

data.description: A 69-year-old female non-smoker presented with a 6-month history of progressive breathlessness. She had no relevant past medical history or drug history. Spirometry showed FEV1 32% predicted and a flow-volume loop suggesting severe small airway disease. Transthoracic echocardiogram was normal.

data.diagnosis: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia (DIPNECH)
data.description: A rare proliferation of pulmonary neuroendocrine cells, typically affecting older nonsmoking women. Associated constrictive bronchiolitis causes airflow obstruction, while tumorlets or carcinoid tumors produce pulmonary nodules. This is the leading consideration, but requires specialist evaluation and often tissue confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Severe airflow obstruction with FEV1 32% predicted
Small-airway disease on the flow-volume loop
CT appearances suggestive of mosaic attenuation and air trapping
Multiple pulmonary nodules or masses visible on the supplied images

data.description: Fibrotic narrowing of small airways causing persistent airflow obstruction and air trapping. It may be idiopathic or associated with autoimmune disease, inhalational injury, infection, or DIPNECH.
symptoms_in_common: Flow-volume loop suggesting severe small-airway disease
Apparent mosaic attenuation and air trapping on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple discrete pulmonary nodules or masses are not explained by isolated constrictive bronchiolitis

data.description: Well-differentiated pulmonary neuroendocrine tumors that may appear as rounded or lobulated nodules and can obstruct adjacent bronchi. Multiple carcinoids may occur in association with DIPNECH.
symptoms_in_common: Rounded and lobulated pulmonary lesions on CT
Airway obstruction and localized air trapping can occur with bronchial involvement
Nonsmoking status is compatible with pulmonary carcinoids
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe diffuse small-airway obstruction is less typical of isolated carcinoid tumors
Widespread mosaic attenuation would suggest an accompanying small-airway disorder

data.description: Inflammatory airway disease causing variable airflow limitation, sometimes presenting later in life with substantial obstruction and air trapping.
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple solid pulmonary nodules or masses are not characteristic of asthma
Steadily progressive breathlessness without reported variability is less characteristic, although possible

data.description: An immune-mediated lung disease caused by inhaled antigens that can involve small airways, producing breathlessness, mosaic attenuation, air trapping, and usually ill-defined centrilobular nodules.
symptoms_in_common: Apparent mosaic attenuation and air trapping on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Large, well-defined solid pulmonary nodules or masses are not typical
Profound predominantly obstructive physiology is less typical than restrictive or mixed impairment

diagnoses.name: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia
diagnoses.title: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia

data.diagnosis: Diffuse idiopathic pulmonary neuroendocrine cell hyperplasia (DIPNECH) with carcinoid tumours
data.description: Preinvasive proliferation of pulmonary neuroendocrine cells in the small airways, typically in middle-aged to elderly non-smoking women, causing constrictive bronchiolitis with mosaic attenuation/air trapping and multiple pulmonary nodules (tumourlets and carcinoid tumours).
symptoms_in_common: Flow-volume loop indicating small airway disease
Multiple well-defined, lobulated pulmonary nodules/masses bilaterally
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic cough not reported, although it is common in DIPNECH
Nodules are larger than typical tumourlets (suggesting carcinoid tumours)
One nodule appears to have low-attenuation areas

data.description: Fibrotic narrowing of the bronchioles causing fixed airflow obstruction, usually related to connective tissue disease, drugs, toxic inhalation, post-infection or transplantation.
symptoms_in_common: Severe airflow obstruction with small airway pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: No known connective tissue disease, drug exposure, transplant or inhalational injury
Multiple lobulated lung nodules/masses are not explained

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary metastases from an occult primary malignancy
data.description: Haematogenous spread of an extrathoracic malignancy to the lungs, producing multiple rounded nodules of varying size.
symptoms_in_common: Possible low-attenuation (necrotic) areas in a nodule
symptoms_not_in_common: No known primary tumour or relevant history
Severe small airway obstruction is not explained by metastases
Mosaic attenuation/air trapping
No reported weight loss or systemic symptoms

data.diagnosis: Primary lung cancer (e.g., adenocarcinoma with synchronous or metastatic lesions)
data.description: Malignant epithelial lung tumour; adenocarcinoma is the commonest type in non-smoking women and may present with multiple lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple lesions could represent synchronous or metastatic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: Non-smoker with no risk factors
Severe small airway obstruction and mosaic attenuation are not explained
Smooth, well-defined margins are more typical of carcinoid than carcinoma
No haemoptysis or weight loss reported

data.diagnosis: Severe asthma or COPD with incidental pulmonary nodules (e.g., hamartomas)
data.description: Chronic obstructive airway disease causing airflow limitation and air trapping, with coincidental benign nodules.
symptoms_in_common: Well-defined, lobulated nodules could be benign
symptoms_not_in_common: Non-smoker, making COPD unlikely
No prior history of asthma, wheeze or symptom variability
New onset at age 69 with rapid progression over 6 months
Multiple sizeable bilateral nodules are unlikely to be incidental
No fat or popcorn calcification described to suggest hamartoma

data.description: A 15-year-old boy presented with recent onset of breathlessness, weight loss, and tiredness for two months and a crusting erythematous scalp rash for six months. The investigations revealed neutrophilia, raised C-reactive protein (CRP), and Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT). The blood urea and electrolytes, thyroid function tests, anti-nuclear antibodies, and clotting studies were normal

A clonal disorder of dendritic cells that can affect skin, lungs, bones, and liver. This is the leading possibility given the scalp eruption, nodular-cystic lung abnormalities, and apparent lytic sternal lesion; tissue biopsy is needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Chronic crusting erythematous scalp rash resembling seborrheic dermatitis
Bilateral pulmonary nodules and irregular cystic or cavitary lesions on imaging
Apparent lytic lesion in the sternum
Raised CRP and ALT, potentially reflecting systemic inflammation and liver involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Neutrophilia is nonspecific rather than a characteristic diagnostic finding

data.description: An inflammatory small-vessel vasculitis that commonly affects the respiratory tract and kidneys and can cause skin lesions and cavitating pulmonary nodules.
symptoms_in_common: Skin eruption, although the described scalp appearance is less characteristic
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic seborrheic-like crusting scalp rash
Numerous irregular pulmonary cysts rather than predominantly discrete cavitating nodules
Apparent lytic sternal lesion
Raised ALT is not a defining feature

data.description: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can cause upper-lung cavitation, constitutional symptoms, and occasionally cutaneous or skeletal disease.
symptoms_in_common: An apparent destructive bone lesion could represent skeletal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic diffuse crusting erythematous scalp rash
Widespread irregular thin- and thick-walled pulmonary cysts
Raised ALT without established hepatic infection is nonspecific

data.description: A geographically associated fungal infection that may involve the lungs, skin, and bones. Its likelihood depends on travel and environmental exposure history.
symptoms_not_in_common: Seborrheic-like scalp rash rather than typical verrucous or ulcerative lesions
Diffuse irregular pulmonary cysts are not a typical imaging pattern
Raised ALT is not a characteristic finding

data.diagnosis: Sarcoidosis with pulmonary, cutaneous, and possible skeletal involvement
data.description: A multisystem granulomatous disease that can affect the lungs, skin, liver, and occasionally bones. The cystic-cavitary imaging pattern makes it less likely than Langerhans cell histiocytosis.
symptoms_in_common: Raised ALT could reflect hepatic involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Chronic crusting scalp rash is an unusual cutaneous presentation
Numerous cavitating nodules and irregular pulmonary cysts
Neutrophilia is not characteristic
A solitary apparent lytic sternal lesion is uncommon

diagnoses.name: Pulmonary involvement in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
diagnoses.title: Adult pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis

diagnoses.name: Skeletal involvement in Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
diagnoses.title: Langerhans cell histiocytosis

data.diagnosis: Langerhans cell histiocytosis (multisystem, with pulmonary, skin, bone and possible liver involvement)
data.description: Clonal proliferation of Langerhans-type dendritic cells that infiltrate multiple organs; classically causes seborrhoeic-like crusting scalp rash, lytic bone lesions, and upper/mid-zone predominant lung nodules that cavitate into bizarre-shaped cysts; liver involvement may raise liver enzymes.
symptoms_in_common: Crusting erythematous scalp rash for six months
Bilateral upper and mid-zone predominant reticulonodular opacities on chest X-ray
Multiple cavitating nodules and thick- and thin-walled cysts on CT
Lytic lesion in the sternum (manubrium) on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Neutrophilia is non-specific
Involvement extending towards the costophrenic angles (usually spared in adults, though often involved in children)
No smoking history reported (isolated pulmonary form is usually smoking-related)
No diabetes insipidus reported

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary tuberculosis (with possible disseminated disease including skeletal and cutaneous involvement)
data.description: Chronic granulomatous infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, typically causing upper-lobe cavitating disease with constitutional symptoms; can disseminate to bone, liver and skin.
symptoms_in_common: Weight loss and tiredness for two months
Upper-zone predominant nodular opacities with cavitation
symptoms_not_in_common: Six-month crusting erythematous scalp rash
Numerous diffuse thin-walled cysts in both lungs
No cough, fever, night sweats or haemoptysis reported
No tree-in-bud pattern or lymphadenopathy described
Neutrophilia is not typical

data.description: ANCA-associated small-vessel necrotising granulomatous vasculitis affecting the respiratory tract, kidneys and skin, typically producing multiple cavitating lung nodules and raised inflammatory markers.
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal urea and electrolytes (no renal involvement)
No sinonasal symptoms or haemoptysis reported
Crusting scalp rash is not a typical skin manifestation
Lytic sternal lesion
Numerous thin-walled cysts
Raised ALT
Uncommon at age 15

data.diagnosis: Septic pulmonary emboli / disseminated staphylococcal infection (e.g. from infected scalp lesion, with osteomyelitis)
data.description: Haematogenous spread of bacteria (commonly Staphylococcus aureus) from a skin or other focus, causing multiple bilateral cavitating nodules, pneumatoceles and possible bone infection.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple bilateral cavitating nodules and cyst-like lesions (pneumatoceles)
Crusting scalp rash as a possible skin source
symptoms_not_in_common: Subacute two-month course without reported fever or acute sepsis
Six-month chronic scalp rash
Upper and mid-zone predominance (septic emboli are usually peripheral and basal)
Prominent weight loss
Normal clotting studies

data.diagnosis: Chronic disseminated fungal infection (e.g. histoplasmosis, coccidioidomycosis or cryptococcosis)
data.description: Systemic mycosis that can cause cavitating pulmonary nodules, constitutional symptoms, and dissemination to skin, bone and liver, particularly in immunocompromised hosts or endemic areas.
symptoms_not_in_common: No known immunodeficiency or endemic exposure reported
Extensive thin-walled cystic change in both lungs
Rash limited to the scalp with a seborrhoeic-like appearance
No fever reported
No lymphadenopathy described

data.description: A 40-year-old woman presented with a palpable lump in her left superior breast. Mammography and US and biopsy performed, confirming invasive carcinoma NST Grade 2. MRI performed pre-operatively due to occult on mammography. Subsequent left breast mastectomy and reconstruction with right breast mastopexy.

data.diagnosis: Invasive breast carcinoma of no special type, grade 2
data.description: An invasive epithelial breast cancer, also called invasive ductal carcinoma NST. This is the biopsy-confirmed diagnosis of the left breast lump.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable lump in the superior left breast
Irregular hypoechoic mass measuring approximately 37 mm on ultrasound
Irregular enhancing left breast mass on MRI
Mammographically occult lesion in dense breast tissue
Biopsy confirming grade 2 invasive carcinoma NST
symptoms_not_in_common: The separate postoperative right breast lesion with apparent internal fat is not typical of an untreated invasive carcinoma

data.description: Benign inflammation and breakdown of breast fat following surgery or trauma. This is a plausible explanation for the separate right breast lesion after mastopexy, particularly given apparent internal fat and peripheral enhancement.
symptoms_in_common: Postoperative right breast lesion near the chest wall
Apparent internal fat signal in the right breast lesion
Peripheral enhancement surrounding the right breast lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy-confirmed invasive carcinoma in the left breast
The preoperative irregular left breast mass cannot be explained by postoperative fat necrosis

data.description: An invasive breast cancer with a diffuse infiltrative growth pattern that can be difficult to detect on mammography. It is an imaging differential, not the established histologic diagnosis here.
symptoms_not_in_common: Biopsy identified carcinoma NST rather than lobular carcinoma
Apparent internal fat in the postoperative right breast lesion is not typical

data.description: A benign fibroepithelial breast tumor that commonly presents as a palpable solid lump. It is a pre-biopsy differential but does not explain the confirmed left breast cancer.
symptoms_in_common: A lesion potentially obscured by dense breast tissue on mammography
symptoms_not_in_common: Irregular mass margins and posterior acoustic shadowing
Irregular enhancing left breast mass on MRI
Biopsy-confirmed invasive carcinoma NST

data.description: A separate primary cancer in the opposite breast. The right breast enhancing focus warrants consideration, but the supplied postoperative features favor fat necrosis and do not establish a second malignancy.
symptoms_in_common: Separate enhancing focus in the right breast
An enhancing right breast lesion visible on subsequent MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent internal fat within the right breast lesion favors fat necrosis
Right breast mastopexy provides a benign postoperative explanation
The reported biopsy confirms only the left breast carcinoma, not a right breast malignancy

data.diagnosis: Fat necrosis of the right breast following mastopexy
data.description: Benign, sterile inflammatory process of adipose tissue after surgery or trauma, forming an oil cyst or nodule. On MRI it typically shows a central fat-signal component with a thin or thick enhancing rim, and it can mimic malignancy.
symptoms_in_common: New enhancing lesion in the posterior right breast on follow-up MRI after right mastopexy
Lesion appears to have a central fat-signal area (bright on non-fat-suppressed images, dark on fat-suppressed and subtraction images)
Rim enhancement around a non-enhancing centre
Located at a site of previous surgery
No corresponding lesion in the right breast on the pre-operative MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Enhancement is fairly avid and nodular, which can overlap with malignancy
Lesion appears to enlarge between follow-up studies, whereas fat necrosis usually stabilises or involutes
History of contralateral invasive carcinoma raises pre-test probability of malignancy

data.diagnosis: Metachronous contralateral primary breast carcinoma (invasive carcinoma NST)
data.description: A new, independent primary cancer in the opposite breast, for which women with a prior breast cancer, particularly those diagnosed young, are at increased risk.
symptoms_in_common: Personal history of invasive carcinoma NST Grade 2 at age 40
New enhancing lesion in the right breast on surveillance MRI
Apparent interval growth of the lesion
Rim enhancement can be seen in malignancy
Dense breasts, with the original cancer occult on mammography
symptoms_not_in_common: Central fat signal within the lesion is unusual for carcinoma
Location at a surgical site in the posterior breast favours a post-operative change
No reported palpable lump or clinical symptoms in the right breast

data.diagnosis: Contralateral breast metastasis or recurrence of the left breast carcinoma
data.description: Spread of the original left breast carcinoma to the opposite breast via lymphatic or haematogenous routes. This is uncommon and usually presents as a well-defined enhancing nodule.
symptoms_in_common: Known left invasive carcinoma (about 37 mm on ultrasound, with satellite enhancing foci on MRI)
New enhancing nodule in the contralateral breast
Posterior and medial location could fit lymphatic spread across the midline
symptoms_not_in_common: Fat-containing centre is not typical of metastasis
No evidence of local recurrence in the reconstructed left breast or of other metastatic disease
Solitary lesion at a surgical site is more suggestive of a post-operative change

data.diagnosis: Post-surgical suture granuloma or scar tissue
data.description: Foreign-body granulomatous reaction or enhancing granulation tissue at a surgical site. It may enhance on MRI for 12 to 18 months or longer after surgery.
symptoms_in_common: Small enhancing focus at the operative bed on follow-up MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Central fat signal is more characteristic of fat necrosis than of a granuloma
Scar enhancement is usually linear or thin and decreases over time rather than appearing nodular, rim-enhancing and enlarging

data.description: Benign lymph node within the breast parenchyma, showing a fatty hilum and avid enhancement with washout. It may enlarge reactively after surgery.
symptoms_in_common: Central fat signal could represent a fatty hilum
symptoms_not_in_common: Posterior, medial-central location near the pectoralis is atypical, as intramammary nodes are usually in the upper outer quadrant
Not seen on the pre-operative MRI
Fat is central with a complete enhancing rim rather than an eccentric hilum with a reniform shape

data.description: A 35-year-old patient presented to A&E with complaints of sudden onset pain in scrotum extending to perineum, scrotal swelling, loss of penile erection following sexual intercourse. On examination the patient had scrotal swelling and bruising at the base of the penis and scrotum, but no penile swelling.

data.diagnosis: Proximal penile fracture of the right corpus cavernosum
data.description: Rupture of the tunica albuginea near the penile base during intercourse. This is the leading diagnosis: the supplied MRI images indicate a right proximal tunical defect with hematoma extending into the scrotum. Urgent urological assessment is required.
symptoms_in_common: Bruising at the penile base and scrotum
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of penile swelling is atypical for a shaft fracture, but compatible with a proximal fracture

data.description: Traumatic rupture of a penile vein can cause bruising and hematoma resembling penile fracture, but without a tunica albuginea tear. The depicted tunical defect makes this less likely as the sole diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Scrotal bruising and swelling from tracking blood
symptoms_not_in_common: Immediate loss of erection is less typical than in penile fracture
Predominantly scrotal and perineal pain without penile swelling

data.description: Accumulation of blood in scrotal and perineal soft tissues after injury. A hematoma is depicted in the supplied images, although the proximal corporal tear is the likely underlying cause rather than an isolated soft-tissue injury.
symptoms_in_common: Acute scrotal pain extending to the perineum
symptoms_not_in_common: Immediate loss of erection is not characteristic of an isolated scrotal hematoma

data.description: Tearing of the urethra can produce perineal and scrotal bleeding and may accompany penile fracture. It is not established by the supplied images; urinary symptoms and dedicated evaluation would help assess it.
symptoms_in_common: Bruising involving the scrotum and penile base
symptoms_not_in_common: Immediate loss of erection is not typical of an isolated urethral injury

data.description: Twisting of the spermatic cord causes acute testicular ischemia and is an emergency consideration in sudden scrotal pain. It is substantially less likely here because the depicted proximal penile tear and hematoma better explain the presentation.
symptoms_not_in_common: Bruising at the penile base and scrotum
Immediate loss of erection associated with intercourse
Pain extending predominantly toward the perineum

data.diagnosis: Penile fracture (proximal rupture of the tunica albuginea of the right corpus cavernosum)
data.description: Traumatic tear of the tunica albuginea of the corpus cavernosum, usually during intercourse with an erect penis. A proximal (crural/base) tear can allow the haematoma to track into the scrotum and perineum rather than the penile shaft.
symptoms_in_common: sudden onset pain during/after sexual intercourse
bruising at the base of the penis and scrotum
MRI annotated as showing a defect in the tunica albuginea of the right corpus cavernosum near the penile base
soft tissue haematoma extending into the scrotal sac on MRI and ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: no penile shaft swelling (the classic 'eggplant deformity' is absent)
pain felt mainly in the scrotum rather than the penis
no cracking/popping sound reported

data.diagnosis: Rupture of the superficial or deep dorsal vein of the penis (false penile fracture)
data.description: Tear of penile dorsal vessels during intercourse, causing haematoma and bruising that mimics penile fracture but with an intact tunica albuginea.
symptoms_in_common: sudden onset pain after sexual intercourse
bruising at the base of the penis
symptoms_not_in_common: immediate loss of erection (detumescence is usually gradual)
tunica albuginea defect on MRI
no penile shaft swelling or bruising, which is typical of dorsal vein rupture
predominantly scrotal and perineal pain

data.description: Blunt scrotal trauma causing a tear of the testicular tunica albuginea or bleeding into the scrotal wall or tunica vaginalis.
symptoms_not_in_common: right testis appears intact with normal contour and echotexture on ultrasound
loss of penile erection
bruising at the base of the penis
cavernosal tunica albuginea defect on MRI
no direct scrotal blow reported

data.diagnosis: Urethral injury (bulbar urethral or corpus spongiosum rupture)
data.description: Tear of the urethra or corpus spongiosum from blunt perineal or coital trauma, which may occur alone or together with penile fracture. Blood and urine can track into the scrotum and perineum.
symptoms_in_common: haematoma at the base of the penis tracking to the scrotum
symptoms_not_in_common: no blood at the urethral meatus reported
no haematuria or difficulty voiding reported
immediate loss of erection is not explained by an isolated urethral injury
the MRI defect is in the corpus cavernosum, not the spongiosum or urethra

data.description: Twisting of the spermatic cord causing acute testicular ischaemia. It presents with sudden severe scrotal pain and swelling and can occasionally be triggered by sexual activity.

data.description: A 17-year-old girl presented to the emergency department with constipation and bloodless vomiting for 3 weeks. The vomiting worsened after food ingestion. The patient was exhausted and underweight, although she did not suffer abdominal pain. At admission, the patient had unwillingly lost 10 kg over 2 years, resulting in a body mass index of 14. During this period, she started prevention medicine due to a loss of menstruation. The patient had no prior medical or surgical history. Blood tests revealed an increased sed rate (ESR) of 33 (normal range: 2-20) as the only outlier. A contrast-enhanced CT was ordered based on the acute exacerbating of vomiting and constipation, with ileus as the tentative diagnosis.

Compression of the third portion of the duodenum between the superior mesenteric artery and aorta, often following loss of the intervening fat pad. This is the leading possibility: the initial CT images show marked gastroduodenal dilation, an aortomesenteric distance of approximately 3.3 mm, and an angle of approximately 13.6 degrees.
symptoms_in_common: Severe underweight status with BMI of 14
Constipation associated with reduced intake and proximal obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of abdominal pain, although painless presentations occur
Mildly elevated ESR, which is not a characteristic finding

data.description: Delayed gastric emptying without a mechanical obstruction, causing food retention and postprandial vomiting. It is less likely if the apparent duodenal vascular compression is confirmed.
symptoms_in_common: Constipation, potentially accompanying generalized gastrointestinal dysmotility
symptoms_not_in_common: Amenorrhea is not a direct manifestation
Elevated ESR is not characteristic
Apparent focal duodenal compression on CT argues against isolated gastroparesis

data.diagnosis: Partial duodenal obstruction from a congenital duodenal web
data.description: A congenital membrane that incompletely narrows the duodenal lumen and can occasionally present in adolescence with chronic feeding intolerance and proximal intestinal dilation.
symptoms_in_common: Marked proximal gastrointestinal dilation on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Amenorrhea is secondary to nutritional compromise rather than a direct feature
Elevated ESR is not characteristic
The narrow aortomesenteric angle and distance favor vascular compression rather than an intrinsic membrane

data.diagnosis: Crohn disease with gastroduodenal involvement and stricture
data.description: Inflammatory bowel disease that can rarely narrow the stomach or duodenum, producing proximal obstruction and nutritional depletion.
symptoms_in_common: Amenorrhea potentially resulting from chronic illness and malnutrition
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of abdominal pain is less typical
Constipation is less typical than diarrhea, unless obstruction develops
The supplied images favor aortomesenteric compression rather than an inflammatory stricture

data.description: A severe intestinal motility disorder that produces obstruction-like symptoms without a fixed mechanical blockage. It is less likely when a focal duodenal compression is demonstrated.
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of abdominal pain is less typical
Amenorrhea is not a direct manifestation
Elevated ESR is not characteristic of a primary motility disorder
Focal narrowing between the aorta and superior mesenteric artery favors mechanical obstruction

data.description: Compression of the third part of the duodenum between the aorta and the superior mesenteric artery due to loss of the mesenteric fat pad, typically after marked weight loss, causing proximal duodenal and gastric obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Marked unintentional weight loss (10 kg, BMI 14)
CT showing massively dilated stomach and proximal duodenum
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of abdominal pain (postprandial epigastric pain is usual)
Mildly elevated ESR
Amenorrhea is not directly explained (likely secondary to malnutrition)

data.description: Eating disorder with restricted energy intake leading to very low body weight, often with amenorrhea, delayed gastric emptying and constipation; it can itself predispose to SMA syndrome.

symptoms_not_in_common: Weight loss described as unwilling/unintentional
Mechanical duodenal compression with narrowed aortomesenteric angle and distance on CT
Acute worsening of vomiting after food
Elevated ESR (usually low or normal)

data.diagnosis: Crohn's disease (with upper gastrointestinal or small-bowel stricture)
data.description: Chronic transmural inflammatory bowel disease that can cause strictures, obstruction, weight loss and raised inflammatory markers in adolescents.

symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal pain
Constipation rather than diarrhea
No blood in stool or vomit
No bowel wall thickening or inflammatory changes described on CT
Obstruction located at the aortomesenteric crossing
Otherwise normal blood tests (no anemia, normal CRP)

data.description: Delayed gastric emptying without mechanical obstruction, causing postprandial vomiting, early satiety and weight loss; may be idiopathic, post-viral or associated with malnutrition.
symptoms_not_in_common: Dilated duodenum with abrupt cut-off at the level of the SMA

No diabetes or other predisposing condition

data.diagnosis: Mechanical small bowel obstruction from another cause (e.g., intestinal malrotation with Ladd bands/midgut volvulus, or duodenal mass)

symptoms_in_common: Dilated stomach and duodenum on CT
Ileus as the tentative clinical diagnosis
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal pain
No prior surgery (adhesions unlikely)
Two-year chronic course
No mass, whirl sign or malposition of mesenteric vessels described
Transition point lies exactly between aorta and SMA
Bloodless vomiting

data.description: A 12-year-old female presented to the Emergency Department with a 48-hour history of abdominal pain localised in the hypogastrium, which had progressively worsened in the last few hours. data.diagnosis: Hematocolpos due to an imperforate hymen

Presentation at an age when menstruation commonly begins

data.diagnosis: Hematocolpos due to a transverse vaginal septum

Pelvic fluid collection containing internal echoes

data.description: Congenital absence or closure of the lower vaginal segment, causing retained menstrual blood above the obstruction. Examination and additional pelvic imaging are needed to define the anatomy.

Ultrasound showing large, well-defined midline pelvic cystic collection with homogeneous low-level internal echoes (retained blood) posterior to the bladder
Uterus seen at the cranial end of the collection

data.diagnosis: Hematocolpos/hematometrocolpos due to transverse vaginal septum or distal vaginal atresia

data.diagnosis: Obstructed hemivagina with ipsilateral renal anomaly (OHVIRA / Herlyn-Werner-Wunderlich syndrome)

data.description: A 58-year-old male with worsening nausea for the past 72 hours presented to the emergency department with severe chest pain radiating to the back in the context of 4 recent episodes of non-bloody, non-bilious emesis. Subcutaneous emphysema

Subcutaneous emphysema

data.description: A 12-year-old Malagasy boy consulted for a fever that had been evolving for two months, with a notion of trauma and pain in the right upper quadrant as well as chronic diarrhoea. data.description: Schistosoma mansoni infection causes intestinal inflammation and hepatic egg deposition, potentially leading to granulomas, periportal fibrosis and portal hypertension. Stool eggs establish infection, but do not prove that all hepatic lesions are attributable to it.

Right-lobe hepatic lesions compatible with an abscess

data.diagnosis: Pyogenic liver abscess associated with Schistosoma mansoni infection

Hypodense multiloculated/clustered lesion with peripheral rim on CT

data.description: Hepatic collection caused by Entamoeba histolytica spreading from the colon through the portal vein, typically a solitary lesion in the right lobe, in tropical regions.

Multiloculated/clustered heterogeneous appearance (amoebic abscess is usually unilocular and homogeneous)

Splenomegaly

No well-defined cyst wall, calcification or daughter cysts
Splenomegaly

data.description: A 13-year-old male presented with pain in the right hypochondrium and loss of appetite for 1 month. There was no history of fever. The patient has a history of a successfully treated abdominal tuberculosis, for which he had taken anti-tubercular treatment for 1 year.

Absence of fever compatible with a noninfectious vascular disorder

data.description: A benign hepatic lesion caused by a localized response to abnormal blood flow. A large lesion can cause discomfort and mimic mass-like liver enlargement; multiphasic imaging or hepatobiliary MRI can help distinguish it from a hypertrophied liver segment.

data.description: A 39-year-old male, with no prior relevant medical history, presents with atraumatic intermittent sharp pain in the lower segment of the right anterior thoracic wall.
